# Experiment audit against DECISIONS.md

Made 2026-10-04 by a workflow: one agent read each experiment, a second agent re-read the code to try to refute every problem. Read-only; no code was changed. These are agent findings with file:line, not measured results.

Rules checked (the owner's, 2026-10-03):
- R1 only the dataset's two approved models (knn only per Step 9)
- R2 every hybrid for a fold comes from a search on that fold's training rows
- R3 every search uses the dataset's decided budgets, importance methods, allocation methods, evaluators, representation counts, augmentation
- R4 per model per fold: 2 best base representations + 2 best hybrids
- R5 noise only: 8 configurations
- R6 a missing per-fold search is built by the experiment

One row is one experiment. NO = breaks the rule. "(partly)" = the second agent agreed with a correction; "(refuted)" = the second agent found the claim wrong. Details per experiment below.

## Shared code every experiment goes through

### search-readers

**_apply_dataset_search_speed** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1015), complies: no

Edits the find_best_hybrid arguments before a search runs. For a dataset in dataset_policy.FAST_SPEED_DATASETS (dataset_policy.py:688-711, 14 names) it sets speed='fast'. When models is None it names the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS, or DISTANCE_MODELS (the five plus knn) on a general_distance tier (1076-1079). It then calls _apply_small_dataset_models. An explicit speed= from the caller wins (1046-1048).

- It is the only per-dataset grid choice in the code, and it does not read DECISIONS.md. A grep of src/ and tests/ .py and .sh files finds no reference to DECISIONS or precompute_cuts.
- The code's fast list has 14 datasets. The DECISIONS 'Fast-tier datasets' table has 10. The four extra in code are flab_expression_koenig, logd, bindingdb_kd and kiba.
- On those four the code runs the fast grid: lightgbm_gain only (find_best_hybrid.py:3674), three allocation methods (:3072), representation counts 3 and all (:3071).
- DECISIONS keeps full-grid settings there. flab_expression_koenig keeps all three importance methods (Step 3). kiba keeps only 'all' representations (Step 6). bindingdb_kd keeps 2 and all (Step 6). Fast has no 2.
- So on kiba and bindingdb_kd the code and DECISIONS differ in three ways at once: importance methods, allocation methods, and representation counts.
- The fast lists are the same for all 10 fast datasets in DECISIONS, so those 10 match. No other Step 2-7 cut is applied anywhere.

**_apply_small_dataset_models** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1084), complies: partly

Adds gp to the model list for registered datasets under 1,000 rows (dataset_policy.py:744-776). Printed in this session: abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho and abagym_EGFR get gp. tcga_brca_pam50, ddg_combined and flab_thermo_tresanco do not. It only adds; it never cuts the list to the dataset's two models.

- Five approved pairs need gp (abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho), and this supplies it on paths that call it.
- abagym_EGFR is approved as svm+dnn, but it also gets gp scored.
- Every search still scores all five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS as well, so R1 (two models only) is not applied.

**search_on_fold** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1389), complies: partly

Runs find_best_hybrid on ONE outer fold's training rows. Every array is sliced to train_idx (1459-1466). The search is filed under the per-fold namespace ocv{n}f{i}s{seed} (1450-1451). One search per augmentation condition. Defaults: budgets FULL_BUDGETS (8 budgets, 1435-1436); models None, then _apply_dataset_search_speed (1484); evaluators, allocation, importance and representation counts are not passed, so the engine defaults apply.

- R2: complies. The search sees that fold's training rows only.
- R3: engine defaults on full datasets are 5 allocation methods (find_best_hybrid.py:3684-3690), 3 importance methods (:3675), evaluators match/rf/lightgbm/dnn (:3705), representation counts 2/3/5/all (:3070). No per-dataset cut from Steps 2-7.
- R1: scores rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm (plus gp under 1,000 rows), not the two approved models.
- Step 8: 'uncapped' and, on the general tier, 'capped' are added whenever the caller passes augmentations (1444-1448). There is no per-dataset augmentation cut.
- R6: under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, the 'general' tier counts as one the precompute owns, and own_search is not passed. find_best_hybrid refuses with RuntimeError when more than 500 configurations are missing (find_best_hybrid.py:705-750, 9355-9369).
- By _expected_config_count (find_best_hybrid.py:608-633), a full-grid fold search is 8,160 configurations and a fast one 816. Both are over 500, so an unwarmed fold search is refused.
- search_on_fold catches that RuntimeError as an ordinary failure (1489-1493) and returns None for that condition. It does not build the search.
- submit_everything.sh sets COLD_REFUSAL=1 by default (line 94) and exports KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 (line 364).

**get_fold_best_search** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1497), complies: partly

Calls search_on_fold for one fold (memoised by the exact training rows, 1531-1566). For each augmentation condition it takes get_best_for_downstream(search, model, budget). It returns the single best across conditions (1568-1590), with selection_scope 'fold_train_rows'. distance=True switches to tier general_distance, DISTANCE_BUDGETS (10-500), DISTANCE_EVALUATORS (knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm) and DISTANCE_MODELS (1518-1527).

- R2: complies. The recipe comes from a search on that fold's training rows.
- R4: it returns one hybrid per call and no base representations. Two hybrids and two base representations need a caller to read the returned search with top_hybrids/top_base_reps.
- It has no check that downstream_model was scored in the fold search. get_best_search_for_downstream has that check (6307-6311); this function does not.
- get_best_for_downstream falls back to a model-agnostic best (7526-7529) and then to any model's best (7540-7545). So a model the fold search never scored is handed another model's recipe under its own name.
- R3: distance defaults are the same six budgets, five evaluators and six models on every dataset. Step 7 cuts budgets, evaluators and representation counts per dataset (e.g. buchwald_hartwig cuts dnn/knn/svm evaluators).
- R6: same refusal path as search_on_fold. A refused fold search returns (None, None) (1578-1579).

**run_nested_cv** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1129), complies: partly

Calls kirby.find_best_hybrid.nested_cv_evaluate. Arguments: models=None (1183), budgets from config or FULL_BUDGETS (1175), importance_methods from config (1200-1201), evaluators only if passed. It does NOT call _apply_dataset_search_speed. The six calls in _shared.py are at 1329, 1484, 4808, 5592, 5895 and the definition; none is inside 1129-1215.

- R2: complies. nested_cv_evaluate runs each inner search on outer-train rows only (find_best_hybrid.py:10898-10905).
- On the 14 fast datasets it runs the full grid, because speed is never set and the engine default is 'full' (find_best_hybrid.py signature, speed='full').
- No gp is ever scored, because _apply_small_dataset_models is never called and gp is tier 'extra'. So the five gp pairs in Step 1 cannot be produced here.
- precompute_nested_cv_searches does call _apply_dataset_search_speed (1329). It writes into the same per-fold namespace as run_nested_cv.
- So the per-fold warm-up and run_nested_cv ask for different searches on fast datasets and on small datasets. They differ in two ways at once: speed and model list.
- R1: models=None gives rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm on every dataset, not the approved two.
- R3: no Step 2-7 cut; budgets are 8, importance 3 from get_config (9343).
- R4: nested_cv_evaluate keeps one hybrid per model (best_by_model, find_best_hybrid.py:10951) and one best single representation per model (11083-11095), and scores every representation.
- R6: an inner refusal is printed as 'inner search FAILED' and that fold is skipped (10906-10910). If every fold fails it raises RuntimeError (11197-11203).

**nested_cv_evaluate** (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:10561), complies: partly

For each outer fold, it slices to outer-train rows. It runs find_best_hybrid there under namespace ocv{n}f{i}s{seed} (10849-10857). For every model in inner.best_by_model it rebuilds that winner on outer-train and scores it on the outer test fold (10942-11015). Every base representation is scored too (11042-11069). The best single representation is picked from the inner search's baselines on outer-train (11079-11095).

- R2: complies.
- R4: one hybrid per model, not two. One picked base representation per model, not two, though all are scored.
- Models, budgets, importance, evaluators, allocation and representation counts are whatever the caller forwards. Nothing in it applies FAST_SPEED_DATASETS or DECISIONS cuts.

**precompute_nested_cv_searches** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1218), complies: partly

Warms the per-fold inner searches. For every outer fold from nested_cv_outer_folds, and every augmentation condition, it runs find_best_hybrid on that fold's training rows (1296-1330). It applies _apply_dataset_search_speed. Defaults: FULL_BUDGETS, models as passed (None by default), engine default evaluators.

- R2: complies; each search is on one fold's training rows.
- It does not match run_nested_cv on fast or small datasets (see run_nested_cv), so its searches are not the ones run_nested_cv reads there.
- R3: no Step 2-7 cut. Step 8: none, uncapped and capped (general) whenever augmentations are passed (1275-1280).
- Failures other than StaleResultDB are recorded and the fold is left None (1339-1347).

**fold_reselection** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1814), complies: no

Arithmetic only, no fitting. For each model in its input, and each held-out fold, it picks the hybrid recipe and the single representation with the best mean over the other folds (_hr_lofo_score, 1632-1724). It reports the paired per-fold difference.

- R2: its per-fold scores come from build_fold_reselection_input, which reads one stored search. In practice that search ran over all rows, so the held-out fold's rows trained the models behind every score.
- The comment at 963-977 says this kind of re-score over a whole-dataset search was removed on 2026-07-13 and must not return. The function was restored on 2026-08-24 (1612-1618). The two disagree.
- R4: one hybrid and one base representation per fold per model, not two of each.
- R1: every model present in the input is scored; nothing limits it to the approved two.

**build_fold_reselection_input** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1961), complies: no

Reads one SearchResult. Hybrid candidates are every row of search.all_results, grouped by model (2011-2022). Baselines are search.baseline_fold_scores for every representation and model (2024-2034). Fold 0 is excluded when the search pruned on fold 0 (2038-2045).

- R2: the per-fold scores are from whatever search is passed; the whole-dataset precompute is the usual source.
- R1: every model in the search enters, including knn or gp where scored.
- R3: every stored configuration enters. No Step 2-7 cut is applied to the candidate list.

**get_fold_pool_recipes** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:6641), complies: no

Reads stored searches only (no search of its own, 6652-6654). For one model, it ranks every stored configuration and every base representation by the mean over the other folds (6846-6963). It returns the top n_hybrids per search family and the best base representation (plus the ranked list). fold_i=None ranks on all folds. distance=True adds DISTANCE_EVALUATORS, DISTANCE_BUDGETS, DISTANCE_MODELS (6774-6777).

- R2: the stored search ran over every row. Its own selection_note says it holds out the fold's scores, not its rows (7038-7042).
- R3: it ranks every stored configuration; no Step 2-7 cut.
- When the named budget was not scored it ranks over every budget the search holds and sets budget_relaxed (6855-6872).
- Step 8: augmentation conditions come from _pool_conditions, with no per-dataset cut.
- R6: a missing search goes through get_precomputed_search. It is built on all rows, or refused, or skipped with a warning (6108-6114). It is never built per fold.

**get_rule_hybrids (RULE_N_GENERAL=2, RULE_N_DISTANCE=1, RULE_N_BASE=2)** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:7069 (constants 7064-7066)), complies: no

Calls get_fold_pool_recipes twice: general with 2 hybrids, distance with 1 (7130-7137). It takes the top 2 base representations from the general read (7183-7185). For knn it names MAIN_MODELS_WITH_KNN for the general read (7124-7127). Missing slots are listed and printed (7171-7202).

- R2: it reads whole-dataset searches through get_fold_pool_recipes. Leaving out fold k's scores does not leave out fold k's rows.
- R4: it gives 3 hybrids per model (2 general + 1 distance), not 2.
- R5: for noise, two models times (2 base + 3 hybrids) is 10 configurations, not 8.
- R1: no restriction to the approved pair; the caller chooses downstream_model.
- R3: no Step 2-7 cut on either the general or the distance read.
- R6: a missing slot is reported missing, not built per fold.

**get_best_search_for_downstream** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:6126), complies: no

Reads the whole-dataset pool: in-memory data['precomputed_searches'] or the distance dict, else disk. For one model and budget it picks the single best (tier, augmentation condition) (6292-6359). Returns metadata with selection_scope 'whole_dataset' (6430). Distance defaults are DISTANCE_EVALUATORS, DISTANCE_BUDGETS, DISTANCE_MODELS (6245-6251).

- R2: whole-dataset search; its own metadata says the recipe was chosen on all rows (6422-6432).
- R4: one hybrid; no base representations.
- R3: same distance lists on every dataset. Step 7 cuts budgets, evaluators and representation counts per dataset.
- R6: with nothing usable it prints a warning and returns (None, None) (6320-6328).

**get_precomputed_search** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5752), complies: no

Returns the in-memory search for an augmentation condition if present (5831-5843). Otherwise it calls find_best_hybrid(cache=True) on the rows passed, with FULL_BUDGETS and adaptive_pruning=False, after _apply_dataset_search_speed (5863-5896).

- R2: the rows passed are the whole dataset in every pool caller, so this builds or reads a whole-dataset search.
- R6: under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH a missing search with 500 or fewer configurations left is built here; a bigger one raises RuntimeError (find_best_hybrid.py:705-750).
- _iter_pool_searches catches that, prints a warning and skips the member (6108-6114). Without the variable, the whole-dataset search is built inside the job.

**_pool_conditions** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:6014), complies: no

Lists the pool members. Always 'none'. 'uncapped' when augmentations are passed, except kiba and bindingdb_kd (UNCAPPED_SKIP_DATASETS, 5989). 'capped' on the general tier, and on the distance tier when there are fewer than 10,000 rows (6036-6037). KIRBY_LOCAL_AUG_CONDITIONS can cut it locally.

- Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 of 41 datasets. It keeps uncapped only on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, on the distance search.
- This function adds uncapped and capped on every dataset whenever the caller passes augmentations. It does not read Step 8.

**precompute_hybrid_searches** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5452), complies: no

One find_best_hybrid call per augmentation condition on all rows (5569-5593). Defaults: FULL_BUDGETS, models as passed, engine default evaluators. It applies _apply_dataset_search_speed. Conditions are none, uncapped and capped whenever augmentations are passed (5543-5549).

- R2: whole-dataset search.
- R3 and Step 8: no per-dataset cut.

**populate_precompute_dicts** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5642), complies: no

Fills data['precomputed_searches'] (general, FULL_BUDGETS, models None) and data['precomputed_searches_distance'] (DISTANCE_BUDGETS, DISTANCE_EVALUATORS, DISTANCE_MODELS) by calling precompute_hybrid_searches on all rows (5684-5718).

- R2: both dicts hold whole-dataset searches; every pool reader above reads them first.
- R3: same global lists on every dataset.

**build_fold_hybrid** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5091), complies: partly

Rebuilds one given blueprint on a fold's training rows with create_hybrid and applies it to the validation rows. It chooses no recipe; the recipe is the caller's.

- The fit is on the fold's training rows. Whether the recipe is per fold depends on where the caller got the blueprint.
- When blueprint.rep_count is below the pool size and the caller passes no precomputed_alloc_scores, it uses blueprint.rep_scores to decide WHICH representations to keep (5256-5286).
- find_best_hybrid fills rep_scores from baselines measured over every row the search ran on, taking each representation's best score across all models (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593).
- The comment at 5349-5354 says whole-dataset rep_scores are not used, to avoid a leak. It is right about the budget split and wrong about the representation count. So with a whole-dataset blueprint, the choice of representations also leaks.

**fold_hybrid_scoring_kwargs** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5070), complies: not applicable

Returns {model, metric_fn, lower_is_better} for a predictive recipe and {} for a recipe searched under a geometry objective. It reads no search and builds none.


**build_hybrid_from_entry / _create_hybrid_from_blueprint** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:7228 and 7248), complies: partly

Fits one recipe from a get_rule_hybrids or get_fold_pool_recipes entry on the rows passed. It restricts to the recipe's representations and calls restrict_to_rep_count with no scores (7259-7260).

- restrict_to_rep_count falls back to blueprint.rep_scores (find_best_hybrid.py:9707-9708). For a stored whole-dataset recipe, that is the same leak as in build_fold_hybrid.
- The recipe itself comes from a whole-dataset search (see get_rule_hybrids).

**get_best_for_downstream** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:7482), complies: no

Looks up one config in a SearchResult. Order: the model at the budget; the model's best across budgets; best_by_budget for any model (7526-7529); best_by_model for the model; then the best of any model (7540-7545).

- The last two fallbacks return another model's recipe under the requested model's name. get_fold_best_search calls it without first checking the model was scored.

**get_fitted_pool_hybrid / get_fitted_hybrid** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:7287 and 7334), complies: no

Pick one recipe from the whole-dataset pool (or one stored search) and build the hybrid on the rows passed, normally all rows.

- R2: whole-dataset recipe and whole-dataset fit.
- R4: one hybrid.

**noise_base_reps_by_model (NOISE_BASE_REP_COUNT=2)** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:4884 (constant 4881)), complies: partly

For each model, it takes the top 2 base representations from the stored search the pool returned. It calls top_base_reps with the default rule='whole_dataset' (4917-4921).

- R5: two base representations per model matches.
- R2: the ranking is the whole-dataset search's mean over its folds. The comment at 4876-4880 says the two were picked with the held-out molecules in view.
- R1: models are whatever the caller passes.

**top_base_reps / top_hybrids / select_model_rep_pairs** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:7676, 7875, 8355), complies: partly

Lookups over one SearchResult, no fits. They give the top n base representations and top n hybrids per model, by the search's own mean or by the mean over other folds. select_model_rep_pairs defaults to 2 base and 2 hybrids for every model the search scored (8373, resolve_comparison_models 8341-8342).

- R4 shape: matches when the caller passes the two approved models.
- Default models: every model the search scored, not the approved pair (R1).
- R2 depends on the search passed. On a per-fold search it complies. On the whole-dataset search, 'other_folds' leaves out scores, not rows.
- top_hybrids ranks only configurations the search kept after pruning (7891-7896).

**top_hybrids_across_models** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:8234), complies: no

Pools the top hybrids of every scored model and ranks them together. Each entry names the model whose score ranked it ('recipe_chosen_by').

I did not edit any file. The only command I ran was one python import, to print the gp and speed lookups.

Nothing reads DECISIONS.md. A grep for 'DECISIONS' and 'precompute_cuts' over the .py and .sh files in src/ and tests/ finds nothing.

The code makes only two per-dataset grid choices:
- FAST_SPEED_DATASETS lists 14 datasets (dataset_policy.py:688-711). DECISIONS has 10 in its fast-tier table.
- gp is added on datasets under 1,000 rows (dataset_policy.py:744-776).

Every other axis is one global list for all datasets:
- 8 budgets for the general search and 6 (10 to 500) for the distance search (_shared.py:494-495).
- Distance evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm (:502).
- Five downstream models (:565).
- Engine defaults for allocation, importance, evaluators and representation counts (find_best_hybrid.py:3070-3072, 3674-3705).

None of Steps 1-8 is applied per dataset. Two things happen to match a decision for every dataset:
- Step 5 (v3) kept the same four evaluators everywhere: match, rf, lightgbm, dnn.
- The distance budgets stop at 500, which is Step 7's upper limit.

Which paths are per fold, and which read the whole-dataset search:
- Searched on the fold's training rows: search_on_fold, get_fold_best_search, precompute_nested_cv_searches, and run_nested_cv through nested_cv_evaluate.
- Read the whole-dataset search: get_best_search_for_downstream, get_fold_pool_recipes, get_rule_hybrids, fold_reselection with build_fold_reselection_input, get_precomputed_search, noise_base_reps_by_model, and the top_* selectors when given the stored search.
- build_fold_hybrid and build_hybrid_from_entry fit on the fold's training rows. They can still choose which representations to keep from whole-dataset scores (blueprint.rep_scores).

How many of each the per-fold paths return, against R4's two hybrids and two base representations per model:
- get_fold_best_search returns one hybrid and no base representations.
- nested_cv_evaluate returns one hybrid and one picked base representation per model.
- get_rule_hybrids returns three hybrids per model, but it is not per fold.

run_nested_cv and precompute_nested_cv_searches write to the same per-fold namespace, but they ask for different searches. run_nested_cv never calls _apply_dataset_search_speed. On the 14 fast datasets it runs the full grid, and it never scores gp. precompute_nested_cv_searches calls it, so it does both.

With the refusal switch on (the default in submit_everything.sh), an unwarmed per-fold search is refused, not built. search_on_fold records that as a failure. get_fold_best_search then returns (None, None). This breaks R6.

Could not determine:
- Whether any per-fold result database already exists on the server. I did not look.
- Which of these functions each experiment actually calls. I did not read the experiment files.
- Step 9's knn rule. DISTANCE_MODELS includes knn for every dataset, including the six nucleotide ones (dataset_policy.py:154 stops knn being skipped). Step 9 says knn is not needed there. It does not say it is forbidden.

I read the code only; I did not run any experiment. On 2026-10-03 I did one dry python import to print constants. It printed DOWNSTREAM_MODELS rf/xgboost/svm/dnn/lightgbm, INTERNAL_EVALUATORS match/rf/lightgbm/dnn, DISTANCE_EVALUATORS knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm, FULL_BUDGETS 10-2000 (8), DISTANCE_BUDGETS 10-500 (6). It also gave the gp list and the 14 fast datasets.

The four helper files build their start-up searches the same way. Each run_all calls precompute_hybrid_searches with all rows of the dataset (_shared.py:5569-5585). complexity and similarity build two searches: general and general_distance. noise builds two as well: general, and general under objective='similarity'. federated builds general only, and nothing at all on herg and lhasa_herg. None of them builds a per-fold search at start-up.

Nothing reads DECISIONS.md. A grep of src/ and tests/ found one match, an unrelated string at noise/n20_clean_before_search.py:1124. So the start-up searches differ from the record on every axis:
- Models: five on every dataset. gp is added on 9 datasets under 1,000 molecules, and knn on the distance search. The record allows two per dataset.
- Budgets: all 8 on general and all 6 on distance, for every dataset. The record sets a range per dataset.
- Importance, allocation, internal evaluator and representation count: engine defaults, or the fast list on 14 datasets. The record sets cuts per dataset.
- Augmentation: uncapped and capped on every dataset with an augmentation list. The record keeps uncapped only, on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic.

The fast list disagrees with the record. FAST_SPEED_DATASETS holds 14 datasets; the record's fast-tier table holds 10. bindingdb_kd, flab_expression_koenig and kiba are decided 'keep deeplift, lightgbm_gain and treeshap'. The fast grid searches lightgbm_gain only.

precompute_hybrid_searches adds 'capped' on the distance tier (:5544-5548), although its own comment says the distance tier never carries it. search_on_fold adds 'capped' on general only (:1444-1448).

The per-fold paths (search_on_fold, get_fold_best_search, run_nested_cv) do use each fold's training rows only. search_on_fold and get_fold_best_search have no argument for allocation methods, importance methods or representation counts, so they cannot apply Steps 3, 4 and 6. run_nested_cv sends models=None, which means five models.

KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 is the default in submit_everything.sh. Per-fold searches are not exempt from it. A missing per-fold search with more than 500 configurations unstored (KIRBY_COLD_SEARCH_MAX_CONFIGS) is refused, not built. That conflicts with R6.

Four launchers set four pruning defaults:
- run_dataset.py: default_pruning
- submit_dataset.sh: aggressive_pruning
- submit_everything.sh: calibrated
- opig_one.sh: calibrated

Other environment variables that change a search:
- KIRBY_LOCAL_ALLOCATIONS, _IMPORTANCE, _EVALUATORS, _REP_COUNTS, _MODELS, _FOLDS, _BUDGETS: applied when _shared is imported (_shared.py:9396-9428, _local_grid.py:43-100).
- KIRBY_LOCAL_AUG_CONDITIONS (_shared.py:5992-6011).

### defaults

**DEFAULT_MODELS tiers and the models=None default** (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:2721), complies: no

When a caller passes models=None, the search scores every model whose tier is 'fast' or 'full' (AUTO_SELECTED_TIERS, line 2979; filter at 8701-8711). That is rf, lightgbm, dnn (tier fast) and xgboost, svm (tier full). gp, knn, linear, ngboost are tier 'extra' and ridge, mlp, catboost, cnn, bnn are tier 'off', so none of them is scored unless named. svm is dropped above 10,000 training rows (2812) and gp above 1,000 (2871). On nt_*/gb_* xgboost is skipped (tests/experiments/dataset_policy.py:36). _shared.DOWNSTREAM_MODELS mirrors the five (tests/experiments/_shared.py:565).

- Every one of the 41 datasets gets five downstream models by default. Step 1 approves two per dataset, so the default scores three models the record excludes. Example: herg_ki is approved for svm+dnn, and the default also scores rf, xgboost and lightgbm.
- On the five nucleotide datasets xgboost is skipped and svm drops out above 10,000 rows, so the default is smaller there, but it still holds rf. No nucleotide pair uses rf.
- ridge is tier 'off' (2955) and is never scored by default. This agrees with R1.
- No dataset's approved pair is missing from this default, except gp, which only _apply_dataset_search_speed adds (see that entry).

**_apply_dataset_search_speed and FAST_SPEED_DATASETS** (tests/experiments/_shared.py:1015), complies: partly

If the caller did not pass speed=, it sets speed='fast' for datasets in dataset_policy.FAST_SPEED_DATASETS (tests/experiments/dataset_policy.py:688-711) and names the five models (or six with knn on general_distance) so the fast setting does not cut them to rf, lightgbm, dnn. It then adds gp on small datasets. Under speed='fast' the engine takes FAST lists for every axis the caller did not name (find_best_hybrid.py:8651-8669). It is called by search_on_fold (1484), precompute_nested_cv_searches (1329), precompute_hybrid_searches (5592), get_precomputed_search (5895) and get_hybrid_features_and_weights (4808). It is not called by run_nested_cv (1181-1215).

- The code's fast list holds 14 datasets. The record's fast-tier table (DECISIONS.md lines 352-363) holds 10. flab_expression_koenig, logd, bindingdb_kd and kiba are fast in the code and not fast in the record.
- For those four, the record keeps methods the fast lists do not contain. Details are in the importance, allocation and representation-count entries below.
- The 10 datasets that are fast in both places get the stored fast grid, which matches the record's fast-tier table on importance, allocation and representation counts.

**Pruning defaults: DEFAULT_PRUNING_SCHEDULE, PRUNING_MODES, _normalize_pruning_schedule** (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:3789), complies: partly

find_best_hybrid defaults to adaptive_pruning=False (8278). With no schedule passed, that switches off every vote and checkpoint (3930-3938). The schedule called 'calibrated' is DEFAULT_PRUNING_SCHEDULE (3789-3890). It votes after folds 0 and 1. On representation count it keeps the single best member and deletes one placing first in under 10% of groups. On importance method it deletes members in the best 2 of under 20% of groups. On internal evaluator, best 3 of under 10%. On allocation method, best 2 of under 20%. At budget 100 it drops the worse half of allocation-by-importance pairs. _shared.PRUNING_MODES['calibrated'] is filled from it (tests/experiments/_shared.py:728-733). Only own_search_kwargs (804) reads PRUNING_MODE with 'calibrated' as its default. search_on_fold and get_fold_best_search pass no schedule by default, so per-fold searches run unpruned. get_precomputed_search forces adaptive_pruning=False (5889).

- A passed schedule is laid over DEFAULT_PRUNING_SCHEDULE (3917-3920). The 'no_pruning' and 'default_pruning' dicts (tests/experiments/_shared.py:679-699) do not set axis_vote_rules or vote_folds. So both still run the three per-axis votes after two folds. I printed this with a tiny import this session.
- tests/precompute_hybrids.py defaults to --pruning-mode no_pruning (1102) and passes that dict to the search (1226, 1348). Its own comment at 1217 says no_pruning is off. Could not determine which mode the server precompute behind DECISIONS.md was run with.
- The four suite helpers default to pruning_mode='default_pruning' (complexity_helpers.py:915, similarity_helpers.py:1251, noise_helpers.py:1706, federated_helpers.py:2961). tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:102 defaults PRUNING_MODE to aggressive_pruning. Neither is 'calibrated'.
- Any active vote deletes members of the importance, evaluator, representation-count and allocation axes per dataset during a search. The record decides those members per dataset and says nothing about pruning on top of them.

SUMMARY PER AXIS (counts are datasets out of 41)

Models: the default scores five models: rf, xgboost, lightgbm, svm, dnn. Step 1 approves two per dataset, so three extra models run on every dataset. gp is added on nine small datasets; four of those (abagym_EGFR, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_titer, humanness_therapeutic) do not approve it. run_nested_cv adds no gp, so it lacks an approved model on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho. ridge is never scored by default.

Budgets: FULL_BUDGETS has eight budgets, 10 to 2000 features. On 39 datasets it contains budgets Step 2 cuts; humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc are the two that keep all eight. DISTANCE_BUDGETS has six budgets, 10 to 500. On 36 of the 38 datasets with a distance decision it contains budgets Step 7 cuts; humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc keep all six. No dataset keeps a budget the defaults lack.

Fast-tier datasets: the code runs 14 datasets fast (dataset_policy.py:688-711). The record's fast-tier table lists 10. The four extra are flab_expression_koenig, logd, bindingdb_kd and kiba. logd's stored grid matches the fast lists on importance and allocation. On the other three the fast lists lack methods the record keeps. flab_expression_koenig and kiba lack deeplift, treeshap and softmax_T1. bindingdb_kd lacks deeplift, treeshap, softmax_T1, wglobal_power2 and count 2.

Importance: in the general search the default contains a cut method on 13 datasets: 12 with a decided cut, plus flab_expression_adams, where deeplift was never stored. It lacks kept methods on 3 (flab_expression_koenig, bindingdb_kd, kiba). In the distance search it contains a cut method on 10.

Allocation: in the general search it contains cut methods on caco2, ddg_combined, ginkgo_acsins and herg_ki. suzuki is held, and the default runs all five there. It lacks kept methods on flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd. In the distance search it contains cut methods on abagym_VEGF, ddg_combined and herg_ki.

Internal evaluators: the general search gets the same four on every dataset. That includes cut evaluators on abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_titer. The distance search gets knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm everywhere, which includes cut evaluators on 11 datasets.

Representation counts: in the general search the default contains cut counts on 19 datasets. bindingdb_kd also lacks a kept count (2). In the distance search it contains cut counts on 13; flab_expression_koenig also lacks 2.

Augmentation: 32 datasets carry augmentation representations. Whenever they are passed, every helper builds uncapped and capped searches. Step 8 cuts both on 30 of the 32. On ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic it keeps uncapped (distance) and cuts capped. The default also builds capped there.

Pruning: per-fold searches run unpruned by default. The precompute's 'no_pruning' mode is not off. The engine lays the passed dict over the calibrated schedule (find_best_hybrid.py:3917-3920). So the representation-count, importance and evaluator votes still fire after two folds. I printed that with a tiny import. The same holds for 'default_pruning', the suite helpers' default. Could not determine which mode produced the stored rows behind DECISIONS.md.

## opig opig shared_vectors_census (tests/experiments/opig_shared_vectors_census.py)

What it measures: For each representation, and for the top stored hybrids per downstream model, it counts how many molecules share an identical row of features with another molecule, and the best score any model could reach given those ties.

Datasets: 29 datasets: every DATASET_REPS key whose registered domain is molecular or antibody (roster(), opig_shared_vectors_census.py:86-93; default domains at :80 and :791). The launcher row names no dataset and passes no --datasets (submit_everything.sh:131), so the roster decides. Printed with a tiny import this session: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, cdr_flexibility, chembl_qsar, ddg_combined, flab_binding_adams, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg, herg_ki, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, logd, qm9, tz_her2_binary, tz_her2_multiclass. chembl_qsar is included although DECISIONS.md has no Step 1 row for it and says nothing is stored for it (DECISIONS.md:53). Representations per dataset: the general list plus the augmentation list, cut to those with a matrix on disk (:96-105, :552-558).

### R1 models: NO

Code: It fits no downstream model itself. It counts tied rows in hybrids picked for six downstream models on every dataset: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm and knn (DISTANCE_MODELS). For knn it asks for two hybrids from the general search as well as one from the distance search. It never asks for gp.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two approved models (Step 1). knn is allowed in the distance search for the census (Step 9 names it), not as a general-search model. It adds four unapproved models plus knn's general slots. ### R2 per fold: by design

Code: There are no folds. The census counts identical rows over every molecule and scores nothing on held-out rows. The hybrids it counts are chosen by the whole-dataset stored search, ranked on the mean over all its folds (fold_i=None). Each hybrid is then rebuilt over every molecule with build_hybrid_from_entry.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows. The census has no fold to apply this to, so no score is inflated. But the hybrids it counts are the whole-dataset winners, not the per-fold hybrids the other experiments will use. So its hybrid rows describe a different feature set from the one any per-fold experiment fits.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: It sets KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 itself, whatever the launcher says. If at least half of a search's configurations are stored, the search is completed on all rows inside this job. Decisions: A needed search that does not exist must be built by the experiment itself. The census needs no per-fold search, but it refuses to build a missing whole-dataset search over 500 configurations. On chembl_qsar nothing is stored, so every hybrid slot is reported missing.

### Other problems

- The census never asks for gp hybrids, because it loops over DISTANCE_MODELS (census:468). The searches it reads do score gp on nine small datasets (_shared.py:1084-1126), so the gp rows exist and are not read.
- It rebuilds each hybrid over every molecule (census:499-501). For a recipe that used fewer representations than the pool, restrict_to_rep_count chooses which to keep from blueprint.rep_scores, the stored search's whole-dataset scores (_shared.py:7259-7260, find_best_hybrid.py:9707-9708). This matches how the recipe was searched, but not how a per-fold experiment would rebuild it.
- The stored search is found only if rep_pool matches: representation names and widths are in the result-database identity (result_cache.py:79-89). The census drops representations with no matrix on disk (census:552-558). So a dataset missing one cached matrix asks for a different search than the one stored, and gets it built or refused. Which datasets that affects on the server could not be determined.
- Augmentation representations enter only if their matrices are cached (census:452-455). aug_names is a per-row configuration column (result_cache.py:123), so a missing donor changes which stored rows match. Not checked on the server.
- The launcher row passes --check-freshness 200 and no dataset (submit_everything.sh:131). The roster therefore includes chembl_qsar, which has nothing stored, no Step 1 row, and no Steps 2-9 rows (DECISIONS.md:53).
- The census forces KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 for the hybrid reads (census:462-463), overriding a launcher run with --no-cold-refusal. It restores the previous value afterwards (census:539-543).
- Ties between hybrids at different budgets are counted under one label per slot. Because the ranking uses budget=None (_shared.py:6855), a 'general1' row can be a 10-feature or a 2000-feature hybrid. The budget is written on the row (census:525), so this is visible, not hidden.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R6: the launcher says the census waits for no precompute job (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:109-111, row at :131 names no dataset). So the census can start before any search it reads is stored. On a dataset whose searches are still running, every hybrid slot can come back as a missing_reason row, or a small search can be built inside the census job.
- R6: the docstring says 'Returns [] when no search is stored, rather than building one' (opig_shared_vectors_census.py:437), and the --with-hybrids help says 'it never searches' (:818-819). find_best_hybrid scores the missing configurations inside the job when 500 or fewer are left, or when half or more are stored (find_best_hybrid.py:691-720).
- R3: on flab_expression_koenig the code's fast grid differs from Steps 4 and 6 as well as Step 3. It drops softmax_T1, which Step 4 keeps (DECISIONS.md:387). It keeps representation count 3, which Step 6 cuts (DECISIONS.md:581; find_best_hybrid.py:3071-3072). The decisions file does not list it among the fast-tier datasets (DECISIONS.md:350-363).
- R3: Step 5 evaluator cuts are not applied. The general search runs the default evaluators match, rf, lightgbm and dnn (find_best_hybrid.py:3705, :8665-8667) on abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_titer. Step 5 cuts rf, then rf/lightgbm/dnn, then dnn, then lightgbm on those four (DECISIONS.md:517, 518, 536, 539).
- R1/R6: for knn the general read asks for a predictive search with knn added to the models (_shared.py:7124-7127). get_rule_hybrids' own docstring says no predictive general search for knn exists (_shared.py:7086-7090). model is a per-row column and not part of the stored-search identity (result_cache.py:113-114 vs :46-105). So the five other models' rows count toward the 50% test, and knn's general configurations may be scored over all rows inside the census job. Whether that happens on the server: could not determine without the result databases.


## opig opig scaffold_similarity (tests/experiments/opig_scaffold_similarity.py)

What it measures: For pairs of antibody variants, it measures the Spearman correlation between the distance a mutation-difference representation gives the pair and the distance a substitution matrix gives it, with the count of differing positions partialled out; no model is trained and no hybrid is built.

Datasets: With no --datasets argument it runs the four entries of SCAFFOLD_DATASETS: flab_expression_koenig, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_binding_adams (opig_scaffold_similarity.py:116-121, default chosen at :517). The launcher row passes no --datasets (submit_everything.sh:132; opig_one.sh:125 runs CMD as written), so these four are what the server runs. The launcher row also names ddg_combined, but the script lists it as excluded (opig_scaffold_similarity.py:126-127) and never loads it. --smoke cuts to flab_expression_koenig and flab_expression_adams with 8000 pairs (:519-521).

### R1 models: -

Code: It fits no downstream model. Every number is a Spearman or partial Spearman correlation between pair distances and a substitution-matrix distance (opig_scaffold_similarity.py:27-31, 322, 327). The helpers it imports compute correlations only: score_subset and greedy_forward (feature_type_study.py:128-175), partial_spearman (scaffold_experiment.py:186-200). The one model fit in scaffold_experiment.py (a k-nearest-neighbour classifier, :203-220) is in a function this file does not import (import list at opig_scaffold_similarity.py:106-109).

Decisions: Step 1 approves two models per dataset: flab_binding_adams lightgbm+xgboost, flab_binding_koenig rf+svm, flab_expression_adams dnn+svm, flab_expression_koenig svm+dnn (DECISIONS.md:24-27). These apply to experiments that fit models; this one fits none.

- --distance-metric is parsed and applied (opig_scaffold_similarity.py:513, :516), but no distance in this script reads it. Representations mode hard-codes cosine and euclidean (:311-317), and features mode hard-codes euclidean (feature_type_study.py:136). Not an R1-R6 breach; a flag that changes nothing.


## opig opig humanness (tests/experiments/opig_humanness.py)

What it measures: It classifies human against non-human therapeutic antibody sequences, scoring each representation with each model by its own 5-fold split, and compares hybrids against the best single representation using one whole-dataset search's per-fold scores.

Datasets: humanness_therapeutic only. The script default is DEFAULT_DATASETS = ['humanness_therapeutic'] (opig_humanness.py:89). The cluster row passes --datasets humanness_therapeutic (submit_everything.sh:133). Representations are the 10 approved ones plus onehot, added by REP_EXCEPTIONS (opig_humanness.py:106, 109-111; _shared.py:3761-3765), so 11 representations. Its DECISIONS rows: models xgboost+rf (DECISIONS.md:37); budgets 10-2000 (:235); importance, allocation, evaluators and representation counts all kept (:331, :397, :542, :591); distance search 10-500 with no cuts (:638); augmentation cut (:684); knn run in the distance search (:734).

### R1 models: NO

Code: The base-representation table fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every representation. The hybrid search it reads also scores gp, because the dataset has under 1,000 rows. The distance read adds knn and gp. The hybrid-against-single comparison and the owner's-set block cover every model the search scored, so six models. The top-2 block covers five. No ridge anywhere.

Decisions: Two models only: xgboost and rf (DECISIONS.md:37). knn is allowed in the distance search on this dataset (DECISIONS.md:734). So svm, dnn, lightgbm and gp are extra: four models the decision excludes.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: It never builds a per-fold search. It asks for the whole-dataset search over 11 representations. The precompute stores the 10-representation search, and the representation list is part of the stored-search identity. So unless rows for the 11 exist, the search is missing. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, set by default for OPIG jobs, a missing search with over 500 configurations is refused. By _expected_config_count this one is 10,080 configurations (5 x 3 x 8 x 4 x 21). The refusal is caught, printed as a pool warning and skipped. get_best_search_for_downstream returns (None, None). The script then writes the base table only and exits 0. Without the variable, the whole-dataset search is built inside the job, still not per fold.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- The comment at opig_humanness.py:294-297 says the hybrids carry 'no full-data selection leak'. The helper it calls marks the recipe as chosen on all rows (_shared.py:6422-6432). The two disagree.
- On the cluster, a refused search does not fail the job. evaluate_dataset returns the base table alone, so the script exits 0 with no hybrid blocks (opig_humanness.py:336, 469-514; _shared.py:6320-6328). The only sign is a printed '[pool] WARNING' line.
- adaptive_pruning=0.25 is passed (opig_humanness.py:332, 353), but an explicit schedule always replaces it (find_best_hybrid.py:3917-3920). The 0.25 has no effect.
- --pruning-mode defaults to default_pruning locally (opig_humanness.py:721) and is calibrated on the cluster (submit_everything.sh:85, 420). Both schedules are laid over DEFAULT_PRUNING_SCHEDULE, so the axis votes fire in both (find_best_hybrid.py:3917-3920).
- The base-representation table uses 5 models and no gp (opig_humanness.py:443). The hybrid comparisons use 6 models including gp (opig_humanness.py:536-538). The two tables cover different model sets.
- Recipe names in build_fold_reselection_input omit the representation count (_shared.py:2018-2020). Two recipes that differ only in representation count get the same name in the saved JSON.
- The module docstring says the classifiers are Ridge and RF (opig_humanness.py:9). The code fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm (opig_humanness.py:113, 443).
- Could not determine whether the groups from _identity_groups (opig_humanness.py:269) hash the same as the groups the precompute loads (precompute_hybrids.py:515). groups_hash is part of the stored-search identity (result_cache.py:48), so a mismatch would also make the search missing.
- Could not determine whether onehot builds on this dataset. If compute_or_load_reps drops it, the pool is 10 representations and the search identity could match the precompute's.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- A refused or failed hybrid search is checkpointed as finished. evaluate_dataset returns the base table alone with no 'error' key. _ck.put stores it (opig_humanness.py:791; _checkpoint.py:290-292 skips only 'error' payloads). On the next attempt _ck.done is true (opig_humanness.py:785-787), so the base-only result is read back and no hybrid search is attempted. That holds even after the search has been filled, unless --force-rerun is passed.
- The outer try at opig_humanness.py:315/439-440 catches every exception, including StaleResultDB that _shared.py:6098-6107 re-raises on purpose so it is not swallowed. Here it becomes the printed line 'Hybrid build failed' and the job exits 0 with the base table only.
- In the owner's-set block the per-fold base representations from get_rule_hybrids(fold_i=k) are discarded (opig_humanness.py:567-570). The saved top 2 base representations are the whole-dataset ranking (553-555). The per-fold comparison in by_slot is against 1 re-picked best single representation (571-580), not 2.
- Under R1 the distance read also scores knn as a downstream model (_shared.py:6777, DISTANCE_MODELS). That is allowed by DECISIONS.md:734. But the experiment never reads a knn row, because the owner's-set loop covers only models in baselines_by_model from the general search (opig_humanness.py:536-537).

## opig opig trastuzumab (tests/experiments/opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py)

What it measures: For the trastuzumab-HER2 binary dataset it measures, per representation and per model, what fraction of the top-ranked held-out molecules are binders, and sets the hybrid against the best single representation on the same held-out folds.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every arm fits five downstream models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. MODELS_LIST is set to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS, which holds those five names. get_model_factories builds the five factories, and the per-representation loop and the per-fold hybrid loop both run over all five. The whole-dataset read asks for one model, rf. No knn, no gp and no ridge are fitted anywhere: ridge is tier 'off' in the engine and nothing names it.

The single model the whole-dataset read asks for, rf, is neither of the two approved ones. Step 9 says the knn downstream pass runs on tz_her2_binary in the distance search; the per-fold distance search here names the five models and leaves knn out, while the whole-dataset distance read asks for the six names in DISTANCE_MODELS, knn included. The two distance paths of this one file therefore ask for different model lists.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: The file has two kinds of hybrid arm. The enrichment arm searches each fold's training rows: it slices every representation, every label and every group to train_idx, then runs find_best_hybrid on those rows for the general tier and again for the distance tier, under a per-fold cache label condition_suffix='enrich_fold<k>'. That arm complies. The AUROC arm reads one search over all 5,000 rows. get_best_search_for_downstream returns it with selection_scope 'whole_dataset' and a note saying the recipe was chosen on all rows. build_fold_reselection_input then takes that search's stored per-fold scores, and fold_reselection re-picks a winner per held-out fold from them. _rule_set_held_out does the same thing a second way: get_rule_hybrids with fold_i=k ranks the stored configurations on the other folds' scores, and those scores come from the whole-dataset search.

Decisions: R2 asks that every hybrid used for a fold come from a search built on that fold's training rows. The per-fold searches do. The whole-dataset read does not: leaving fold k's score out of the ranking does not leave fold k's rows out of the models that produced every score. That is the fold_reselection pattern R2 names. So the two numbers this file reports disagree about which rows chose the recipe: the enrichment number is chosen on training rows only, and the AUROC number is chosen on all rows.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: The two per-fold searches call find_best_hybrid directly and pass no speed, so the engine's full grid applies: three importance methods (deeplift, lightgbm_gain, treeshap), five allocation methods, representation counts 2, 3, 5 and the whole pool, and eight budgets from FULL_BUDGETS (10 to 2000 features). The general fold search passes the four internal evaluators match, rf, lightgbm, dnn. The distance fold search passes the six budgets of DISTANCE_BUDGETS (10 to 500 features) and the five evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm. The whole-dataset read goes through get_precomputed_search, which calls _apply_dataset_search_speed; tz_her2_binary is in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS, so that read runs the fast grid, with eight budgets. Nothing in the file or in its helpers reads DECISIONS.md. Augmentation: the file passes augmentations=None and augmentation_strategy='none' on every call, and the approved pool for this dataset has no augmentation representations.

Decisions: tz_her2_binary is in the Step 'Fast-tier datasets' table, whose decided grid is lightgbm_gain alone, the three allocation methods performance_weighted, power_2 and rank_exp_d0.3, and representation counts 3 and all. The per-fold general search therefore differs from the record in three ways at once: it adds the importance methods deeplift and treeshap, it adds the allocation methods softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2, and it adds the representation counts 2 and 5. Step 2 (v3) sets the budget range 100-500 features and cuts 10, 25, 50, 1000 and 2000; every search in this file runs all eight budgets, so five cut budgets are searched. Step 5 (v3) keeps all four internal evaluators, which the general searches match. Step 7 sets the distance budget range 100-500 features and cuts nothing on the other four axes; the distance fold search adds the budgets 10, 25 and 50 features, and runs the full importance, allocation and representation-count lists, which the fast-tier general decision does not cover for the distance tier. Step 8 cuts augmented searches on this dataset, which the file follows.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: The supervised table scores every representation in the pool against every one of the five models, with five-fold CV per pair. The pool is 13 representations: the 10 approved for tz_her2_binary plus esmc_llr, antiberty_llr and esm2, each named with a reason at the call site. The hybrid side keeps three hybrids per model per fold, not two: general1 is the fold search's own fitted recipe for that model, general2 is the second-ranked configuration of the same fold search, and distance1 is the top configuration of the fold's distance search. Those three names come from RULE_SLOTS, and the counts from RULE_N_GENERAL=2 and RULE_N_DISTANCE=1. Two further keys hold rankings and no new fits: select_model_rep_pairs writes the top 2 representations and top 2 configurations per model off the whole-dataset search, and extract_top3_base_reps writes 3 representations ranked by rf.

Decisions: R4 asks for the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids per model per fold, for each of the dataset's two models. This file scores every representation rather than two, and keeps three hybrids per model rather than two, and does both for five models rather than two. The three-hybrid shape is deliberate and dated in the file: a comment at line 109 records it as the owner's set of 2026-10-02, top 2 general plus top 1 distance. The all-representation table is the point of the experiment, which asks which embedding separates binders from non-binders. The five-model list is not covered by either statement.

### R6 missing search: yes

Code: The per-fold searches build themselves and are never refused. Each passes condition_suffix='enrich_fold<k>', and find_best_hybrid appends that to the tier, giving 'general__cond-enrich_fold0'. _refuse_cold_search returns early unless the tier's root, split on the objective marker alone, is 'general' or 'general_distance', so the per-fold tier does not match and the KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH check never fires on it. A fold search that raises for any other reason is caught, the fold is padded with a missing score, and the reason is printed. The two whole-dataset reads do carry the plain tiers and are subject to the refusal: a refusal there is caught in _iter_pool_searches, which prints a warning and returns no search, and the AUROC block and the owner's-set block then record the slot as missing.

Decisions: R6 asks that a needed per-fold search be built by the experiment itself and that no path refuse or skip instead. The enrichment arm meets that. The whole-dataset reads are not per-fold searches, so the refusal on them does not break R6; what it does is drop the AUROC comparison with a printed warning rather than an error.

### Other problems

- The representation pool this file searches is 13 representations: the 10 approved for tz_her2_binary plus esmc_llr, antiberty_llr and esm2 (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:96, 101; _shared.py:3761). The precompute searches the approved 10 alone (precompute_hybrids.py:474). The set of representations and their widths is an identity column of the stored result database, 'rep_pool' (result_cache.py:89; find_best_hybrid.py:9147, 6021). So no row the precompute wrote for tz_her2_binary can be read by this file's whole-dataset calls. Either the cold-search refusal rejects them, or the job builds a whole-dataset search over 13 representations inside its own wall.
- build_fold_hybrid is called with no model and no metric_fn (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:643-646), and fold_hybrid_scoring_kwargs is not imported (same file, lines 66-74). A configuration whose internal evaluator is 'match' then resolves to lightgbm inside create_hybrid, because that is what the no-model branch sets (hybrid.py:5870, 5891). 'match' is one of the four evaluators the general searches run (_shared.py:864). So the general2 and distance1 hybrids can be ranked under one evaluator and rebuilt under another, and the score is filed under the ranked configuration's name.
- The models _rule_set_held_out loops are taken from the whole-dataset search's baselines_by_model, that is every model the search scored, and fall back to the five of MODELS_LIST (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:165-166). Nothing restricts that loop to the dataset's two approved models.
- The script's own default pruning mode is 'default_pruning' (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:1401), while opig_one.sh and submit_everything.sh pass 'calibrated' (runbook/opig_one.sh:57, 60; submit_everything.sh:414). The schedule a mode supplies is laid over the calibrated schedule, and 'default_pruning' sets no axis_vote_rules, so the calibrated per-axis votes stay on in both modes (find_best_hybrid.py:3917-3920; _shared.py:694). Those votes delete members of the importance, internal evaluator, representation count and allocation axes after folds 0 and 1 of each search (find_best_hybrid.py:3834, 3855, 3886-3890). Which members of the decided grid survive is therefore decided inside each run, per fold, on top of Steps 3 to 6.
- The explicit adaptive_pruning=0.25 passed on all four search calls has no effect, because the schedule from resolve_pruning_kwargs is also passed and wins (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:533, 568, 926; _shared.py:839; find_best_hybrid.py:3917-3920).
- The whole-dataset read passes adaptive_pruning=0.25 into get_precomputed_search, which sets adaptive_pruning=False for cache alignment and is then overridden by the caller's value (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:926; _shared.py:5889, 5893). The comment at _shared.py:5886 says an experiment that passes adaptive_pruning is asking for a different search and should not be served the precomputed one.
- extract_top3_base_reps ranks 3 representations by rf and is called on both the whole-dataset search and fold 0's search (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:931, 578; _shared.py:867). rf is not one of this dataset's two approved models.
- The AUROC arm drops fold 0 from both sides, because the search filtered its own configuration list on fold 0's scores (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:945-955; _shared.py:2043). At five folds that leaves four paired folds for the AUROC comparison while the enrichment comparison keeps all five (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:804-809).
- The top-1 percent enrichment is counted over about 1,000 held-out rows per fold, so the top fraction holds about 10 molecules. The file says so itself and still reports that column first in its table (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:104, 1278).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R6: the per-fold searches are never refused. Their tier becomes 'general__cond-enrich_fold<k>' (find_best_hybrid.py:8986-8987). _is_precompute_tier only matches 'general' and 'general_distance' (find_best_hybrid.py:598-605). So the refusal returns early and the file builds both per-fold searches itself.
- R6: the whole-dataset read can be refused under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH. submit_everything.sh:415 exports that variable when COLD_REFUSAL is 1. The refusal is caught at _shared.py:6108-6114. get_best_search_for_downstream then returns (None, None) at _shared.py:6320-6328, and the AUROC arm writes nothing. The only signal is a printed warning.
- R3: the two distance paths in this file search different grids. The per-fold distance search (opig_trastuzumab_enrichment.py:549-570) passes no speed, so it runs the full importance, allocation and representation-count lists. The whole-dataset distance read goes through _apply_dataset_search_speed (_shared.py:1049-1053), so it runs the fast lists. The two also differ by knn, so they differ in two ways at once, not one.


## opig opig cgr_comparison (tests/experiments/opig_cgr_comparison.py)

What it measures: For each reaction dataset it compares two hybrid searches, one over the SMILES-based representations and one that adds the three reaction-graph (CGR) representations. It reports the RMSE difference per downstream model, and it also scores every single representation with five models.

Datasets: buchwald_hartwig, bh_doyle_plates and suzuki. The list is ALL_DATASETS at opig_cgr_comparison.py:206. It is used when --datasets is not given (opig_cgr_comparison.py:1252). The cluster row at submit_everything.sh:136 passes no --datasets, so all three run. The dataset names at the end of that row are only printed by opig_one.sh (opig_one.sh:52, 120).

### R1 models: NO

Code: MODELS_LIST is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. Every single representation is fitted with all five on every fold. Both general searches pass no model list, so the engine scores the same five. The distance searches add knn as a sixth downstream model. The CGR comparison is reported for all five models.

Decisions: Step 1 approves rf+dnn for bh_doyle_plates, and rf+lightgbm for buchwald_hartwig and suzuki. Step 9 allows knn in the distance search on all three. ridge is excluded.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid comes from a search run once over all rows of the dataset. The headline CGR difference (delta_by_model) uses fold_reselection over that search's stored per-fold scores. The second difference (delta_by_model_rule) re-ranks the same stored scores with fold k left out (get_rule_hybrids fold_i=k). That leaves out fold k's scores, not its rows. The hybrid_eval rows rebuild each model's winner on all labels, then score it on the same folds. Only the single representations are fitted per fold, with the scaler fitted on that fold's training rows.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. Re-picking from a whole-dataset search's per-fold scores leaks.

Its distance search: 100-500, cut dnn/knn/svm evaluators, cut counts 3/5/all. suzuki general: 50-250, keep all importance methods, evaluators and counts. Allocation is HELD. Its distance search: 50-250, allocation HELD. Step 8 cuts augmentation on all three.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: The experiment compares two representation pools by design, which is a legitimate difference. Within each pool it reports four different selections per model. The headline difference uses one hybrid and one single representation per held-out fold (fold_reselection). The second difference uses 2 general hybrids, 1 distance hybrid and 2 single representations per held-out fold: 3 hybrids, not 2. A top2_selection block holds 2 single representations and 2 hybrids per model, ranked on the whole dataset with no fold; nothing reads it. Phase A scores every representation with all five models.

Decisions: For each of the dataset's two models, per fold: the 2 best single representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: It reads no precomputed search. condition_suffix renames the tier to general__cond-smiles_only and general__cond-smiles_plus_cgr (and the same for general_distance). Those names are not precompute tiers, so the cold-search refusal returns early. The job then builds the searches itself, at any size. But it builds them on all rows, never per fold. A search that raises is printed as a warning and skipped. The pool then returns (None, None), and that pool gets no hybrid rows.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, with no refusal or skip.

### Other problems

- The hybrid_eval RMSEs are printed first in the pool table (opig_cgr_comparison.py:1125-1148). Each comes from a recipe and features fitted on every row's label (find_best_hybrid.py:9510-9516), then scored on the same folds (:555). The code's own comment says both sides carry selection optimism (:567-570).
- The comment above the rule read says the distance search is 'read, or built when missing and small' (opig_cgr_comparison.py:731). The renamed tier is never refused (find_best_hybrid.py:598-605, 650-651), so it is built at any size.
- The comment at opig_cgr_comparison.py:592-593 says the pools hold 17 and 20 representations. The generators name 20 representations plus 8 molecular variants times 3 roles (opig_cgr_comparison.py:287-317, reaction.py:1261-1270): up to 41 and 44. How many generate on the server could not be determined.
- The family comparison and top3_base rank by rf only (opig_cgr_comparison.py:867, 496). On bh_doyle_plates rf is approved. On buchwald_hartwig and suzuki rf is approved, but lightgbm is not used.
- The printed verdict says the hybrid pool 'improves' with CGR if any one of the five models has a negative RMSE difference (opig_cgr_comparison.py:1200-1201).
- --n-folds changes only the single-representation folds (opig_cgr_comparison.py:933, 393). The search always uses DEFAULT_N_FOLDS = 5 (find_best_hybrid.py:3706). Any value other than 5 puts the single representations and the hybrids on different folds.
- The pruning mode differs by launcher: the script defaults to default_pruning (opig_cgr_comparison.py:1236), and opig_one.sh passes calibrated (opig_one.sh:57-60). Either one overrides get_precomputed_search's adaptive_pruning=False, because kwargs are applied after it (_shared.py:5889, 5893).
- The FAMILIES comparison uses diff_ecfp4 and drfp_2048 (opig_cgr_comparison.py:213). Both were cut from the approved 10-representation pools of buchwald_hartwig and bh_doyle_plates (complexity_helpers.py:547-549, 560-562). This is by design for the CGR question, but those searches are not the dataset's decided representation set.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R2: the CGR feature-selection answer (question 3 of the docstring, and the 'CGR Feature Selection' table) reads rf's recipe refitted on all rows. selected_reps comes from search.fitted_results['rf'] (tests/experiments/opig_cgr_comparison.py:513-518). extract_cgr_selection_info reads it (:791-801), and print_analysis prints it (:1174-1180). So whether CGR was picked is answered from a search that saw every row's label, not per fold.
- R4: the family head-to-head picks the best CGR and the best SMILES representation by mean RMSE over the same 5 folds it then reports (tests/experiments/opig_cgr_comparison.py:894-905, used at :878-884). Neither the representation choice nor the winner is held out from the folds it is scored on.
- R2/R4: the owner's-set read drops folds using the general search's fold-0 flag (hr_exclude_folds(reselection_block) at tests/experiments/opig_cgr_comparison.py:737). The same dropped folds are then applied to the distance search read (:97, :172-173). Whether the distance search also filtered on fold 0 is never checked. Could not determine from the code whether the two searches' flags differ in practice.


## opig opig ginkgo (tests/experiments/opig_ginkgo_developability.py)

What it measures: For each Ginkgo antibody property, it compares hybrids searched and rebuilt on each fold's training rows against single representations, scored by spearman on the competition's five held-out folds.

Datasets: Five datasets: ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_titer, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal. The list is ALL_PROPERTIES at opig_ginkgo_developability.py:131-134, used when --properties is not given (:1173-1174). The server row names the same five (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:137). opig_one.sh runs it with --pruning-mode calibrated by default (tests/slurm_scripts/runbook/opig_one.sh:57,60). Representations per dataset come from DATASET_REPS: 10 general plus paratope and structural (_shared.py:3761, printed this session).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every search and every scored arm uses five downstream models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. MODELS_LIST is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS with gp removed, and DOWNSTREAM_MODELS holds no gp anyway. The general search passes no models, so the engine scores its 'fast' and 'full' tiers, the same five; gp is tier 'extra' and never scored. The distance search is given the same five by name. No knn downstream model is used. No ridge.

Decisions: Step 1 approves two models per dataset: ginkgo_acsins lightgbm+gp, ginkgo_colloidal dnn+svm, ginkgo_hic gp+dnn, ginkgo_pr_cho gp+dnn, ginkgo_titer dnn+rf. On ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, gp is one of the two and is never scored. On every dataset, three or four unapproved models are searched and scored: acsins rf/xgboost/svm/dnn, colloidal rf/xgboost/lightgbm, hic rf/xgboost/svm/lightgbm, pr_cho rf/xgboost/svm/lightgbm, titer xgboost/svm/lightgbm. All five datasets break R1.

### R2 per fold: yes

Code: For each of the five competition folds it slices representations, augmentation representations, groups and labels to that fold's training rows. It runs one general search and one distance search on those rows only. The three hybrids per model on that fold come from those two searches and are rebuilt on the same training rows. It never reads the whole-dataset precompute. Each fold's searches are filed separately, because condition_suffix ginkgo_hold_fold{i} is folded into the tier name. fold_reselection is used, but only on held-out scores this file computed itself, not on a stored whole-dataset search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only.

Counts (Step 6): acsins cuts 3, colloidal 2, hic 2 and 3, pr_cho 3; the code runs them. titer matches. Distance search (Step 7): budgets acsins 50-500, others 100-500; the code adds 10,25 on acsins and 10,25,50 elsewhere. Importance: hic cuts deeplift, pr_cho cuts lightgbm_gain; both run. Evaluators: acsins cuts rf, colloidal and hic cut knn, titer cuts lightgbm and svm; all run. Counts: hic cuts 2; it runs. Augmentation (Step 8): acsins, pr_cho, titer are cut; the code runs uncapped on both searches. hic and colloidal keep uncapped on the distance search; the general search is open. All five datasets break R3.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: Hybrids: three per model per fold, not two. general1 is the general search's best_by_model winner, refit by the search. general2 is rank 2 of the general search. distance1 is rank 1 of the distance search. Base representations: every one of the 12 representations (10 general plus paratope and structural) is scored per model on every held-out fold. fold_reselection then picks one best single representation per model per held-out fold, by its mean held-out score over the other folds. So it reports one base representation per model per fold, not two. A fold-0 block also records the top 2 base representations (rf only) and top 2 of each per model, on training-fold scores. Those are recorded, never scored on held-out rows.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. This file is designed around the owner's 2026-10-02 set (top 2 general plus top 1 distance hybrid), so it gives 3 hybrids and 1 reselected base representation per model.

### Other problems

- general1 and general2 are rebuilt two different ways. The search's refit for general1 passes the real downstream model and the spearman metric to create_hybrid (find_best_hybrid.py:9538-9541). general2 and distance1 go through build_fold_hybrid with no model and no metric_fn (opig_ginkgo_developability.py:716-722). Its docstring says that falls back to the internal evaluator scored by r2 (_shared.py:5129-5134). So the general2 and distance1 hybrids are not built the way the search scored them.
- general1 is best_by_model, the maximum over all finite rows keeping the first on a tie (find_best_hybrid.py:7961-7965). general2 is rank 2 from top_hybrids, which sorts ties by label (_shared.py:8062-8063). On an exact tie, general2 could be the same recipe as general1. Not observed; plausible from the code only.
- Hybrids wider than 500 features are cut to 200 features by a LightGBM filter before scoring (opig_ginkgo_developability.py:663-664; run_baseline_survey.py:591-592, 604-618). The decided general budgets for these datasets reach 2000 features. A hybrid the search ranked at 1000 or 2000 features is scored on 200 of them.
- The search runs no 'none' augmentation condition on any of the five datasets (opig_ginkgo_developability.py:539, 576). So no hybrid without augmentation candidates is ever built, even where Step 8 cuts augmentation.
- The single-representation side scores 12 representations: the 10 general plus paratope and structural (opig_ginkgo_developability.py:899; _shared.py:3761). The hybrid searches see only the 10 general as base representations, with the other two as augmentation (:860-868).
- The inner search has 4 folds, not 5. The groups are the competition fold IDs (antibody_baseline_survey.py:289-291), and a fold's training rows hold 4 of them. find_best_hybrid then drops to 4-fold GroupKFold (find_best_hybrid.py:4074-4081).
- Pruning votes run inside each fold's search. The script default is default_pruning (:1157); the server passes calibrated (opig_one.sh:57). Either way DEFAULT_PRUNING_SCHEDULE's per-axis votes stay on (find_best_hybrid.py:3917-3920). They delete importance, evaluator, count and allocation members per fold, on top of whatever DECISIONS keeps.
- print_analysis's 'Delta' and 'Hybrid wins' take a maximum over five models on the hybrid side against a maximum over all representations and five models on the other side (opig_ginkgo_developability.py:1053-1068). The per-model held-out table (print_reselection_analysis, :1083-1132) is the paired comparison.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- general1's per-fold score list can drop out of fold order. When a model has no fitted recipe, assembly fails, or the fit fails, the loop continues without appending anything (opig_ginkgo_developability.py:744, 765, 773). general2 and distance1 append NaN for a slot they could not score (:731-737). The single-representation lists have one entry per fold (:260-268). fold_reselection pairs the two by list position (_shared.py:1855-1862 'fold-aligned'). So after one missing fold, the general1 score from fold k+1 is compared with the single-representation score from fold k.
- A general search that raises skips the whole fold (opig_ginkgo_developability.py:560-562 'continue'). No slot gets a NaN for that fold, so general2 and distance1 lose their fold order too, along with general1.
- adaptive_pruning=0.25 (opig_ginkgo_developability.py:556, 593) has no effect. resolve_pruning_kwargs always passes a schedule, and the schedule path returns before adaptive_pruning is read (find_best_hybrid.py:3917-3920). The allocation vote uses the default final_strategy_threshold 0.20 and strategy_top_n 2 (find_best_hybrid.py:3883, 3890).


## opig opig qsar (tests/experiments/opig_activity_cliff_qsar.py)

What it measures: For each of three ChEMBL targets, it measures how well each representation and each hybrid predicts held-out activity, and how well those predictions classify matched pairs as activity cliffs.

Datasets: One dataset, chembl_qsar, split into three ChEMBL targets: d2, fxa and mpro (ALL_TARGETS, opig_activity_cliff_qsar.py:152; --targets can narrow it, :1215). Each target is loaded with load_chembl_qsar (:639). Every search is filed under dataset_name='chembl_qsar' with the target in condition_suffix (:700, :705, :512-513, :884). The launcher row is submit_everything.sh:138 ('qsar|64G|opig_activity_cliff_qsar.py PM|'), run through runbook/opig_one.sh with --pruning-mode calibrated (opig_one.sh:57, :60). chembl_qsar is left out of the main dataset roster (submit_everything.sh:211-213). DECISIONS.md has no row for it in any step: line 53 says 'Nothing stored: chembl_qsar.'

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every representation and every per-fold hybrid is scored with five downstream models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm (MODELS_LIST = DOWNSTREAM_MODELS). The distance searches, general and per fold, also score knn as a downstream model. That happens because no models= is passed, so DISTANCE_MODELS (the five plus knn) is the default. chembl_qsar runs at full speed and gets no gp. ### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Two sides. The per-fold hybrid table (rows kirby_hybrid, kirby_hybrid__general2, kirby_hybrid__distance1) follows the rule. Each scaffold fold slices every array to its training rows. It then runs its own general and distance searches on those rows, under a per-fold condition_suffix. Each recipe is rebuilt on that fold's training rows and predicts the held-out rows. The representation scores used to pick which representations to keep (blueprint.rep_scores) come from that same per-fold search. The other side reads one whole-dataset search per target. Its outputs are saved: the fold_reselection block, printed as 'Honest per-model held-out', the top2_selection block, and rule_hybrids_by_model.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows. The fold_reselection block re-picks per fold from a search that saw every row. That is the leaking pattern the rule names. The top-2, hybrid_deltas and whole-dataset rule rows read the same search, so they leak as well. They are reported beside the per-fold rows, not used to build them.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Hybrids: for each model and fold it builds and scores 3 hybrids, the top 2 from the general search and the top 1 from the distance search. Decisions: For each model and fold, the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. The code gives 3 hybrids instead of 2. On the base side it scores all representations instead of picking 2 per fold. Scoring every representation is part of the Dablander replication, so the base side differs by design. The third hybrid follows the 2026-10-02 rule of 2 general plus 1 distance, not R4.
