### R6 missing search: yes

The fold then records the missing slot in rule_missing.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. This one does that.

### Other problems

- The per-fold hybrid arm runs only if the whole-dataset block reaches line 742. If get_best_search_for_downstream raises, the per-fold arm is skipped for that target. One case is a StaleResultDB, which _iter_pool_searches re-raises at _shared.py:6107. The per-fold arm does not use that search (opig_activity_cliff_qsar.py:673-748, 900-901, 954, 1019-1021).
- maccs is in the per-representation table as one of the 7 base representations. In every hybrid search it is only an augmentation, so hybrids draw on 6 base representations (:676-678, 743).
- The script defaults to --pruning-mode default_pruning (:1199). The launcher passes calibrated (opig_one.sh:57, :60). A direct run and a cluster run therefore search with different pruning schedules.
- Every search passes adaptive_pruning=0.25 (:514, :706, :885). Pruning removes grid members during each search, on top of whatever grid is asked for.
- Lines 721-723 print 'Top-3 base reps (by RF)' from the whole-dataset search. That is three representations ranked by one model on every row.
- The comment at :454-457 and the slot names say the top 2 general and top 1 distance hybrids are built per fold. The code does build those 3. R4 asks for 2.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R6 should not be marked as followed without a caveat. There are two skip paths. (a) The whole per-fold arm is skipped when the whole-compound block raises before line 742. That is reported in OTHER PROBLEMS and is a skip with a warning: opig_activity_cliff_qsar.py:900-901 and :1019-1021. (b) _iter_pool_searches drops any augmentation condition whose search raises. It prints a warning and continues (_shared.py:6108-6114). It does not add that drop to the returned warnings, so a per-fold hybrid can be chosen from fewer augmentation conditions and the saved output does not say so. The per-fold searches themselves are never refused. Their stored name carries '__cond-<target>_heldout_fold<i>' (find_best_hybrid.py:8986-8987). _is_precompute_tier keeps only 'general' or 'general_distance' as the part before '__obj-' (find_best_hybrid.py:598-602), so _refuse_cold_search returns without refusing (find_best_hybrid.py:650-651).
- R3, svm on d2: the engine skips svm when an 'uncapped' search has more than 5,000 training molecules (find_best_hybrid.py:3083-3085, 8695-8698). d2 has 6,333 compounds (src/kirby/datasets/chembl_qsar.py:44). Four of five scaffold folds are about 5,066 training molecules, so svm is likely missing from each fold's uncapped search too. That count is inferred from the 4/5 fraction; actual fold sizes were not checked. So on d2, svm's hybrids come from the none and capped conditions only, while the other four models also get uncapped. The code comment at opig_activity_cliff_qsar.py:529-532 names the ceiling but not that it applies per fold.
- R2, a smaller point: pruning settings for the per-fold searches come from the whole compound count (opig_activity_cliff_qsar.py:679-680, 733-735). This only sets the schedule and uses no labels, so it is not a label leak.


## opig opig blueprint_transfer (tests/experiments/opig_blueprint_transfer.py)

What it measures: It measures whether a hybrid recipe found on logd, either re-fitted on herg_ki or applied as logd's exact selected features, beats herg_ki's own best single representation and herg_ki's own searched hybrids, fold by fold.

Datasets: Two datasets: logd is the source and herg_ki is the target. They are set by the submit row in tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:139 ("--source logd --target herg_ki --mode full PM"). The script's own defaults are the same (opig_blueprint_transfer.py:1086-1089). The representations are the 7 that appear in both datasets' 10-representation DATASET_REPS 'general' lists (opig_blueprint_transfer.py:1120-1124): avalon, chembert, ecfp4, grover, mhg_gnn, mordred, smited. I printed that list with one import this session. pruning_mode is 'calibrated', from opig_one.sh:57 and :60.

### R1 models: NO

Code: The models come from config['models']. get_config sets that to the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. The code keeps only models scored by both whole-dataset general searches, and both score all five. So every arm runs on rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm, on both datasets. The four distance searches also score knn as a downstream model, but knn is never evaluated as an arm. ridge is never scored. gp is not added on either dataset; I printed small_dataset_extra_models as [] for both.

Decisions: Step 1 approves svm+dnn for herg_ki and dnn+svm for logd, so the same two models on both datasets. Step 9 allows knn in the distance search on both. Ridge is excluded.

None of these is scored on a fold.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search on that fold's training rows only.

Code: Each per-fold search passes condition_suffix 'heldout_fold{i}', which turns the tier into 'general__cond-heldout_fold{i}' or 'general_distance__cond-heldout_fold{i}'. _is_precompute_tier strips only '__obj-', so those tiers are not precompute tiers. The cold-search refusal returns without refusing, so the run builds its per-fold searches itself. The four whole-dataset searches keep the plain tiers 'general' and 'general_distance' and the plain dataset names. Their stored-result identity includes the representation pool, by name and feature count. Their pool is the 7 shared representations, not the 10 the precompute used, so no precompute rows match them. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, which submit_everything.sh exports for OPIG jobs by default, they need more than 500 configurations scored: 816 on logd general and 8,160 on herg_ki general. So both are refused. The logd and herg_ki general calls are not inside a try, so the RuntimeError stops the whole run before any fold is scored. The two distance calls are inside a try, so a refusal there is written to rule_missing and the distance slots come back empty.

Decisions: A needed search that does not exist is built by the experiment itself. It is never refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- The logd hybrids come from two different grids. The recipes transferred to herg_ki come from the logd search over all rows, which runs the fast grid through _speed_kw and _evals_for (lines 255, 265). The logd per-fold check searches pass neither (355-367), so they run the full grid. The two differ in three ways at once: importance (1 method against 3), allocation (3 against 5) and representation counts (3/all against 2/3/5/all). The comment at 261-264 records that only the whole-dataset call was fixed on 2026-09-29.
- On herg_ki, the scored per-fold arms are per fold, but the results file also saves selections ranked on all herg_ki rows: top2_selection['target'] and ['target_distance'], target_blueprint_whole_data and base_rep_whole_data (lines 793-799, 809, 1033-1042, 1069-1070). Nothing marks top2_selection as a whole-dataset ranking except its 'which_search' key.
- The summary table and the RESULT verdict use only the general1 slot of each arm (keys 'native', 'recipe_transfer', 'full_transfer', lines 698-700, 871-893). The general2 and distance1 transfer arms are saved but enter no verdict. The verdict counts wins across all five models, including the three that Step 1 does not approve.
- --max-folds is accepted (line 1101) and stored by get_config (_shared.py:9362-9363), but run() never reads config['max_folds']. The flag does nothing.
- The rep-overlap check (lines 147-161) checks representation names and widths only. Whether logd and herg_ki share molecules is not checked. Could not determine the overlap, so I cannot say whether the transfer arms see any herg_ki held-out molecule through logd.
- The search pool is the 7 representations the two datasets share, not either dataset's 10. So none of the four whole-dataset searches can be served from the precompute: the representation pool is part of the stored-result identity (find_best_hybrid.py:9147). Could not determine whether rows from an earlier run of this experiment exist on the server.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The two transfer arms differ in more than whether features are re-selected. recipe_transfer is built per herg_ki fold by build_fold_hybrid (opig_blueprint_transfer.py:667-669), which keeps only the recipe's number of representations (_shared.py:5256-5286) and judges each feature with the downstream model and the dataset metric (_shared.py:5129-5134, model=mk() and metric_fn passed). full_transfer replays features from create_hybrid on all logd rows (opig_blueprint_transfer.py:522-542), which passes no representation count, no model and no metric_fn. create_hybrid has no representation-count parameter (hybrid.py:5636-5680). So when logd's winning recipe used 3 of the 7 representations (the fast grid allows 3 or all), full_transfer's features are drawn from all 7. full_transfer then differs from recipe_transfer in three ways at once, not one: the representation pool, the scorer that keeps or drops features, and the fixed versus re-selected features.
- The source-side 'hybrid' context arm on logd (opig_blueprint_transfer.py:743-755) is built with the full-grid per-fold recipe, while the recipe it is meant to sanity-check (the transferred one, lines 491-493) came from the fast-grid whole-dataset search. The logd check therefore does not test the recipe that is transferred.


## opig opig scaffold_hybrid (tests/experiments/opig_scaffold_hybrid.py)

What it measures: For each of four antibody datasets, it adds two mutation-difference representations (dphyschem, dphyschem_pos) to the 10 approved representations and measures, on held-out outer folds, how each representation scores alone and how much the best hybrids beat the best single representation.

Datasets: flab_expression_koenig, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_binding_adams. The default list is at opig_scaffold_hybrid.py:98-99 (--datasets default at :308). The server row passes no --datasets (submit_everything.sh:140, the wrap at :420-421; opig_one.sh:120-125 adds only --output-dir), so all four run. The dataset names in that row are used for job dependencies only (submit_everything.sh:408-411).

The engine then scores every model of tier fast or full: rf, lightgbm, dnn, xgboost, svm (find_best_hybrid.py:8701-8711; tiers printed this session). svm's 10,000-row cap does not bite: the four datasets have 4,275 or 5,000 molecules (BILL_OF_MATERIALS.md:41-45, a dated source). ### Other problems

- general2 can skip the true second-ranked recipe. The c14 function _bp_identity compares six fields and leaves out representation count (c14_cross_domain_summary.py:70-74). top_hybrids ranks with representation count in the identity (_shared.py:7985-7988). So a configuration that differs from the winner only in representation count is treated as the winner and skipped (c14:170-173). general2 is then the third-ranked or later. If the top three all share the winner's six fields, general2 is reported missing for that fold (c14:174-179).
- The general2 record is labelled tier 'general' (c14_cross_domain_summary.py:148). The search it came from ran on tier 'scaffold_cmp' (opig_scaffold_hybrid.py:417). The written JSON names a search that did not produce it.
- The top 2 base representations in the printed summary are ranked by their mean score on the held-out folds (opig_scaffold_hybrid.py:173, 194-198; find_best_hybrid.py:11433-11435). The comparator inside every delta is instead picked per fold on training rows (find_best_hybrid.py:11084-11096). The two lists can name different representations.
- The comment at opig_scaffold_hybrid.py:312-316 says models=None is kept so the search hits what the SLURM precompute wrote. No precompute writes tier 'scaffold_cmp': it appears only in this file and in a comment at submit_scaffold_hybrid.sh:17.
- The distance evaluators have no 'match' (_shared.py:502). On flab_binding_adams the approved pair is lightgbm+xgboost (DECISIONS.md:24). In the distance run, xgboost is never scored with an xgboost evaluator. Step 7 describes the stored distance rows as including a model's own type where it was downstream (DECISIONS.md:609). Whether the engine adds it without 'match' in the list: I did not open that code, so this is unverified.
- Every search here runs over 12 representations, the 10 approved plus dphyschem and dphyschem_pos (opig_scaffold_hybrid.py:400, 408-409). The representation-count decisions in Step 6 and Step 7 were measured on a pool of 10 (DECISIONS.md:561). That difference is by design: adding the two representations is the question.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The distance hybrid is compared with a different single representation than the general hybrids. general1 and general2 are measured against the representation the general run picked on each fold's training rows. distance1 is measured against the representation the distance run picked from its own inner search (tests/experiments/opig_scaffold_hybrid.py:221-222 reads block['distance'] deltas; src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:11084-11096 picks per run). The c14 note says all three share one comparator (tests/experiments/complexity/c14_cross_domain_summary.py:64-65). Whether the two picks ever differ in practice: could not determine without running.
- general2 identity also leaves out which representations a configuration used, not only the count: _bp_identity has no 'reps' field (c14_cross_domain_summary.py:70-74), while Blueprint carries reps (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:1446).
- get_config builds config['allocations'] (tests/experiments/_shared.py:9342), but run_nested_cv never forwards it (:1181-1204). Passing a dataset's decided allocation list through config would therefore have no effect; it must go as an explicit allocation_methods= keyword.
- The distance run scores every one of the 12 single representations again for six models on every fold (find_best_hybrid.py:11042-11069 runs inside the second nested_cv_evaluate). knn therefore also appears as a downstream model in the distance block's single-representation table, not only in its hybrid (tests/experiments/opig_scaffold_hybrid.py:478).


## opig opig shared_vectors_remedy (tests/experiments/opig_shared_vectors_remedy.py)

What it measures: For one representation that gives several molecules the same row of features (chemberta by default), it measures two things on the same outer folds. The first is whether a hybrid with partner representations, or donor features added as augmentation, improves the held-out score. The second is whether fewer molecules still share a row in the matrix that was built.

Datasets: herg_ki in the main run. The script default is ['herg_ki'] (opig_shared_vectors_remedy.py:123, used at :720). submit_everything.sh:141 runs the script with no --datasets, so it runs herg_ki only. A second launcher, tests/slurm_scripts/submit_opig_shared_vectors.sh:57, defaults to herg_ki, caco2, logd and qm9. It is not in submit_everything.sh's roster.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Under the general search it passes no models (args.models is None by default), so run_nested_cv sends models=None. The engine then scores rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm. herg_ki has 1,412 rows, so svm is kept. Under the distance search it passes DISTANCE_MODELS, which is those five plus knn. summarise_comparison writes one row per model the search scored, so the output has 5 models under the general search and 6 under the distance search. general2 rows are built for every model in result.by_model. ridge is never scored.

Decisions: herg_ki: svm+dnn only (Step 1). Step 9 allows knn as a downstream model in the distance search on herg_ki. So rf, xgboost and lightgbm are three models the record excludes, in both searches. On the second launcher's datasets: caco2 and logd are dnn+svm, qm9 is dnn+lightgbm. All three would also get the three extra models.

### R2 per fold: yes (partly)

Code: Every score comes from run_nested_cv, which calls nested_cv_evaluate. For each outer fold, nested_cv_evaluate slices the representations, labels, groups and donor features to that fold's training rows. It runs find_best_hybrid there under a per-fold cache namespace. The fold's winning recipe is rebuilt on its training rows and scored on its test rows. Each base representation is fitted on training rows and scored on test rows. The second general recipe comes from rule_general2_outer, which reads the same fold's inner search (ncv.inner_searches[i]) and rebuilds it on that fold's training rows. No whole-dataset search is read. Two whole-row choices exist; neither picks a recipe by score. First, the target, partners and donor are chosen on every row before folds exist. The defaults name the target and partners. The donor is picked by a tie count over the features, with no labels. Second, see other_problems for the margin unit, a number taken from the outer test-fold scores.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search on that fold's training rows only.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: All searches use tier 'shared_vec' or 'shared_vec_distance', speed='full' by default, and rep_counts=[None], which means the whole pool only. General search: budgets come from config, which is FULL_BUDGETS (10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000 features). Importance comes from config: deeplift, lightgbm_gain, treeshap. Allocation is not passed, so the engine's full list applies: performance_weighted, power_2, softmax_T1, rank_exp_d0.3, wglobal_power2. Evaluators are not passed, so the engine default applies: match, rf, lightgbm, dnn. Distance search: budgets 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500. Evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm. Importance and allocation are the same as the general search. Augmentation: arms B and D sweep strategies none, uncapped, capped and all over 228 settings, each under both searches.

Decisions: herg_ki, general search: budgets 250 to 2000 (Step 2 v3); cut deeplift (Step 3 v2); cut wglobal_power2 (Step 4); keep match, rf, lightgbm, dnn (Step 5 v3); cut counts 2, 3 and 5, so the whole pool only (Step 6). Distance search (Step 7): budgets 100 to 500, cut deeplift, cut wglobal_power2, no evaluator cut, cut counts 2, 3 and 5. Step 8: no augmented searches on herg_ki.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Each arm gives three hybrids per model per fold. general1 is the fold's inner winner from the general search. general2 is the fold's second-ranked inner recipe from that same search. distance1 is the fold's inner winner from the distance search. Each hybrid is compared with one fixed base representation, the target (chemberta), not with the best base representations. The code labels this the owner's set of 2026-10-02: 2 general hybrids plus 1 distance hybrid. nested_cv_evaluate scores every representation in the pool, but the rows written report only the target.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. The experiment asks whether the hybrid fixes one named representation, so comparing against that representation alone is a design choice. Having three hybrids and not two is not required by that design.

### R6 missing search: yes

Code: Every search is built inside the job. The tiers 'shared_vec' and 'shared_vec_distance' are not the precompute's tiers, 'general' and 'general_distance'. So _refuse_cold_search returns before counting stored configurations, even when KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 is set. If one fold's inner search raises, nested_cv_evaluate prints it and skips that fold. If every fold fails it raises. A raise in arms B and D is caught and written as an error row, and the script then exits 1. A raise in arm C is not caught and stops the script.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- The margin unit leaks fold scores into the inner searches of arms B and D. The script takes the target's spread across all outer test folds, the largest across models (:942-946). It sets augmentation_margin to a multiple of that spread (:209). That number then sits inside the training-rows-only search of every fold, including the folds whose test scores produced it. No recipe is picked by it, but each fold's search reads a number computed partly from that fold's test score.
- On the second launcher's datasets (submit_opig_shared_vectors.sh:57), --speed full is the default (:52). run_nested_cv never applies the fast-tier rule. So qm9 and logd are searched with all three importance methods and all five allocation methods. The record keeps lightgbm_gain only on qm9 and cuts deeplift and treeshap on logd (DECISIONS.md:340, :334). qm9's allocation is fixed to the three stored methods (DECISIONS.md:406).
- The --models help text (:733-737) says the default matches what the precompute wrote, so the cache is hit. The script searches under its own tier 'shared_vec' (:116), so no precompute row is ever read. The text is out of date; it has no effect on results.
- The docstring of rebuild_fold_matrix (:356) cites find_best_hybrid.py:10128-10160 as the steps it mirrors. Those steps are now at find_best_hybrid.py:10950-10996. The code still matches; only the line reference is out of date.
- general2 rows have no tie counts and no_op is None (:593-595, :662-664). So the second hybrid per model reports a score but not the row-sharing count, which is half of the question the file asks.
- The pools of arms C and D are 3 representations chosen by name, not the dataset's 10 approved representations. This is by design; the file says why (:125-131).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R1/R3, second launcher: arms B and D under capped drop svm on caco2 and logd. dataset_policy.py:80-81 lists svm, and svm is one of their two approved models. The script then leaves svm out of the printed table for those datasets (opig_shared_vectors_remedy.py:1029-1036). Under capped and uncapped, knn is also dropped on caco2, logd and qm9 in the distance search (dataset_policy.py:80-81, :86, :106-107), but Step 9 runs knn there (DECISIONS.md:718, :737, :743). Step 8 cuts augmentation on all three, so this only happens because the script runs augmentation anyway.
- R3, second launcher: representation count. The script searches only the whole pool (opig_shared_vectors_remedy.py:482). The record keeps every count on logd (DECISIONS.md:594), and qm9 stores counts 'all' and 3 (DECISIONS.md:361). With a 3-representation pool, count 3 is the whole pool, and count 5 also collapses onto it. Only count 2 is actually missing on logd. The code gives a reason at :478-481.
- R1: the margin unit at opig_shared_vectors_remedy.py:942-946 is the largest spread across all five models. Three of those five (rf, xgboost, lightgbm on herg_ki) are excluded by Step 1, so excluded models set a number that every B and D search reads.
- R3, caco2 distance search: the record cuts treeshap (DECISIONS.md:622), but the script searches all three importance methods there (_shared.py:1200-1201 -> :9343).


## federated fed01 (tests/experiments/federated/fed01_noise_heterogeneity.py)

What it measures: On labels binarised to two classes, with label flips spread unevenly across five silos, it compares MCC across seven conditions. The KIRBy hybrid conditions are C0, C5 and C6; the FLuID ensemble conditions are C1 to C4. It repeats this at six flip levels and five feature budgets, plus a noise-detection analysis and a smoothing sweep.

Datasets: lhasa_herg, caco2 and logd. The roster is FEDERATED_DATASETS="lhasa_herg caco2 logd" at tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:99. Federated jobs are queued only for those three (submit_everything.sh:378-390). fed01 is last in the federated run order (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:317). run_all also accepts 'herg', which loads the same Lhasa data (federated_helpers.py:3026-3028), but no submit script sends it. On lhasa_herg, run_all passes an empty representation list (federated_helpers.py:3008-3009). load_lhasa_herg_data then turns that into the 'all' preset (federated_helpers.py:123-128), not the 10 representations in DATASET_REPS['lhasa_herg'] (complexity_helpers.py:147-151).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every condition is fitted with one FLuID classifier per run. run_all loops over rf, xgb and dnn × seeds 0, 1 and 2, so nine runs per dataset. The hybrid recipes are looked up for that same model, renamed rf, xgboost or dnn. The searches behind those lookups score five downstream models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm. The distance search adds knn. ridge is never named.

Decisions: Step 1: lhasa_herg lightgbm+xgboost; caco2 dnn+svm; logd dnn+svm. Step 9 allows knn in the distance search on all three.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: All hybrid recipes are chosen before the folds exist. That covers general1, general2, distance1 and the single-best fallback. There is one choice per (flip level, budget), from searches over every row of the dataset. get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index, so it ranks on the mean over all folds of those searches. The same recipe is then used on all five fed01 folds. Only the features are refitted, on each fold's training rows (C0) or each silo's rows (C5, C6). The returned metadata itself says selection_scope 'whole_dataset'.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search run on that fold's training rows only.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: The general search uses all 8 budgets, 10 to 2000 features, with no pruning. caco2 and lhasa_herg get the full engine grid: 5 allocation methods, 3 importance methods, evaluators match/rf/lightgbm/dnn, and representation counts 2/3/5/all. logd gets the fast grid: lightgbm_gain, 3 allocation methods, counts 3/all. The distance search uses budgets 10 to 500, evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm, and the same allocation, importance and count lists. On caco2 and logd it builds 'none', 'uncapped' and 'capped' searches. lhasa_herg has no augmentation. The arms themselves are built at 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1000 features. Nothing reads DECISIONS.md.

Decisions: caco2 general: budgets 500-2000, all importance methods, cut wglobal_power2, all four evaluators, count 'all' only (cut 2/3/5). caco2 distance: 100-500, cut treeshap, cut counts 2/3. logd general: 500-2000, lightgbm_gain only, the three stored allocation methods, all four evaluators, all stored counts. logd distance: 100-500, nothing else cut. lhasa_herg general: 100-2000, everything else kept; no distance decision exists. Step 8: augmentation cut on all three.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: At flip levels above 0, the tier name gets a '__noise_' suffix. The cold-search refusal does not apply to that tier, so the whole-dataset noisy searches are built inside the job. At flip level 0 the tier is plain 'general' or 'general_distance'. submit_everything.sh exports KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 by default. On caco2 and logd, fed01 searches the 0/1 labels under AUC. The precompute stored the continuous labels under RMSE. Labels hash and metric are both in the stored-row identity, so nothing matches. 8,160 configurations (caco2) and 816 (logd) are both over 500, so each search is refused. The refusal is caught and printed as a warning, and that pool member is skipped. The single-best lookup then returns nothing. C0, C5 and C6 run on fixed settings: performance_weighted, treeshap, rf evaluator, uncapped. The distance search on lhasa_herg has no stored rows (Step 7), so at flip level 0 it is refused the same way and distance1 is reported missing. Whether the lhasa_herg flip-level-0 general search is served from the precompute: could not determine. Its representations and groups come from a different loader than the precompute's.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- On caco2 and logd the decisions in DECISIONS.md were measured on the continuous labels under RMSE. fed01 searches 0/1 labels under AUC (fed01:315-317, 369-370; federated_helpers.py:365, 373). So even a search cut to the decided grid would apply cuts measured on a different target.
- At flip level 0 on caco2 and logd, C0, C5 and C6 can run on fixed settings, not on any search (fed01:401-405). The result file records only 'single best lookup (set had none)' (fed01:437). It does not record that the lookup itself returned nothing and fell back to fixed settings.
- On lhasa_herg the representations are the 'all' preset of get_molecular_representations (federated_helpers.py:123-128, 3008-3009). They are not the 10 approved in DATASET_REPS['lhasa_herg'] (complexity_helpers.py:147-151). I did not check what 'all' contains.
- Every summary table reads the 100-feature arms only (fed01:360, 1287-1290). 100 features is below the decided range of 500-2000 on caco2 and logd.
- C5 and C6 pass only the allocation method, importance method and internal evaluator to federated_feature_selection (fed01:775-784, 929-940). So general1 and general2 build the same features there whenever those three agree. The code records this in rule_missing (fed01:163-170) rather than preventing it.
- The search is trained on uniform flips at the mean silo flip fraction, seeded by fed_seed (fed01:466-468). The arms train on per-silo flip fractions spread from 0 to sigma, seeded by fed_seed and the fold index (fed01:319-331, 574-583). So the flips the recipe was chosen on are not the flips the arms see.
- Above flip level 0, each flip level and each fed_seed gets its own whole-dataset general and distance search, built inside the job (noise_spec.py:266; find_best_hybrid.py:8954-8955). fed_model does not change the search.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The hybrids are rebuilt without the recipe's representation count. In the search, a recipe can win on the top 2, 3 or 5 representations (rep_count). fed01 rebuilds every hybrid over all representations: _recipe_kwargs (fed01:103-124) and the C0 create_hybrid call (fed01:655-674) never pass rep_count. The shared builder does restrict it (_shared.py:7251-7260, restrict_to_rep_count at find_best_hybrid.py:9686-9706). So a hybrid scored on 2 representations is built and reported from all 10.
- The duplicate check leaves out representation count. _same_recipe_check compares the allocation method, importance method, evaluator, augmentation and _recipe_kwargs (fed01:449-453). Two hybrids that differ only in representation count are therefore recorded as the same recipe, and both are built from the same features.
- Along the flip-level axis the recipe source changes along with the noise. At flip level 0, on all three datasets, general1 is the fixed fallback (performance_weighted, treeshap, rf evaluator; fed01:401-412) and distance1 is missing. Above 0, the recipes come from searches built in the job (fed01:466-468). So the curve from flip level 0 to 0.05 differs in two ways at once: noise and recipe source.
- The caco2 and logd distance searches at flip level 0 are refused under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 too. They use 0/1 labels under auc, but the precompute stored continuous labels under rmse (fed01:315-317, 369-370; result_cache.py:46-52). By my count from find_best_hybrid.py:607-633, the grids are 10,800 configurations on caco2 and 1,080 on logd, both over the 500 limit (find_best_hybrid.py:705-750). The first audit named only lhasa_herg's distance search.
- lhasa_herg runs on a different representation pool from the one its precompute was built on. fed01 uses the 'all' preset (federated_helpers.py:123-128, find_best_hybrid_molecular.py:148-162). The precompute's load_data path uses the 10 DATASET_REPS representations (_shared.py:4075-4092). rep_pool is part of the stored-row identity (result_cache.py:79-89), so no stored lhasa_herg search can serve fed01.
- The noisy searches above flip level 0 add caco2/logd augmentation members on both lineages. On the distance lineage this includes 'capped', because both datasets are under 10,000 rows (_shared.py:6030-6046). Step 8 cuts augmentation on all three datasets (DECISIONS.md:668, 686, 687). C5 and C6 never use the augmentation the recipe picked (fed01:775-784).


## federated fed02 (tests/experiments/federated/fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py)

What it measures: On 5-fold scaffold CV, it compares one representation per silo (C1) and two FLuID prediction ensembles (C2, C3) against three feature-level hybrids built on the five silo representations (C4 all five, C5 top three, C6 clustered). Each hybrid is swept over 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1000 features, for each FLuID model (rf, xgb, dnn) and each seed (0, 1, 2).

Datasets: lhasa_herg, caco2 and logd. The list is FEDERATED_DATASETS at tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:99, repeated at tests/slurm_scripts/submit_all_datasets.sh:70. The fed02 docstring says herg, logd and caco2 (fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:17). federated run_all loads herg and lhasa_herg the same way, from Lhasa's data, and builds no start-up search for either (federated_helpers.py:2998-3009, 3026-3028). For lhasa_herg the representation list is not DATASET_REPS['lhasa_herg']. run_all passes an empty list, and load_lhasa_herg_data turns that into the 'all' preset (federated_helpers.py:3009, 123-128). For caco2 and logd the representations are DATASET_REPS[...]['general'], 10 each (federated_helpers.py:3007).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every fitted arm uses the FLuID model of the run, swept over rf, xgb and dnn (fed_to_kirby_model gives rf, xgboost, dnn). Each run reads a recipe searched for that model. The report-only rows (top2_pairs_by_model, rule_set_by_model, hybrid_deltas_by_model) loop over every model the whole-dataset search scored, which is five: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. ridge is never used.

Decisions: caco2: dnn and svm. logd: dnn and svm. lhasa_herg: lightgbm and xgboost. knn is allowed only in the distance search. On caco2 and logd the code fits dnn (approved), plus rf and xgboost (not approved), and never svm. On lhasa_herg it fits xgboost (approved), plus rf and dnn (not approved), and never lightgbm. All three datasets break the rule, each in two ways: two unapproved models fitted and one approved model missing.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: No search runs on a fold's training rows. The hybrid recipes come from whole-dataset searches. get_best_search_for_downstream marks its pick selection_scope 'whole_dataset'. get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold_i, so it ranks on the mean over every fold of the whole-dataset search. The same recipe is then used in all five outer folds. Only the features are refit, on each fold's training rows, with create_hybrid and fluid_within_kirby_across. The base representations (C1) are per fold: an inner 3-fold group-aware CV on the training rows ranks the five silo representations.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. The recipe choice here saw every row, including each fold's held-out molecules. So the hybrid arms C4, C5 and C6 (general1, general2, distance1) do not comply. C1's two picks do comply.

(3) fed02's own rebuild budgets: 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1000 features.

Decisions: caco2 general: budgets 500-2000, all 3 importance methods, cut wglobal_power2, all four evaluators, cut counts 2/3/5, no augmentation. The code differs in four ways: five extra budgets (10-250), wglobal_power2, counts 2/3/5, and uncapped and capped. caco2 distance: budgets 100-500, cut treeshap, cut counts 2/3, no augmentation. The code differs in four ways: budgets 10/25/50, treeshap, counts 2/3, and augmentation. logd general: budgets 500-2000, lightgbm_gain only, the three stored allocation methods, all four evaluators, all stored counts, no augmentation. The code matches on importance and allocation. It differs on budgets (10-250 extra) and augmentation (uncapped and capped). Whether counts 3/all are all logd stored could not be determined. logd distance: 100-500, nothing cut. The code adds budgets 10/25/50 and augmentation. It runs logd fast there, so whether it lacks stored methods could not be determined. lhasa_herg general: budgets 100-2000, everything else kept, no augmentation. The code adds 10/25/50 only, and has no augmentation representations. lhasa_herg has no stored distance search, and Step 7 has no row for it. fed02's own rebuild budgets also differ. 50, 100 and 250 are below the decided range on caco2 and logd. 50 is below it on lhasa_herg. 2000 is never swept on any of the three. The headline budget, 100 features, is outside the range on caco2 and logd.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: For each fold and each FLuID model, fed02 gives two base representations: the inner ranking's first and second picks among the five silo representations. It gives three hybrids per model: general1, general2 and distance1, from the 2026-10-02 set. Each is built three ways (C4 all five silos, C5 top three, C6 clustered silos). That is nine hybrid arms per budget, at five budgets. It also reports C2 and C3, two FLuID ensembles. The base representations are limited to the five silo representations (ecfp4, mordred, molformer, pdv, chemberta, or substitutes). They are not the dataset's best two of its ten.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. fed02 differs in three ways. The hybrid count is three, not two. The base representations come from a fixed list of five silo representations. The hybrids are fit to those five, not to the ten representations the recipe was searched on. The silo design is the experiment's question. The third hybrid (distance1) comes from the superseded 2+1 rule.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: fed02 never builds a per-fold search. When the whole-dataset general read fails or is refused, it prints the reason and switches to fixed settings: performance_weighted, treeshap, match. It records that budget as 'hard_defaults' and still builds and scores C4, C5 and C6 from them. When the 2+1 read cannot fill a slot, the slot goes in rule_missing and is not built. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, the default in submit_everything.sh, a missing whole-dataset search over 500 configurations is refused. _iter_pool_searches catches that, prints a warning and skips it. lhasa_herg gets no start-up search, and its distance search is not stored (DECISIONS.md:750). So with the refusal on, lhasa_herg's distance1 is missing. Its C4, C5 and C6 may run on the fixed settings unless its general search is already stored. Without the refusal, the whole-dataset searches are built on all rows inside the job, not per fold.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist must be built by the experiment itself. fed02 builds none. It falls back to fixed settings, or reports the slot missing.

### Other problems

- The recipe is searched on the dataset's ten general representations, but fed02 applies it to the five silo representations. The two sets differ. On caco2, mordred and chemberta are absent, and silos B and E become graph_kernel and avalon. On logd, pdv and chemberta are absent, and silos D and E become chembert and avalon (fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:57-68, 297-341; DATASET_REPS printed this session).
- For lhasa_herg the representations come from the 'all' preset of get_molecular_representations, not DATASET_REPS['lhasa_herg']. So the search fed02 reads for lhasa_herg may not be the stored one, which used the 10 approved representations. Whether the identities match could not be determined (federated_helpers.py:3009, 123-128).
- When the recipe lookup is refused or fails, C4, C5 and C6 still run on performance_weighted, treeshap and match. They are scored like searched arms. The only marker is recipe_source_by_budget = 'hard_defaults' in budget_sweep_per_fold (fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:418-421, 763-764, 980).
- C6 takes only the allocation method, importance method, internal evaluator and budget (fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:914-918). So general1 and general2 can build identical C6 features. fed02 records this in rule_missing; it does not prevent it (fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:165-172).
- A recipe whose winning augmentation condition is uncapped or capped is rebuilt with augmentation in C4 and C5 on caco2 and logd. Step 8 cut augmentation on both (fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:804-805, 861-862; DECISIONS.md:668, 687).
- fed02 fits FLuID's settings for rf and xgb: RandomForestRegressor with 150 trees and depth 15, or FLuID.create_classifier. Whether these match the rf and xgboost the search scored was not checked (federated_helpers.py:514-536, 557-572).
- The docstring names herg as a dataset, but the launchers run lhasa_herg (fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:17; submit_everything.sh:99).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3/R8 augmentation, fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:417-418: the hard-defaults path forces augmentation even when no searched recipe exists. If the lookup returns nothing and the dataset has augmentation representations, aug_cond is set to 'uncapped'. On caco2 and logd, C4 and C5 are then built with uncapped augmentation, which Step 8 cut (DECISIONS.md:668, 687). The first agent only flagged a searched recipe whose winning condition is augmented.
- R3 representations, lhasa_herg: the search is read or built on about 33 base representations from the 'all' preset, not the 10 decided ones (federated_helpers.py:3002-3003, 123-128; find_best_hybrid_molecular.py:148-163). The representation list is not part of the stored identity (result_cache.py:46), so rows from the 10-representation search can come back labelled as this one. The rule read's base-representation ranking also covers about 33 representations, not 10.
- R2 report-only rows, fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:1234-1351: top2_base_reps, top2_hybrids, top2_pairs_by_model, rule_set_by_model and hybrid_deltas_by_model all rank on the whole-dataset search with no fold held out. They fit nothing, but they are written to the result file next to the per-fold arms.
- Fold alignment, for any per-fold fix: fed02 splits its outer folds with seed=fed_seed, which is 0, 1 or 2 (fed02_rep_diversity_silos.py:506-507; federated_helpers.py:449). The stored searches' folds use seed 42 (_shared.py:6664-6670 docstring). Fold i in fed02 is therefore not fold i of the stored search.
- R1, every run: one run is made per FLuID model and seed, so 3 models x 3 seeds = 9 runs (federated_helpers.py:3231-3241). No run uses svm or lightgbm, and none can, because _FED_TO_KIRBY_MODEL has no entry for either (federated_helpers.py:456).


## federated fed03 (tests/experiments/federated/fed03_synthetic_private.py)

What it measures: Part A measures whether selecting features separately inside each hERG data source (three silos) beats single-source and FLuID ensemble models, and Part B measures the same when each silo holds a different family of representations.

Datasets: On the server fed03 runs on three datasets: lhasa_herg, caco2 and logd. FEDERATED_DATASETS is set at tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:99, and the federated job is queued per dataset at :378-392. fed03 is in the federated run order at tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:317. The dataset name picks the part. lhasa_herg (also herg, herg_ki) goes to Part A, source-based hERG (fed03_synthetic_private.py:2006-2010). caco2 and logd go to Part B, where each silo holds one family of representations (fed03_synthetic_private.py:2021-2025). The file's command-line default is herg_ki (fed03_synthetic_private.py:2053). herg_ki is not in the federated roster.

### R1 models: NO

Code: run_all runs fed03 once per model in FED_MODELS and once per seed: rf, xgb and dnn, times seeds 0, 1 and 2. Every fit uses that model: silo baselines, C2, C4, C6, C8 and C9. Recipes are read for the same model under its KIRBy name, which is rf, xgboost or dnn. C7 in Part A weights each representation with a fixed RandomForestClassifier, whatever model the run uses. At start-up on caco2 and logd, run_all builds the whole-dataset search with models=None. That scores rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm. knn and ridge are not used.

Decisions: lhasa_herg: lightgbm+xgboost. caco2: dnn+svm. logd: dnn+svm. ridge is excluded everywhere. knn is allowed only in the distance search (Step 9).

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid comes from get_rule_hybrids, called without fold_i, or from get_best_search_for_downstream. With no fold_i, the ranking uses the mean over all folds of one search built on every row of the dataset. That one recipe is then refit on each fold's training rows. On caco2 and logd the general search is the start-up search over all rows. The distance search is read from disk or built over all rows. On lhasa_herg the search ran on Lhasa's training file alone. Part A's folds also contain the Lhasa test file. So the search did not see the same rows the folds split.

Decisions: Every hybrid used in a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: fed03 sweeps feature budgets of 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1000 on every dataset. At each budget it ranks every stored configuration for the model, and applies none of the cuts from Steps 2-7. The pool for caco2 and logd has none, uncapped and capped augmentation on the general search. The distance search has none, uncapped, and capped under 10,000 rows. fed03 drops capped recipes but keeps uncapped ones. When no recipe is found it falls back to fixed settings: performance_weighted, treeshap and match. In Part B the fallback is uncapped whenever the dataset has augmentation. Distance reads use the global lists: budgets 10-500 and evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm. Above 500 features the distance read ranks over every budget it holds.

Decisions: lhasa_herg has a budget range of 100-2000 and keeps every importance method, allocation method, evaluator and representation count. It has no distance row, and augmentation is cut. caco2 has a range of 500-2000 and cuts wglobal_power2 and representation counts 2, 3 and 5. Its distance search uses 100-500 features with treeshap and counts 2 and 3 cut, and augmentation is cut. logd has a range of 500-2000 and cuts deeplift and treeshap. Its distance search uses 100-500 features with no cuts, and augmentation is cut.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: fed03 never builds a per-fold search. A missing stored search goes to get_precomputed_search, which calls find_best_hybrid over all rows. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, the submit default, a search with more than 500 configurations left is refused. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips it. The empty slot is written to rule_missing. If general1 is empty, a whole-dataset single-best lookup fills it, or fixed settings do. An empty general2 or distance1 is not built at all. This hits the lhasa_herg distance search, which DECISIONS lists as not stored. Without the flag, the whole-dataset search is built inside the job.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, with no separate precompute script and no refusal or skip.

### Other problems

- On lhasa_herg the data is Lhasa's own training file, not ChEMBL. run_all loads it with load_lhasa_herg_data (federated_helpers.py:3026-3028, 109). Part A still calls it the ChEMBL silo (fed03:365-367). Part A then loads the same training file again as the lhasa_train silo (fed03:503-504). Deduplication keeps the first copy (lhasa_herg_loader.py:211-237). So the lhasa_train silo should lose nearly all its molecules. I did not run this; it is inferred from the code. Part A on lhasa_herg then has two silos from one curator, not three sources. Its ChEMBL-against-Lhasa disagreement count compares Lhasa with itself.
- On lhasa_herg the representations are not the dataset's 10 approved ones. run_all sets rep_names to [] for lhasa_herg (federated_helpers.py:2998-3009). load_lhasa_herg_data turns [] into the 'all' preset (federated_helpers.py:123-128). That preset has more than 30 representations (tests/find_best_hybrid_molecular.py:148-160). DATASET_REPS lists 10 for lhasa_herg (complexity_helpers.py:147-150), and that list is never read here. Could not determine whether the stored lhasa_herg search was built on the same pool.
- In Part B, C2 and C3 under one recipe differ in internal evaluator as well as in how the budget is split. C3 always turns 'match' into rf (fed03:1735). C2 hands 'match' to create_hybrid with the run's model, which turns it into xgboost or dnn (hybrid.py:5870-5880). So on the xgb and dnn runs, C2 minus C3 differs in two ways at once, not one.
- C3 in Part B passes no metric_fn to create_hybrid (fed03:1785-1795, 1815-1823). C2 passes the dataset's metric (fed03:1687). That is a third difference between the two arms.
- The fallback recipe uses treeshap (fed03:418, 1440). Step 3 cuts treeshap on logd.
- At 1000 features the distance slot is built from a recipe scored at another budget. Distance searches stop at 500 (_shared.py:6855-6872). The result records budget_relaxed (fed03:306), but the row is still labelled 1000.
- run_all averages each model over seeds 0, 1 and 2 (federated_helpers.py:3242-3245). Each seed also changes fed03's folds, because cv_split takes seed=fed_seed (fed03:779-780, 1560-1561). So the seed spread mixes model seed with fold assignment.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Part B C2 and C3 differ in augmentation as well. C2 builds with the slot's augmentation condition, which can be uncapped, and adds the selected augmented features (fed03:1667-1698). C3 never passes augmentations, and keeps only step_size and objective from the recipe (fed03:1762-1763, 1785-1795). So C2 minus C3 differs in up to four ways at once: budget split, evaluator, metric, augmentation.
- Part A C8 and C9 differ in features, not only in selection. C8 fits on 2048-bit Morgan fingerprints (fed03:1068). C9 fits on features selected from the dataset's representations (fed03:1108-1114). The comment at fed03:1033 reads C9 minus C8 as what the selection is worth. It differs in two ways at once, not one.
- On lhasa_herg the start-up search and its augmentation step are skipped (federated_helpers.py:3026-3029). Every lhasa_herg read therefore goes to disk or builds a search through get_precomputed_search (_shared.py:5845-5896). Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH that build can be refused, and the slot is skipped.
- The R1 list of searched models on logd comes from naming the models explicitly. On logd the fast grid also changes the other axes: 3 allocation methods, rep counts 3 and all, lightgbm_gain only (find_best_hybrid.py:8650-8669; _shared.py:1046-1079). On the general search this matches Steps 3, 4 and 6 for logd. That is because the fast grid is what was stored, not because fed03 applies a cut.


## federated fed04 (tests/experiments/federated/fed04_cluster_aware_importance.py)

What it measures: It clusters each fold's training molecules into 5 groups, then compares three things in MCC. The first is a hybrid built per cluster and fitted on that cluster's rows. The second uses the same features, fitted on all training rows. The third is one hybrid for the whole training fold. It also compares the per-cluster importance profiles against a random partition of the same sizes.

Datasets: lhasa_herg, caco2 and logd. submit_everything.sh queues federated jobs on these three only (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:99, 378-390), and submit_dataset.sh runs fed04 as one federated experiment (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:317). run_all also has a herg branch (federated_helpers.py:3026-3028), but no submit script sends herg. caco2 and logd labels are continuous; fed04 turns them into two classes at log10(2) and logD 3.0 (federated_helpers.py:365, 373, 377-404; fed04:152-153).

### R1 models: NO

Code: run_all runs fed04 once per FLuID model, rf, xgb and dnn, times 3 seeds (federated_helpers.py:447, 3231-3241). Each model is a FLuID classifier fitted after random undersampling (federated_helpers.py:539-554). The recipe is ranked for KIRBy's rf, xgboost or dnn (fed04:216, 222; federated_helpers.py:456). The three datasets get the same three models.

Decisions: Step 1 approves lhasa_herg lightgbm+xgboost, caco2 dnn+svm, and logd dnn+svm. On lhasa_herg, fed04 runs xgboost (approved) plus rf and dnn (not approved), and never runs lightgbm. On caco2 and logd it runs dnn (approved) plus rf and xgboost (not approved), and never runs svm. So each dataset gets one approved model, two unapproved models, and misses one approved model. ridge is not used. knn is not used as a downstream model in fed04 itself.

Code: get_rule_hybrids is called once per (model, seed), before the fold loop, with fold_i left as None (fed04:219-231). With fold_i=None, every fold of the stored search enters the ranking (_shared.py:7082-7084, 6746-6749). That search ran over every row of the dataset (get_precomputed_search is given all rows, _shared.py:5863-5896). Inside each fold, fed04 takes only the allocation method, importance method, internal evaluator and augmentation condition from the recipe (fed04:248-253). It then refits the features with create_hybrid on that fold's training rows (fed04:94-103, 301-309). The feature fit is per fold. The recipe choice saw every row, including each fold's held-out molecules.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. Here the recipe comes from one whole-dataset search ranked on all folds' scores, so it leaks.

### R3 same cuts: NO (partly)

Code: The general read asks for FULL_BUDGETS (8 budgets) with the engine's default grid. That grid is full on caco2 and lhasa_herg, and fast on logd, because logd is in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS. The full grid is 5 allocation methods, 3 importance methods, evaluators match/rf/lightgbm/dnn, and representation counts 2/3/5/all. The fast grid is 3 allocation methods, lightgbm_gain, and counts 3/all. The distance read uses DISTANCE_BUDGETS 10-500, evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm, and models rf/xgboost/svm/dnn/lightgbm/knn. Augmentation conditions none, uncapped and capped are read on caco2 and logd. The recipe is ranked at 100 features. It is then rebuilt at 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1000 features, from federated_budgets. The rebuild uses every representation and ignores the recipe's representation count.

Decisions: caco2, general search. Budgets: the code reads 10/25/50/100/250, which Step 2 cuts. It ranks the recipe at 100 and rebuilds at 50/100/250, all cut. It never runs 2000. Allocation: it reads wglobal_power2, which Step 4 cuts. Representation counts: it reads 2/3/5, which Step 6 cuts. Augmentation: it reads uncapped and capped, which Step 8 cuts. Importance and evaluators match. caco2, distance search: Step 7 is 100-500 features, cuts treeshap, and cuts counts 2/3. The code reads 10/25/50, treeshap, and counts 2 and 3. logd, general search: Step 2 is 500-2000 features. The code reads 10-250, and rebuilds at 50/100/250 but never at 2000. Augmentation is read but cut. Importance, allocation, evaluators and counts match the fast grid. logd, distance search: the code reads 10/25/50, which Step 7 cuts. lhasa_herg, general search: Step 2 is 100-2000 features. The code reads 10/25/50 and rebuilds at 50, but never at 2000. The other axes match, and there is no augmentation. lhasa_herg has no Step 7 row, yet the code reads a distance search for it. One further difference applies everywhere. caco2 and logd are read with binarised labels and auc, and lhasa_herg with 45 representations. Neither matches the stored searches the decisions were made on, so no decided search is read on any of the three datasets.

Code: For each FLuID model it runs every phase three times: once for each of the 2 best general hybrids, and once for the best distance hybrid (fed04:210-215, 794-803; _shared.py:7064-7066). It builds no base representation arm. The rule's base representations are read and then discarded.

Decisions: Two best base representations and two best hybrids per approved model per fold. fed04 uses three hybrids where R4 asks for two. They are chosen once for the whole dataset, not per fold. It has no base representations. Leaving out the base representations fits the question fed04 asks, which compares per-cluster features with whole-fold features. The third hybrid does not follow from that design.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: No stored search matches what fed04 asks for, so the read needs a new search. On caco2 and logd that is because the labels are binarised and scored with auc. On lhasa_herg it is because there are 45 representations. submit_everything.sh sets KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 by default. With that on, find_best_hybrid refuses any search with more than 500 configurations unstored. _iter_pool_searches prints that refusal as a warning and skips the search. fed04 then runs on its hand-written fallback recipe. With refusal off, the search is built inside the job over every row of the dataset. It is never built per fold.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, on that fold's training rows. Here a refused search turns into a fallback recipe, recorded only as config.recipe_source='fallback_defaults'. A search that is allowed to run is a whole-dataset search.

### Other problems

- The recipe's internal evaluator is changed before the hybrid is rebuilt. fed04 resolves 'match' to rf for every model (fed04:253, federated_helpers.py:1273-1277). In the search, 'match' meant the downstream model's own type. So a dnn or xgboost recipe scored with evaluator dnn or xgboost is rebuilt with rf instead.
- The recipe's representation count and representation list are ignored. create_hybrid runs on every representation in train_reps (fed04:94-103, 301-309). The shared rebuild path restricts to bp.reps and the recipe's count (_shared.py:5254-5260); fed04 does not use it. On caco2, Step 6 keeps only the full set of representations, so a recipe there should not be affected. On lhasa_herg and logd, a recipe chosen at 2, 3 or 5 representations is rebuilt on all of them.
- On lhasa_herg, run_all sets rep_names to an empty list (federated_helpers.py:3008-3009). load_lhasa_herg_data turns an empty list into the 'all' preset (federated_helpers.py:123-128). That preset is 45 representations (tests/find_best_hybrid_molecular.py:145, printed this session), not the 10 in DATASET_REPS['lhasa_herg'] (complexity_helpers.py:147-150). The precompute's lhasa_herg path loads the 10 (_shared.py:4075-4091). Whether all 45 build on the server: could not determine.
- The recipe is ranked at 100 features and rebuilt at 50, 250, 500 and 1000 as well (fed04:51, 223, 260, 296, 306). So the hybrid at each budget other than 100 uses a recipe that was not ranked at that budget.
- When a read finds no configuration at 100 features, it ranks over every budget and sets budget_relaxed (_shared.py:6855-6872). fed04 records the flag (fed04:716) but still labels its results by the swept budgets.
- The fallback recipe uses treeshap (fed04:251). On logd, Step 3 cuts treeshap and deeplift. So a run that falls back on logd uses a cut importance method.
- The search ranks recipes by a KIRBy model's own cross-validation score. fed04 then fits a FLuID classifier with FLuID's hyperparameters after random undersampling (federated_helpers.py:514-554). So the model that chose the recipe and the model that is scored differ in hyperparameters and in the class balance they were trained on.
- All three seeds and all five folds use the same recipe, read once per model. fed04's own folds come from cv_split with seed fed_seed (0, 1 or 2; fed04:258-259). The stored search's folds use seed 42 (_shared.py:6664-6670). The fold numbers on the two sides are different rows. This does not affect the ranking here, because fold_i is None.
- A refused or failed read is recorded only as config.recipe_source='fallback_defaults' and in rule_missing (fed04:247, 709, 812). The run does not fail, so a result file can hold fallback-recipe numbers for some models and searched-recipe numbers for others.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The report's first other problem is wrong for searched recipes. The search does not store 'match' as an evaluator name. It stores the downstream model's own name: xgboost for xgboost, dnn for dnn (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:6379-6393, 7023-7029). fed04 only turns the literal 'match' into rf (federated_helpers.py:1273-1277). So a searched xgboost or dnn recipe keeps its own evaluator. Only the fallback recipe, which says 'match', is rebuilt with rf (fed04:252-253).
- The report's second other problem says a caco2 recipe should not be affected. That is wrong. The caco2 read still ranks representation counts 2, 3 and 5 (full grid, find_best_hybrid.py:3070, 8667-8669). So a caco2 recipe chosen at 2, 3 or 5 representations is also rebuilt on all of them (fed04:94-103, 301-309).
- The report's third other problem gives 45 representations for lhasa_herg. The number built is 33. The 'all' preset names 45, and get_representations removes the 12 per-fold ones (tests/find_best_hybrid_molecular.py:148-173, 608-609).
- The fallback recipe uses augmentation too. When augmentation representations exist, it uses the uncapped condition (fed04:248-249). caco2 and logd have them (complexity_helpers.py:189, 209-210). Step 8 cuts augmentation on both (DECISIONS.md:668, 687). So every fallback run on caco2 or logd uses a cut augmentation condition.
- The tables in aggregate, and the printed summary, use the 100-feature width only (fed04:557-558, 572-582). On caco2 and logd, Step 2 cuts 100 features (DECISIONS.md:219, 238). So the summary numbers fed04 reports first are at a width outside the decided range on two of its three datasets.
- rule_missing does not say that a search was refused. _iter_pool_searches prints the refusal and skips that search (_shared.py:6108-6114). get_rule_hybrids then records only 'the pool held no search under this family' (_shared.py:7171-7178). The result file cannot tell a refused search from one that does not exist.
- run_all also runs a search for caco2 and logd before fed04 starts (federated_helpers.py:3126-3139). It uses FULL_BUDGETS (_shared.py:5518-5519) and the engine's default grid, and includes the uncapped and capped conditions. So it has the same R3 problems: budgets 10-250, wglobal_power2 and counts 2/3/5 on caco2, and augmentation on both. fed04 does not read it (fed04:229), but it runs in the same job.


## federated fed05 (tests/experiments/federated/fed05_antibody_federated.py)

What it measures: Across three antibody datasets treated as silos, it measures a hybrid built per silo (C1), importance transferred between silos (C2), importance stability across clusters within a silo (C3), and three conditions that pool or compare silos (C4-C6).

Datasets: fed05 is queued under three dataset names: lhasa_herg, caco2 and logd (submit_everything.sh:99, 378-392; submit_dataset.sh:317). It ignores that name. It always loads the same three antibody datasets, one per silo: ddg_combined, abagym_EGFR and flab_thermo_tresanco (fed05:85-89, 240-243, 1095). So the DECISIONS rows that apply are those three silo datasets, not lhasa_herg, caco2 or logd. The same computation runs three times and is saved under three names it never loads. When fed05 is the only experiment in its process, run_all loads no data and builds no whole-dataset search (federated_helpers.py:2994-2995, 3022-3025). submit_dataset.sh runs one experiment per process (submit_dataset.sh:448-449).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every condition fits the federated model, swept over rf, xgb and dnn (FED_MODELS) on all three silos. xgb maps to xgboost. svm is never fitted. The general search scores five models: rf, lightgbm, dnn, xgboost and svm, because models=None and only the 'fast' and 'full' tiers run. The distance search scores six: those five plus knn. No gp and no ridge are scored.

Decisions: ddg_combined: svm+dnn. abagym_EGFR: svm+dnn. flab_thermo_tresanco: dnn+svm. knn is allowed in the distance search on all three (Step 9: run). So on every silo, dnn matches. rf and xgboost are fitted although neither is approved. svm is approved on all three and is never fitted.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: Both searches use one global grid on every silo. Distance search: budgets 10 to 500 features, evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm, with the same allocation, importance and representation-count lists. The augmentation setting is 'none' on both. Separately, the hybrids built afterwards ignore the searched budget (see R4).

Decisions: ddg_combined, general search: the code adds budgets 10, 25, 50, 1000 and 2000 against a 100-500 range. It runs deeplift, which is cut. It runs power_2 and wglobal_power2, which are cut. It runs count 2, which is cut. Evaluators match. ddg_combined, distance search: the code adds budgets 10, 25 and 50 and runs deeplift. It runs performance_weighted, power_2 and wglobal_power2, the lightgbm evaluator, and counts 2 and 3, all of which are cut. abagym_EGFR, general search: the code adds budgets 10, 25, 50 and 100 against a 250-2000 range. It runs deeplift, which is cut, and the rf evaluator, which is cut. abagym_EGFR, distance search: the code adds budgets 10, 25 and 50. It runs deeplift and treeshap, both cut, and the rf evaluator, also cut. flab_thermo_tresanco, general search: the code adds budgets 10 and 25 against a 50-2000 range, and runs deeplift, which is cut. flab_thermo_tresanco, distance search: the code adds budgets 10 and 25 and runs deeplift. Step 8 cuts augmentation on all three; the code matches.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each federated model, silo and seed, it takes the top 2 hybrids from the general search and the top 1 from the distance search. That is three recipes, ranked by the search's own mean over its inner folds. It never selects base representations. Each recipe is rebuilt using only three of its fields: allocation method, importance method and internal evaluator. The budget is create_hybrid's default of 100 features, not the searched budget. The representations are the silo's whole loaded set, not the searched representation count. Representations are scored by the internal evaluator's R², not the downstream model and metric (fed05's own comment at 697-704). So the hybrid that runs differs from the one the search ranked in three ways at once: budget, representations, and how they are scored.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: fed05 builds its own per-silo search with find_best_hybrid(cache=True). It passes no own_search, the tiers are 'general' and 'general_distance', and the dataset names have no '__'. A 10-representation silo needs 8,160 configurations for the general search and 10,800 for the distance search. ### Other problems

- The three silos share no representation by name. Printed from DATASET_REPS this session: ddg_combined has 8, abagym_EGFR 10, flab_thermo_tresanco 10, and the three-way intersection is empty. So shared_reps is empty (fed05:383-384). C4 then records 'only 0 valid pooled reps' (fed05:737). C5 records 'insufficient shared reps for pooling' (fed05:841). Neither produces a number on the server lists.
- C5 pools only ddg_combined and abagym_EGFR, but it filters by the intersection over all three silos (fed05:754, 765-774). Those two share mutation_features and esm2_concat, so C5 could have run on them.
- C2 sweeps transfer budgets of 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1000 features (federated_helpers.py:248-265). Its source is C1's feature_info, built at create_hybrid's default of 100 features (hybrid.py:5647). importance_profile_transfer only trims, never adds (federated_helpers.py:2904-2911). So 250, 500 and 1000 cannot select more than the source picked. This assumes create_hybrid selects at most its budget; I did not verify that.
- C4, C5 and C6 use one 'cross-silo' recipe taken from whichever silo comes first in dict order: ddg_exp (fed05:362-367). C6 then applies it to the lead silo, the one with the most rows (fed05:858). The comment at fed05:79-84 makes that flab_thermo_tresanco at 672 rows (not re-measured). So a recipe searched on ddg_combined rows is applied to flab_thermo_tresanco rows.
- Budgets actually built: C1 and C6 at 100 features, C3 at min(30, cluster size / 3) features (fed05:552). abagym_EGFR's decided range is 250-2000, so C1 on that silo builds outside it. C3 is below every silo's decided range.
- C3 drops a cluster's failure silently: 'except Exception: pass' (fed05:582-583).
- adaptive_pruning=0.25 deletes configurations during each silo search (fed05:300). top_hybrids then ranks the survivors only (_shared.py:7891-7896). This pruning is in addition to any DECISIONS cut.
- The resume check in run_all fingerprints a placeholder with no rows when fed05 runs alone. So a change in the silo data does not trigger a re-run (federated_helpers.py:3167-3170).
- When a search is refused, the result file still holds C1, C2, C3 and C6 numbers. They come from the fixed recipe performance_weighted, treeshap and rf, which no search chose. Only the rule_missing list says so (fed05:1068).

The recipe it uses (fed05:823-825) came from a silo search over all of each silo's training rows (fed05:306, 319-320), and those include p_te. So the recipe was chosen with C5's test labels in view. Today C5 does not run, because shared_reps is empty (fed05:841).
- Run count: fed05 runs three times on the same three silos. It is in the federated list (federated_helpers.py:409-415; submit_dataset.sh:317). submit_everything.sh submits a federated job for each of lhasa_herg, caco2 and logd (:16, :376-391). fed05 ignores its dataset name (fed05:71) and writes fed05_antibody_federated/<dataset>.json in each. What it measures: For each downstream model, it scores hybrids at every budget and records which budget, allocation method and importance method win, with PCA baselines and a model-by-budget table.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. submit_everything.sh:207-213 takes every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (41 printed this session). It queues the complexity category on all of them (submit_everything.sh:95). submit_dataset.sh:312 includes c02 in the complexity order, and complexity_helpers.py:847 lists c02 in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS. complexity_helpers.py has no call to should_skip_experiment (grep empty), so no dataset is skipped. run_dataset.py:209-214 passes no config, so run_all's default config applies (complexity_helpers.py:942-954).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c02 builds no per-fold search at all, so the per-fold searches R2 needs never exist. Its own whole-dataset searches are not marked own_search. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, the default in submit_everything.sh, tiers 'general' and 'general_distance' are refused when under 50% is stored and more than 500 configurations are left. The no-augmentation, uncapped and capped searches have no try around them, so a refusal ends c02 with no result file. A refused distance search is caught and recorded as distance_search_error. The fine-tuned search (tier general_ft) and the top-representation-width searches are never refused.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment builds it itself; no refusal or skip.

### Other problems

- Models, gp: on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, gp is one of the two approved models. c02 scores gp in its searches but reports only config['models'], which has no gp (c02:103-105, 957-958). So half of the approved pair is never in best_by_model, baselines, top2 or rule_hybrids on those five datasets.
- Models, gp extra: gp is also scored on abagym_EGFR, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_titer and humanness_therapeutic, where it is not approved (printed small_dataset_extra_models this session).
- Budgets (general search, 8 budgets on every dataset): only humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc have a decided range of 10-2000. The other 39 datasets get budgets the record cuts, e.g. abagym_Ang2 is decided 25-100 and c02 runs 10, 250, 500, 1000 and 2000 as well (DECISIONS.md:209).
- Budgets (distance search, 10-500 on every dataset): humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc keep all six. Every other dataset with a Step 7 row gets cut budgets, e.g. 10, 25 and 50 on each dataset decided 100-500 (DECISIONS.md:613-650).
- Importance, general search, runs a cut method: deeplift on abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, ddg_combined, flab_binding_adams, flab_binding_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, herg_ki; treeshap on bh_doyle_plates; lightgbm_gain on buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer. flab_expression_adams never stored deeplift; c02 runs it (DECISIONS.md:305-345).
- Importance, general search, lacks kept methods: flab_expression_koenig, bindingdb_kd and kiba keep all three. c02 treats them as fast and runs lightgbm_gain only. logd's decision (cut deeplift and treeshap) matches the fast list.
- Fast list: the code's FAST_SPEED_DATASETS has 14 names; the record's fast-tier table has 10 (DECISIONS.md:352-363). The extra four are bindingdb_kd, flab_expression_koenig, kiba and logd. c02's own comment at line 113 says 12.
- Allocation, general search: runs wglobal_power2 on caco2, ginkgo_acsins, herg_ki; runs power_2 and wglobal_power2 on ddg_combined; runs all five on suzuki, where the decision is held (DECISIONS.md:381-407). Lacks softmax_T1 on flab_expression_koenig and kiba, and softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2 on bindingdb_kd (fast list).
- Evaluators, general search: runs rf on abagym_EGFR; rf, lightgbm and dnn on abagym_VEGF; dnn on buchwald_hartwig and ginkgo_colloidal; lightgbm on ginkgo_titer (DECISIONS.md:516-556).
- Representation counts, general search (2/3/5/all on full datasets): runs cut counts on abagym_Ang2 (2), adme_hlm (2,3), adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, herg_ki (2,3,5), buchwald_hartwig (3,5,all), ddg_combined (2), flab_binding_koenig (3,5), ginkgo_acsins (3), ginkgo_colloidal (2), ginkgo_hic (2,3), ginkgo_pr_cho (3). Fast list 3/all runs cut count 3 on gb_human_enhancers_cohn, nt_promoter_tata, flab_expression_koenig, kiba; on bindingdb_kd it runs 3 and lacks the kept count 2 (DECISIONS.md:565-605). logd: could not determine which counts were stored.
- Distance search, Step 7: runs cut importance methods on 11 datasets (abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, adme_hlm, caco2, cdr_flexibility, ddg_combined, flab_binding_adams, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, herg_ki); cut allocation methods on abagym_VEGF, ddg_combined, herg_ki, and all five on suzuki (held); cut evaluators on 11 (abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ddg_combined, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_titer, qm9); cut counts on 13 (DECISIONS.md:613-650).

Its primary search, which every selection is read from, is the uncapped one (line 328). So on those 30 datasets every reported top-2 and rule hybrid comes from a search the record cuts.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- svm can drop out of the search c02 reads every selection from. Under augmentation 'uncapped', the engine drops svm above 5,000 molecules (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:3221-3233, _STRATEGY_MAX_SAMPLES printed {('svm','uncapped'): 5000}). Above 10,000 it drops svm in every search (find_best_hybrid.py:2812). nt_promoter_tata has svm as an approved model, has augmentation representations, and its registry n_samples is 5274. So its uncapped search, read at c02:328, would hold no svm rows, and resolve_comparison_models drops svm (c02:957-958). Unverified: the 5274 is the registry figure, not a row count loaded this session. For most svm-approved datasets the registry has no n_samples, so I could not check them.
- The two stale comments are not the only ones. c02:150-152 says 'find_best_hybrid is called with models=None'. c02:171-178 says to 'Pass models=None so model_names normalizes'. On the fast and small datasets, the code passes a named list (c02:125-132).
- best_per_model_across_conditions (c02:762-790) chooses which search wins for each model. It compares the whole-dataset means of no augmentation, uncapped, capped, fine-tuned and top-representation width. This is one more selection made on all rows (R2), and it compares augmented conditions the record cuts (R3/Step 8).
- The PCA baselines (c02:621-649) fit five models at 8 budgets on every fold. This is c02's own design, not a search. It still fits three non-approved models per dataset and never fits gp where gp is approved (R1).


## complexity c03 (tests/experiments/complexity/c03_cross_dataset_transfer.py)

What it measures: Across datasets, it correlates each dataset's complexity descriptors with the budget (number of features) of each downstream model's best stored hybrid. It also fits SVR and ElasticNet on those hybrids for the regression datasets.

Datasets: On the cluster it runs on all 41 datasets in one job. submit_all_stages.sh:385 passes $FULL_ORDERED to cross_one.sh, which calls c03 with --mode full --datasets <all> (cross_one.sh:58-59). $FULL_ORDERED comes from $FULL (submit_all_stages.sh:311). Unless --full is passed (:114), $FULL is every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (:146; stage1_prelim_noise.py:192-194). A tiny import this session printed 41 names. Run by hand without --datasets, it defaults to logd, caco2 and herg_ki (c03:867). It is not in the per-dataset complexity list (complexity_helpers.py:846-870), so complexity run_all never calls it. Every dataset goes through load_data with augment=False (c03:881-884). No loader path sets augmentations (for example _shared.py:4725), so c03 only ever reads the 'none' augmentation condition.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every per-model result loops over the same five names on every dataset: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. That covers the per-model best, the per-fold re-pick, the owner's set and the correlation. The top-2 table also adds every model the distance search scored. That includes knn on every dataset and gp on 9 small datasets. On the 5 datasets whose approved pair includes gp, gp gets no per-model best, no owner's set and no correlation entry. On every regression dataset it also fits SVR(C=1) and ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, l1_ratio=0.5). Their recipe comes from svm's search, or rf's if svm has none.

Decisions: Step 1 allows two models per dataset. Step 9 allows knn only in s02, s05, s06, s08, s10, s13 and the OPIG census, not c03. gp is approved on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid and base representation comes from searches run over all rows of the dataset. The distance read and the owner's set both resolve through get_precomputed_search, which runs find_best_hybrid on data['reps'] and data['labels'] unsliced. The per-fold picks rank the stored per-fold scores of those whole-dataset searches on the other folds. This holds out each fold's scores, not its rows. The two SVR/ElasticNet blocks rebuild those recipes on c03's own fold training rows. The recipe choice was still made by the whole-dataset search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. Re-picking per fold from a whole-dataset search does not comply.
