### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c03 never builds a per-fold search. When a whole-dataset search is missing, find_best_hybrid builds it inside the job under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH. That only happens if 500 or fewer configurations are missing; otherwise it raises. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that search. c03 then lists the model under models_dropped, or the owner's slot under rule_missing. The cluster job sets KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1. DECISIONS says no distance search is stored for bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg. By the count formula each of those three is over 500 configurations, unverified by a run. So on those three, all five models drop out of the correlation.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment must build it itself.

### Other problems

- The first SVR/ElasticNet block rebuilds each recipe with create_hybrid over every representation in bp.reps (c03:498-516). bp.reps is the whole pool (find_best_hybrid.py:5389-5398). There is no restrict_to_rep_count call. So a recipe stored with a representation count of 2, 3 or 5 is rebuilt over all 10 representations. Those are different features from the recipe named in novel_model_fold_recipes.
- The second SVR/ElasticNet block goes through build_hybrid_from_entry, which does call restrict_to_rep_count (_shared.py:7259-7260). With no scores passed, that ranks representations by blueprint.rep_scores (find_best_hybrid.py:9706-9708). Those scores come from the whole-dataset search.
- fold_reselection is called without recipe_selection='whole_dataset' (c03:362-367). Its docstring says to pass it whenever the candidates come from a search over every row (_shared.py:1838-1845). So the saved per-fold difference does not record that the candidate list was chosen on all rows.
- The winning budget behind every correlation is read from the distance search, whose budgets stop at 500 features (_shared.py:495). Step 2 ranges reach 2000 features on most datasets (DECISIONS.md:209-249). So no dataset can show a winning budget of 1000 or 2000 features.
- The SVR/ElasticNet folds come from c03's own cv_split (c03:470-471). It assumes c03 fold i and the stored search's fold i hold the same rows. _winner_per_fold checks only that the fold counts match (c03:77). The first block never checks; the rule block checks only the count (c03:547-551). Same rows: could not determine without running both splits.
- On bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg no distance search is stored (DECISIONS.md:750). In the cluster job the distance read is refused there, so per_model is empty. Those three datasets have no winning budget and drop out of every correlation. Their owner's sets still read the general search.
- The code runs 14 datasets fast (printed this session); the record's fast-tier table lists 10 (DECISIONS.md:352-363). On flab_expression_koenig, bindingdb_kd and kiba, c03 asks for the fast search, with lightgbm_gain only. The record keeps deeplift and treeshap there (DECISIONS.md:313, 321, 332).
- On ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, Step 8 keeps the uncapped distance search (DECISIONS.md:678-679). c03 loads no augmentation representations (c03:881-884), so it never reads that search.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- c03:410-421 and c03:616-621: the dataset's 'best model' and every best_* field are an argmax over all five models in DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. On most datasets that includes models outside the two approved ones (R1).
- c03:507-516: besides representation count, the first SVR/ElasticNet rebuild does not pass the recipe's step_size, candidate_ranking or objective. The second path does pass them (_shared.py:7262-7281). Whether any stored recipe uses a step_size other than create_hybrid's default of 5 could not be determined without reading the stored rows.
- c03:331 and c03:297-330: the top-2 table is read out of each of the five per-model distance reads. So the same knn and gp rows are written up to five times, once under each model's pool read (R1, R4).
- R5 does not apply: c03 is a complexity experiment, not a noise experiment.


## complexity c04 (tests/experiments/complexity/c04_importance_as_metric.py)

What it measures: It measures whether weighting features by their importance scores improves predicting each molecule's label from its nearest training molecules, in the concatenation of all ten representations.

Datasets: Queued on all 41 datasets. submit_everything.sh takes every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:207-213). It queues the complexity category for each (submit_everything.sh:95, 350-374). c04 is in the complexity list (complexity_helpers.py:854; submit_dataset.sh:313). c04 returns a skip record on classification datasets (c04_importance_as_metric.py:326-331). By the registry (dataset_policy.py:230, printed with one import this session), 15 are classification and skipped: cdr_flexibility, flab_binding_adams, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, herg, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, the five nt_* datasets, tcga_brca_pam50, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary, tz_her2_multiclass. It computes on the 26 regression datasets: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, the five ginkgo_* datasets, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki.

### R1 models: NO

Code: The only predictive models are nearest-neighbour ones. The kNN arm fits KNeighborsRegressor with k = 5, 10 and 20 molecules. The other arms predict from the 10 nearest training molecules, weighted by inverse distance. The importance scorers also train models, one per representation, on the fold's training rows: a random forest for treeshap, LightGBM for lightgbm_gain, a small neural network for deeplift. None of the 26 datasets' two approved models is ever fitted as a downstream model.

Decisions: Step 1 fixes two models per dataset, for example svm+dnn on herg_ki and rf+lightgbm on buchwald_hartwig. The note under Step 1 says knn is not allowed as a downstream model. Step 9 keeps knn only for the distance search read by s02, s05, s06, s08, s10, s13 and the OPIG census. c04 is not named. knn is the subject of c04, so swapping to the approved pair would change the question it asks. That is her call.

### R3 same cuts: by design

Code: c04 runs and reads no hybrid search. It does use two search settings as its own fixed axes. It runs all three importance methods (deeplift, lightgbm_gain, treeshap) on every dataset, from run_all's config. Its low-dim and cross-test arms keep 25 features on every dataset, because run_all never passes a budget. The importance methods are what c04 compares, so cutting one removes a row of its result.

Decisions: Step 3 (v2) cuts importance methods per dataset. Among the 26 regression datasets, c04 runs a cut method on 12. deeplift: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, herg_ki. lightgbm_gain: buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer. treeshap: bh_doyle_plates. deeplift and treeshap: logd. qm9 is lightgbm_gain only, so deeplift and treeshap are extra. Step 2 (v3) sets budget ranges. 25 features lies inside the range only on abagym_Ang2 (25-100) and abagym_VEGF (10-500). On the other 24 regression datasets 25 is below the lowest decided budget.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: It picks no two best base representations and no two best hybrids, and has no per-model selection. It scores every one of the ten representations alone, unweighted, with 10-neighbour prediction. It scores the concatenation of all ten, unweighted and weighted by each importance method. It scores 25-feature subsets chosen and weighted by each importance method, and every pairing of a choosing method with a weighting method.

Decisions: Per each of the dataset's two models, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### Other problems

- On the cluster path the result file names the wrong metric. run_all saves c04's result with the dataset's own metric, for example rmse with lower_is_better true on herg_ki (complexity_helpers.py:1153-1155, 1251-1255). c04's result dict carries no metric_name, so save_experiment_results keeps the dataset's metric (_shared.py:9079-9082). Every number in the file is an R-squared or an MAE. c04 stamps 'r2' only under its own __main__ (c04_importance_as_metric.py:475-486), which submit_dataset.sh does not use (submit_dataset.sh:448-449).
- The kNN arm and the retrieval arms use two different distances. KNeighborsRegressor is built with sklearn's default, Euclidean (c04_importance_as_metric.py:116, 122). The retrieval arms use make_nearest_neighbors, which is manhattan by default (_shared.py:2957-2958). So the kNN rows and the retrieval rows in one file differ in distance as well as in neighbour weighting.
- The kNN arm's KNeighborsRegressor is not tuned. make_nearest_neighbors' own note says a kNN fitted as a model should tune its metric per fold (_shared.py:2953-2955). c04 fixes k at 5, 10 and 20 molecules and uniform weights (c04_importance_as_metric.py:94, 116).
- Two ways of combining folds sit in one file. The kNN arm averages the per-fold R-squared (c04_importance_as_metric.py:149-150). The retrieval, low-dim and single-representation arms pool all folds' predictions into one R-squared (c04_importance_as_metric.py:155-161, 262-264, 300-303). The pooled arms keep no per-fold score, so they report no fold spread.
- A failed cross-test pairing leaves no record. The exception is swallowed with 'pass' and nothing is printed or stored (c04_importance_as_metric.py:392-393).
- Each experiment runs in its own process under submit_dataset.sh (submit_dataset.sh:448-449). So c04's job builds or reads both whole-dataset start-up searches, which it never uses (complexity_helpers.py:1065-1125). Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH a missing one is refused and caught; without it, it is built inside c04's job.
- c04 produces nothing on 15 of the 41 queued datasets, all classification (c04_importance_as_metric.py:326-331). This covers all five nt_* datasets, both tcga_* datasets, herg, lhasa_herg, cdr_flexibility, flab_binding_adams, humanness_therapeutic and both tz_her2_* datasets.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- A stale result store for the general start-up search stops c04 before it runs. precompute_hybrid_searches re-raises StaleResultDB (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5610-5617). The general start-up call in run_all has no try around it (complexity_helpers.py:1065-1082), unlike the distance call (:1095-1118). c04 never reads that search, yet c04 then writes no result.
- flab_expression_adams: DECISIONS.md:320 shows deeplift as never stored ('-') with 'keep all stored methods'. c04 runs deeplift there anyway (complexity_helpers.py:942-954 with find_best_hybrid.py:3675). The report's list of datasets running a cut method leaves it out.
- The start-up searches use the uncut grid on every dataset: all 8 budgets, all three importance methods, the default allocation methods and evaluators (complexity_helpers.py:942-954, _shared.py:5518-5519). That breaks R3 for those searches even though c04 does not read them. The report describes the grids but never states this against R3.
- The code's fast list has 14 datasets (dataset_policy.py:688, printed this session); the decided fast-tier table has 10 (DECISIONS.md:352-363). bindingdb_kd, flab_expression_koenig, kiba and logd are fast in code but not in the record. This affects the start-up searches only.
- R2 holds for c04's own numbers. Importance is computed on each fold's training rows only (c04_importance_as_metric.py:60-66). Features are chosen per fold from those scores (:187-191, :230-233). The scaler is fit on training rows (:108-110). c04 reads no hybrid search.


## complexity c05 (tests/experiments/complexity/c05_learning_curves.py)

What it measures: At each sample size it compares the best hybrid score with the best single-representation score, per downstream model, to see whether the hybrid's advantage changes with the number of molecules.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. submit_everything.sh builds the list from every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213). It queues complexity on each one (:95, :350-374). c05 is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (complexity/complexity_helpers.py:854) and in RUN_ORDER (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:312-314). complexity run_all never calls should_skip_experiment, so no dataset is skipped. A python import this session printed 41 datasets, 9 of them without augmentation representations: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, cdr_flexibility, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, tz_her2_binary, tz_her2_multiclass. Sample sizes are 10, 25, 50, 75 and 100% of the rows (c05:144-145). Above 5,000 rows they are 250, 500, 1000 and 2000 rows instead (c05:109-115; _shared.py:544-545).

### R1 models: NO

Code: The models are config['models'], which is the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. Both searches at every sample size score all five, and so does the read of the whole-dataset precompute. gp is never scored, because gp is not in that list. knn is never a downstream model, because the distance search only takes c05's own model list. ridge is never scored. On nt_* and gb_* datasets the engine drops xgboost by name prefix. get_model_factories receives the full row count, so svm is dropped from every sample size on datasets over 10,000 rows. That happens even though no subsample there is larger than 2,000 rows.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models. Five datasets need gp: abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho. knn only where Step 9 allows it, and ridge nowhere.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: c05 has no outer held-out fold. At each sample size and seed it runs one search over every row of that subsample. It reports that search's own cross-validated mean for the winning hybrid and for the best single representation. So the folds that pick the winner are the folds it is scored on. At the last sample size, on datasets of 5,000 rows or fewer, the subsample is every row of the dataset. The leave-one-fold-out arrays call fold_reselection on that same search, which is the pattern R2 names as leaking. The second pass reads the whole-dataset precompute and rebuilds those recipes on the subsample folds. The file's own comment says those scores are not held out. That rebuild has no fold-level scores to rank representations. So for a recipe that keeps 3 representations, it chooses which 3 from the whole-dataset blueprint.rep_scores.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only. Re-picking from stored per-fold scores of one search over all rows leaks.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: The general and distance searches at each sample size are c05's own searches. Both use the fast grid on all 41 datasets, from own_search_kwargs. That grid is importance lightgbm_gain only; allocation performance_weighted, power_2 and rank_exp_d0.3; representation counts 3 and all. General evaluators are rf, match, dnn and lightgbm. ### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: The curve keeps one hybrid and one base representation per model at each sample size, averaged over seeds. ### R6 missing search: NO

### Other problems

- c05 never runs the un-augmented search on the 32 datasets that have augmentation representations. Both searches use 'capped' only (c05:460). Step 8 keeps 'none' on all 41 datasets and keeps augmentation only on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, uncapped, on the distance search. So on those two, c05 runs capped where the record keeps uncapped.
- On four datasets the general search uses only an importance method the record cut. Step 3 cuts lightgbm_gain on buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer (DECISIONS.md:314, 316, 327, 328). The fast grid c05 uses is lightgbm_gain alone (find_best_hybrid.py:3674). Step 7 cuts it on the distance search for cdr_flexibility and ginkgo_pr_cho too (DECISIONS.md:623, 634).
- buchwald_hartwig keeps representation count 2 only (Step 6, DECISIONS.md:574; Step 7, :621). c05 searches 3 and all, both cut, and never searches 2.
- On full-tier datasets c05 leaves out choices the record keeps. It never runs deeplift or treeshap, softmax_T1 or wglobal_power2, or representation counts 2 and 5. Example: abagym_VEGF keeps all three importance methods and all five allocation methods (DECISIONS.md:307, 373).
- Its fast grid includes power_2, which Step 4 cuts on ddg_combined (DECISIONS.md:383). On suzuki, power_2 and performance_weighted are HELD and c05 searches both (DECISIONS.md:407).
- Its general evaluators include ones Step 5 cuts: rf on abagym_EGFR; rf, lightgbm and dnn on abagym_VEGF; dnn on buchwald_hartwig and ginkgo_colloidal; lightgbm on ginkgo_titer (DECISIONS.md:517-539).
- Its distance evaluators include ones Step 7 cuts on 11 datasets, for example dnn, knn and svm on buchwald_hartwig (DECISIONS.md:621).
- Budgets cannot follow Step 2 at the small sample sizes by construction. The decided lower limit is 250 or 500 features on most datasets. A 10% subsample often has fewer training rows than that, so c05 searches 10, 25 or 50 (c05:437).
- On datasets over 5,000 rows the largest subsample is 2,000 molecules, about 1,600 training rows, so budget 2000 is never searched there (c05:112, 437).
- When no swept budget fits the training rows, c05 searches a budget equal to the training row count. That budget is not on the grid (c05:439-447, 532-533).
- The hybrid side takes its maximum over many configurations and budgets. The single-representation side takes its maximum over about 10 representations. Both are scored on the folds that chose them. The file says so and leaves it uncorrected (c05:184-191, 366-375).
- svm is dropped from the whole curve when the full dataset is over 10,000 rows, though every subsample there is at most 2,000 rows (c05:92-94; _shared.py:3066-3069). The datasets where svm is approved and this applies could not be determined. The registry printed no row count for most datasets in a python import this session.
- The search is named '<dataset>_n<size>_s<seed>' (c05:474). The per-dataset model skips are keyed on the exact dataset name, so they do not apply to c05's searches (dataset_policy.py:168-171). An example is svm dropped under capped on adme_*, caco2 and logd (dataset_policy.py:78-83). So c05 scores models there that the whole-dataset capped search drops.
- The top-2 blocks and the rule_hybrids_last_search block come from one search only: the last sample size, at the last seed that did not raise (c05:939-1019). They do not describe the other sample sizes.
- The second pass is on by default on the cluster (c05:308-310). It scores whole-dataset recipes at each subsample. The file says these numbers are not held out (c05:269-275).

- Representation count 3 is searched on every dataset (find_best_hybrid.py:3071, via c05:479-481). Step 6 cuts 3 on the general search for 15 datasets: adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_koenig, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, herg_ki, kiba, nt_promoter_tata (DECISIONS.md:569-599). ## complexity c06 (tests/experiments/complexity/c06_within_family_gradient.py)

What it measures: For each capacity setting of seven model families, it finds the number of features at which the best hybrid scores highest, then correlates capacity with that number per family.

Datasets: Queued on all 41 datasets: submit_everything.sh:207-213 lists every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis. run_dataset.py:209-214 calls complexity run_all with no config, so run_all builds its own (complexity_helpers.py:942-954). c06 returns 'skipped' on any dataset whose task_type is not regression (c06:191-196). A tiny import of the registry (dataset_policy.py:230) this session gave 26 regression datasets: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. The other 15 are classification and c06 records a skip there. Of the 26, four have no augmentation representations (abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd); the other 22 do.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Each search has one downstream model: one capacity setting of one family. The families are RF, kNN, DNN, Lasso, XGBoost, SVM and GP, four settings each, up to 28 searches per dataset. They run on all 26 regression datasets. The only cuts are size and skip gates from _resolve_models, e.g. GP above 1,000 rows. lightgbm is not a family, so it is never a downstream model here. kNN and Lasso are downstream models on every dataset.

Decisions: Step 1 allows each dataset's two approved models only, and says knn is not allowed as a downstream model anywhere. c06 differs from that in three ways at once: it fits five or more unapproved families per dataset, it fits knn as a downstream model, and it fits Lasso, which no pair includes. On abcov_kd, buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_acsins, qm9 and suzuki one approved model is lightgbm, which c06 never fits. The comparison across families is the experiment's question, so restricting it to two families is a decision for her.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Each c06 search runs on every row of the dataset, with the engine's 5-fold split inside it. For each budget, c06 takes best_by_model_budget: the configuration with the highest mean over those 5 folds. It reports that same mean, and its per-fold scores, as the result. The optimal budget is the argmax over those means. Within a fold the hybrid is fitted on that fold's training rows. But the recipe for every fold is chosen by the scores of all five held-out folds.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only. In c06 the score reported for fold k comes from a recipe picked using fold k's own held-out score. There is no outer fold whose rows the search never saw.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: Every search uses speed='fast' on every dataset (c06:96, 485). Budgets are the 8 FULL_BUDGETS, 10 to 2000 features, from run_all's config. Evaluators are the fast list rf, match, dnn, lightgbm with match replaced by the family's own model. Allocation (Step 4): ddg_combined cuts power_2, which c06 runs. suzuki is held, and c06 runs performance_weighted and power_2 there. Most full datasets keep softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2, which c06 never runs. Evaluators (Step 5): c06 runs cut evaluators on abagym_EGFR (rf), abagym_VEGF (rf, lightgbm, dnn), buchwald_hartwig (dnn), ginkgo_colloidal (dnn) and ginkgo_titer (lightgbm). Augmentation (Step 8): on 20 of the 22 augmented regression datasets c06 runs only the uncapped condition, which is cut there. On ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic uncapped is kept for the distance search; for a search like this one it is open. Because c06 reports the optimal budget, the decided budget range changes what it measures. That trade is hers.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: Per capacity setting and per budget it keeps one hybrid: the best configuration at that budget. It never reads or reports base representations. The search computes them, but c06 reads only best_by_model_budget. The output is the score per budget, the optimal budget, and a Spearman correlation between capacity and optimal budget per family.

Decisions: Two best base representations and two best hybrids per approved model per fold. c06 measures where the score peaks over budgets for each capacity setting, so one hybrid per budget is its unit. Two base representations have no role in that question as written.

### R6 missing search: yes

Code: c06 builds its own 28 searches under tier 'c06_variant'. The cold-search refusal applies only to tiers 'general' and 'general_distance', so these searches are never refused. A failed search is recorded with budget None and the loop continues. The extra get_precomputed_search call is tier 'general' and can be refused; c06 catches that and rebuilds importance scores per fold inside its own searches.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment, not refused or skipped. c06 never refuses its own search. What it builds is over all rows, not per fold; that fault is under R2.

### Other problems

- On the 22 regression datasets with augmentation representations, c06 searches only 'uncapped' (c06:311). It never runs 'none' there, so every optimal budget includes the augmentation features in the pool.
- The docstring of _family_evaluators says the fast list is ['rf', 'match'] and the RF family searches ['rf'] alone (c06:102-104). The comment above it (c06:91-92) and FAST_INTERNAL_EVALUATORS (find_best_hybrid.py:3063) give ['rf', 'match', 'dnn', 'lightgbm']. The code follows the latter; the docstring is wrong.
- The comment at c06:366-368 says c06 runs 1 fold with no --mode flag. That is true when the file is run directly (get_config, _shared.py:9330). Under run_all, the path the cluster uses, it runs 5 folds (complexity_helpers.py:948).
- run_all's start-up general search passes a pruning schedule from pruning_mode (complexity_helpers.py:1078). c06's get_precomputed_search call forces adaptive_pruning=False and passes no schedule (_shared.py:5884). Could not determine whether both map to the same stored search. If not, and KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is unset, a whole-dataset general search may be built inside c06 only to supply importance scores.
- c06 sets speed='fast' on all 26 regression datasets itself (c06:96). It does not consult FAST_SPEED_DATASETS, so the 21 datasets that are full-tier in both code and DECISIONS also run the fast grid.
- The per-budget winner is the best of 18 or 24 configurations (3 allocation methods x 1 importance method x 3 or 4 evaluators x 2 representation counts) by its 5-fold mean. c06 reports that same mean, so each heatmap cell is the maximum of 18 or 24 noisy means, and the optimal budget is an argmax over those maxima.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3/R1, start-up searches in every c06 process: the cluster runs each experiment as its own python process (submit_dataset.sh:52-59, 448-449). Each process goes through run_all, which first runs or reads two whole-dataset searches (complexity_helpers.py:1065-1114). The general one uses FULL_BUDGETS, the engine's default grid, the five default models and augmentation 'none', 'uncapped' and 'capped' (_shared.py:5543-5550). The distance one uses DISTANCE_MODELS including knn as a downstream model, and DISTANCE_BUDGETS. Neither applies Steps 1-8. c06 reads neither result, but the audit's R3 covered only c06's own grid.
- R3, representation count: c06 never runs counts 2 or 5 (find_best_hybrid.py:3071 FAST_REP_COUNTS [3, None]). On datasets that keep every count, including abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, bh_doyle_plates, flab_expression_adams, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_titer, logd and suzuki (DECISIONS.md:570-603), c06 omits two kept counts. The audit named only the cut count 3.
- R3, allocation: logd's decided allocation set equals c06's fast list (DECISIONS.md:395). The audit's statement that most full-tier datasets keep softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2 is right, but logd is an exception. qm9 is the other match.
- R6 (marked follows, confirmed): c06's own searches use tier 'c06_variant', which is not in _PRECOMPUTE_TIER_ROOTS ('general', 'general_distance'; find_best_hybrid.py:598, 601-605). So _refuse_cold_search returns early (find_best_hybrid.py:651-652) and c06 builds each search itself. Only the importance read through get_precomputed_search (tier 'general') can be refused. c06 catches that (c06:390-391) and the importance scores are then rebuilt per fold inside each search.


## complexity c07 (tests/experiments/complexity/c07_data_complexity_partitions.py)

What it measures: For each of four ways of splitting a dataset into an easy half and a hard half, c07 searches each half separately and asks whether the winning hybrid configuration (model, budget, importance method) differs between the halves.

Datasets: All 41 datasets in DATASET_REPS except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:213). The complexity job runs c07 because c07 is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (complexity_helpers.py:855) and in RUN_ORDER (submit_dataset.sh:312). c07 has no dataset filter of its own. Inside the file, datasets over 2,000 rows are cut to about 2,000 rows by drawing whole scaffold groups with seed 42 (c07:171-195). This cut applies to the per-half searches only. The all-rows pass at c07:124-146 runs before the cut. A half with fewer than 50 molecules is skipped (c07:289-291). The molecular_complexity split is skipped when there are no SMILES, e.g. on antibody datasets (c07:211-213). The _shared.py:533-543 comment says c07 is skipped above 5,000 rows. c07 never reads LARGE_DATASET_N, so it is not skipped.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Each half gets two searches of its own. The general search scores the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm (c07:363, own_search_kwargs at _shared.py:799, list at _shared.py:565). The distance search scores the same five (c07:436-438). knn is left out because DOWNSTREAM_MODELS has no knn. Neither search scores gp. The all-rows pass reads hybrids for rf, svm, lightgbm and dnn (c07:124). It reads none for xgboost or gp. The headline winner for each half is the best of all five models (c07:392-402). top3_base_reps is ranked for rf on every dataset (c07:365; extract_top3_base_reps defaults to model='rf', _shared.py:867). No ridge or knn is scored anywhere.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two models from Step 1. knn is a downstream model only in the distance search (Step 9). ridge is never used.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: c07 has no outer folds. Its hybrids come from two places. First, the all-rows pass calls get_rule_hybrids with no fold index (c07:126-133). It ranks recipes by their mean over every fold of the whole-dataset search (_shared.py:7082-7084, 6746-6748). Those recipes are then rebuilt on each half's own folds with build_fold_hybrid (c07:542-551). When a recipe uses fewer representations than the pool, build_fold_hybrid picks them with blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5260-5262). Those scores also come from the whole-dataset search. c07's own comment says these scores are not held out (c07:107-113). Second, each half's own search uses every row of that half (c07:349-364, 440-452). The winner, the top-2 sets and the three-hybrid set are all picked on the mean over all of that half's folds. The same scores are then reported as the result (c07:394-411, select_model_rep_pairs default rule='whole_dataset' at _shared.py:8357, top_hybrids default rule='whole_dataset' at _shared.py:7876). fold_reselection inputs come from that same search (c07:466, 580). Leaving out one fold's scores does not leave out that fold's rows.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: Each half's two searches use the fast grid on all 41 datasets (own_search_kwargs, _shared.py:798-803). That grid has importance lightgbm_gain only, three allocation methods (performance_weighted, power_2, rank_exp_d0.3) and representation counts 3 and all (find_best_hybrid.py:3071-3072, 3674). The general search uses evaluators rf, match, dnn and lightgbm (find_best_hybrid.py:3063). The general search uses all eight budgets in FULL_BUDGETS, 10 to 2,000 features (c07:90, 351; complexity_helpers.py:952; _shared.py:494). The distance search uses evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm (c07:439, _shared.py:502). It uses the six DISTANCE_BUDGETS, 10 to 500 features (c07:442, _shared.py:495). Both searches use 'capped' augmentation whenever the dataset has augmentation representations (c07:335, 353, 444). 32 of the 41 datasets have them; all but nine (printed this session). Pruning comes from PRUNING_MODE, default calibrated (_shared.py:804). It can drop more methods during each search. The all-rows pass reads the whole-dataset searches that complexity run_all builds (complexity_helpers.py:1069-1080, 1096-1114). Those searches use FULL_BUDGETS and the engine defaults, or the fast grid on 14 datasets. Their augmentation settings are none, uncapped and capped (_shared.py:6014-6046). Nothing applies a cut from Steps 2 to 8 for a particular dataset.

Decisions: Every search uses the dataset's decided budget range (Step 2 v3, Step 7) and importance methods (Step 3 v2, Step 7). It uses the decided allocation methods (Step 4, suzuki held) and evaluators (Step 5 v3, Step 7). It uses the decided representation counts (Step 6, Step 7) and augmentation (Step 8). The fast grid is the decided grid only on the 10 fast-tier datasets.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c07 builds its own searches for each half in the job. They pass own_search=True, so KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH never refuses them (_shared.py:798; find_best_hybrid.py:9355-9369). c07 never asks for or builds a search on one fold's training rows. The all-rows pass reads the whole-dataset searches. If one is missing, get_precomputed_search builds it on every row (_shared.py:5863-5896). Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, which is the default in submit_everything.sh (lines 94 and 364), a search with more than 500 configurations left to score is refused instead (find_best_hybrid.py:705-716). The refusal is caught, a warning is printed, and that augmentation setting is skipped (_shared.py:6108-6114). The empty places are written to rule_missing (c07:134-140). An exception from a half's own search is printed and that half gets no winner (c07:422-425, 453-455).

Decisions: If a needed search for a fold does not exist, the experiment builds it itself. No refusal and no skip with a warning.

### Other problems

- R1 by dataset: on every dataset, c07's own searches score three models outside the approved pair. On abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, gp is approved and c07 never scores it. Those five lose one approved model and gain four unapproved ones. The all-rows pass reads no xgboost hybrids. Nine approved pairs include xgboost: abcov_kd, cdr_flexibility, flab_binding_adams, herg, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass. So on those nine the all-rows pass covers one approved model, not two (c07:124).
- R3 importance: c07's own searches use lightgbm_gain only. On buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer, Step 3 cut lightgbm_gain. So on those four c07 searches only the importance method the record cut, and none it kept (DECISIONS.md:314, 316, 327, 328).
- R3 importance on the other full datasets: Step 3 keeps deeplift or treeshap there, and c07 runs neither. logd matches; its record cuts deeplift and treeshap. The 10 fast-tier datasets also match.
- R3 allocation: c07 runs three methods. It runs power_2 on ddg_combined, which Step 4 cut. On suzuki it runs power_2 and performance_weighted, which are held. It lacks softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2 on every full dataset that keeps them.
- R3 representation counts: c07 runs count 3 everywhere. Step 6 cuts 3 on 15 datasets: adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_koenig, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, herg_ki, kiba and nt_promoter_tata. On buchwald_hartwig, c07 runs 3 and all, both of which are cut. It lacks 2, the only kept count.
- R3 evaluators, general search: c07 runs evaluators that Step 5 v3 cut. These are rf on abagym_EGFR; rf, lightgbm and dnn on abagym_VEGF; dnn on buchwald_hartwig and ginkgo_colloidal; and lightgbm on ginkgo_titer.
- R3 evaluators, distance search: c07 runs knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm everywhere. Step 7 cuts at least one of these on 11 datasets: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ddg_combined, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_titer and qm9.
- R3 budgets: only humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc keep all eight general budgets (DECISIONS.md:235, 247). Every other dataset gets budgets Step 2 v3 cut. On the distance search, the same two keep all six budgets. Every other dataset gets budgets Step 7 cut. c07 also builds a distance search on bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg. DECISIONS has no distance row for those three.
- R3 augmentation: both of each half's searches run 'capped' only on the 32 datasets with augmentation representations (c07:335). Step 8 cuts all augmented searches on 30 of those. ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic keep uncapped only. So c07 runs the setting the record cut and never the one it kept. On those 32 datasets, no search for a half runs without augmentation.
- The all-rows pass and the halves' own searches differ in three ways at once. First, the grid: the all-rows recipes come from the full engine grid, or fast on 14 datasets, while the halves use the fast grid on all 41. Second, augmentation: the all-rows recipes may use none, uncapped or capped, while the halves use capped only. Third, the rows: the all-rows recipes saw the halves' held-out rows.
- The second pass discards every error without a record: `except Exception: pass` (c07:567-568). A recipe that fails to rebuild on a half leaves no score and no reason.
- The second pass also skips any recipe whose budget is above the half's row count, without a record (c07:506-507).
- The comment at c07:162-170 says the half searches are 'uncached', but both pass cache=True (c07:357, 448). The comment at _shared.py:533-543 says c07 is skipped above 5,000 rows. c07 actually cuts the dataset to about 2,000 rows (c07:171).
- Pruning for each half's searches comes from the PRUNING_MODE environment variable (_shared.py:804). submit_everything.sh exports calibrated (line 85). submit_dataset.sh defaults its own PRUNING_MODE to aggressive_pruning (line 102). Unverified this session: whether submit_dataset.sh exports that value to the python process when it runs on its own.

- R1, all-rows pass: the first agent counted only the nine datasets whose approved pair includes xgboost. ## complexity c08 (tests/experiments/complexity/c08_calibration.py)

What it measures: For each held-out fold it measures how well conformal 90% prediction intervals (regression) or prediction sets (classification) cover the true labels, at the searched budget, a too-small budget, full width, and full width with a linear model.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. c08 is in the complexity list (complexity_helpers.py:856) and in submit_dataset.sh RUN_ORDER (submit_dataset.sh:312), after c02 (submit_dataset.sh:319). submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:207-213, 95). complexity run_all has no dataset skip for c08 (grep of complexity_helpers.py finds no should_skip_experiment call).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: c08 fits up to eight model types on every dataset. The 'conditions' block uses one model: the best of five from c02's file, or the best of rf, svm, lightgbm, dnn from the stored search (knn is listed but never found there; xgboost is not tried). The rule block fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm and knn, one per downstream model. The 'mismatched' condition fits Ridge(alpha=0.01) on regression and LogisticRegression on classification. gp is never fitted. The hardcoded fallback is RandomForest.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two Step 1 models. Step 1 says knn is not allowed as a downstream model; Step 9 allows knn only in the distance search for s02, s05, s06, s08, s10, s13 and the OPIG census. ridge is excluded everywhere.

### Other problems

- On the c02 path, the 'optimal' rebuild differs from c02's winner in two ways at once. c02 stores model, allocation, importance and budget only (c02_complexity_grid.py:402-410). c08 then uses internal evaluator 'match' (c08:101) and all 10 representations (c08:116-120). The winner may have used another evaluator and 2, 3 or 5 representations.
- The two recipe paths pick from different model lists. The c02 path ranks five models (c02:398). The pool path ranks rf, svm, lightgbm, dnn and knn (c08:151); knn is never in the general search and xgboost is never asked for.
- The hardcoded fallback recipe uses treeshap (c08:97). On the 10 fast-tier datasets DECISIONS keeps lightgbm_gain only, so the fallback builds a method the record says not to run.
- The 'mismatched' condition fits Ridge(alpha=0.01) or LogisticRegression on every dataset (c08:236-241). ridge is excluded everywhere under R1.
- Underfit is built at min(25, total features/4) and overfit at the total feature count (c08:246-253). Neither budget was searched; on most datasets 25 is below the Step 2 range.
- The printed summary table reads results['conditions'] only (c08:766-785). The rule-hybrid conditions are saved but never printed.
- Each fold's representation choice uses whole-dataset scores. When rep_count is below 10, c08 keeps the top rep_count by blueprint.rep_scores (c08:356-361). find_best_hybrid fills rep_scores from baselines over every row (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593).
- Under submit_dataset.sh each experiment runs in its own process (submit_dataset.sh:448-449, per the helper map, not re-opened). So c08's process repeats both whole-dataset start-up searches before c08 starts (complexity_helpers.py:1065-1114).
- Unused imports: find_best_hybrid, INTERNAL_EVALUATORS and FULL_BUDGETS are imported (c08:21, 24) and never used in the file.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- c08 picks a different set of representations from the search it copies, separate from the leak. The search keeps the top N representations ranked by that fold's allocation scores (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:4963-4982). c08 keeps the top N by blueprint.rep_scores (c08_calibration.py:356-361). Those are each representation's best baseline across all models, over every row (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9585). So when the recipe used 2, 3 or 5 representations, c08 can rebuild it on a different subset.
- c08 builds augmented features itself, not only reads augmented searches. On the c02 path, optimal_aug_strategy is 'uncapped' whenever augmentation representations exist (c08_calibration.py:103). It is passed to create_hybrid per fold (c08_calibration.py:368-369). The rule block passes each hybrid's aug_condition, which can be uncapped or capped (c08_calibration.py:750). Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 datasets (DECISIONS.md:658-698).
- Allocation methods on the four datasets the code runs fast that the record does not treat as fast. The fast grid has performance_weighted, power_2 and rank_exp_d0.3 only (find_best_hybrid.py:3072). Step 4 keeps softmax_T1 on flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd, and wglobal_power2 on bindingdb_kd (DECISIONS.md:379, 387, 398). The report lists the importance mismatch on these datasets but not this one.
- On rule hybrids that used fewer than 10 representations, the overfit and mismatched conditions still ask for total_dim features (c08_calibration.py:740-745). total_dim is summed over all 10 representations (c08_calibration.py:75). The kept subset has fewer features, so the width built is smaller than the budget asked for. condition_widths_built records the width built (c08_calibration.py:387-388, 762), but no warning is printed.
- convert_numpy is also imported and never used (c08_calibration.py:18), alongside the three unused imports the report names.


## complexity c09 (tests/experiments/complexity/c09_formal_analysis.py)

What it measures: For each feature budget, it measures the hybrid's information about the labels, how much of all features it retains, its effective rank, and its train-to-validation gap; it also splits c02's grid scores by model and budget (ANOVA).

Datasets: All 41 datasets in the roster. submit_everything.sh builds the roster from every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213). It queues the complexity category on each (submit_everything.sh:95, 350-374). c09 is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (tests/experiments/complexity/complexity_helpers.py:857). complexity run_all never calls should_skip_experiment (a grep of complexity_helpers.py finds no call), so no dataset is skipped. submit_dataset.sh runs c09 after c02 and c06 (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:319). A python import printed 41 datasets this session.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every recipe c09 uses was chosen by a search over all rows. The single recipes in 9b, 9c and 9d come from get_best_search_for_downstream, which reads the whole-dataset pool and labels its choice 'whole_dataset'. The rule hybrids come from get_rule_hybrids with fold_i=None, which ranks on the mean over all folds of the whole-dataset search. c09 then refits the features on each fold's training rows. So the features are fitted per fold, but the allocation method, importance method, internal evaluator and augmentation condition were chosen with every fold's rows. 9d writes val_score_is_held_out=False for this reason. The ANOVA observations are c02's selection scores from its own whole-dataset search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search on that fold's training rows only.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c09 never builds a per-fold search. When a whole-dataset search is missing, two things happen. Without KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, get_precomputed_search builds it on all rows inside the job. With it set (the submit_everything.sh default), a search with more than 500 configurations left is refused. The pool reader prints a warning and skips that member. If no member is left, get_best_search_for_downstream returns (None, None). c09 then builds the hybrid from fixed engine defaults and marks it from_fallback. A missing rule hybrid is only listed in rule_missing.

Decisions: If a per-fold search does not exist, the experiment builds it itself.

### Other problems

- Representation count is dropped in every rebuild. A recipe searched on 2, 3 or 5 representations is rebuilt over all of them. c09 never reads blueprint.rep_count or calls restrict_to_rep_count (grep, no hits). create_hybrid has no rep_count parameter (grep of src/kirby/hybrid.py, no hits). The Blueprint field says a rebuild without it uses different features (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:1523-1530). So the hybrid c09 measures can differ from the one the search picked.
- Internal evaluator 'match' is built as lightgbm in all three sub-analyses. 9b and 9c record this (c09:599-608, 825-834). 9d does not record it. evaluate_cv_with_train passes no model to create_hybrid (tests/experiments/_shared.py:2728-2739), so 'match' becomes lightgbm (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5891-5892).
- Rule hybrids are rebuilt at the requested budget, not the budget they were ranked at. The distance read stops at 500 features. At 1000 and 2000 features it ranks over the budgets it holds (tests/experiments/_shared.py:6855-6872). c09 still builds at 1000 or 2000 (c09:632-633, 864-866, 1107-1111). It records budget_relaxed beside the number (c09:641, 874, 1129).
- The no-search fallback differs between sub-analyses. 9b and 9c use internal evaluator rf (c09:598, 824). 9d uses lightgbm (c09:1055-1056). So two curves at the same budget can be built under different evaluators.
- 9b, 9c and 9d pass no data= to get_best_search_for_downstream (c09:563-568, 789-794, 1035-1040). They skip the in-memory searches run_all built and read from disk with adaptive_pruning=False (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5889). run_all built those searches with its pruning schedule (complexity_helpers.py:1078). Pruning is not in the stored-search identity (src/kirby/result_cache.py:46-60). Could not determine whether the stored rows satisfy an unpruned read, or whether the read is refused and falls back to engine defaults.
- 9a computes F statistics and p-values for model, budget and their interaction (c09:346-353). The memory index records a rule of no significance tests. That rule is a dated memory claim, not checked against DECISIONS.md.
- 9c compares hybrid, PCA and random effective ranks at different widths, as its own comment says (c09:844-851). It prints a warning but the rank difference still mixes in a width difference.
- 9c swallows every hybrid build failure and random-subset failure with a bare pass (c09:766-767, 909-910). A fold dropped there shrinks the mean with no record.
- run_all's distance search scores knn on all 41 datasets, including the six nucleotide ones (complexity_helpers.py:1111). Step 9 says knn is not needed there (DECISIONS.md:726, 738-742). c09 reads that search but never asks for knn.

If refused, the slot is only listed in rule_missing (c09:57-61). Whether it is refused depends on how many configurations would be left, which could not be determined without the result database.

## complexity c11 (tests/experiments/complexity/c11_ensemble_vs_hybrid.py)

What it measures: For each downstream model, it compares the held-out score of one model on a searched hybrid with ensembles that average the predictions of one model per representation. It also reports what each needs at deployment.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. c11 is in the complexity default list (complexity_helpers.py:862). submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:211-213, :95). A tiny import printed 41 names this session. complexity run_all has no dataset skip; a grep of complexity_helpers.py for should_skip finds nothing. The launcher default is --c11-recipe-search per_fold (run_dataset.py:95-96; complexity_helpers.py:917, 1235-1236), and no submit script passes another value.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every arm is fitted for each model in config['models']. On every dataset that is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. svm is dropped above 10,000 rows. gp is never in the list. Both per-fold searches score the same five; the distance search scores knn only as an internal evaluator, not as a downstream model. The ensemble_s2 arm lets each representation pick whichever of the five scored best. extract_top3_base_reps reads rf.

Decisions: Two models per dataset (Step 1). For example: herg_ki svm+dnn, buchwald_hartwig rf+lightgbm, abagym_Ang2 gp+svm. knn is not a downstream model here.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Under the default per_fold setting, each outer fold runs its own general and distance searches on that fold's training rows. The recipe at each budget for that fold comes from those searches. The hybrid is then fitted on the fold's training rows. Two later choices are not made inside the fold. First, the budget for held-out fold k and the best single representation for fold k are picked by fold_reselection. It uses the mean of the other outer folds' held-out scores, and those folds' models were trained on rows that include fold k. Second, the best_single arm and its top2_reps are ranked directly by the mean held-out score over all outer folds. Under --recipe-search whole_data, the recipe comes from the whole-dataset search. That setting is not the launcher default.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search on that fold's training rows only.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per model, per fold, at each budget, it builds three hybrids: general1 (the best general configuration), general2 (the next best) and distance1 (the best distance configuration). This is the 2026-10-02 rule of 2 general hybrids and 1 distance hybrid. The budget is then re-picked per fold by fold_reselection. For base representations it fits every representation on every fold. It reports one best per fold (fold_reselection) and one best overall by held-out mean, plus a top2_reps list ranked by held-out mean. The ensemble, PCA and oracle arms are by design; the oracle reads the held-out fold, and the file labels it an upper bound. The top2_base_reps, top2_hybrids and top2_pairs_by_model keys read one fold's search only.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. c11 gives 3 hybrids, not 2. It picks 1 base representation per fold, not 2.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c11 calls find_best_hybrid itself for each fold and is meant to build its searches. But it passes the plain dataset name and tier 'general' or 'general_distance', and no own_search. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH the refusal therefore applies. submit_everything.sh turns that on by default. The refusal raises when under 50% is stored and more than 500 configurations are left. One general fold search per augmentation condition is 8,160 configurations: 17 model-evaluator pairs x 5 x 3 x 8 x 4. One distance fold search is 9,000: 25 pairs x 5 x 3 x 6 x 4. c11 catches the error, prints 'recipe search failed' and carries on. That fold's hybrid scores NaN. If every fold fails, it prints 'hybrid arm empty' and writes only ensemble and single-representation results. A missing general1 recipe is printed, not added to rule_missing.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search is built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- The hybrid side and the ensemble side of the head-to-head choose things in two different ways. The self-contained ensemble picks its representation set and aggregator on an inner CV inside the fold's training rows (c11:1294-1320). The hybrid's budget per fold is picked from the other outer folds' held-out scores (c11:1361, 1514; _shared.py:1632-1700). The file's own docstring says that second pattern leaks (c11:31-35). So auto_minus_hybrid compares an in-fold choice against a cross-fold choice.
- The distance1 hybrid at general budgets 1000 and 2000 is not built at those budgets. The distance searches stop at 500, so c11 takes the best distance configuration at any budget (c11:676-680). build_fold_hybrid then builds it at blueprint.budget (_shared.py:5288), since no budget_override is passed (c11:1029-1035). The rows hybrid_distance1_b1000 and _b2000 repeat a lower-budget recipe under a higher budget's name. The rows record this in budget_relaxed_folds (c11:1096-1098).
- On the five datasets whose approved pair includes gp (abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho), c11 never fits gp. So one of the two approved models is absent from every arm (complexity_helpers.py:953; _shared.py:565).
- Under the default per_fold setting, complexity run_all still builds or reads two whole-dataset searches before c11 starts (complexity_helpers.py:1065-1114). c11 does not read them.
- top2_base_reps, top2_hybrids and top2_pairs_by_model come from one fold's search only, whichever was assigned to last_search last (c11:640, 1675-1678). top3_base_reps uses rf whatever the dataset's pair (c11:1661; _shared.py:867).
- A fold with no general1 recipe is only printed (c11:796, 1011-1012). It is not added to rule_missing, so the result file does not say why a general1 hybrid arm has fewer folds.
- Could not determine: whether c11's outer folds from cv_split (c11:418-419) are the same splits as nested_cv_outer_folds (find_best_hybrid.py:10387-10411). If they differ, a per-fold warm-up under the same ocv namespace would store searches for different training rows than the ones c11 asks for.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3, four datasets the first agent did not name. On each, the decision says 'keep all stored methods' but the stored search held fewer methods than the engine default. c11 runs the full defaults, so it adds methods that were never stored. logd: softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2 (DECISIONS.md:395). kiba: wglobal_power2 (DECISIONS.md:393). flab_expression_koenig: wglobal_power2 (DECISIONS.md:382). flab_expression_adams: deeplift importance (DECISIONS.md:317). c11 passes no allocation or importance list (c11:504-534), so defaults apply (find_best_hybrid.py:8651-8659).
- R3/R1, the distance search's downstream models. Step 7 says the distance search's downstream models are the decided pair (DECISIONS.md:607). c11's distance search scores all five run models (c11:485, 507). This is the R1 fault again, applied to the distance search.
- R3, could not determine. Step 7 lists the distance evaluators as knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm, 'and a model's own type where it was downstream' (DECISIONS.md:609). c11's distance evaluators have no 'match' entry (_shared.py:502, c11:509), so xgboost and gp are never scored as their own evaluator there. I could not tell whether the stored distance searches scored them.
- R6, the whole-dataset searches as well. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, the two whole-dataset searches that run_all starts before c11 are general and general_distance tiers too (complexity_helpers.py:1069-1114). So they meet the same refusal. Not verified: whether precompute_hybrid_searches catches that refusal or stops the process.


## complexity c12 (tests/experiments/complexity/c12_modality_ablation.py)

What it measures: For each pair of omics modalities, and for all modalities together, it measures whether placing one representation from each modality side by side at full width scores better than the best single representation.

Datasets: The two TCGA datasets, tcga_brca_pam50 and tcga_luad_vs_lusc. complexity run_all adds c12 only for a dataset whose name starts with tcga_ (complexity_helpers.py:958-961). submit_dataset.sh does the same when it builds its own list (submit_dataset.sh:322-323). c12 itself raises on any dataset whose domain is not 'tcga' (c12_modality_ablation.py:707-711). Under run_all it sees only the dataset's 10 'general' representations (complexity_helpers.py:471-496, 971, 1036-1039).

### R1 models: NO

Code: It fits every model in config['models']. Under run_all that is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. Both TCGA datasets are classification, so get_clf_model_factories builds rf, xgboost and lightgbm from its own catalog and svm and dnn from find_best_hybrid.get_model. ridge is refused by name and knn is never asked for. The HELPS/HURTS label is read from the mean delta over all five models.

Decisions: Step 1: tcga_brca_pam50 uses dnn+svm only; tcga_luad_vs_lusc uses lightgbm+xgboost only. Both datasets break the rule. tcga_brca_pam50 gets three extra models: rf, xgboost and lightgbm. tcga_luad_vs_lusc gets three extra models: rf, svm and dnn.

### R2 per fold: -

Code: c12 builds no hybrid and reads no search. Every model is fitted on one fold's training rows, after a StandardScaler fitted on those rows. For held-out fold f, each modality's representation is chosen by its mean score over the other folds, per model. The comparison single representation is chosen the same way. The other folds' models were trained on rows that include fold f's rows. So fold f's labels do enter the choice, through training, but fold f's own scores do not.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows. c12 uses no hybrid, so the rule has nothing to apply to.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: No hybrids. For each model and each held-out fold, it takes one representation per modality: the one best on the other folds. It places those side by side at full width and scores them on the held-out fold. This is done for every pair of modalities and once for all modalities together. The comparison is one single representation, re-picked the same way. Every representation is scored on every fold for every model. The design was decided on 2026-09-12 and is recorded in the file.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### Other problems

- c12 itself calls no search. Neither the file nor its imports (get_config, create_experiment_parser, save_experiment_results, get_model_factories, cv_split, fold_reselection) run find_best_hybrid (c12_modality_ablation.py:66-71). Under submit_dataset.sh, each experiment runs in its own process through run_all. So the two whole-dataset start-up searches above are built or read on every c12 run, and c12 uses neither.
- The HELPS/HURTS label for each modality pair is the mean of the per-model deltas over all five models (c12:124-126, 1079-1081, 1131-1133). It is not a per-model result. On each TCGA dataset, three of those five models are not the dataset's two approved models.
- The two entry points load different representations. run_all keeps only the 10 'general' representations and drops augmentation-only ones (complexity_helpers.py:1036-1039). On tcga_brca_pam50 this leaves no methylation, mutation, immune or clinical representations. The standalone __main__ path loads whatever preset --reps names (c12:1321-1327). The docstring lists nine modalities (c12:24-41). Under run_all, tcga_brca_pam50 has at most five active modalities: expression, rppa, cnv, wsi and mirna (complexity_helpers.py:490-492).
- The output still stores numbers that pick over all folds and over all models: score_mean, delta_vs_a/b, delta_vs_best_single, and best_rep_per_modality (c12:813-823, 874-896, 974-991). They are printed as 'Δbest' in phase 2 (c12:943). The file's own comment says these have no honest direction (c12:1061-1063).
- The final 'HONEST PER-MODEL RE-SCORE' table prints r['delta'], a difference of two means (c12:1211). It does not print delta_mean_of_folds, the paired per-fold mean (_shared.py:1948-1949). The two differ when either side has a NaN fold. The pair-level deltas do use delta_mean_of_folds (c12:115).
- In the honest block, fold_reselection runs a second leave-one-fold-out pick on top of the first. Its candidates are each combination's fold scores, and each of those scores is already a representation re-picked on the other folds (c12:1155-1200). The single representation side is picked once, from every representation of every modality (c12:1177-1182). Not checked: whether picking at two levels on one side and one level on the other changes the comparison.
- c12's lightgbm classifier uses n_jobs=-1 (c12:504-505). The engine's lightgbm classifier uses lgbm_n_jobs() (find_best_hybrid.py:2544-2546). So KIRBY_LGBM_THREADS does not reach c12's lightgbm fits. rf and xgboost use the same settings as the engine's (find_best_hybrid.py:2722-2727, 2520-2524). xgboost adds only eval_metric='logloss'.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3 budgets, tcga_brca_pam50: the decision is 25-2000 for the general search (DECISIONS.md:246) and 25-500 for the distance search (DECISIONS.md:647). run_all's searches use FULL_BUDGETS and DISTANCE_BUDGETS, and both include 10 (_shared.py:494-495; complexity_helpers.py:950, 1092). c12 does not read them, but they run in c12's process (complexity_helpers.py:1059-1114).
- R3 augmentation (Step 8): both TCGA datasets are 'cut (no augmented searches)' (DECISIONS.md:695-696). Both TCGA datasets have augmentation lists (complexity_helpers.py:480-483, 493-495), so run_all builds data['augmentations'] (complexity_helpers.py:1023-1043). precompute_hybrid_searches then adds uncapped and capped searches on both tiers (_shared.py:5543-5549). That is four augmented whole-dataset searches per TCGA dataset that the record says are cut.
- R1 in run_all's general search: models is not passed (complexity_helpers.py:1069-1080), so the engine default list is fitted (find_best_hybrid.py:8701-8711). That is not the dataset's two approved models (DECISIONS.md:48-49). The distance search's six models with knn are allowed by Step 9 (DECISIONS.md:745-746).
- R1 also applies to the standalone __main__ path: get_config defaults models to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS (_shared.py:9350), so c12 run by hand fits all five unless --models is given (_shared.py:9368-9369).


## complexity c13 (tests/experiments/complexity/c13_forward_compatibility.py)

What it measures: For each learned embedding model, it measures how much a hybrid gains when that representation is added, against the same hybrid with a random-Gaussian matrix of the same width added instead.

Datasets: Every dataset complexity run_all is launched on. c13 is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (tests/experiments/complexity/complexity_helpers.py:863) and in the complexity RUN_ORDER (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:313). submit_everything.sh takes every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213); a tiny import this session printed 41 names. c13 has no dataset filter of its own. On a dataset where no representation is a learned embedding model and no candidate loads, it returns error 'no_embedding_models' (c13:1177-1195). Which of the 41 actually produce subjects could not be determined without loading each dataset's representations. Above 5,000 rows it runs on a random 2,000-row subsample (c13:1068-1080; _shared.py:544-545).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Condition A and both controls fit the first model in config['models'], which is rf on every dataset. Condition B fits all five of rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on the subject alone. Every hybrid condition (C, D, D_random and the side-2 three) is searched for and scored with condition B's single winner. Each search also scores gp on 9 small datasets, but c13 never reads a gp recipe. ridge and knn are never fitted.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models. Example: herg_ki is svm+dnn, but c13 also fits rf, xgboost and lightgbm, and the hybrids may use any of the five. On abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, gp is one of the two approved models and is never a downstream model here. rf is fitted for condition A on all 41 datasets; it is approved on only 8 (bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, humanness_therapeutic, kiba, suzuki). Every dataset breaks the rule.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per subject, c13 uses one downstream model, the condition-B winner on the subject alone. For each hybrid condition it scores three hybrids: the best general configuration, the second general configuration from the same search, and the best distance configuration. It reports the subject itself as the single-representation side (conditions A and B). It never takes the 2 best base representations.

Decisions: Per each of the dataset's two models, per fold: 2 best base representations and 2 best hybrids. Leaving out the 2 best base representations follows from the design: the comparison is the pool with and without one named representation. Two other departures do not follow from that design. One: one model picked by score, not the two approved models. Two: three hybrids (2 general plus 1 distance, marked 'Owner's set 2026-10-02') where R4 asks for two.

### R6 missing search: yes

Code: Every search c13 asks for carries a condition_suffix. find_best_hybrid appends it to the tier ('general__cond-...' or 'general_distance__cond-...'). That tier is not a precompute tier, so the KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH refusal returns without raising and the search is built in the job. A search that raises for another reason is recorded: the condition scores nan and the reason is printed and stored in models_dropped or rule_missing.

Decisions: A missing search must be built by the experiment, not refused or skipped. c13 does build its own. But what it builds is a whole-row search, not a per-fold one (see R2); no per-fold search exists anywhere in c13.

### Other problems

- Two things disagree about which representations a reduced recipe keeps. The search ranks representations by each inner fold's own scores. The per-fold rebuild ranks them by blueprint.rep_scores, measured over every row, because c13 passes no precomputed_alloc_scores (c13:824-830; _shared.py:5256-5262). So with representation count 3, the held-out rows also help pick which 3 representations are kept.
- A fold whose rebuild raises is dropped with no message (c13:831-832, 'except Exception: continue'). C, D and D_random can then be means over different numbers of folds. Only general2 and distance1 record n_folds_scored (c13:874); general1 does not.
- Condition B picks the best of five models by its mean over the same folds that then score it (c13:1329-1342). D - B subtracts that best-of-five score, so B is selected on the folds it is reported on.
- Above 5,000 rows c13 draws 2,000 rows at random, ignoring groups (c13:1071-1076). The comment at _shared.py:526 gives logd as 5,028 rows, so logd would run on 2,000; I did not count logd's rows this session.
- Condition A and both controls are documented as a linear probe (c13:14-16). With the default model list they fit rf, not a linear model (c13:1297-1302). The stored probe_model says rf, so the number is labelled correctly.
- general2 is the second configuration inside the one winning augmentation condition's search (c13:876, 886). It is not the second best across augmentation conditions.
- Could not determine whether the search's inner folds are the same molecule splits as c13's own evaluation folds. Neither call passes n_folds or a seed to the search (c13:754-762); c13's folds come from cv_split with seed 42 (_shared.py:2114).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3, buchwald_hartwig representation count: Step 6 cuts 3, 5 and all, so only count 2 is kept (DECISIONS.md:572). c13's general search runs only 3 and all (find_best_hybrid.py:3071). So neither count c13 runs is allowed there, and the allowed count is never run. Step 7 makes the same cut on the distance search (DECISIONS.md:622).
- R3, distance-search importance: Step 7 cuts lightgbm_gain on cdr_flexibility and ginkgo_pr_cho (DECISIONS.md:624, 635). c13's distance search runs lightgbm_gain and nothing else (speed='fast', c13:906; find_best_hybrid.py:3674). So on those two datasets the distance search runs only a method the decision removed.
- R3, distance-search allocation: Step 7 cuts performance_weighted, power_2 and wglobal_power2 on ddg_combined (DECISIONS.md:625). c13's distance search runs performance_weighted and power_2 there.
- R3, datasets with no Step 7 decision: bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg have no Step 7 row (DECISIONS.md:609). c13 still runs a distance search on them whenever condition B's winner is in DISTANCE_MODELS (c13:893-907), with no decided grid to follow.
- R6: c13's searches are not refused by KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH. condition_suffix turns the tier into 'general__cond-...' (find_best_hybrid.py:8986-8987), and _is_precompute_tier accepts only the bare roots 'general' and 'general_distance' (find_best_hybrid.py:598-605). These searches are built over all rows, not per fold, so R6's per-fold search is still never built. That is the R2 fault, not a refusal.
- R1, Condition B: the five models are fitted on the subject without the search's svm row cap. find_best_hybrid drops svm above 10,000 rows inside a search (comment at _shared.py:1059-1062). c13's condition B builds svm directly through get_model_factories (c13:1086-1089, 1329-1332). On large datasets the size gate cuts to 2,000 rows first (c13:1071), so this only matters if the gate is off. I did not run it.


## complexity c14 (tests/experiments/complexity/c14_cross_domain_summary.py)

What it measures: For each dataset, it measures how much the best hybrid beats the best single representation on held-out outer folds, then summarises that difference across datasets.

Datasets: Whatever --tasks names; the argument is required (c14:1096-1099, 1109). No per-dataset job runs c14 (cross_one.sh:10-12; grep of complexity_helpers.py finds no 'c14'). The server job x_cross_c14 passes C14_TASKS (submit_all_stages.sh:393, cross_one.sh:60-61). Its default is logd, caco2, herg, flab_thermo_tresanco and tcga_luad_vs_lusc (submit_all_stages.sh:104). Each dataset loads its 10 'general' representations from DATASET_REPS (_shared.py:4047-4057). All five carry an augmentation list (printed this session from DATASET_REPS).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: Both nested CVs score five downstream models on every dataset: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. The single-representation loop in section 1 also fits all five per representation. The headline model is whichever of the five has the best held-out hybrid mean. No ridge, knn or gp is fitted.

Decisions: Two models per dataset. logd, caco2 and flab_thermo_tresanco: dnn+svm. herg and tcga_luad_vs_lusc: lightgbm+xgboost. So every one of the five default datasets gets three models the record excludes. On logd, caco2 and flab_thermo_tresanco those are rf, xgboost and lightgbm. On herg and tcga_luad_vs_lusc they are rf, svm and dnn. The headline model can be one of these three.

### R2 per fold: yes

Code: Every hybrid comes from a search on one outer fold's training rows. nested_cv_evaluate slices to outer-train rows and runs find_best_hybrid there. general1 is that search's winner. general2 is the same search's next-ranked recipe, rebuilt on outer-train rows. distance1 is the winner of a second nested CV on the distance tier. The per-fold single representation is picked from the inner search's own baselines. Two side lists do not follow this; see R4.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: Neither search passes speed, importance methods, allocation methods or representation counts, so the engine's full lists apply on every dataset. That is 3 importance methods, 5 allocation methods and counts 2, 3, 5 and all. General budgets are FULL_BUDGETS, 10 to 2000 (8 budgets). General evaluators are match, rf, lightgbm, dnn. Distance budgets are 10 to 500 (6); distance evaluators are knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm. Every search runs 'uncapped' augmentation only, because all five datasets carry an augmentation list.

Decisions: General search. caco2: budgets 500-2000, cut wglobal_power2, keep only all representations. flab_thermo_tresanco: budgets 50-2000, cut deeplift. herg (fast tier): budgets 100-2000, lightgbm_gain only, three allocation methods, counts 3 and all. logd: budgets 500-2000, lightgbm_gain only, its three stored allocation methods. tcga_luad_vs_lusc: no cut. Distance search: caco2 100-500, cut treeshap, cut counts 2 and 3; flab_thermo_tresanco 50-500, cut deeplift; herg and logd 100-500; tcga_luad_vs_lusc 10-500. Step 8 cuts augmentation on all five. So caco2, flab_thermo_tresanco, herg and logd break the general and distance cuts. tcga_luad_vs_lusc matches on every axis except augmentation. On every dataset the code runs only the augmented search the record cut, and never the unaugmented one it kept. Could not determine which representation counts logd stored.

### R6 missing search: yes

Code: Neither nested_cv_evaluate call passes cache, so find_best_hybrid runs with cache=False. The cold-search refusal only fires when cache is on. So every per-fold search is built inside the job, every run, and none is stored. An inner search that raises is printed, and that outer fold is skipped. If every fold fails, the task is dropped with a warning.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped. The job runs with KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, but that setting has no effect when cache is off.
