### Other problems

- It runs a Wilcoxon signed-rank test across datasets, and within each domain (c14:913-934, 954-960). The memory index records her rule: no significance tests, not across folds and not across datasets.
- It averages the delta and the percent improvement across datasets, overall and per domain (c14:856-866, 945-953). The memory index records a rule against averaging across datasets.
- The summary labels its delta 'against the best single rep scored on its own surviving folds' (c14:867-868). But the numbers it averages are r['delta'] (c14:838), which is the nested CV's paired fold difference (c14:486, 765-766). The label describes a different number.
- The headline hybrid score is the model with the best held-out hybrid mean among five (c14:459-466). That model is picked on the outer test scores it then reports.
- general2 treats two recipes as the same when they differ only in representation count, because its identity leaves rep_count out (c14:70-74). top_hybrids keeps rep_count in its identity (_shared.py:7985-7988). Only the top 3 are inspected (c14:164), so general2 can be missing, or be the third-ranked recipe.
- Section 1 fits every representation with all five models on cv_split folds, and picks the winner on the folds it reports (c14:297-370). Its delta_cf subtracts that number from the nested hybrid mean (c14:502-511). I did not verify that cv_split and nested_cv_outer_folds produce the same fold boundaries.
- Nothing is cached and nothing is saved until the end. cross_one.sh says a cut-off run starts again (cross_one.sh:33). The server job asks for 29 days 23 hours (submit_all_stages.sh:393).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- On herg and logd the 'uncapped' skip policy drops rf from both nested CVs. On herg the 5000-row svm limit also drops svm. So section 1 fits five models and the nested CV fits three (herg) or four (logd). The comment says both arms use the same list. (dataset_policy.py:106,108; find_best_hybrid.py:3083-3085, 3261, 8717-8721; c14:297-298, 457-458)
- On herg and logd, rf is dropped from the nested CV. extract_top3_base_reps(ncv) ranks by rf by default, so top3_base_reps comes back empty on both datasets. (c14:468, 776; _shared.py:867)
- complexity_matching_strength and delta_std average the absolute delta across a domain's datasets. That is a third average across datasets, besides mean_delta and mean_pct_improvement. (c14:966-967)
- delta_cf subtracts the hybrid mean from section 1's single-representation mean as two means. The file's own comment says never to do that, because the two diverge when either arm drops a fold. (c14:478-480 vs 507-510)
- herg and logd are on the code's fast list, but c14 never passes speed. Both searches therefore run the full grid there. The record says the stored fast grid is the decided search for herg. For logd, the record keeps its stored three allocation methods. (dataset_policy.py:688-692; c14:436-448, 621-634; DECISIONS.md:355, 395, 400)
- Section 1's single-representation loop and the summary table in run() are not in the standard selection of 2 base representations and 2 hybrids per model per fold. c14 says it differs by design: 'top 2 general + top 1 distance hybrids per model', dated 2026-10-02. That is an older rule than the owner's 2026-10-03 rule. (c14:54-67, 801-803)


## complexity c15 (tests/experiments/complexity/c15_ml_theory_depth.py)

What it measures: It measures whether hybrids avoid high-dimensional problems: distance concentration (15a), RBF kernel degradation (15b), a double-descent sweep of budget around the row count (15c), and memorisation of permuted labels (15d), against PCA and random-feature baselines.

Datasets: c15 is in the complexity list (complexity_helpers.py:864). submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:207-213, 95). run() returns 'skipped' for any dataset whose task_type is not regression (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:1731-1737). I did not open each dataset's task_type. Reading it from the Step 1 metric column (spearman, rmse or ci = regression), 26 datasets run c15: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. The other 15 (auc, mcc, f1_weighted metrics) are skipped. That split is an inference, unverified.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Only two models are fitted, both hard-coded: a random forest and a Ridge with alpha=1.0. 15a and 15b read rf's recipes. 15c scores rf and ridge. 15d scores ridge only. The same two run on all 26 regression datasets. The searches c15 reads score more models: the start-up general search scores five (plus gp under 1,000 rows), the distance search six with knn, and the 15d read names RIDGE_MODELS (five plus ridge).

Decisions: Each dataset's two Step 1 models, and no ridge anywhere. rf is approved on 7 of the 26: bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, kiba, suzuki. On the other 19, neither model c15 fits is approved. ridge is fitted on all 26. Step 1 says 'Ridge: not yet answered'. A code comment calls c15 an 'approved exception' for ridge.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: No search in c15 is built on one fold's training rows. 15a and 15b read the whole-dataset start-up searches, rank on the mean over all their folds (fold_i is never passed), and build each hybrid on every row. 15b also rebuilds that recipe on an 80/20 group split, but the recipe was still chosen on all rows. 15c runs its own search per budget on every row, then rebuilds the winner per fold and scores it on the held-out fold. 15d reads a whole-dataset search the same way, then rebuilds per fold. So in 15c and 15d the held-out fold's rows helped choose the recipe that is scored on them. When a recipe uses fewer than all representations, build_fold_hybrid also picks which ones from the whole-dataset blueprint.rep_scores, because c15 never passes per-fold scores.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search on that fold's training rows only. Reading a whole-dataset search and re-picking leaks.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: Three different grids, none read from DECISIONS. (a) 15a/15b general read: the start-up search, FULL_BUDGETS (8 budgets, 10-2000), engine default lists or the fast lists on the code's fast datasets, augmentation none/uncapped/capped. (b) 15a/15b distance read: DISTANCE_BUDGETS 10-500, evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm, six models. (c) 15c own search: budgets 0.25, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2 and 4.0 times the row count, and the fast lists on every dataset: lightgbm_gain only; performance_weighted, power_2, rank_exp_d0.3; evaluators rf/match/dnn/lightgbm; representation counts 3 and all; augmentation 'uncapped' only when augmentation representations exist. The 15c distance search swaps the evaluators for the five distance ones. (d) 15d: a whole-dataset general search under RIDGE_MODELS with FULL_BUDGETS and engine defaults. The readers rank every stored configuration; no cut filters the candidates.

Decisions: Each dataset's Step 2-7 budgets, importance, allocation, evaluators and representation counts, and Step 8 augmentation. Examples of disagreement on regression datasets. Budgets: no regression dataset keeps all 8 FULL_BUDGETS. Importance: 15c runs only lightgbm_gain, which Step 3 cuts on buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer; elsewhere it drops methods Step 3 keeps (only qm9 and logd match). Allocation: the fast three include power_2, which ddg_combined cuts, and lack softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2 kept on most datasets. Evaluators: the four include ones Step 5 cuts on abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_titer. Representation counts: 3 is cut on 13 regression datasets, and buchwald_hartwig keeps only 2, which the fast list lacks. Augmentation: Step 8 cuts it on every regression dataset except ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic. 15c's budget sweep around the row count differs by design; the other axes do not.

### R4 standard selection: by design (partly)

Code: No sub-analysis picks the 2 best base representations per model. 15a and 15b measure distance and kernel statistics on every base representation, with no model. Their hybrids are rf's 2 general plus 1 distance hybrid, 3 in total. 15c scores rf's 3 hybrids and ridge's 2 general hybrids, beside PCA and random features at the same width. 15d scores ridge's 2 general hybrids beside PCA and all features concatenated. None of this is per fold: one recipe set per budget is used for every fold.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. c15 compares hybrids against PCA, random features and the full concatenation, which is a different design. The rf hybrid count is 3, from the 2026-10-02 rule (2 general + 1 distance), not 2.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c15 never builds a per-fold search. 15c builds its own per-budget searches, but on every row. They are never refused: own_search=True and the '__c15c_b' dataset name both bypass the refusal. A failed 15c search is printed and that budget scores nan. In 15a and 15b, a missing start-up search goes through get_precomputed_search. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 and more than 500 configurations missing, it raises. The pool reader prints a warning and skips it, and the slot is written to rule_missing. 15d names RIDGE_MODELS, so it skips the in-memory searches and asks for a whole-dataset ridge search on disk. That needs the precompute's --with-ridge pass, or the same refusal, warning and skip apply. Its cells then score nan. submit_everything.sh sets KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 by default.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search is built by the experiment itself, with no refusal or skip.

### Other problems

- A code comment calls c15 and c16 'the two approved exceptions' for ridge (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:77-78). DECISIONS.md:56 says 'Ridge: not yet answered'. The two disagree.
- 15c and 15d return only the mean over folds (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:1282-1284, 1578, 1679). The per-fold scores are computed and then discarded.
- In 15c, when augmentation representations exist, the search runs 'uncapped' only and never 'none' (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:881). Step 8 keeps only 'none' on 20 of the regression datasets that carry augmentation. This count of 20 comes from the helper map, unverified.
- 15a and 15b at budgets 1000 and 2000: the distance search holds budgets up to 500 only. The reader then ranks over other budgets (_shared.py:6855-6872). build_hybrid_from_entry builds at the recipe's own budget (_shared.py:7264). So a row filed under budget 1000 holds a hybrid built at 500 or less. The row records recipe_budget, budget_relaxed and dim (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:205-206, 304).
- 15a and 15b compute every hybrid statistic on a hybrid built over every row, from a recipe chosen on every row. 15b's held-out kernel-target alignment rebuilds on an 80/20 split, but the recipe still saw all rows (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:559-562, 599).
- c15 never passes per-fold allocation scores to build_fold_hybrid (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:574-588, 1242-1255, 1644-1653). So a recipe with representation count 3 keeps the 3 representations ranked by the whole-dataset blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5260-5285).
- 15d depends on a whole-dataset ridge search from the precompute's --with-ridge pass (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:1192-1196). Whether that search exists for any dataset: could not determine. I did not look at stored results.
- The 15c 'distance' search differs from the 15c general search only in its internal evaluators. It uses the 15c budget, fast grid and rf alone. It is not the general_distance search that Step 7 decides.
- Under KIRBY_LOCAL_GRID, 15c cuts its budget factors to 0.25/0.9/1.1/4.0 and 15d cuts permutation trials to 2 (c15_ml_theory_depth.py:845-847, 1423-1424). This is local only; the server gets the defaults.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- c15_ml_theory_depth.py:907-908 against 938-942: a failed 15c general search is only printed. It is never added to 15c's rule_missing, but a failed 15c distance search is. So a budget can score nan for rf and ridge with no entry saying why (R6).
- c15_ml_theory_depth.py:1433-1435: 15d's 'real_score_full' is PCA of the concatenation at min(features, rows-1) components, fitted by Ridge. It is not the raw concatenation the first agent described under R4.
- c15_ml_theory_depth.py:1026-1043: the 15c PCA and random-feature comparisons are fitted with rf, and the PCA comparison again with Ridge. These are extra fits of models not approved for 19 of the 26 regression datasets, plus ridge everywhere (R1). The first agent's R1 names only the hybrid scoring.
- _shared.py:1033-1042 against c15_ml_theory_depth.py:899: the docstring says c15c's searches 'keep full speed'. c15 passes speed='fast' on every one. The docstring is stale; this does not change any rule verdict.
- Not verified: that bindingdb_kd and kiba (metric ci) load with task_type 'regression' and so pass the gate at c15_ml_theory_depth.py:1732. The count of 26 regression datasets assumes they do.


## complexity c16 (tests/experiments/complexity/c16_feature_selection_as_regularization.py)

What it measures: For three model families, it measures the held-out score over a grid of regularisation strength by hybrid budget. It then asks whether a small-budget hybrid at default regularisation matches a tuned model at near-full width.

Datasets: c16 runs on all 41 datasets in DECISIONS Step 1. complexity_helpers.py:865 lists c16 in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS. submit_everything.sh:211-213 queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis. Nothing in complexity run_all skips c16 by dataset. Inside c16, a family is dropped only when _resolve_models gates its model name, for example svm above 10,000 rows (c16:468-480; _shared.py:1073-1075).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: Every dataset gets three families, whatever its approved pair. On regression they are Ridge (alpha 0.001-100), RandomForest (max_depth 3/5/10/None) and SVR (C 0.01-10). On classification they are LogisticRegression, RandomForestClassifier and SVC. Each family's recipe is chosen for 'ridge', 'rf' or 'svm'. The searches it reads score six named models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm and ridge. gp is added on small datasets, and the distance search adds knn.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models, and no ridge anywhere. DECISIONS:56 says 'Ridge: not yet answered'. The code cites a 2026-09-12 owner decision making c16 an exception (c16:52-57, c16:484-491); I could not find that decision in DECISIONS.md. Only flab_binding_koenig (rf+svm) has both of its approved models among the families. The other 40 datasets lack at least one approved model, because dnn, lightgbm, xgboost and gp are never fitted downstream. Sixteen have neither approved model fitted: abcov_kd, cdr_flexibility, flab_binding_adams, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, herg, lhasa_herg, nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3, qm9, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary. Ridge or LogisticRegression is fitted on all 41.

Second agent (partly right): The rule is broken, as reported. Two of the counts are wrong. c16 removes whole model families before any search runs (c16:468-480). It checks each family against the skip table under 'uncapped' whenever the dataset carries augmentation representations (c16:462-463). Under complexity run_all, 34 datasets carry them (complexity_helpers.py:1003-1032). On herg, qm9 and logd, the 'uncapped' skip list removes rf and ridge (dataset_policy.py:106-108). svm under 'uncapped' is capped at 5,000 rows (find_best_hybrid.py:3083-3085). herg has 7,772 rows, logd 5,028 and qm9 10,000, so all three families are removed and c16 fits nothing on them. On flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_koenig, flab_binding_adams and flab_expression_adams, svm and ridge are skipped under 'uncapped' (dataset_policy.py:120-123), so only RF runs. On kiba and bindingdb_kd, rf is skipped (dataset_policy.py:112-113). So 'Ridge or LogisticRegression is fitted on all 41' is wrong for at least 7 datasets. The claim that flab_binding_koenig fits both of its approved models is also wrong on this path: its SVM family is removed, so no dataset fits both. Five more datasets then fit neither approved model: logd, flab_expression_koenig, flab_expression_adams, kiba and bindingdb_kd. That is 21 or more, not 16. I could not determine nt_promoter_tata's row count, so I do not know whether its SVM family survives. When c16 is run alone through its own __main__, load_data gets no augmentation representations (c16:1057). Then strategy is 'none' and the reported counts hold.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every recipe comes from a search over all rows. The general and distance reads call get_rule_hybrids with no fold_i, so the ranking is the mean over every fold of the whole-dataset search. The capped_full search is find_best_hybrid on the unsliced reps and labels. Each cell then rebuilds the recipe on the fold's training rows. When the recipe's representation count is below the pool size, which representations to keep comes from blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores were measured on all rows, because c16 passes no fold scores on the cluster (_C16_REUSE_FOLD_WORK defaults off). c16 writes recipe_selected_on='all rows' into its own results.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: The general read asks get_precomputed_search for a six-model search on FULL_BUDGETS. That search uses engine defaults on importance, allocation, evaluators and representation counts, or the fast lists on the 14 datasets in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS. The distance read uses DISTANCE_BUDGETS (10-500), DISTANCE_EVALUATORS (knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm) and DISTANCE_MODELS on every dataset. The capped_full search passes no speed and never goes through _apply_dataset_search_speed. So it runs the full grid on every dataset: 5 allocation methods, 3 importance methods, 4 evaluators, and counts 2/3/5/all. Augmentation conditions are none, uncapped and capped on the general reads. They are none, uncapped, and capped under 10,000 rows on the distance reads. capped_full uses uncapped wherever augmentations exist. The heatmap budgets are every FULL_BUDGETS value up to the pool width, plus capped_full = min(pool width, 2 x rows, 2048).

Decisions: Steps 2-7 set budgets, importance methods, allocation methods, evaluators and representation counts per dataset. The fast-tier table says not to run the methods the fast grid left out on 10 datasets. Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 datasets. Nothing in c16 or its helpers reads those cuts. Datasets that break the rule: all 41 on at least one axis. Budgets: 39 datasets run budgets Step 2 cut. Only humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc keep all 8, and capped_full is off-grid on every dataset. Fast tier: the capped_full search runs deeplift, treeshap, softmax_T1, wglobal_power2 and counts 2 and 5 on gb_human_enhancers_cohn, herg, nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3, nt_promoter_tata, qm9, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass. Augmentation: every dataset that carries augmentation representations gets uncapped and capped searches. Step 8 keeps only uncapped, on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic. On the general six-model search, the per-dataset excesses are the same as the engine defaults: for example deeplift on herg_ki, wglobal_power2 on caco2, and counts 2/3/5 on adme_mdr1. The heatmap's budget axis is the experiment's subject, so the budget sweep is by design. The other axes are not.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per family, not per approved model, it builds three hybrids: general1, general2 and distance1. Each runs the whole heatmap. Ridge and LogReg get no distance1 because ridge is not in DISTANCE_MODELS. No base representation is ever fitted on its own. The general read returns base_reps, but c16 reads only 'hybrids' and 'missing'. The distance read asks for n_base=0. The comparison arm is a hybrid at capped_full under tuned regularisation. The same hybrids are used for every fold; nothing is picked per fold.

Decisions: Per model and per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. Comparing families and no single-representation arm are c16's design. Three hybrids per family instead of two, and one set for all folds, are not part of that design.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c16 never builds a per-fold search. A missing six-model general search is built on all rows inside the job when allowed. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH it is refused when under 50% is stored and more than 500 configurations are left. The refusal is caught in _iter_pool_searches, which prints a warning and skips that search. The slot then goes into rule_missing or pool_lookup_errors, and its cells are NaN because _evaluate_cell skips a fold with no recipe. The docstring tells the user to run tests/precompute_hybrids.py --with-ridge first, which is a separate precompute script. The capped_full search has '__' in its dataset name, so it is never refused and is always built, but on all rows.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, with no separate precompute script, and must not be refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- c16:510-516 says build_fold_hybrid no longer falls back to the recipe's whole-dataset representation scores. _shared.py:5256-5262 still does that when choosing WHICH representations to keep, whenever the recipe's count is below the pool size and no fold scores are passed. On the cluster c16 passes none (c16:102-104, c16:312-313). The comment is right about the budget split (_shared.py:5349-5356) and wrong about the representation choice.
- The LogReg family fits LogisticRegression, but its recipe is chosen for 'ridge', which resolves to RidgeClassifier (c16:423, _shared.py:610-612). So on classification datasets the recipe and the fitted model differ. On auc datasets the code itself says ridge cannot be scored, so Ridge or LogReg arms can come back blank (c16:687-691). Whether that happens on each auc dataset I could not determine without the stored searches.
- Rows at budgets 1000, 2000 and capped_full in the distance1 arm are built from a recipe ranked only on budgets 10-500. This is recorded in rule_budget_relaxed (c16:583, c16:682-683, c16:729).
- When capped_full equals the pool width, every cell at that budget is skipped as an all-representations concatenation (c16:285-286). The tuned-full comparison is then impossible for every family. This is recorded in hybrid_wins_reason (c16:859-864). Which datasets this hits depends on pool width, which I did not compute.
- fold_reselection is called with recipe_selection='whole_dataset' (c16:1025-1027). So its leave-one-fold-out delta re-picks budget and regularisation per fold, but the recipes behind every candidate were still chosen on all rows.
- c16's general read names six models, so it bypasses the five-model whole-dataset search that complexity run_all builds at start-up. That start-up search is built or loaded in the same process and not used by c16 (complexity_helpers.py:1069-1080; _shared.py:6782-6792).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- c16:462-480 decides which families exist by checking the skip table under 'uncapped', but its stored reads also use 'none'. Under complexity run_all this removes all three families on herg, qm9 and logd, so c16 writes no heatmap for them. It removes Ridge and SVM on the four flab_binding/expression datasets and RF on kiba and bindingdb_kd (dataset_policy.py:106-123; find_best_hybrid.py:3083-3085). A removed family goes into no results field; it is only printed (c16:477-480).
- c16:462-467 runs its capped_full search under 'uncapped' on kiba and bindingdb_kd. The pool reader never asks for 'uncapped' on those two (UNCAPPED_SKIP_DATASETS, _shared.py:5989 and _shared.py:6029-6043). So the last budget column on those datasets comes from an augmentation condition the other budgets do not use. Step 8 cuts augmentation there anyway (DECISIONS.md:666, 685).
- Four datasets are fast in code but missing from DECISIONS' fast-tier table: flab_expression_koenig, logd, kiba and bindingdb_kd (dataset_policy.py:688-711; DECISIONS.md:350-363). On three of them, c16's general read drops methods the record keeps and runs representation counts it cut. Details are under R3.
- _evaluate_cell catches any exception from build_fold_hybrid and skips that fold silently (c16:341-342). A recipe whose representation choice cannot be made raises at _shared.py:5263-5279, and that fold is then lost with no record of why. Only fold_scores=None marks it.
- In the R1 report, 'ridge is fitted on all 41' and 'only flab_binding_koenig has both models' assume every family survives. Neither holds on the run_all path. Details are under R1.


## complexity c17 (tests/experiments/complexity/c17_information_theoretic_decomposition.py)

What it measures: For each budget in features, it compares how much mutual information with the label per feature seven feature-selection methods keep on held-out rows: three hybrids, PCA, mRMR, recursive elimination and random.

Datasets: c17 is in the complexity list (complexity_helpers.py:866). submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis, 41 datasets (submit_everything.sh:207-213, 349-370). c17 returns a skip on any dataset whose task_type is not regression (c17:391-398). By DATASET_REGISTRY_DATA (dataset_policy.py:230), printed this session, 26 of the 41 are regression: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. I did not trace load_data to confirm it takes task_type from that table.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every method is scored with one model, a RandomForestRegressor with 100 trees (c17:354-356). The three hybrid recipes are the ones ranked best for downstream_model='rf' (c17:630-636). No second model is fitted on any dataset.

Decisions: Step 1 gives each dataset two approved models. rf is approved on 7 of the 26 regression datasets: bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, kiba, suzuki. On the other 19, rf is not approved at all. On all 26, the second approved model is never fitted.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: c17 compares feature-selection methods at a fixed budget. It uses three hybrids for one model, rf: general ranks 1 and 2 and distance rank 1 (c17:44-45, 585-586; _shared.py:7064-7066). Decisions: R4 asks, per fold, for each of the two approved models: 2 best base representations and 2 best hybrids. c17 has one model, three hybrids and no scored base representation. The method comparison is the experiment's design. The extra distance hybrid and the single model are not.

The rest of the claim holds: c17 builds no per-fold search, a refused member is skipped with a warning, and the empty slot leads to a stored error.

### Other problems

- Only the hybrid methods choose a recipe with the held-out rows in view. PCA, mRMR, recursive elimination and random choose on each fold's training rows only. So the hybrid methods differ from the other four in two ways at once: how they select features, and what data chose their settings (c17:588-592, 761-763).
- When a recipe uses fewer representations than the dataset has, build_fold_hybrid picks which ones to keep from blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5286). Those scores come from the whole-dataset search. So with representation counts 2, 3 or 5, the choice of representations also uses the held-out rows. c17 passes no fold-local precomputed_alloc_scores (c17:684-694).
- Above 500 features, the distance hybrid's recipe was ranked at a different budget, between 10 and 500 features. It is then rebuilt at 1000 or 2000. The output records budget_relaxed per entry (c17:644-647), but the method keeps the name hybrid__distance1 at that budget.
- bindingdb_kd and kiba have no stored distance search (DECISIONS.md:609, 750). On those two the distance hybrid comes from run_all building it on all rows, or it is refused and missing under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH.
- c17's own folds come from cv_split with config['n_splits'] (c17:403, 504). It passes no n_outer_folds to get_rule_hybrids, so a fold-count mismatch with the stored search is never checked. With fold_i=None this does not change the ranking, but it means no fold alignment exists to reuse for a per-fold read.
- c17 passes augmentation representations to build_fold_hybrid even for a recipe whose augmentation condition is 'none' (c17:673-676, 686). Whether create_hybrid ignores them under strategy 'none': could not determine; I did not open create_hybrid. It also makes _hybrid_fold_importance return None on every augmented dataset, so the importance shortcut is never used there (c17:240-241).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Under a capped or uncapped recipe, a hybrid method can draw features from the augmentation representations. run_all removes augmentation-only representations from data['reps'] (complexity_helpers.py:1033-1039). c17's X_concat is built from data['reps'] (c17:408), so PCA, mRMR, recursive elimination and random never see those features. So the hybrid methods choose from a larger set of features than the other four. That is one more difference on top of the two the agent named. Evidence: c17:673-676, c17:686, hybrid.py:5984.
- The budget fallback applies to the general search, not only the distance search. At a requested budget with no stored row, the general ranking also falls back to every stored budget and sets budget_relaxed (_shared.py:6856-6870). Once the stores hold only each dataset's Step 2 range, every c17 budget outside that range would get this treatment. The recipe would then be rebuilt at the cell's budget under the names hybrid and hybrid__general2 (c17:687). Whether the stores on disk are already cut: could not determine; I did not open them.
- One condition of the refusal was left out of the R6 report. The refusal fires only when under 50% of the configurations are stored and more than 500 are left (find_best_hybrid.py:594, 691-696, 705-715). Otherwise find_best_hybrid finishes the missing part of the search on all rows, inside the c17 job.
- R5 does not apply to c17, a complexity experiment. The agent flagged no R5 problem, and none exists.


## complexity c18 (tests/experiments/complexity/c18_diversity_vs_depth.py)

What it measures: At each feature budget, it compares a RandomForest fitted on features taken from the top 1, 2 or 3 representations, or spread evenly across all of them, against the stored search's hybrids rebuilt per fold.

Datasets: c18 has no dataset filter of its own. It runs on whatever dataset complexity run_all is given (complexity_helpers.py:867, 899, 912-1291), and run_all has no skip check. submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213, 350-366). A tiny import this session printed 41 datasets, the same 41 as DECISIONS Step 1. submit_dataset.sh lists c18 in the complexity run order (submit_dataset.sh:312). So c18 runs on all 41.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every model c18 fits is a RandomForest. It is used in the depth arms, the even-split arm and the hybrid arms. Every stored-search read asks for downstream model 'rf'. No second model is fitted on any dataset. The two whole-dataset searches that run_all builds before c18 score five models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. gp is added on 9 datasets under 1,000 rows. knn is added on the distance search on every dataset. ridge is not scored.

Decisions: Each dataset's two approved models from Step 1. rf is one of the two on only 8 datasets: bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, humanness_therapeutic, kiba, suzuki. On those 8, c18 never fits the second approved model. On the other 33, c18 fits no approved model. Step 9 says the knn distance search is not needed on the six nucleotide datasets. run_all builds it there anyway.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: The four hand-built arms are per fold. Each fold ranks its representations by importance on its own training rows, and depth_1/2/3 and uniform_all take features from that ranking. The hybrid arms are not per fold. Their recipes come from get_rule_hybrids, which reads the whole-dataset searches. c18 passes no fold_i, so recipes are ranked on the mean over ALL folds of a search run on every row. The held-out fold's own scores take part in that ranking. Only the features are refit on the fold's training rows. When a recipe used fewer representations than the pool, build_fold_hybrid picks which ones from blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores are measured over every row. The importance method the hand-built arms use is copied from the whole-dataset winner. top2_base_reps, top2_hybrids, hybrid_deltas and the fold_reselection input are all read from the whole-dataset search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c18 never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search has two outcomes. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH unset, it is built on all rows: first at run_all start-up, or again through get_precomputed_search. With it set, a search with more than 500 configurations still missing is refused. submit_everything.sh sets it by default. At start-up the refusal is stored as None. At read time the pool member is skipped with a warning, and get_best_search_for_downstream returns (None, None). c18 then carries on. It runs no hybrid arm, writes the missing slots to 'rule_missing', and gives the hand-built arms lightgbm_gain marked 'fallback'.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment builds it itself. It must not refuse or skip.

### Other problems

- Hand-built arms vs general2 and distance1. The hand-built arms rank features with general1's importance method (c18:467-470). general2 and distance1 may use deeplift or treeshap instead, and the code says so (c18:442-444). So those two arms differ from the hand-built arms in two ways at once, not one: how the budget is split, and the importance method.
- Width. The depth and uniform arms always take the full budget of features (c18:147-148). That includes features with zero importance. The hybrid arms stop at the last feature that scored above zero (c18:133-146). So at the same budget the arms are built on different numbers of features. The code records the widths (c18:403-407, 679-681) but does not make them equal.
- Augmented recipes. The general and distance pools include the 'uncapped' and 'capped' searches (_shared.py:6040-6046, 6030-6037). A recipe ranked by its augmented score keeps that augmentation setting (_shared.py:6996). c18 rebuilds every hybrid with augmentations=None (c18:648-649). create_hybrid only adds augmentation features when augmentations are passed (hybrid.py:5984). So that recipe is built without the features it was scored with, and the result is filed under its name.
- Distance arm at 1000 and 2000 features. The distance search stops at 500 features (_shared.py:495). So the arm labelled 1000 or 2000 holds a recipe built at 500 or fewer. budget_relaxed is written to the result (c18:701), but the row stays labelled with the larger budget.
- Representations for a recipe. When a recipe used fewer representations than the pool, build_fold_hybrid picks which ones from blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5286). c18 passes no fold-local scores (c18:646-654). Those scores are each representation's best score over every row and every model (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593). So the choice of representations saw the held-out fold.
- Model passed into the rebuild. c18 passes a RandomForest instance into every predictive rebuild (c18:651-654). Per _evaluate_allocation's docstring, a passed model decides which features are kept, in place of the recipe's internal evaluator (hybrid.py:2758-2763). Could not determine whether the search used the internal evaluator or the downstream model at that step, so it is unknown whether the rebuild matches the stored recipe.
- fold_reselection input. fold_reselection_by_budget is built from the whole-dataset search (c18:492-497). A reader who runs fold_reselection on it gets per-fold scores from models whose training rows included the held-out fold.
- Docstring vs code. get_best_search_for_downstream's docstring says general/capped is absent from the pool (_shared.py:6168-6175). _pool_conditions adds 'capped' to the general pool (_shared.py:6044), and to the distance pool under 10,000 rows (_shared.py:6036-6037).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The RandomForest c18 fits differs from the 'rf' the stored searches scored. The search's rf sets max_features='sqrt' (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:2722-2726). c18's _RF(n_estimators=100, random_state=42) leaves max_features at the sklearn default (c18_diversity_vs_depth.py:617, 630, 653, 659). That default is 1.0 for regression in local sklearn 1.6.1; server version not checked. So on regression datasets, recipes and top 2 lists ranked for one forest are scored with another. The same forest is passed into the rebuild, so its keep or drop decisions can also differ from the search's.
- The general precompute adds 'capped' to the distance search as well. precompute_hybrid_searches appends 'capped' with no tier check (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5543-5549), although its own comment says distance does not emit capped. Step 8 cuts capped everywhere (DECISIONS.md:652-698).
- DECISIONS.md:348-363 lists ten fast-tier datasets. dataset_policy.FAST_SPEED_DATASETS holds 14 (python import printed it). bindingdb_kd, flab_expression_koenig, kiba and logd are searched on the fast lists in code. The record treats them as full-grid datasets with their own cuts (e.g. DECISIONS.md:332, 398 for kiba).
- If KIRBY_POOL_SUBSET is set (read in resolve_pool_subset, tests/experiments/_shared.py), get_rule_hybrids returns recipes for more than one family. c18 then builds extra hybrid arms named natural__<slot>__<family> (c18:212-223). Under R4 this would add more hybrids beyond the 3 already reported.


## complexity c19 (tests/experiments/complexity/c19_importance_weighted_training.py)

What it measures: For each hybrid it reads, c19 scores five ways of using feature importance in training: no weighting, features scaled by importance, molecules weighted by neighbour agreement, both together, and below-median features deleted.

Datasets: All 41 datasets in DECISIONS Step 1. c19 is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (tests/experiments/complexity/complexity_helpers.py:869) and in the complexity run order (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:312). submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213, 95). complexity run_all has no per-experiment skip, so c19 runs on every one of them.

### R1 models: NO

Code: c19 fits only models in WEIGHTED_MODELS = rf, lightgbm, xgboost, intersected with config['models']. complexity run_all sets config['models'] to the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS, so c19 fits rf, xgboost and lightgbm on every dataset. svm, dnn and gp are never fitted. Against Step 1, 17 datasets get none of their two approved models: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, herg_ki, logd, tcga_brca_pam50. 14 datasets get one of their two: bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, flab_binding_koenig, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_titer, kiba, nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3, nt_promoter_tata, qm9, tz_her2_multiclass. 10 datasets get both approved models plus one unapproved model: abcov_kd, buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, flab_binding_adams, herg, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, suzuki, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary. So every one of the 41 datasets fits at least one unapproved model. On the six nucleotide datasets xgboost is skipped by policy; if the stored search follows that, c19 records xgboost under hybrid_recipe_missing and still fits rf. No knn and no ridge.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: c19 calls get_rule_hybrids with no fold_i. With fold_i=None, get_fold_pool_recipes ranks every stored configuration by its mean over all folds of the whole-dataset search. So one recipe set per model is chosen for the whole dataset, using every row. c19 says so itself: 'recipe_selected_on': 'all rows'. The features are then rebuilt per fold on that fold's training rows (build_fold_hybrid). That rebuild still leaks in one more way. c19 passes no precomputed_alloc_scores, so for a recipe using fewer than all representations, build_fold_hybrid picks WHICH representations from blueprint.rep_scores. find_best_hybrid fills rep_scores from baselines measured over every row of the search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per model, c19 scores three hybrids: general rank 1, general rank 2 and distance rank 1 (RULE_N_GENERAL=2, RULE_N_DISTANCE=1). Leaving out base representations is by design: the docstring says c19 asks only which weighting helps on the hybrid. The third hybrid is not by design in the R4 sense; it comes from the 2026-10-02 rule of 2 general plus 1 distance. The selection is one set per dataset, not per fold.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c19 never builds a per-fold search. When the in-memory pool has no search for a condition, get_precomputed_search calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 (the submit_everything.sh default) and more than 500 configurations missing, find_best_hybrid raises. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that member. get_rule_hybrids lists unfilled slots in 'missing'. c19 writes them to rule_missing and hybrid_recipe_missing and carries on. With no recipe at all, it returns error 'no_hybrid_recipe' and scores nothing.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist must be built by the experiment itself.

### Other problems

- c19 drops svm and dnn because WEIGHTED_MODELS lists only rf, lightgbm and xgboost (c19:97). Its own fit already falls back to an unweighted fit when a model rejects sample_weight (c19:404-415). So the drop is not needed for the code to run.
- That fallback scores 'sample_weighted' and 'combined' with no sample weights, under the weighted names, and records nothing to say so (c19:408-413).
- The budget asked for is a fixed 100 features (c19:125), not the dataset's decided range. run_all passes no budget kwarg (complexity_helpers.py:1180-1194 builds kwargs without one).
- build_fold_hybrid is called without precomputed_alloc_scores (c19:312-321). For recipes with a representation count below 10, the representations kept per fold are chosen from whole-dataset baseline scores (_shared.py:5256-5286; find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593).
- c19's folds come from cv_split (c19:283), not nested_cv_outer_folds. With fold_i=None this does not affect the ranking, but the stored per-fold scores and c19's folds need not be the same rows.
- The importance weights use the hybrid's recipe importance method (c19:352-355), recomputed on the fold's standardized training features. That part is per fold.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Search-call record, general precompute: gp is added to datasets under 1,000 rows on both the full and the fast path, not only on the fast path. _apply_dataset_search_speed calls _apply_small_dataset_models at _shared.py:1047, 1051 and 1079. For models=None at full speed, the engine scores only fast- and full-tier models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm.
- Search-call record, standalone __main__: whether load_data fills augmentations was left open. It does not. _load_data_impl returns 'augmentations': None on every path (_shared.py:4103, 4148, 4230, 4285, 4418, 4523, 4592, 4725). So a standalone c19 reads only the none member of each search.
- R3 augmentation detail: _pool_conditions gives bindingdb_kd and kiba no uncapped member (UNCAPPED_SKIP_DATASETS, _shared.py:5989, 6029). precompute_hybrid_searches still builds uncapped for them (_shared.py:5543-5548), and c19 never reads it.
- R1 detail: if none of the configured models is rf, lightgbm or xgboost, c19 fits rf anyway (c19:120-121). A run asking only for a dataset's approved svm+dnn pair would still fit rf.
- R5 does not apply to c19, which is a complexity experiment, not a noise one.


## complexity c21 (tests/experiments/complexity/c21_single_rep_augmentation.py)

What it measures: For each base representation alone, it measures how much the per-fold score changes when a few extra features are added, compared with fixed-recipe multi-representation hybrids at 500, 1000 and 2000 features.

Datasets: All 41 datasets in the record. submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). c21 is in the complexity default list (tests/experiments/complexity/complexity_helpers.py:853) and in the submit order (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:314). complexity run_all has no skip check before mod.run (complexity_helpers.py:1164-1239). Within a dataset, the conditions that add the curated augmentation representations (B, D, Rb and the H1 hybrid) run only where DATASET_REPS lists augmentation representations (c21:429, 434, 454, 1134). Condition C, which takes features from the other base representations, runs on every dataset (c21:431-433).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Under run_all, c21 takes config['models'], which is the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. It uses the same list for every dataset. The standalone command line gets the same five from get_config. gp is never in the list. knn and ridge are never used.

Decisions: Step 1 gives each dataset two models. Five of them include gp: abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn) and ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn).

Code: c21 runs no search and reads none. Each fold's hybrid is built by build_fold_hybrid on that fold's training rows from a recipe written into the file. The single-representation arms pass a fixed allocation score of 1.0. The H arms pass none, so the representations are re-scored on the fold's training rows. The recipes set no representation count, so the whole-dataset rep_scores route is never taken. Scalers are fit on training rows only. The decoy features and random control features are drawn over all rows but use no labels.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from that fold's training rows only.

### Other problems

- The run_all list says c21's hybrid reference arms reuse the precompute built at start-up (complexity_helpers.py:847-850). c21 builds its H arms from a fixed recipe and reads no stored search (c21:480-492). The two disagree. The start-up general and distance searches run in c21's process and are never used (complexity_helpers.py:1065-1114).
- DEFAULT_TOP_N = 9 is described as how many other base representations are offered as donors (c21:89-94). The code uses it as features taken from each donor (c21:432-433, 446, 779). Every other representation is always offered. So the 2026-09-12 change from 5 to 9 raised features per donor, not the number of donors.
- The H0/H1 hybrids use the allocation method weighted_global. The engine lists it among methods that did not survive the 2026-09-01 cut (find_best_hybrid.py:3714-3730). It is in no Step 4 row.
- On five datasets c21 runs only one of the two approved models. They are abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, where gp is approved. gp is never in c21's model list.
- Budgets outside the Step 2 range. abagym_Ang2, cdr_flexibility and suzuki: all three H budgets (500, 1000, 2000 features). abagym_VEGF, bh_doyle_plates, ddg_combined and tz_her2_binary: 1000 and 2000. flab_binding_koenig and tz_her2_multiclass: 2000. On seven of these the headline budget of 1000 features is outside the range.
- The summary's head-to-head picks the best base representation and best augmented arm per model. It picks them by the same fold scores it prints (c21:1182, 1190). The hybrid rows it prints beside them are fixed and not picked. The file removed this kind of selection from the hybrid side for this reason (c21:104-107).
- Stale docstrings. run() says the default models are rf, xgboost, lightgbm (c21:629-631); the code uses config['models'], five under run_all (c21:715-716). It says the default strategy is ('uncapped',) (c21:636-638); the code ships ('capped', 'uncapped') (c21:207). _plant_capped_decoys says donors offer 5 features each (c21:380); top_n is now 9.
- The H arms name lightgbm as the internal evaluator. Because the downstream model is passed, allocation is scored with that model instead (hybrid.py:2758-2764). Whether lightgbm is used anywhere else in that build: could not determine without reading create_hybrid in full. Step 5 cuts the lightgbm evaluator on abagym_VEGF and ginkgo_titer.
- Under KIRBY_LOCAL_GRID, c21 cuts its own conditions, budgets, base representations and H arms (c21:154-296). This applies to local runs only. Server runs use the shipped values.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The H arms use the lightgbm internal evaluator to split the features between representations. The audit said the downstream model does this instead, which is wrong for the budget split. See src/kirby/hybrid.py:2318-2331 and 3239-3260, and tests/experiments/complexity/c21_single_rep_augmentation.py:504. So the H arms break the Step 5 cut of lightgbm on abagym_VEGF and ginkgo_titer (DECISIONS.md:518, 539).
- The comment at tests/experiments/complexity/c21_single_rep_augmentation.py:876-879 says choosing the extra features does not depend on the model. The code disagrees: c21 passes model=model_factory() (c21:946, 562). The engine scores each candidate number of extra features with that downstream model (src/kirby/hybrid.py:4472-4475 uncapped; 4083-4084 capped). So all five models, three of them not approved, also decide which extra features get in.
- The H arms' allocation is plain 'weighted_global' (linear weighting, pool multiplier 2; src/kirby/hybrid.py:601). It is not the Step 4 method 'wglobal_power2' (power 2; hybrid.py:602). On the ten fast-tier datasets, the decided allocation methods are only performance_weighted, power_2 and rank_exp_d0.3 (DECISIONS.md:354-363).
- The comment at tests/experiments/complexity/complexity_helpers.py:846-850 names tier 'top'. That tier is retired (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5539-5540).


## complexity c22 (tests/experiments/complexity/c22_explainability.py)

What it measures: For rf and xgboost, it rebuilds each stored hybrid on every fold's training rows and fits the model. It explains the better-scoring model with SHAP and reports each representation's share of the attribution.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. c22 has no dataset filter of its own. It is in the complexity list (complexity_helpers.py:869, 902). submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). submit_dataset.sh runs it third in the complexity order (submit_dataset.sh:312). complexity run_all never calls should_skip_experiment, so nucleotide datasets are not skipped.

### R1 models: NO

Code: The model list is written into the file as rf and xgboost on every dataset. It does not read the dataset's approved pair. On the six nucleotide datasets the stored search never scores xgboost, so xgboost gets no recipe and is dropped. Only rf is explained there.

Decisions: Each dataset's two Step 1 models. Only humanness_therapeutic (xgboost+rf) matches c22's pair exactly. Seven datasets have rf but not xgboost: bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, kiba, suzuki. Eight have xgboost but not rf: abcov_kd, cdr_flexibility, flab_binding_adams, herg, lhasa_herg, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary, tz_her2_multiclass. The other 25 datasets approve neither model: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, herg_ki, logd, the five nt_* datasets, qm9 and tcga_brca_pam50. So 40 of 41 datasets break R1. No knn or ridge is used.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Recipes come from get_rule_hybrids, and c22 passes no fold index. With fold_i=None the ranking is the mean over every fold of the whole-dataset search. One set of recipes then serves every fold. complexity run_all builds both stored searches on all rows. Each recipe is refitted on the fold's training rows. When a recipe uses fewer than all 10 representations, the kept representations are chosen by blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores were measured over all rows. c22 itself writes recipe_selected_on 'all rows'.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only.

On each fold, SHAP is run only on whichever of rf and xgboost scores better on that fold's validation rows.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. Leaving out base representations could be by design, since c22 explains hybrids. The third hybrid, from the distance search, is not. Neither is explaining only one model per fold.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: No per-fold search is ever built. If a stored search is missing, get_precomputed_search calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is on by default in submit_everything.sh. With it set, that call raises when more than 500 configurations are missing. _iter_pool_searches catches the error, prints a warning and skips that search. The slot is then listed in rule_missing. A model left with no slots goes into models_unscored and is not trained. If no model has a recipe, c22 returns 'no_search_result'.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist must be built by the experiment itself.

### Other problems

- On each fold, the model SHAP explains is picked by its score on that fold's validation rows (c22_explainability.py:276-283). The per-representation shares are then averaged over folds that may have explained different models, built from different recipes. c22 prints a warning about this at :491-496 but still reports the average.
- On the six nucleotide datasets (gb_human_enhancers_cohn and the five nt_*), only rf is explained. Their approved pair is dnn+lightgbm, or lightgbm+svm for nt_promoter_tata. So c22 there explains a model the record does not use at all.
- The recipe score c22 records is filed under the key 'score_other_folds'. With fold_i=None it is the mean over all folds of the whole-dataset search (c22_explainability.py:161-163, 175).
- When a recipe uses fewer than 10 representations, build_fold_hybrid keeps the representations ranked highest by whole-dataset rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5260). The comment at _shared.py:5349-5354 says whole-dataset rep_scores are not used. That holds for the budget split, not for which representations are kept.
- The top-feature listing and the feature-to-representation map come from one fold only, the last fold that both built and explained (c22_explainability.py:413-418). This is stated in the output.
- When augmentation features are in the hybrid, the per-representation SHAP breakdown leaves them out. c22 prints this at :458-462 but does not correct it.
- get_precomputed_search is imported but not called directly by c22 (c22_explainability.py:44).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R6, concrete case: DECISIONS.md Step 7 header (line 609) and line 760 say bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg have no stored distance search. That is the record's dated claim, not checked against disk. On those three datasets c22's distance1 slot either runs a cold distance search on all rows or is refused and skipped. The path is _shared.py:5853-5896, then _shared.py:6107-6114, then rule_missing at c22_explainability.py:153.
- R3 detail: bindingdb_kd and kiba read no 'uncapped' search on either the general or the distance side (_shared.py:5989, 6029-6032, 6052-6054). The precompute side (_shared.py:5543-5549) does not check that list, so the two sides disagree on those two datasets.
- R3 detail: precompute_hybrid_searches adds 'capped' on every tier, including general_distance (_shared.py:5543-5549). The comment there says the distance precompute emits no capped search. The read side asks for distance 'capped' only under 10,000 rows (_shared.py:6035-6036).
- R3 exception the report missed: humanness_therapeutic. Its decided grid matches what c22 reads on budgets, importance, allocation, evaluators, representation counts and augmentation. Its augmentation list is empty (complexity_helpers.py:417-420; DECISIONS.md:236, 326, 391, 542, 591, 638, 684). Its only failures are R1 (none here, its pair is rf+xgboost), R2 and R4.
- R2 side point: c22 splits folds with cv_split(groups, n_folds, ...) at c22_explainability.py:212-215. The pool's stored per-fold scores come from its own 5-fold, seed-42 split (_shared.py:6667-6674). With fold_i=None this does not change the ranking, but the stored fold numbers do not correspond to c22's folds.


## complexity c23 (tests/experiments/complexity/c23_evaluator_model_matching.py)

What it measures: For each downstream model, it measures how much the held-out score changes when the model that scores candidate hybrids inside the search is the same model, a similar one, or a different one.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. c23 is in the complexity list SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (complexity_helpers.py:870) and in submit_dataset.sh RUN_ORDER (submit_dataset.sh:312-314). submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:207-213, 350-372). A python import this session printed 41 keys. complexity run_all never calls should_skip_experiment, so no dataset is skipped for c23 (complexity_helpers.py:1166-1239).

### R1 models: NO

Code: c23 takes the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS (rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm) as downstream models on every dataset. It keeps only names with a MATCH_TABLE row, and gp has no row. svm is dropped above 10,000 rows. ridge and knn are never downstream models. knn appears only as the internal evaluator of dnn's strong-mismatch condition.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models. On 36 datasets both approved models are among c23's five, so c23 also fits three models the record excludes. On 5 datasets one approved model is gp, which c23 cannot run: abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn), ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn). There c23 lacks gp and fits four unapproved models. All 41 datasets break the rule.

### R6 missing search: yes

Code: c23 builds every per-fold search itself through nested_cv_evaluate, with cache=True. It passes condition_suffix, so the engine renames the tier to 'general__cond-c23_<model>_<evaluator>'. The cold-search refusal applies only when the tier, cut at '__obj-', is exactly 'general' or 'general_distance'. So it returns without checking, even with KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1. An inner search that raises is printed and that fold is dropped. If every fold fails, nested_cv_evaluate raises, c23 prints FAILED, and that condition has no result.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment, not refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- gp cannot be a downstream model in c23, because MATCH_TABLE has no gp row (c23:68-72, 82-94). On the five datasets whose approved pair includes gp, c23 cannot measure the approved pair at all.
- The cache key and the run disagree on which models were fitted. With dict models, _resolve_models fits every model handed in and ignores the skip policy (find_best_hybrid.py:3265-3266). The cache-key model list drops skipped names (find_best_hybrid.py:8712-8715). Example: on logd under 'uncapped', rf is skipped (dataset_policy.py:108). The rf arm fits rf while its key lists no model. The same happens with xgboost on the nt_/gb_ datasets (dataset_policy.py:36). Whether this causes a wrong cache hit was not checked.
- A comment at c23:226-236 says a per-dataset budget cap exists on 22 datasets. dataset_policy.py:204-207 says nothing registers a budget policy now, so the cap does not exist.
- The recipe fields c23 reports per arm (budget, allocation method, importance method, winning evaluator) come from ncv.best_by_model. c23 labels this as the first outer fold with a winner (c23:265-269, 470-473). They describe one fold, not all five. The held-out scores are per fold and are not affected.
- Before c23 runs, complexity run_all builds or reads two whole-dataset searches over the full default grid (complexity_helpers.py:1065-1114). c23 does not use them. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH they can be refused, and the error is caught and recorded (complexity_helpers.py:1117-1125).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R6, for the record: c23's own per-fold searches are never refused by KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH. They run under tier 'general__cond-c23_*' (find_best_hybrid.py:8986-8987). _is_precompute_tier only matches 'general' and 'general_distance' (find_best_hybrid.py:598-605), so the refusal at find_best_hybrid.py:9360 is a no-op for them. Only the two run_all start-up searches can be refused.
- R6 skip paths: when an outer fold's inner search raises, nested_cv_evaluate prints a line and drops that fold (find_best_hybrid.py:10900-10906). c23 then pairs fewer folds. A whole condition that raises is caught, printed as FAILED, and written to the output as nothing at all (c23:271-273, c23:500-501).
- R3 internal evaluators: the decided set is rf, lightgbm, dnn and match, with per-dataset cuts (DECISIONS.md:514-556). c23 also uses xgboost (condition E, c23:117), svm, gp, knn, dnn_small and dnn_wide (c23:84-93, 113). That differs by design. But condition E's set {rf, lightgbm, xgboost} also ignores the decided cuts, for example 'cut lightgbm' on ginkgo_titer (DECISIONS.md:537).
- Fast-tier mechanism: dataset_policy.FAST_SPEED_DATASETS (dataset_policy.py:688) reaches a search only through _apply_dataset_search_speed (_shared.py:1015). c23 calls nested_cv_evaluate directly at c23:223 and c23:443, so it runs speed 'full' on those 10 datasets. This is the cause of the fast-tier breaks the first agent counted.


## complexity c24 (tests/experiments/complexity/c24_blueprint_transfer.py)

What it measures: For each held-out fold, how much the held-out score changes when the hybrid recipe and its selected features are searched on one fold fewer of training rows, plus the Nogueira stability index of the features selected across folds.

Datasets: All 41 datasets that submit_everything.sh queues for the complexity suite. The roster is every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213), and complexity is one of the default categories (submit_everything.sh:95). c24 is in the complexity default list (tests/experiments/complexity/complexity_helpers.py:871) and in submit_dataset.sh's run order (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:313). The complexity runner never calls should_skip_experiment (grep of complexity_helpers.py finds no call), so no dataset is skipped by name. c24 itself skips a dataset only when it has fewer than 2 distinct groups (c24_blueprint_transfer.py:323-328). Fold count is config['n_splits'] = DEFAULT_N_FOLDS, 5 (complexity_helpers.py:948, find_best_hybrid.py DEFAULT_N_FOLDS = 5).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Neither c24 search passes models, so the engine scores every model in the 'fast' and 'full' tiers: rf, lightgbm, dnn, xgboost, svm. gp is tier 'extra' and is never scored here, because c24 calls find_best_hybrid directly and never goes through _apply_small_dataset_models. Step 1 then keeps the single best of those five models for each fold. The off-diagonal cells reuse that fold's model. svm is also dropped from any search on more than 5,000 training rows under 'uncapped' augmentation, which c24 uses on 32 datasets.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two approved models from Step 1. ridge never; knn only in the distance search per Step 9.

### R2 per fold: yes

Code: Step 1 runs one find_best_hybrid per outer fold on that fold's training rows only. Each off-diagonal cell runs a second find_best_hybrid on the rows left after removing both the source fold and the target fold. The hybrid is then built on those same rows and applied to the target fold's held-out rows. Neither search sees the rows it is scored on. c24 never reads data['precomputed_searches'], the whole-dataset search the complexity runner builds at start-up. get_precomputed_search and get_best_for_downstream are imported but never called. The blueprint's rep_scores, which build_fold_hybrid can use to choose representations, come from these per-fold searches, so they carry no held-out rows either.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: Per fold, c24 keeps one hybrid recipe for one model: the single best across all five scored models. It scores no base representation at all. Each off-diagonal cell takes one recipe from the pair search for the target fold's model. The design compares one fold's own selection with a selection made on less data, so it needs one recipe per fold, not two hybrids and two base representations. What it does not do by design is restrict that one model to the dataset's approved two.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### Other problems

- On the 32 datasets with augmentation representations, every c24 search is 'uncapped'. The record keeps augmentation 'none' on all of them and cuts 'uncapped' on 30 (DECISIONS.md:654-698). So c24 runs only the cut condition and never the kept one there. ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic keep uncapped on the distance search only; the general search is open.
- gp is never scored. On abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho one of the two approved models cannot be chosen by c24.
- Step 1 can pick any of five models per fold, and different folds can pick different models. The diagonal score of fold j and the off-diagonal cells scored on fold j share fold j's model (600-608). Different target folds may still be scored with different models, so the per-target deltas pooled at 695-697 can mix models.
- When the pair search has no entry for the target fold's model, c24 takes the best recipe of another model and scores it with the target model (567-574). This is recorded in cell_recipe_provenance (593-596) but still enters the transfer matrix.
- The fold split is called without task_type (c24_blueprint_transfer.py:337; _shared.py:2186-2193). Classification datasets therefore get plain grouped folds, not class-stratified grouped folds.
- The comment at c24_blueprint_transfer.py:80-83 says each search scores 2 budgets x 2 models x 3 allocation methods. That is the laptop grid. On the server, by the lines above, it is 8 budgets x 5 models x 5 allocation methods, plus 3 importance methods and 4 representation counts.
- The Nogueira pool width total_features counts base representation features only (308). If selected features include augmentation representations, the union can exceed it and the guard at 221-223 silently replaces the width. Whether build_fold_hybrid's feature info lists augmentation representations: could not determine without opening it.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- c24_blueprint_transfer.py:80-81: the comment says the search runs over 3 inner folds. c24 passes no n_folds, so find_best_hybrid uses DEFAULT_N_FOLDS = 5 (find_best_hybrid.py:3706, 8670).
- The attached search-call note gives 8,640 configurations per search. By _expected_config_count (find_best_hybrid.py:618-633) it is 8,160: model-evaluator pairs sum to 17 (rf, lightgbm, dnn get 3 each; xgboost, svm get 4 each), not 18.
- c24_blueprint_transfer.py:427-431 with hybrid.py:6567-6574: the Nogueira stability index leaves out every augmentation feature a fold selected. On the 32 datasets that run 'uncapped', two folds can differ only in augmentation features and still score as identical.
- c24_blueprint_transfer.py:787-794: run standalone through __main__, load_data's loaders set 'augmentations': None (for example tests/experiments/_shared.py:4725 for molecular datasets). Only the complexity run_all path (complexity_helpers.py:1003-1044) fills them. So the same file runs 'none' or 'uncapped' depending on how it is launched. Whether the --augment flag of load_data fills them: could not determine without reading load_data's augment branch.
- Step 4 records suzuki's allocation cut as HELD (DECISIONS.md:407). c24 searches all five allocation methods there, which matches the hold. It is listed so the R3 finding is not read as covering suzuki's allocation axis.


## complexity c33 (tests/experiments/complexity/c33_budget_overfitting.py)

What it measures: For each model and each feature budget, it measures the hybrid's score on the held-out outer fold. It compares that with the score the inner search predicted, including budgets above the training row count.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. c33 is in the complexity list SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (tests/experiments/complexity/complexity_helpers.py:872) and in the complexity run order (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:312-314). submit_everything.sh queues complexity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213, 350-370). A tiny import this session counted 41 such datasets. c33 has no dataset check or skip of its own (c33_budget_overfitting.py:595-729).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: The general search scores six models on every dataset: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm from the runner's config, plus 'linear'. The distance search scores the same five without 'linear'. gp is never added. 'linear' is sklearn Ridge(alpha=1e-6) for regression and LogisticRegression(C=1e6) for classification.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two approved models from Step 1. No ridge. On abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, gp is one of the two.

All 41 datasets break the rule. Each gets four models beyond its approved pair in the general search, and three in the distance search.

On those five gp datasets, one approved model is never scored at all. 'linear' is a near-unregularised ridge under another name. Ridge is excluded everywhere.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: The base representations are scored per model and per outer fold. Rank 1 is the nested-CV pick from the inner search. Rank 2 comes from top_base_reps on the same inner search. Both get held-out scores.

The hybrids are three per model, following the 2026-10-02 rule. general1 is the nested winner. general2 is the next differently-labelled recipe from the same inner search. distance1 is the winner of a second nested run on the distance tier.

The experiment's main output is different again. It reports one held-out hybrid per budget, per model, per fold, to draw the budget curve.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

The per-budget curve is a legitimate design difference, because the budget is what c33 measures. The rule set is not one: it gives 3 hybrids per model, not 2.

It applies that set to six models, not the dataset's two. rank 2 only feeds delta_vs_rank2_single on the budget curve. The three hybrid slots are compared with rank 1 only.

top2_hybrids_per_fold records the inner search's own scores on outer-train rows. None of those are held-out scores.

### R6 missing search: yes

Code: Both nested runs pass own_search=True. The cold-search refusal is skipped, so every per-fold search is built inside the c33 job. Failures are handled in three ways.

An inner search that raises on one outer fold is printed, and that fold is skipped. If it raises on all 3, nested_cv_evaluate raises, and run_all records c33 as FAILED.

A failed distance nested run is caught. It is listed in rule_missing, and c33 continues without distance1.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, with nothing refusing or skipping it.

Nothing refuses. The two skips above happen only after a search has raised. They are not refusals.

### Other problems

- general2 can skip a recipe that really is different. _bp_identity compares allocation method, importance method, budget, evaluator, step size and augmentation strategy. It leaves out representation count (Blueprint.rep_count, find_best_hybrid.py:1530) and the representation list.

With counts 3 and all on the grid, the second-ranked configuration can differ from the winner only in its count. It is then treated as the winner and skipped (c14_cross_domain_summary.py:70-74, 170-173).
- Rank 1 and rank 2 of the base representations come from two different code paths. Rank 1 is nested_cv_evaluate's pick from inner.baselines (find_best_hybrid.py:11084-11094). Rank 2 is top_base_reps(require_full=False) (c33:834-837).

The comment at c33:805-810 says they agree on the direction for every current run. I did not check whether their rank 1 can differ. If it can, the 'rank 2' representation could be the nested pick itself.
- Adaptive pruning (calibrated, own_search_kwargs at _shared.py:804) removes configurations during each inner search. So the per-budget winners, general2 and the top-2 lists come only from the configurations that survived pruning. That pruning is not part of the DECISIONS record.
- The runner builds or reads two whole-dataset searches on every dataset before c33 starts (complexity_helpers.py:1065-1114). c33 reads neither. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH a refused one is stored as None and the run continues.
- The docstring cites nested_cv_evaluate at find_best_hybrid.py:9263-9325 and :9553-9581 (c33:24-27). nested_cv_evaluate now starts at :10561, so those line numbers are stale.
- svm is dropped above its training-row limit and gp is never named. I did not check which approved pairs that affects on the large datasets (kiba, bindingdb_kd, qm9).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3, representation count: c33 runs only counts 3 and all on every dataset, so datasets that keep count 2 or 5 never get them. The agent listed only the 14 'keep all' datasets. Count 5 is kept but never run on abagym_Ang2, ddg_combined, ginkgo_colloidal, adme_hlm and ginkgo_hic. Count 2 is kept but never run on bindingdb_kd and flab_binding_koenig. Both 2 and 5 are kept but never run on ginkgo_acsins and ginkgo_pr_cho. Sources: DECISIONS.md:565, 569, 573, 577, 579, 584-587; FAST_REP_COUNTS at src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:3071.
- R3, distance budgets: c33 runs DISTANCE_BUDGETS up to 500 features on every dataset (c33_budget_overfitting.py:754-755). Step 7 ends the range at 100 features on abagym_Ang2 and cdr_flexibility, and at 250 on suzuki (DECISIONS.md:613, 623, 646). So c33 runs cut budgets above the range there, not only below it.
- R6: when an inner search raises on an outer fold, nested_cv_evaluate prints a line, stores None for that fold and moves on (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:10898-10911). That fold is then scored on no hybrid, and nothing rebuilds it. Every hybrid for that fold is then missing: the per-budget values, general1, general2 (marked missing at c14_cross_domain_summary.py:158-160) and the rank-2 lookups. The distance nested run's failure is caught the same way and only recorded in rule_missing (c33_budget_overfitting.py:776-779).
- R1 knock-on: the general search's 'match' evaluator stands for the downstream model's own type (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:3691-3693). So for 'linear', the evaluator that picks features inside the search is the near-unregularised ridge as well (unverified that 'match' resolves to 'linear' specifically; the resolution code was not opened).


## similarity s01 (tests/experiments/similarity/s01_similarity_baseline.py)

What it measures: For each base representation on all rows, s01 computes the Spearman correlation between pair distance and activity difference (sampled pairs), the share of 5 nearest neighbours with a very different activity, and a structure-activity landscape index; it fits no model and builds no hybrid.

Datasets: submit_everything.sh queues the similarity category on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis. That is 41 datasets (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213, 350-374; a small import this session printed 41). Each job runs run_dataset.py, which calls similarity_helpers.run_all (tests/experiments/run_dataset.py:209-214). run_all calls should_skip_experiment before s01 (tests/experiments/similarity/similarity_helpers.py:1582). That skips s01 on the 6 nucleotide datasets, gb_human_enhancers_cohn and nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3, nt_promoter_tata (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3557, 3672-3675, 3703). s01 is not in the over-15,000-row skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685). Above 15,000 rows it switches to a sampled nearest-neighbour path instead (s01_similarity_baseline.py:47, 78-85). So s01 produces numbers on 35 datasets.

Code: s01 fits no downstream model. It computes distance matrices on each base representation and scores them against the labels with Spearman correlation, neighbour counts and a landscape index. No model is named or used in its run() or per-representation functions.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two approved models from Step 1, knn only where Step 9 allows, no ridge.
