### Other problems

- s01 runs after two whole-dataset searches it never uses. run_all builds the general search (similarity_helpers.py:1396) and the distance search (1425) before the skip check at 1582. So on the 6 nucleotide datasets s01 is skipped, but its process still builds or reads both searches first.
- s01 records a permutation p-value and a 'sac_significant' flag (p < 0.05) per representation, plus a scipy Spearman p-value (s01_similarity_baseline.py:195-198, 205, 211, 222, 261, 272). The owner's standing rule says no significance tests. That rule names folds and datasets; whether it also covers this within-representation shuffle test is hers to decide. The same file also stores the spread of the shuffled correlations (sac_permutation_null_sd, 218-219), which is a raw spread, not a test.
- Distances are standardised and computed over all rows of each representation (s01_similarity_baseline.py:189). s01 makes no prediction, so no held-out fold exists for this to leak into. The result describes the whole dataset, not held-out performance.
- The dense path (up to 15,000 rows) and the sampled nearest-neighbour path (above 15,000 rows) compute the three scores by different methods (s01_similarity_baseline.py:78-85, 179-285). The file says they compute 'the same three scores'; I did not check that the two paths agree numerically. On the 41-dataset roster this only matters for datasets above 15,000 rows, which I did not list.
- The standalone __main__ path (s01_similarity_baseline.py:288-302) calls get_config and load_data and runs no search. It differs from the cluster path only in skipping run_all's start-up searches and its NaN/zero screen of representations (similarity_helpers.py:1324).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The two start-up searches that s01's process runs use none of the decided cuts. models=None gives the engine's five models, not the dataset's two (DECISIONS.md:9-51; _shared.py:5461, 5574). s01 reads neither result, so this is a cost to s01's job, not a fault in its numbers.
- Budgets in those searches are FULL_BUDGETS 10-2000 features and DISTANCE_BUDGETS 10-500 features (_shared.py:494-495), not the per-dataset ranges in Step 2 v3 and Step 7 (e.g. DECISIONS.md:613 abagym_Ang2 distance 25-100).
- Those searches run uncapped and capped augmentation on every dataset that has augmentation representations (_shared.py:5543-5548). Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 of 41 datasets and keeps only uncapped on ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_colloidal (DECISIONS.md:654-698).
- No code reads the decisions. A grep for 'precompute_cuts', 'DECISIONS.md' and similar names in src/kirby, tests/experiments/_shared.py and tests/experiments/dataset_policy.py returned nothing.
- ddg_combined has 8 representations in DATASET_REPS 'general', not 10 (python import of similarity_helpers.DATASET_REPS).
- The standalone __main__ path loads the 'fast' preset by default (_shared.py:9264; s01_similarity_baseline.py:298) and skips the nucleotide check (only run_all calls it, similarity_helpers.py:1582). So it can score a different representation list from the cluster path.


## similarity s02 (tests/experiments/similarity/s02_hybrid_similarity.py)

What it measures: It measures whether a hybrid's distance, unweighted and importance-weighted, tracks activity differences better than the best single representation's distance does. The statistic is the Spearman correlation between pairwise distance and pairwise activity difference.

Datasets: s02 runs inside the similarity suite. submit_everything.sh queues that suite on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis, which is 41 datasets (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). should_skip_experiment then drops s02 on nucleotide datasets (_shared.py:3672-3675, 3703) and on datasets over 15,000 rows (_shared.py:3665, 3684, 3713). DECISIONS Step 9 names those as the six nucleotide datasets plus kiba and bindingdb_kd. I did not load data to check domains or row counts. That leaves 33 datasets: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, cdr_flexibility, ddg_combined, flab_binding_adams, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, the five ginkgo_*, herg, herg_ki, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, logd, qm9, suzuki, tcga_brca_pam50, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass. The similarity runner passes s02 all eight budgets (similarity_helpers.py:1610-1618).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: Every hybrid s02 scores is ranked for knn alone (_SAC_MODEL_KEY='knn', s02:110, 807-811). The two general hybrids come from a general search that names knn, using MAIN_MODELS_WITH_KNN (_shared.py:7124-7127). The distance hybrid comes from the distance search, which also names knn (_shared.py:6774-6777). Report rows read six models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm and knn (s02:312-319, 863-869). On the small datasets gp is added to every one of these searches (_shared.py:1084-1125, 5895). The dataset's two approved models are never used to pick or score a hybrid. ridge is never named.

Decisions: Step 1 gives each dataset two models, and knn is not one of them. Step 9 allows knn as the model in the distance search for s02 on the non-nucleotide datasets. Step 9 says nothing about knn in the general search.

### R2 per fold: NO

The per-fold block (s02:144-260) rebuilds the features on each fold's training rows (s02:199-208). That rebuild still uses the recipe chosen on all rows. Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: s02 never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search goes to find_best_hybrid(cache=True) on all rows (_shared.py:5845-5896). It is built on all rows in three cases: KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is off, 50% or more is already stored, or 500 or fewer configurations are left (find_best_hybrid.py:690-716). Otherwise it raises (find_best_hybrid.py:718-750). That error is caught, a warning is printed, and that search is skipped (_shared.py:6108-6114, 7134-7142). The hybrid is then written as an empty slot with a reason (s02:404-409, 818-820). submit_everything.sh turns the refusal on by default (lines 94, 364).

Decisions: If a per-fold search does not exist, the experiment must build it itself, not refuse or skip.

### Other problems

- The family kept for each hybrid slot is the one with the higher held-out delta (s02:887-898). That same held-out delta is then reported as the cell's result (s02:908-917). So the choice between the two families is made on the numbers that are reported.
- The numbers at the top of the result file are the whole-dataset ones. They are the primary cell's best_sac, weight_methods and sac_delta_comparator (s02:936-948). s02:929-931 says s09 and three plotting scripts read them. That cell's best representation was picked on all rows (s02:659-690), and its hybrid was built on all rows (s02:416-417).
- No general predictive search with knn is precomputed. The knn precompute pass is '--with-knn --objectives similarity' (_precompute_passes.sh:34). s02 still asks for one (s02:751-752 with _shared.py:7124-7127). This is from reading the code, not from a run. knn rows are counted under the same stored-result identity as the five-model rows (find_best_hybrid.py:661-686, result_cache.py:46). So if 50% or more of a grid is stored, the missing knn rows are built on all rows inside the s02 job. The get_rule_hybrids docstring says this slot is reported missing instead (_shared.py:7086-7090).
- s02 asks for the similarity family on tz_her2_binary, tz_her2_multiclass and tcga_brca_pam50 (s02:751-752), and checks no dataset names. The policy says objective='similarity' is undefined on those three (dataset_policy.py:608-645), and the precompute skips them (precompute_hybrids.py:689). What the engine does when s02 asks there could not be determined without running it.
- lhasa_herg has no stored distance search (DECISIONS.md:609, 750), and Step 7 has no row for it. s02's distance hybrid on lhasa_herg is built on all rows or refused, depending on the cold-search switch.
- flab_expression_koenig and logd are in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS. So s02's reads there use the fast lists (_shared.py:1046-1081). The DECISIONS fast-tier table does not list either dataset (DECISIONS.md:352-363).
- The weighted whole-dataset arm computes feature importance on all rows (s02:649, 493). It sits beside the per-fold arm, whose importance comes from each fold's training rows (s02:215-220).
- The comment at s02:99-104 says the recipe comes from get_fitted_pool_hybrid. Since 2026-10-02 it comes from get_rule_hybrids (s02:807).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3/R1: before s02 runs, similarity run_all builds or reads whole-dataset searches. The general search uses models=None, the full grid and augmentation (similarity_helpers.py:1393-1407). The distance search uses DISTANCE_MODELS (1422-1439). Both are subject to the same cold-search rule. The first agent listed this under search calls but did not flag it against R1/R3.
- R3: for the distance slot at 1000 and 2000 features, the ranking falls back to every stored budget, 10 to 500 (_shared.py:6855-6872). So one distance recipe can be built and scored up to three times, labelled 500, 1000 and 2000. Step 7 gives most datasets a 100-500 range (DECISIONS.md:613-650), and s02 still asks every one of the 8 budgets.
- R3 Step 8: on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic the general pool still asks for 'capped' and 'uncapped' (_shared.py:6040-6046). Step 8 keeps 'uncapped' only, on the distance search (DECISIONS.md:678-679). On ginkgo_hic the distance pool also asks for 'capped' under 10,000 rows (_shared.py:6036), which Step 8 excludes ('uncapped only').
- R2: the per-fold single-representation side and the per-fold hybrid side use s02's own cv_split (s02:190-191). With fold_i=None the pool's fold partition is never compared against it. The hybrid recipe and the per-fold rebuild therefore have no tie to the folds being scored, and there is no n_folds_in_pool check.


## similarity s03 (tests/experiments/similarity/s03_feature_concentration.py)

What it measures: For each hybrid, it measures how much mutual information with the label sits in the features the hybrid kept from each representation, against all features, a random subset of the same size and a PCA projection, all on every row with no held-out fold.

Datasets: 35 datasets. submit_everything.sh queues the similarity suite on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213, 350-366); s03 is in the similarity list (tests/experiments/similarity/similarity_helpers.py:1141-1145; tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:315). should_skip_experiment skips s03 on nucleotide datasets (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675, 3703), and nucleotide means a name starting nt_ or gb_ (_shared.py:3557, 3641-3642, 4241, 4284). That removes gb_human_enhancers_cohn and the five nt_ datasets, leaving the other 35 of the 41. s03 is not in the over-15,000-rows skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685), so kiba and bindingdb_kd run.

### R1 models: NO

Code: s03 asks for rf, lightgbm and dnn on every dataset. run_all passes exactly those three names, keeping only the ones the search scores by default. No dataset gets its own two models. knn and ridge are never asked for.

Decisions: Each dataset's two approved models from Step 1. knn is not among them (Step 9 lists s03 nowhere as needing knn). ridge is excluded.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: s03 never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search goes to find_best_hybrid on every row. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, more than 500 missing configurations raise RuntimeError. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that member. get_rule_hybrids lists the slot as missing, and s03 writes {'error': 'slot empty: ...'} for that cell. submit_everything.sh turns the refusal on by default.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

- R3 augmentation: 26 of the 35 datasets carry augmentation representations (printed this session from DATASET_REPS). s03 reads their uncapped and capped searches. Step 8 cuts both on 24 of them and keeps only uncapped-on-distance for ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic.
- R3 importance, allocation, evaluator and representation count: the read never filters on them. On every dataset with a Step 3-6 or Step 7 cut, the top-ranked recipe can be a cut configuration. humanness_therapeutic is the only one of the 35 with no cut on any axis s03 touches.

## similarity s04 (tests/experiments/similarity/s04_activity_cliffs.py)

What it measures: It measures how well kNN (k=5) predicts the activity of cliff molecules versus non-cliff molecules, for each single representation, the pool's top two single representations, up to six pool hybrids, and one rf baseline.

Datasets: Nine datasets: adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, herg, herg_ki, lhasa_herg, logd, qm9. The similarity job is queued on all 41 datasets (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). s04 returns a skip on any dataset whose domain is not 'molecular' (s04_activity_cliffs.py:159-175). The domain comes from the registry (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3950-3960). Printed this session with one import: 9 molecular, 19 antibody, 3 reaction, 2 dta, 2 tcga, 6 nucleotide. The six nucleotide datasets are also skipped earlier by should_skip_experiment (_shared.py:3672-3675, called at similarity_helpers.py:1582). s04 is not in the over-15,000-row skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every hybrid arm and every base-representation arm is scored with kNN (k=5). The only other model fitted is rf, as one baseline on one representation per fold. No other model is fitted on any of the nine datasets.

Decisions: Step 1 approves svm+dnn on adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm and herg_ki. It approves dnn+svm on caco2 and logd, lightgbm+xgboost on herg and lhasa_herg, and dnn+lightgbm on qm9. Step 9 allows knn as a downstream model in the distance search on all nine. The two sides differ in two ways at once. First, none of the approved models is ever fitted, on any of the nine datasets. Second, rf is fitted, and rf is approved on none of them. kNN is also read from the general searches (models rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm, knn), and Step 9 covers only the distance search. Step 9 names s02, s05, s06, s08, s10 and s13 as the experiments that need knn; s04 is not on that list.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: For each held-out fold it calls get_rule_hybrids with fold_i set, passing the whole dataset's representations, labels and groups. That reads stored searches built on every row. Recipes and base representations are ranked by their mean over the other folds' stored scores. The fold's rows were inside every one of those searches. The file says this itself: it holds out the fold's scores, not its rows. The rf baseline's representation comes from the same read. A hybrid rebuilt with fewer than 10 representations is restricted using blueprint.rep_scores, which are whole-dataset scores, because s04 passes no fold-local scores. Only the plain per-representation kNN baselines are clean. Each one is fitted on the fold's training rows, and no search chooses it.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. Re-picking from stored per-fold scores of a whole-dataset search leaks.

### R3 same cuts: NO (partly)

Code: Every search it reads uses one global grid. General: FULL_BUDGETS (10 to 2000 features) with the engine's default methods; the fast list applies on herg, logd and qm9. Distance: DISTANCE_BUDGETS (10 to 500), evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm, and DISTANCE_MODELS. Augmentation: none, uncapped and capped on the 8 of 9 datasets that carry augmentation representations; lhasa_herg carries none. Within that grid it ranks only configurations scored at a budget of 100 features. Nothing reads DECISIONS.md.

Decisions: Per-dataset cuts from Steps 2-8. Budget: 100 features is below the decided general range on 7 of 9 datasets. Those are adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, logd and qm9 (500-2000) and herg_ki (250-2000). 100 is inside the range only on herg and lhasa_herg. It is inside the distance range (100-500) on the eight datasets that have one. Importance: herg_ki cuts deeplift in the general search, and the full default runs it. In the distance search adme_hlm and herg_ki cut deeplift and caco2 cuts treeshap. Allocation: caco2 and herg_ki cut wglobal_power2, and the default runs it. Representation counts in the general search: adme_hlm cuts 2 and 3. adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2 and herg_ki cut 2, 3 and 5. The default runs 2, 3, 5 and all. Distance evaluators: qm9 cuts svm, which DISTANCE_EVALUATORS contains. Augmentation: Step 8 cuts it on all nine, and the read asks for uncapped and capped on eight. Steps 2-7 decide nothing for the searches built under objective='similarity'. They also decide nothing for the general search that scores knn. s04 reads both of those.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For kNN, per fold, it reads up to six hybrids: the top 2 general and top 1 distance hybrid from the predictive searches, and the same three from the similarity searches. Each hybrid is scored unweighted and importance-weighted, so up to 12 hybrid arms. The base side has all 10 representations, unweighted and weighted, plus the pool's rank-1 and rank-2 single representations. For rf it fits one base representation per fold and no hybrid. The docstring says kNN is the experiment's design.

Decisions: Per each of the dataset's two approved models, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. The two differ in three ways at once. The models are kNN and rf, not the approved pair. Each model gets 3 hybrids per family, across two families, instead of 2. And rf gets 1 base representation and no hybrid.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: No per-fold search is read or built. When a stored search is missing, get_precomputed_search builds it on every row of the dataset inside the s04 job. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH it is refused instead, when under 50% of its configurations are stored and over 500 are left. _iter_pool_searches catches the refusal, prints a warning and skips that search. The empty slot is then listed in results['rule_missing'], and get_rule_hybrids prints a [rule] line. If the whole read raises, no hybrid arm runs and hybrid_search_status records the error. If the rf read fails, the rf baseline falls back to the representation with the best kNN score.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, on that fold's training rows. Skips and refusals do not comply.

### Other problems

- The feature budget is fixed at 100 (s04_activity_cliffs.py:293), and run_all passes s04 no budget (similarity_helpers.py:1600-1676 has no s04 block). On 7 of 9 datasets the decided general range starts at 250 or 500 features. The general-search slots rank only configurations at 100 features (_shared.py:6856-6858).
- The rf fallback representation is the one with the best kNN score_all (s04_activity_cliffs.py:947-951). score_all is the mean over all of this file's folds, the held-out fold included, so that fold's score can choose its own rf representation (960-961).
- _rule_as_pool sets fold0_pruned to None (s04_activity_cliffs.py:96). Its docstring says get_rule_hybrids does not pass that value through (79-81). get_rule_hybrids does return it (_shared.py:7210-7212). So fold 0 is always excluded from the fold_reselection block (s04_activity_cliffs.py:1108), whatever the pool reported.
- A hybrid with fewer than 10 representations is rebuilt per fold. Which representations it keeps is decided by blueprint.rep_scores, which are whole-dataset scores (s04_activity_cliffs.py:778-784, _shared.py:5256-5281). The comment at _shared.py:5349-5354 says whole-dataset rep_scores are not used; that holds for the budget split, not for this choice.
- lhasa_herg has no stored distance search (DECISIONS.md:609, 750). s04 reads the one run_all builds on all rows at start-up, or gets nothing if that build was refused.
- No decision in Steps 2-7 covers the searches under objective='similarity', or the general search that adds knn (MAIN_MODELS_WITH_KNN). s04 reads both, so no decided cut exists to apply to them.
- Step 9 names s02, s05, s06, s08, s10 and s13 as needing knn, not s04 (DECISIONS.md:702). s04 reads knn-ranked hybrids from both the general and distance searches.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Distance-search cuts the report left out. Step 7 cuts wglobal_power2 on herg_ki (DECISIONS.md:636). It cuts representation counts 2 and 3 on adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm and caco2 (617-619, 622), and 2, 3 and 5 on herg_ki (636). The distance read passes no allocation or representation-count list (_shared.py:6773-6777, 5863-5896). So the engine defaults run there: five allocation methods including wglobal_power2, and counts 2, 3, 5 and all (find_best_hybrid.py:3070, 3684-3690).
- The predictive general search with knn is never precomputed, by design. The precompute scores knn on the general tier only under the similarity objective. Its own comment says 'There is no six-model PREDICTIVE search on the general tier' (submit_precompute_extra_passes.sh:9-13, 21-24). s04 asks for exactly that search for kNN (_shared.py:7124-7127). It names the models, so the in-memory store is skipped (_shared.py:6782-6792). On every dataset, then, s04 either builds a whole-dataset six-model search in its own job or is refused. If refused, both predictive general slots are empty.
- The report could not tell whether similarity-objective rows carry model='knn'. The engine prints that under a geometry objective no downstream model is fitted, 'so every model shows the same number' (find_best_hybrid.py:5561-5566). The knn pass names the six-model list under that objective (submit_precompute_extra_passes.sh:9-13). So knn rows exist there with the same scores as every other model. The two similarity-family general hybrids s04 calls kNN's are therefore not chosen by kNN's performance.
- logd runs at the fast grid in code (dataset_policy.py:692; applied at _shared.py:5895). DECISIONS' fast-tier table lists herg and qm9 but not logd (DECISIONS.md:352-363). For importance the two agree, since Step 3 keeps only lightgbm_gain on logd (DECISIONS.md:334). The fast representation counts are 3 and all (find_best_hybrid.py:3071). Step 6 keeps 'all stored rep counts' on logd (DECISIONS.md:594). Whether 2 and 5 were ever stored for logd: could not determine without reading the stored results.


## similarity s05 (tests/experiments/similarity/s05_knn_prediction.py)

What it measures: For each fold, it asks whether predicting each molecule's activity from its k nearest neighbours (k = 5 and 10) in a hybrid's features beats doing the same in each single representation's features, at each budget from 10 to 500 features.

Datasets: submit_everything.sh queues the similarity suite on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213, CATEGORIES at :95). That is 41 datasets per the helper map; I did not re-count the keys. similarity run_all calls should_skip_experiment before s05 (tests/experiments/similarity/similarity_helpers.py:1582). s05 is in NUCLEOTIDE_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675), and the domain is 'nucleotide' for names starting nt_ or gb_ (_shared.py:3557, 4284). So s05 is skipped on gb_human_enhancers_cohn, nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3 and nt_promoter_tata. s05 is not in the over-15,000-rows skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685), so it runs on kiba and bindingdb_kd. It runs on the remaining 35 datasets.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every model s05 fits is a k-nearest-neighbour model: the hybrid arms and the single-representation baselines alike (s05:479-483, 683-686, 815-817). It also builds a reference table for each model in DISTANCE_MODELS. That is rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm and knn, read from stored baseline scores with no new fit. Each model's delta is reported under delta_by_model. The hybrid arms are read from the general searches as well as the distance searches, with knn as the model.

Decisions: Step 1 gives two models per dataset, and knn is never one of them. Step 9 allows knn as a downstream model in the distance search on the 35 non-nucleotide datasets. It says nothing about knn in the general search. gp is approved on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: No search in s05 is built on a fold's training rows. For each fold it reads stored searches that ran over every row of the dataset. It ranks their configurations by the mean over the other folds' stored scores (get_fold_pool_recipes). The function's own note says it holds out the fold's scores, not its rows. s05 records this as recipe_selection 'other_folds_of_pool_search'. The two base representations per fold come from the same ranking. Only the final fit is per fold: build_fold_hybrid builds the chosen recipe on that fold's training rows. When a recipe used fewer representations than the pool, s05 passes no fold scores. build_fold_hybrid then picks which representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores, which the whole-dataset search measured.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. Re-picking from stored per-fold scores of a whole-dataset search leaks.

It uses those budgets for the general read and the distance read alike. run_all passes s05 no budgets. get_fold_pool_recipes ranks every stored configuration for the model at that budget. It does not filter by importance method, allocation method, internal evaluator or representation count. Any missing search is requested with FULL_BUDGETS or DISTANCE_BUDGETS and engine-default or fast-tier lists. Augmentation: s05 passes data['augmentations'], so _pool_conditions reads 'uncapped' and 'capped' members whenever the dataset has augmentation representations.

Decisions: Steps 2-7 set per-dataset budget ranges, importance methods, allocation methods, evaluators and representation counts for the general and distance searches. Step 8 cuts augmentation everywhere except ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, which keep uncapped only, on the distance search.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: One downstream model, knn. Per fold and budget, the hybrid side is 2 general plus 1 distance hybrid for each of two search families: features chosen for prediction and features chosen under objective='similarity'. That is 6 hybrids, each scored unweighted and importance-weighted at k = 5 and 10. The base side per fold is the top 2 single representations for knn (pool_base_rep, pool_base_rep2). They are taken from the distance read, not from the general read that get_rule_hybrids uses for its own base_reps. Every representation is also scored at each k and enters the held-out reselection.

Decisions: For each of the dataset's two models, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: s05 never builds a per-fold search. A missing stored search goes through get_precomputed_search, which calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH (on by default in submit_everything.sh) it is refused when more than 500 configurations are left. _iter_pool_searches then prints a warning and skips that search. get_rule_hybrids lists the empty slots, and s05 stores them in results['rule_missing'] and prints a per-fold warning. The file's docstring tells the user to run tests/precompute_hybrids.py first.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment must build it itself, with no separate precompute script.

### Other problems

- gp is an approved model on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho. The reference table loops over DISTANCE_MODELS, which has no gp, so gp gets no reference row on those five (s05:1086; _shared.py:568).
- s05 asks for the similarity-objective family on every dataset. It has no check for tcga_brca_pam50, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass, where dataset_policy says that objective is undefined (dataset_policy.py:636-645). A failure there becomes a printed warning and a skipped search (_shared.py:6108-6114).
- Fold 0 is dropped from the held-out reselection whenever any rule hybrid was read (s05:1355-1357). So the number s05 says to report uses 4 of 5 folds on every dataset where the pool returned hybrids.
- The importance-weighted single-representation baseline always uses lightgbm_gain (s05:793-795). Step 3 cuts lightgbm_gain on buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer (DECISIONS.md:314, 316, 327, 328).
- run_all passes s05 a 'conditions' argument (similarity_helpers.py:1622), but s05 never reads it. The loop names hybrid_unweighted and hybrid_weighted itself (s05:605).
- The general read passes a budget from 10 to 500 features. When no knn configuration was stored at that budget, it ranks over every stored budget instead (_shared.py:6855-6872). The matrix is then built at the asked budget anyway (s05:536), so the recipe was picked at a different budget from the one it is built and scored at. s05 records this in pool_budget_relaxed_folds (s05:734-736).
- The base representations come from the distance read (s05:901, _fold_pool distance=True at :331). get_rule_hybrids takes its own base representations from the general read (_shared.py:7183-7185), and s05 discards those. So the base side and the general hybrids are ranked on two different stored searches.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3 count: 30 of the 32 non-nucleotide Step 7 datasets read distance budgets that Step 7 cut. The audit said 31. Only humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc match 10-500 (DECISIONS.md:638, 648; nucleotide skip at _shared.py:3672-3675).
- R4: the held-out number s05 says to report (fold_reselection_result) compares the hybrid cells with every representation at every neighbour count. It does not use the top 2 base representations s05 computes. pool_base_rep and pool_base_rep2 are kept out of the reselection on purpose (s05_knn_prediction.py:888-890, 1365-1366).
- s05's comment at s05_knn_prediction.py:1352-1354 says get_rule_hybrids does not pass through fold 0 pruning. It does (_shared.py:7206-7213). So fold 0 is dropped whether or not any search pruned on it (s05:1355-1357).
- R3, fast-tier nuance: herg, qm9, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass have a stored grid that is the decided cut for allocation, importance and representation count (DECISIONS.md:348-363). s05 does not break those three axes there. Budgets and augmentation still break. qm9's Step 7 svm evaluator cut (DECISIONS.md:645) is not applied.


## similarity s06 (tests/experiments/similarity/s06_applicability_domain.py)

What it measures: For each held-out molecule it measures the distance to its k nearest training molecules in each representation and in each hybrid, and correlates that distance with a random forest's prediction error (Spearman), plus conformal interval width and coverage.

Datasets: submit_everything.sh queues the similarity category on every DATASET_REPS dataset (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:95, 205-220). The similarity run_all calls should_skip_experiment before s06 (similarity_helpers.py:1582-1588). s06 is in NUCLEOTIDE_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS (_shared.py:3672-3675), so it is skipped on the six nucleotide datasets: gb_human_enhancers_cohn and the five nt_* (dataset_policy.py:321, 324 give their domain). s06 is not in the over-15,000-rows skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685), so kiba and bindingdb_kd are included. Result: 35 of the 41 Step 1 datasets. s06 itself has no dataset check, including none for the three datasets where objective='similarity' is undefined (dataset_policy.py:644-645).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Two models are used. knn picks every hybrid recipe and the comparator representation from the stored searches. rf is fitted on every dataset: it produces the prediction errors, the neutral-model errors, and every conformal interval. rf also scores the feature admission when each predictive hybrid is rebuilt per fold. The report rows also read stored scores for six models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm, knn. Those are reads, not fits.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two Step 1 models. knn is allowed in the distance search for s06 on 35 datasets (Step 9). Step 9 says nothing about knn in the general search.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe comes from searches run over all rows of the dataset. get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index, so it ranks on the mean over all folds of those searches. The recipe is fixed once and rebuilt on each s06 fold's training rows. The comparator representation is also ranked on the whole-dataset distance search. When a recipe uses fewer than all representations, which ones are kept comes from blueprint.rep_scores, measured on all rows.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: It does not compare model scores, so it has no per-model 2+2 set. knn alone picks up to six hybrids: per search family (predictive, similarity) the top 2 general and the top 1 distance recipe. Every base representation, and its importance-weighted twin, is an arm. The top 2 base representations and top 2 hybrids for knn, and a 2+2 grid for six models, are only reported from the stored distance search. After the run, the named comparator is replaced by the representation with the best reported correlation.

Decisions: Per each of the dataset's two models, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: s06 never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search is built on all rows inside the job, unless KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is set. With it set, it is built when 500 or fewer configurations are left, otherwise refused. A refused search is printed as a warning and skipped. Unfilled hybrid slots go to results['rule_missing']. If no hybrid at all comes back, s06 returns an error and measures nothing. kiba, bindingdb_kd and lhasa_herg have no stored distance rows.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist is built by the experiment itself.

### Other problems

- The comparator representation is replaced after the run by the one with the best reported correlation (s06:1271-1299). That correlation is the outcome itself, measured on every fold, so the named comparator is chosen from the result it is then compared on.
- Each hybrid recipe is ranked for knn. Each predictive hybrid is rebuilt per fold with rf scoring the feature admission, and the errors come from rf (s06:674-676, 703-713). So the arm differs from the searched recipe in two ways at once: the model that admits features and the model whose errors are measured.
- The budget is 100 features on every dataset (s06:132, 330; similarity_helpers.py:1606-1674 passes none). On 19 of the 35 datasets, 100 is outside the Step 2 general range: abagym_EGFR, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, tz_her2_multiclass. 100 is inside every Step 7 distance range.
- rf is an approved model on 8 of the 35 datasets: bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, humanness_therapeutic, kiba, suzuki. On the other 27, every error and every interval in s06 comes from a model outside the Step 1 pair.
- On flab_expression_koenig, logd, bindingdb_kd and kiba the code reads fast-grid searches (dataset_policy.py:688-711). DECISIONS lists only 10 fast-tier datasets, without these four (DECISIONS.md:352-363).
- The knn general read names MAIN_MODELS_WITH_KNN on tier 'general'. The get_rule_hybrids docstring says no predictive general search scores knn (_shared.py:7086-7090), so the predictive general1 and general2 arms may be missing or built live. Whether a stored knn general search exists on the server: could not determine; I did not look at the server.
- s06 asks for the similarity family on tcga_brca_pam50, tz_her2_multiclass and tz_her2_binary, where that objective is undefined (dataset_policy.py:644-645). s06 has no name check. What the engine does there could not be determined without running it.
- results['top3_base_reps'] is ranked by rf, the default of extract_top3_base_reps (s06:433; _shared.py:867), while every other ranking in the file is for knn.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R2/R3/R6: the similarity run_all runs precompute_hybrid_searches inside the job before s06, on every row. It builds the general search with the config grid and the general_distance search with DISTANCE_BUDGETS, DISTANCE_EVALUATORS and DISTANCE_MODELS (similarity_helpers.py:1392-1450). So missing searches are built by the experiment job, but on the whole dataset, on the global grid, not per fold.
- R3: _apply_small_dataset_models adds gp to the model list of every search s06 reads on datasets under 1,000 rows (_shared.py:1084-1126). That also applies to the knn general read and the distance read. Where gp is not in the Step 1 pair, those searches score a model outside it.
- Comparator mismatch after re-pointing. results['conformal']['hybrid_genuinely_tighter'] is set against the original cmp_rep (s06_applicability_domain.py:1244-1245). The per-fold printouts also use the original (s06:989, 1023). Then results['comparator_rep'] is overwritten with a different representation (s06:1287). The stored flag and the stored comparator name can refer to two different representations. The note at s06:1291-1295 says the re-point decides which representation the flag names, but the flag was computed before the re-point. This is not an R1-R6 problem, but it makes the result file contradict itself.
- R2: per fold, importance weights are computed with bp.importance_method on the fold's training rows (s06:680-682). But bp itself, its importance method and rep_scores, was chosen on all rows. Only the weights are refit, not the choice of method.


## similarity s08 (tests/experiments/similarity/s08_optimal_dimension.py)

What it measures: For each of six feature budgets (10 to 500 features), it measures how well distances in the hybrid predict activity differences, and how well each downstream model predicts, to see whether the two peak at different budgets.

Datasets: 33 datasets. submit_everything.sh queues the similarity category on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis, which is 41 (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). similarity run_all then skips s08 on the six nucleotide datasets: gb_human_enhancers_cohn and the five nt_* (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3557, 3672-3675, 3703; similarity_helpers.py:1582-1588). It also skips s08 above 15,000 rows (_shared.py:3665, 3684-3685, 3713). DECISIONS Step 9 says that removes kiba and bindingdb_kd (DECISIONS.md:702, 716, 735); I did not re-check their row counts. The 33 left, printed this session: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, cdr_flexibility, ddg_combined, flab_binding_adams, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg, herg_ki, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, logd, qm9, suzuki, tcga_brca_pam50, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary, tz_her2_multiclass. The budgets s08 sweeps are 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500 features on every dataset. run_all hands it FULL_BUDGETS (similarity_helpers.py:1289, 1623-1628) and s08 keeps only the DISTANCE_BUDGETS among them (s08:234-238).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: Every dataset gets the same six prediction models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm and knn (DISTANCE_MODELS). They are fitted on every hybrid cell and on every single representation, in every fold. svm drops out above 10,000 rows. gp is never fitted. The optimal-budget trade-off and Pareto front are computed against rf alone.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models. knn is allowed here only as a downstream model in the distance search (Step 9 lists s08). Five approved pairs include gp: abagym_Ang2 and abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn). On those five, s08 never fits gp, so it lacks one of the two approved models. On all 33 datasets it fits three non-knn models outside the approved pair. Fewer are fitted where svm drops out. rf is approved on 6 of the 33: bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, humanness_therapeutic and suzuki. So on the other 27, the trade-off and Pareto numbers are read off a model outside the pair. knn is also asked for a recipe from the general search, in the general1/general2 slots. Step 9 covers knn in the distance search only.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe comes from get_rule_hybrids called with no fold index. That ranks configurations by their mean over all folds of a search run on every row. s08 passes the whole-dataset reps and labels. The fold loop rebuilds each recipe on the fold's training rows (build_fold_hybrid). But the allocation method, importance method, internal evaluator, representation count and augmentation condition were all chosen on all rows. When a recipe uses fewer representations than the pool, build_fold_hybrid picks WHICH ones from blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores are measured on all rows. The headline fields are computed on all rows with no folds: sac_rho, violation_rate, dist_corr_with_full and mle_id per budget, and best_sac_budget and the Pareto front built from them. The top2_base_reps, top2_hybrids, top2_pairs_by_model and hybrid_deltas rows read the whole-dataset distance search's own scores. s08 marks its fold_reselection calls recipe_selection='whole_dataset'.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. The whole-dataset precompute does not comply, and neither does re-picking from its stored scores.

Code: Every search s08 reads goes through get_precomputed_search. No per-dataset Step 2-8 cut is applied. General reads use all 8 budgets (10-2000 features) and the engine default lists. Step 7 distance budget ranges: only humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc keep all six of s08's budgets. lhasa_herg has no Step 7 row. ### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: The set is chosen once for the whole dataset, not per fold. For each of six budgets, two families (predictive, similarity) and three slots (general1, general2, distance1), it builds one cell. That is 36 cells. In each cell, the similarity numbers use knn's recipe in that slot. Each model's prediction score uses that model's own recipe in that slot. So each model gets 3 hybrids per family per budget, not 2. On base representations, every representation is fitted with every model in every fold. It reports the top 3 per model by mean held-out score (top3_by_model), and top 3 by rf from the stored search (top3_base_reps). It also reports the top 2 per model from get_rule_hybrids (rule_rows_by_model) and from the distance search (top2_base_reps).

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. Sweeping budgets is this experiment's design. The hybrid count per model (3, not 2), the base count (3 or 2), and the whole-dataset choice are not part of that design.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: A missing search never becomes a per-fold search. get_precomputed_search calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. When KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is unset, it builds the whole-dataset search inside the job. When it is set and more than 500 configurations are missing, find_best_hybrid raises. submit_everything.sh sets it by default. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that member. get_rule_hybrids lists the slot as missing. s08 then writes an error cell. If knn has no recipe in a slot, the whole cell is skipped, including every other model's prediction in that slot. s08 skips the slot under 'continue', not just the knn side. Three searches s08 reads are not built at start-up. The similarity-family searches: run_dataset.py never passes precompute_objectives. The predictive general search that scores knn, which needs MAIN_MODELS_WITH_KNN. And the distance search on lhasa_herg, which DECISIONS says is not stored.

Decisions: If a per-fold search is missing, the experiment builds it itself, per fold. No refusal, no skip.

- tests/experiments/_shared.py:5845-5896 (on-demand find_best_hybrid on rows passed)
- src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:636-650, 700-750 (refusal above KIRBY_COLD_SEARCH_MAX_CONFIGS, default 500)

Second agent (partly right): The refusal has two conditions, not one. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, find_best_hybrid proceeds if at least half of the configurations are already stored. It also proceeds if 500 or fewer are missing. It raises only when both fail: under half stored and more than 500 missing. Every other part of the claim holds. In every case the search that gets built covers all rows, not one fold.

### Other problems

- build_fold_hybrid is handed every training representation (s08:616, 627-634, 685-698). When a recipe used fewer representations than the pool, the ones kept are chosen from blueprint.rep_scores, measured on all rows (_shared.py:5256-5286). The comment at _shared.py:5349-5354 says whole-dataset scores are not used. That holds for the budget split only.
- The two held-out SAC comparisons do not measure the same distance. The hybrid side is importance-weighted and the single-representation side is unweighted (s08:1373-1374). The _unweighted block exists for the like-for-like comparison (s08:1381-1407).
- Weighted single-representation SAC (sac_rho_weighted) uses lightgbm_gain importance computed on all rows (s08:953, 982-985).
- Under the default cold refusal, the predictive family's general1 and general2 cells may never be built. The knn general recipe needs a search that scores knn on tier general. get_rule_hybrids' docstring says none exists for the predictive objective (_shared.py:7086-7090). When knn has no recipe, s08 skips the whole cell (s08:401-406, 446-454), so rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm get no prediction score in that slot either. Whether that search exists on disk: could not determine; I did not look at the server.
- Each similarity cell uses knn's recipe for its distance and SAC numbers. Each model's prediction score uses that model's own recipe (s08:398-399, 552-563). Within one cell, the similarity optimum and each model's optimum come from different recipes. So best_sac_budget against best_rf_budget compares recipes that differ in their search choices, not only in budget.
- The optimal-budget fields read results['budgets'], which holds only the predictive family's distance1 cells (s08:371-374, 1073). The similarity family and the general1/general2 slots never enter best_model_budgets, best_sac_budget or the Pareto front (s08:1100-1107, 1191-1199).
- top3_base_reps is reported once, from the first budget's search, ranked by rf (s08:437-445; _shared.py:867). It is three representations, by a model outside the approved pair on 27 of the 33 datasets.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Similarity-family recipes are rebuilt per fold under the predictive objective, not the similarity one. Whole-data build (build_hybrid_from_entry, _shared.py:7246-7249) passes the entry's objective. The per-fold calls to build_fold_hybrid pass no objective (s08:627-634, 685-698). build_fold_hybrid then omits it (_shared.py:5360-5361), so create_hybrid uses its default 'predictive' (hybrid.py:5636 signature, objective default at its line 48 of the def). Under 'similarity' the allocation methods score by predicting each molecule's activity from its five nearest neighbours (hybrid.py:130-133). So in a similarity cell, the all-rows hybrid and the per-fold hybrids are built under different objectives. That breaks R3 for every similarity-family cell.
- R6, a second skip: a model with no recipe of its own in a slot gets no prediction score in that cell. It is recorded in prediction_recipe_missing and nothing is built in its place (s08:552-563).
- R6, a third skip: when the knn entry has no blueprint, the cell is skipped with 'continue' and is not stored (s08:518-521).
- R6, a fourth skip: if the stored distance search cannot be read, the top-2 rows for the distance1 cell are left empty and only a print records it (s08:424-434, 739-741).
- Silent fold loss: if the per-fold hybrid build raises, that fold is dropped with no record (s08:635-636). A model fit that raises drops that fold's score with no record (s08:708-714, and s08:1000-1001 area for single representations). The number of folds behind each mean is not stored per model.
- flab_expression_koenig runs on the fast lists in code (it is in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS), but DECISIONS' fast-tier table lists only ten datasets and does not include it (DECISIONS.md:352-363). Step 3 keeps deeplift and treeshap there, Step 4 keeps softmax_T1, and Step 6 cuts 3. The fast lists drop the first three and keep the fourth (find_best_hybrid.py:3071-3072, 3674).

### Other problems

- It runs a Wilcoxon signed-rank test across datasets on every series (s09:702-720). The owner ruled out significance tests across datasets on 2026-09-27 (memory file feedback_no_significance_tests.md).

So the s02, s04 and s05 held-out numbers carry the plain 'held-out' label, although all three came from searches over every row.
- s09's source label for s04 says the per-fold scores are the overall metric, not rmse_cliff (s09:384-391). s04 now stores fold_score_stratum 'cliff_rows_only' (s04_activity_cliffs.py:1107). The two disagree about which rows the number covers.

That branch exits with an error; the working launcher is runbook/cross_one.sh.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3: s09 does not check that its inputs were computed under the decided cuts. Its input check reads four things only: distance coefficient, molecule count, label hash and fold count (s09_cross_dataset_summary.py:783-818). It never reads budget, importance method, allocation method, internal evaluator or representation count. Stored numbers from searches outside Steps 2-7 enter the same column as compliant ones. One example: s04 reads at budget 100 by default (s04_activity_cliffs.py:292), whatever the dataset's decided budget range is.
- R6: s09 builds nothing when an input is missing. A dataset whose s02, s04, s05, s06 or s08 file is absent prints 'Missing' and is left out (s09:765-767). An unreadable number is recorded as absent (s09:283-290, 310, 394-397, 508). The run refuses to write a file only when no quantity was read for any dataset (s09:648-652, 837-840). For a cross-dataset summary this is arguably correct, but it is a skip-and-continue path that the audit did not note.
- R1, s05 optimistic series: knn_delta takes the best over every budget, condition and k of the hybrid_weighted knn scores (s09:430-447). knn is allowed for s05 by Step 9 (DECISIONS.md:702). But this series and SAC_delta are read on all datasets s05/s02 ran on, including any not in the Step 9 'run' list. s09 does not filter the six nucleotide datasets marked 'not needed' (DECISIONS.md:726, 738-742); it relies on the inputs having skipped them. I could not determine from s09 alone whether those inputs exist on disk.


## similarity s10 (tests/experiments/similarity/s10_importance_downstream.py)

What it measures: On each fold it compares a distance-based model on z-scored features against the same model on features multiplied by their importance. It does this for kNN, a Gaussian process, an SVR, and a random forest given four neighbour-derived features. Each comparison is made per base representation and per hybrid.

Datasets: Every dataset the similarity runner is given, except the six whose domain is 'nucleotide'. submit_everything.sh queues the similarity category on 41 datasets: every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:95, :207-213). similarity run_all calls should_skip_experiment before each experiment (tests/experiments/similarity/similarity_helpers.py:1582). That skips s10 when domain == 'nucleotide' (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675, :3703). The loader sets that domain for names starting nt_ or gb_ (_shared.py:3557, :4241, :4284). So s10 runs on 35 datasets: the 41 minus gb_human_enhancers_cohn, nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3 and nt_promoter_tata. s10 is not in the over-15,000-row skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685), so kiba and bindingdb_kd run. Inside s10, Task 2 (Gaussian process) is skipped above 5,000 molecules and on classification sets (s10:1095-1097, :2624-2627). Task 3 (support vector regressor) is skipped above 10,000 molecules and on classification sets (s10:1427-1429, :2640-2643). No check stops the similarity-objective read on tcga_brca_pam50, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass, where dataset_policy.py:644 calls that objective undefined.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Four task models are fixed in the code and are the same on every dataset: knn for Task 1, gp for Task 2, svm (sklearn SVR, C=1, gamma='scale') for Task 3, and rf for Task 4. knn is allowed here, because Step 9 lists s10 and says run on all 35 non-nucleotide datasets. gp, SVR and rf are fitted whatever the dataset's two approved models are. Beside these, the top-2 blocks report base representations and hybrids for all six DISTANCE_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm and knn. Those blocks fit nothing; they are read off the stored search. The searches s10 reads score five models, plus knn on the distance search and gp on 9 datasets under 1,000 molecules.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models; knn only where Step 9 allows it, and Step 9 allows it for s10 on all 35 datasets s10 runs on.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe comes from a search run once over every row of the dataset. For each held-out fold, get_rule_hybrids re-ranks that search's stored per-fold scores on the other folds. This leaves fold i's scores out of the ranking, but not fold i's rows. s10's own result note says the same. For the Gaussian process where no gp rows exist, the recipe is re-ranked over every model, from the same whole-dataset searches. build_fold_hybrid then fits the recipe on the fold's training rows. But s10 passes no fold-local allocation scores. So a recipe that keeps fewer representations than the pool chooses which ones from blueprint.rep_scores, which were also measured on every row. The base-representation arms select nothing: every representation is scored on each fold, so they do not leak. The fold_reselection, top3, top2 and hybrid_deltas blocks are all read from the whole-dataset search.

Decisions: Every hybrid for a fold comes from a search on that fold's training rows only; re-picking from a whole-dataset search's stored per-fold scores does not comply.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: No search s10 reads applies a Step 2-7 cut. General searches use all eight budgets, 10 to 2,000 features. Distance searches use all six, 10 to 500. Importance methods, allocation methods and representation counts are the engine defaults, or the fast lists on the 14 code-fast datasets. General evaluators are the engine default four: match, rf, lightgbm, dnn. Distance evaluators are always knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm. Augmentation: whenever the dataset has augmentation representations, s10 asks for 'none', 'uncapped' and 'capped' searches. The exceptions are no 'uncapped' on kiba or bindingdb_kd, and no distance 'capped' at 10,000 molecules or more. s10 also ranks every stored recipe at 100 features (requested_budget=100). Step 2 cuts 100 from the general range on 19 of the 35 datasets.

Decisions: Per dataset: general budget range (Step 2 v3), importance cut (Step 3 v2), fast-tier stored grid, allocation cut (Step 4, suzuki held), evaluator cut (Step 5 v3), representation-count cut (Step 6), the distance search's own five cuts (Step 7), and augmentation per Step 8. Step 8 keeps augmentation only as 'uncapped' on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, on the distance search.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Hybrids: for each of the four task models and each fold, s10 takes three recipes per search family. Two come from the general searches (general1, general2) and one from the distance searches (distance1). There are two families, predictive and similarity, so up to six hybrid spaces exist, and all four tasks run in each. Base representations: each task scores every representation on every fold, with no top-2 selection. That is by design, since the question is whether weighting helps each representation. The only top-2 output is a report-only block per model (top2_base_reps, top2_hybrids, top2_pairs_by_model). It is read from the whole-dataset search with the whole-dataset rule, not per fold, and fits nothing.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: s10 builds no per-fold search anywhere. Every read goes through get_precomputed_search, which calls find_best_hybrid on all rows when nothing is in memory. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH set and more than 500 configurations missing, find_best_hybrid raises RuntimeError. submit_everything.sh sets that variable by default. _iter_pool_searches catches the error, prints a warning, and skips that search. s10 then records the empty slot in rule_missing, pool_family_errors or task_recipe_errors and does not build that hybrid space. If no fold gets a recipe, every hybrid arm is skipped and only the base-representation arms run. Without the variable, the missing search is built on all rows inside the job, which is a whole-dataset search, not a per-fold one. Searches likely to be missing: the predictive general search with knn, which get_rule_hybrids' docstring says does not exist; every similarity-family search, which similarity run_all does not build by default; and the distance search on bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg (Step 7, 'no distance rows').

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist is built by the experiment itself, per fold.

Second agent (partly right): The main fault stands: s10 builds no per-fold search, and a missing search is either refused and skipped or built on all rows. Two details are off. First, the similarity-family searches are not likely missing just because run_all skips them. precompute_hybrids.py builds them in separate passes. The 'knn' pass runs '--with-knn --objectives similarity' and the 'sim' pass runs predictive and similarity (_precompute_passes.sh:34-36). A '--distance' pass now runs both objectives (precompute_hybrids.py:1265-1276). They exist only if those passes were submitted, which could not be determined from code. Second, the refusal is not absolute. A missing search with 500 configurations or fewer left is built inside the job on all rows (find_best_hybrid.py:705-716). The knn predictive general search is missing by design, since the knn pass runs the similarity objective only.

### Other problems

- The comment at s10:228-233 says no stored search holds gp. _apply_small_dataset_models adds gp to both the general and distance searches on 9 datasets under 1,000 molecules (_shared.py:1112-1125). A tiny import printed them: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, humanness_therapeutic. On those 9 the Gaussian process task can get its own rows; elsewhere it gets another model's recipe.
- Where gp has no rows, its general1 and general2 recipes are the top configurations over every model. They come from the general search picked for rf (s10:2174-2180, :2266-2271, :2285-2287). results['task_recipe_chosen_by'] names the model whose score chose each one.
- results['pool_fold_read'] writes n_hybrids_per_fold = 1 (_N_POOL_HYBRIDS, s10:248, :2408). The same dict's 'rule' says top 2 general + top 1 distance per family (s10:2409). The two disagree.
- pool_fold0_pruned and pool_n_folds_seen are never filled (s10:1995-1996, :2413-2414), so the result always stores None and an empty list. The comment at s10:2019-2020 says get_rule_hybrids does not return them. It does: fold0_pruned and n_folds_in_pool at _shared.py:7206-7214.
- The per-representation weighted arms use lightgbm_gain importance on every dataset (s10:2470-2471). The hybrid weighted arms use the importance scores in feat_info (s10:543-551, _shared.py:4954-4978). build_fold_hybrid builds those with the recipe's own importance method (_shared.py:5293); I did not open create_hybrid to confirm. So the two weighted arms can differ in importance method as well as in features. Step 3 cut lightgbm_gain from the search on buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer.
- s10 asks for the similarity-objective family on every dataset (s10:205, :1934, :2013). dataset_policy.py:644 lists tcga_brca_pam50, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass as datasets where that objective is undefined. Neither s10 nor should_skip_experiment checks it. What the similarity reads return there could not be determined without running.
- Every hybrid arm is also built at all eight FULL_BUDGETS widths plus the recipe's own width (s10:274, :2357). That includes 1,000 and 2,000 features for distance recipes searched only up to 500. It also includes widths outside each dataset's Step 2 range. The docstring records this sweep as the owner's decision (s10:270-273); listed here as a fact, not a fault.
- top3_base_reps ranks by rf (extract_top3_base_reps default model='rf', _shared.py:867, called at s10:1954). It reads a search that was fetched for knn. The block is report-only.
- On humanness_therapeutic the axes s10's searches use happen to match Steps 2-8. It keeps all budgets, methods, evaluators and representation counts, and has no augmentation representations. It is the only one of the 35 datasets where that holds. I did not check pruning.

## similarity s11 (tests/experiments/similarity/s11_bayesian_optimization.py)

What it measures: It measures how fast a Bayesian optimisation loop finds the best molecules from a 5% seed set. It compares compact hybrid features with raw ECFP4, PCA, random projection, the best single representation and random picking.

Datasets: s11 runs only on regression datasets in the molecular or reaction domain, with at least 200 rows and at least 20 groups. The checks are in run(): domain at s11_bayesian_optimization.py:1054-1057, classification skip at :1064-1068, under 200 rows at :1070-1072, groups at :1080-1090. similarity run_all also skips nucleotide datasets first (similarity_helpers.py:1582, _shared.py:3672-3675). A registry print this session gives 10 of the 41 datasets that pass the domain and task checks. Molecular: adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, herg_ki, logd, qm9. Reaction: bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, suzuki. I could not determine whether each of these has 20 or more groups without loading the data. The launcher queues similarity on all 41 datasets, and the other 31 are skipped inside run().

### R1 models: NO

Code: Each seed's hybrid recipes are picked for downstream model rf at 50 features. The general search scores rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm. The distance search scores those five plus knn. The optimisation loop then fits a probabilistic surrogate on the chosen features: a scikit-learn GP, NGBoost, an MC-dropout network, or a Gauche Tanimoto GP. A GP also scores the hybrid build and picks the best single representation. None of the approved pairs is ever fitted in the loop.

Decisions: Step 1 pairs for the 10 datasets: adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, herg_ki svm+dnn; caco2, logd dnn+svm; qm9 dnn+lightgbm; bh_doyle_plates rf+dnn; buchwald_hartwig and suzuki rf+lightgbm. rf is approved on the three reaction datasets only. On the other seven, recipes are picked by a model the record excludes. Every search also scores three or four models outside the pair. The loop needs a model that predicts an uncertainty, so a surrogate other than the pair is a design difference; picking the recipe with rf is not.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: For each seed, every hybrid condition runs once per recipe slot: general1 (best for rf), general2 (next distinct recipe for rf) and distance1 (distance search's best for rf). That is 3 hybrids, all chosen by rf, and each is fed to each surrogate variant. Base representations are not ranked per model. The code uses fixed ECFP4 (RBF and Tanimoto kernels) and one best single representation chosen by GP cross-validation on seed rows. With --per-rep-bo it also runs every representation.

Decisions: R4 asks for the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids per approved model, per fold. The comparison here is between feature spaces under one optimisation surrogate, not between downstream models, so the shape differs by design. It still has 3 hybrids, not 2, and 1 chosen base representation, not 2.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: s11 builds its own per-seed searches through get_fold_best_search and search_on_fold. Nothing else warms them; a grep for bo_seed outside s11 finds nothing. The searches keep tier general or general_distance and the plain dataset name. So KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH applies to them, because the exemption reads dataset_name, not the namespaced cache name. submit_everything.sh sets that variable by default. A fresh seed search is 8,160 configurations on the general tier at full speed, or 816 at fast. It is 10,800 or 1,080 on the distance tier. All are above the 500 that a run may build itself. find_best_hybrid raises; search_on_fold catches it and stores None. s11 then records 'the search returned no recipe for rf' and skips every hybrid seed. The hybrid conditions end as skipped with reason no_blueprint.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- When the cold-search refusal fires, s11 records the reason for an empty slot as 'the search returned no recipe for rf' (s11:1148-1151). The refusal message sits in the failures record of search_on_fold's result (_shared.py:1491-1493), which s11 never reads. So the result file does not say the search was refused.
- The search picks recipes with rf, and a GP consumes the features, fitted on the same seed rows. The code comment says 'RF blueprint reused across surrogates — see EXPERIMENT_DEBUGGING.md' (s11:1131). I did not open that document.
- general2 is taken only from the augmentation condition that won general1 (s11:1161 uses that condition's search). A second-best recipe under another augmentation condition is never considered.
- Which end of the label is hunted is recorded for 3 datasets only: herg_ki, caco2, adme_mdr1 (s11:519-523). The other 7 fall back to the metric's direction (s11:1242-1244). All 7 use RMSE, so all 7 hunt the lowest label.
- That fallback includes the three reaction yield datasets (bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, suzuki). On those the loop searches for the lowest yield. The printed line names the fallback, but nothing stops the run.
- The hybrid is built at a fixed 50 features (s11:1033, budget_override at :896). The PCA and random projections also use 50. Step 2 excludes 50 features on 9 of the 10 datasets.
- Each per-seed search runs once per seed, not once per condition, through the memo at s11:1121-1122 and _shared.py:1551-1566. The search for seed 0 is triggered by the first condition, ecfp4_raw (s11:1478). So the search cost is paid even when only non-hybrid conditions run.
- Could not determine how many groups each of the 10 datasets has. A dataset with fewer than 20 groups is skipped whole (s11:1086-1090).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3, Step 8 augmentation. Step 8 cuts augmentation on all 10 of s11's datasets (DECISIONS.md:662-669, 683, 687, 693-694). s11 still runs augmented searches. The general search runs none, uncapped and capped; the distance search runs none and uncapped (_shared.py:1444-1448). All 10 datasets carry augmentation representations in DATASET_REPS (e.g. adme_hlm: pharmacophore3d, maccs, usrcat, coulomb_matrix, usr), loaded at similarity_helpers.py:1335-1347. That is two to three times the per-seed search work Step 8 allows.
- R3, Step 8, the recipe itself. The chosen recipe can be an augmented one. get_fold_best_search picks the best over all augmentation conditions (_shared.py:1569-1590). s11 stamps that condition on the recipe (s11:1154, 1174). The build then adds augmentation features to the hybrid (s11:883-898, 1947-1957). Step 8 says no augmented searches on these datasets.
- R3, the run_all whole-dataset precompute. It runs in the same process as s11, with the full uncut grid and augmentation conditions (similarity_helpers.py:1396-1407, 1425-1439). s11 never reads it, so it does not leak. It still breaks R3, which covers every search the experiment runs.
- R3 on logd, from the stored data rather than the record. The stored logd general search has counts 2 and 5, but only under performance_weighted and without dnn (sqlite on /Volumes/seagate/slim_precompute/logd.slim.db). The code runs logd at counts 3 and all only (find_best_hybrid.py:3071, dataset_policy.py:692). Whether Step 6's 'keep all stored rep counts' (DECISIONS.md:594) means 2 and 5 as well could not be settled from the record.


## similarity s12 (tests/experiments/similarity/s12_cross_domain_cliffs.py)

What it measures: For each model, it compares how well single representations and hybrids predict the held-out molecules that are activity cliffs, against the held-out molecules that are not.

Datasets: The submit script queues similarity on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis, which is the 41 datasets in DECISIONS Step 1 (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). similarity run_all calls should_skip_experiment before s12 (tests/experiments/similarity/similarity_helpers.py:1582-1588). That function skips s12 on nucleotide datasets (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675, 3703). Nucleotide means a name starting with nt_ or gb_ (_shared.py:3557, 3641-3642). So s12 runs on 35 datasets: all 41 except gb_human_enhancers_cohn, nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3 and nt_promoter_tata. s12 is not in the over-15,000-rows skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685), so it also runs on kiba and bindingdb_kd.

### R1 models: NO

Code: s12 fits the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS on every dataset: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. svm is dropped above 10,000 rows. It ignores config['models'] and --models; the list is hard-coded. It never fits gp, knn or ridge.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two approved models from Step 1. All 35 datasets s12 runs on break this rule. On 30 datasets both approved models are fitted, plus two or three unapproved ones. On abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, gp is approved and never fitted. So one approved model is missing there, and four unapproved ones are fitted. knn and ridge are absent, which matches.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Base representations are fitted on each fold's training rows by s12 itself, so that side is per fold. The hybrid recipes are not. s12 calls get_rule_hybrids with fold_i. That ranks configurations of the whole-dataset search by their mean over the other folds' stored scores. The search behind those scores trained on every row, including fold i's. The result file says this itself. Two further leaks exist. build_fold_hybrid gets no fold-local allocation scores. So when a recipe uses fewer representations than the pool, it picks which ones from whole-dataset scores (blueprint.rep_scores). Separately, which molecules count as cliffs is decided from all labels, held-out rows included.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only. Re-picking from stored per-fold scores of a whole-dataset search is named as leaking.

### R3 same cuts: NO (partly)

Code: s12 reads two whole-dataset searches that similarity run_all builds at start-up. The general one uses 8 budgets and the engine's default lists: 5 allocation methods, 3 importance methods, evaluators match/rf/lightgbm/dnn, and representation counts 2/3/5/all. The distance one uses 6 budgets (10-500), evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm, and six models. 14 datasets use the fast lists instead. s12 then filters stored rows by model and budget only. It ranks every configuration at 100 features, whatever its importance method, allocation method, evaluator or representation count. Augmented searches (uncapped, capped) are read whenever the dataset has augmentation representations.

Decisions: Every search read must use the dataset's Step 2-7 budgets, importance, allocation, evaluator and representation-count cuts, and Step 8 augmentation. Datasets that break the rule, by axis. General budget: 100 features is outside the decided range on 19 datasets. They are abagym_EGFR, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams and flab_expression_koenig. Also ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9 and tz_her2_multiclass. Distance budget: 100 is inside every Step 7 range, so that matches. Steps 3-6 and the other Step 7 axes: no cut is applied on any dataset. So every dataset with a decided cut can have a cut recipe ranked, e.g. deeplift on herg_ki or wglobal_power2 on caco2. Fast tier: flab_expression_koenig, logd, bindingdb_kd and kiba run the fast lists in code but not in DECISIONS. Augmentation: uncapped and capped recipes are ranked on every dataset that has augmentation representations. Step 8 cuts both everywhere except uncapped on the ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic distance search. On those two the distance read also includes capped (242 rows, under the 10,000-row limit).

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each model and fold, s12 fits every base representation in the pool (about 10), not the best 2. It also builds 3 hybrids: the top 2 from the general search and the top 1 from the distance search. Its headline comparison then keeps one of each per held-out fold. That is the best base representation and the best of the 3 hybrids, both chosen on the other folds' cliff scores. A second comparison sets the general rank-1 hybrid against the base representation that does best on the same folds it is scored on.

Decisions: Per model and per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. s12 differs in two ways at once. It scores all base representations instead of 2, and 3 hybrids instead of 2. Its headline then reduces each side to 1. Scoring every base representation could be a design choice for a cliff study, but nothing in the file says so.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: s12 builds no search, per fold or otherwise. When a pool member is missing, the read falls through to find_best_hybrid on every row of the dataset. That is a whole-dataset search, not a per-fold one. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH set, that build is refused when more than 500 configurations are unstored. The refusal is caught, printed as a warning, and the member is skipped. s12 then records the slot as missing and scores it NaN on that fold. The same refusal at start-up is caught too and stored as None.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. s12 never builds a per-fold search. A missing search is either built over all rows or skipped with a warning.
