### Other problems

- kiba and bindingdb_kd are not skipped, and s12 builds a dense similarity over every pair of rows. It does this either from ECFP4 or from the concatenated representations (similarity_helpers.py:808-812, 825-828; s12:345-347). A comment says both datasets have about 100,000 rows (dataset_policy.py:701-702). I did not measure them. At that size one float64 matrix is about 80 GB. s12 is not in LARGE_N_OOM_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS (_shared.py:3684-3685).
- Which molecules are cliffs is calibrated on every label, held-out rows included (s12:328-341). The activity gap is solved on all labels to hit a target share of cliff molecules. The code calls this accepted leakage, citing n01 as precedent.
- The hybrid budget is fixed at 100 features on every dataset (s12:401). run_all passes s12 no budget (similarity_helpers.py:1606-1677). So s12 never reads the decided budget range. On 19 datasets it reads a budget that Step 2 cuts.
- The distance search for bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg is not stored yet (DECISIONS.md:750). On those three, the distance1 hybrid is built over all rows at start-up, or refused and left NaN.
- The docstring says 'This file runs no search of its own' (s12:20-21). get_precomputed_search can still run find_best_hybrid on every row inside the job when a pool member is missing and KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is unset (_shared.py:5845-5896).
- The fold-0 base ranking is always reported for rf (s12:468). rf is an approved model on only 8 of the 35 datasets s12 runs on. They are bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, humanness_therapeutic, kiba and suzuki.
- When any pool member pruned using fold 0, fold 0 is dropped from both sides of the held-out comparison (s12:821-826). The default schedule prunes. So the headline delta can rest on 4 folds, not 5.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH set, a missing pool member with 500 or fewer configurations unstored still runs find_best_hybrid on every row inside the s12 job. It is not refused. So a whole-dataset search can be built even under the refusal switch (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:697-716; tests/experiments/_shared.py:5845-5896).
- The fallback build in get_precomputed_search passes adaptive_pruning=False (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5889). The start-up build in run_all instead passes the run's pruning schedule, default 'default_pruning' (tests/experiments/similarity/similarity_helpers.py:1251, 1405, 1437). I did not check whether find_best_hybrid treats these two calls as the same stored search. If it does not, a rebuilt member is a different search from the one start-up builds.
- Once the stored general grid no longer holds 100 features, get_fold_pool_recipes stops filtering by budget. It ranks over every stored budget instead and sets budget_relaxed (tests/experiments/_shared.py:6855-6872). Step 2 cuts 100 on 19 datasets, so this will happen there. s12 saves budget_relaxed per hybrid (s12_cross_domain_cliffs.py:657). Its printout and its pool_read['budget'] still say 100 features (s12_cross_domain_cliffs.py:423-425, 761).
- The cliff calibration builds a dense n-by-n matrix before any pool read (s12_cross_domain_cliffs.py:330-341). On a dataset too large for memory, the job dies before any skip or warning path is reached. No result marker is written, unlike the 'skipped' marker that should_skip_experiment writes (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3713-3721).


## similarity s13 (tests/experiments/similarity/s13_clustering_retrieval.py)

What it measures: For each fold, s13 measures how well k-means clusters fitted on training rows group the held-out rows' labels, and how close each held-out molecule's label is to its five nearest training neighbours' labels, in every single representation, PCA controls and up to six hybrids.

Datasets: s13 runs inside similarity run_all, which submit_everything.sh queues on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:95, 211-213). should_skip_experiment skips s13 on any dataset whose domain is nucleotide (_shared.py:3672-3675, 3703-3711), called at similarity_helpers.py:1582. s13 is not in the over-15,000-row skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685), so kiba and bindingdb_kd stay in. DECISIONS Step 9 names six nucleotide datasets (gb_human_enhancers_cohn and five nt_*); I did not print each dataset's domain, so the count of 35 datasets is taken from Step 9, not checked. Nothing in s13 selects datasets itself; its usage lines (s13:70-71) name logd and flab_thermo_tresanco only as examples.

Code: s13 fits no supervised model. Its hybrids are all chosen for one downstream model, knn (s13:468). Per family it takes knn's top 2 hybrids from the general search and its top 1 from the distance search (s13:143, _shared.py:7130-7137). For the general read it names the model list rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm, knn (_shared.py:7124-7127, 586), plus gp on small datasets (_shared.py:5895, 1080). The dataset's two approved models are never used.

Decisions: Step 1: knn is not one of any dataset's two models (DECISIONS.md:56-57). Step 9 allows knn as a downstream model in the distance search for s13, on every non-nucleotide dataset (DECISIONS.md:702-748). Step 9 says nothing about knn in the general search.

### Other problems

- The get_rule_hybrids docstring says the predictive knn slot on the general search is reported missing (_shared.py:7086-7090). The code does not check that. It passes the knn model list to get_precomputed_search, which runs find_best_hybrid on all rows when the refusal allows (_shared.py:7124-7127, 5895-5896).
- The similarity family is read on every dataset (s13:136). The precompute drops that objective on datasets where it is undefined (precompute_hybrids.py:689-699). s13 has no such check. What find_best_hybrid does with it on tcga_brca_pam50, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass: could not determine without running it.
- Step 7 records no distance rows for bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg (DECISIONS.md:609, 750). On those, s13's distance slots depend on run_all building the whole-dataset distance search inside the job, or are refused and reported missing.
- The summary block picks the best single representation on the same folds it is compared on (s13:1020-1039). The code says this carries optimism; only the fold_reselection blocks re-pick per fold.
- The k-means half measures squared Euclidean distance, while the retrieval half reads the process-wide distance, manhattan by default (s13:171-199, 388-398). summary.metrics_agree compares the two halves' wins anyway (s13:1081-1082). The matched clusterer is off unless KIRBY_S13_MATCHED_CLUSTERING is set (s13:125).
- The fixed PCA control is built at budget=100 features (s13:369, 724). That is not a budget the hybrids were ranked at; the per-slot controls at s13:817-828 are the matched ones.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3: the code gives 14 datasets the fast search lists (dataset_policy.FAST_SPEED_DATASETS, printed in this session; used at _shared.py:1049-1053). The record's fast-tier section names ten (DECISIONS.md:350-363). Any whole-dataset search s13 builds live uses the fast lists on four more datasets: logd, flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd. The record does not list those four as fast-tier.
- R3: under run_all, s13's predictive distance slot reads the in-memory search. run_all built that search with its own pruning schedule (similarity_helpers.py:1425-1439, 1437). get_precomputed_search returns that entry as soon as the key exists, whatever grid or model list the caller asked for (_shared.py:5841-5843). Run directly through s13's own __main__ (s13:1366-1371), data comes from load_data; whether load_data fills precomputed_searches_distance: could not determine, not opened.
- Stale comment: s13:481-482 says get_rule_hybrids does not pass fold0_pruned through. It does now (_shared.py:7206-7213). The fold 0 exclusion therefore follows the real flag, not the always-pruned fallback the comment describes. This bears on which folds the R2 comparison uses.

Datasets: c10 is in the noise suite's default experiment list (tests/experiments/noise/noise_helpers.py:54-59). submit_everything.sh queues the noise suite on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213). c10 then skips any dataset whose task_type is not regression (c10_noise_robustness.py:143-148). Going by the metric column of DECISIONS Step 1 (rmse, spearman or ci), that leaves 26 datasets: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. This list is inferred from the metric, not read from each loader's task_type. c10 is dropped from a job submitted with NOISE_CONDITION set, because it does not take a condition (noise_helpers.py:1586-1589, 1755-1781).

Code: c10 names the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm. _apply_dataset_search_speed then adds gp on small datasets. Every model scored is analysed and reported under by_model. ridge and knn are never named.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: c10 never builds a per-fold search; every search it runs is over the whole dataset. Each noisy-level search gets tier 'general__noise_<spec>__lb<hash>'. The cold-search refusal covers only tiers whose root is 'general' or 'general_distance', so noisy searches are always built inside the job. The clean level-0 search keeps tier 'general' and the plain dataset name, so KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH can refuse it. submit_everything.sh turns that on by default. A refused search is caught, recorded in search_failures, and every level-0 cell is dropped. The distance read in get_rule_hybrids is also refusable, and a refused member is skipped with a printed warning.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist must be built by the experiment itself, with no refusal or skip.

### Other problems

- The TODO at c10:464-469 says the noisy-label searches are refused under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH. The code does not refuse them. find_best_hybrid renames their tier to 'general__noise_...' (find_best_hybrid.py:8954-8955), and the refusal only checks tiers whose root is 'general' or 'general_distance' (find_best_hybrid.py:601-605). Only the clean level-0 search can be refused.
- If the level-0 search is refused or fails, every condition loses its clean point. A curve is still computed when 2 levels score (c10:482-483). Its baseline then becomes nan and retention is set to 0.0 (c10:508-523). So a curve with no clean point is still written out.
- Calibrated pruning votes on folds 0 and 1 (find_best_hybrid.py:3802, 7079-7080). c10 drops only fold 0 from both sides, because exclude_folds is [0] or [] (_shared.py:2042). So the fold-1 hybrid score is read from recipes that fold 1 helped keep, and the representations had no such filter. The docstring says four folds are reported (c10:113-114).
- Phase 2a decides whether the clean and noisy recipes differ by comparing allocation, importance and evaluator only (c10:431-432, 788). Representation count is not compared. Two recipes with different counts are reported as the same recipe.
- The get_rule_hybrids block is labelled report-only (c10:608-616). Its distance read can still build a whole-dataset general_distance search inside the c10 job, because the noise runner never builds one.
- Phase 3 uses one budget, budgets[4] = 250 features (c10:544). Step 2 cuts 250 on 9 regression datasets: adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ginkgo_colloidal, logd, qm9 and flab_expression_adams. On those 9, the feature-stability numbers come from a budget the record cuts.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3, the general pool read: get_rule_hybrids reads data['precomputed_searches'], which noise run_all builds with config['budgets'] = FULL_BUDGETS, 10 to 2000 features (noise_helpers.py:1744-1751, 1829-1842). On the 21 regression datasets that dataset_policy marks 'full', this read uses the full grid, not the decided cuts. It also reads augmented 'uncapped' and 'capped' members where Step 8 cuts augmentation (_shared.py:6040-6046; DECISIONS.md:658-697).
- R3, the distance read: get_fold_pool_recipes sets budgets to DISTANCE_BUDGETS, 10 to 500 features, and evaluators to knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm (_shared.py:495, 502, 6775-6776). Step 7 decided narrower ranges and evaluator cuts per dataset. Examples: herg_ki 100-500 with deeplift cut; buchwald_hartwig cuts dnn, knn and svm evaluators (DECISIONS.md:621, 636).
- R1, the distance read: it searches models=DISTANCE_MODELS, which is all five downstream models plus knn (_shared.py:568, 6777), plus gp on small datasets. c10 then reads it for each of its 5 or 6 models (c10:618-622), not for the dataset's two.
- R3, dataset_policy disagrees with the record for c10's inputs. A python import this session gave speed 'fast' for bindingdb_kd, flab_expression_koenig, kiba, logd and qm9. The record's fast-tier table lists only qm9 among regression datasets (DECISIONS.md:352-363). c10 ignores this anyway because it passes speed='fast' everywhere (c10:305).
- The engine drops any budget above the dataset's row count (find_best_hybrid.py:8640-8646), but c10 loops over the unfiltered config['budgets'] (c10:410, 713, 778). On a small dataset the dropped budgets come back as empty candidate lists and 'NO SCORES' entries, not as an error. Which datasets this hits could not be determined; the registry lookup for abagym_Ang2 raised KeyError.


## noise n01 (tests/experiments/noise/n01_activity_cliff_framework.py)

What it measures: For each downstream model, it compares prediction error on molecules that have a close neighbour with a very different label against error on all other molecules, for every single representation and for three hybrids.

Datasets: n01 runs through noise run_all. It is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (noise_helpers.py:60). submit_everything.sh queues the noise suite on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis, which is the 41 Step 1 datasets (submit_everything.sh:95, 211-213). should_skip_experiment then skips n01 on the six nucleotide datasets (_shared.py:3672-3675, 3703): gb_human_enhancers_cohn, nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3, nt_promoter_tata. It also skips n01 above 15,000 rows (_shared.py:3665, 3684-3685, 3713). Which datasets cross 15,000 is decided at run time from the labels. The registry has no row count for kiba or bindingdb_kd (printed this session). DECISIONS Step 9 says both are over 15,000 rows, which is a dated claim I did not check. So n01 runs on 33 to 35 datasets. The docstring says 'MOLECULAR datasets' (n01:5), but the code has branches for antibody, reaction, drug-target and TCGA data (n01:358-418), and run_all applies no domain filter beyond nucleotide. n01 does not run under a NOISE_CONDITION job, because it injects no noise (noise_helpers.py:1558, 1768-1770).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: n01 fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. The list comes from config['models'] = DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, the same five as DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. svm is dropped above its row limit by get_model_factories. Both per-fold searches are told to score these five by name. The distance search also scores knn as a downstream model, but n01 never fits or reports knn. gp is never asked for, and ridge never appears.

Decisions: Two models per dataset (Step 1). On every dataset n01 runs on, it fits three models outside the approved pair. On five datasets it lacks one approved model, because their pair includes gp: abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn), ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn). So on those five it differs in two ways at once: three extra models, and one approved model missing. knn in the distance search is allowed by Step 9 on every non-nucleotide dataset, and n01 never runs on nucleotide data. ridge is excluded, as required.

### R2 per fold: yes

Code: n01 builds the folds once with make_cv_splitter at seed 42. For each fold it runs two find_best_hybrid calls on that fold's training rows only: a general search and a distance search. Each is filed under that fold's own cache namespace. Every hybrid recipe, the top-2 base representations and the top-2 hybrids are read out of that fold's searches. The hybrid is rebuilt on the fold's training rows and applied to its held-out rows. n01 reads no whole-dataset search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows. n01 does this. One caveat that is not a training leak: the cliff labels are computed from every row's activity, including held-out rows. The activity threshold is twice the label spread over all rows. That only decides which held-out molecules are counted as cliffs; no model or recipe sees it.

Distance search: all 6 budgets from 10 to 500 features; the same importance, allocation and counts; evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm; augmentation none. On buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer it searches only lightgbm_gain, the one method Step 3 cut. On the other 26 it lacks deeplift or treeshap, which Step 3 kept. Allocation: matches on the same five. It lacks softmax_T1 everywhere else and wglobal_power2 wherever kept. On ddg_combined it also runs power_2, which Step 4 cut. On suzuki it runs two held methods. Evaluators: runs cut evaluators on abagym_EGFR (rf), abagym_VEGF (rf, lightgbm, dnn), buchwald_hartwig (dnn), ginkgo_colloidal (dnn), ginkgo_titer (lightgbm). Representation counts: runs the cut count 3 on 12 datasets (adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bindingdb_kd, caco2, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_koenig, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, herg_ki, kiba). On buchwald_hartwig it runs 3 and all, both cut, and lacks 2, the only kept count. It lacks counts 2 or 5 on most full-grid datasets that keep them. Distance search: extra budgets 10/25/50 on every dataset whose Step 7 range starts at 100. It runs only a cut importance method on cdr_flexibility and ginkgo_pr_cho. It runs cut evaluators on 11 datasets (abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ddg_combined, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_titer, qm9). It builds a distance search on lhasa_herg, which has no Step 7 row. Augmentation: none everywhere matches Step 8 on 33 datasets. On ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, Step 8 keeps uncapped on the distance search, and n01 lacks it. Could not determine which representation counts logd stored.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per model and fold, n01 fits every base representation in the pool, not the top 2. It also fits three hybrids, not two: rank 1 and rank 2 of the general search, and rank 1 of the distance search. The top-2 base representations per model are computed per fold but only recorded. They feed the neighbour spaces used for the cliff sweep, not the model fits. The summary picks the three representations with the smallest cliff-versus-non-cliff gap, ranked by gap, not by score. top3_base_reps is ranked by rf's score alone.

Decisions: Per model and fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n01 fits all base representations instead of 2, and 3 hybrids instead of 2. So it differs in two ways at once. Fitting every representation can be read as by design, because the comparison is the hybrid's gap against the representations with the smallest gaps. The third hybrid (distance rank 1) is not by design under R4. It follows the 2026-10-02 set of 2 general + 1 distance (n01:524-525, 597-604).

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: n01 builds its own per-fold searches, which is what R6 asks for. But it calls find_best_hybrid with tier 'general' or 'general_distance', the plain dataset name and own_search left False. So the cold-search refusal applies whenever KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is set. submit_everything.sh sets it by default. The refusal raises when over 500 configurations are unstored. Computed this session, one fold's general search is 816 configurations and one fold's distance search is 1,080. I found nothing that warms these per-fold namespaces. precompute_nested_cv_searches has no caller, and neither precompute_hybrids.py nor the submit scripts mention the namespace. n01 catches the refusal, sets that fold's search to None and carries on. The hybrid arms then lose that fold; the base-representation arms still run. The file's own TODO at 486-492 records this conflict as unresolved.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped. Under the default submit settings n01's searches are refused, and the run continues without the hybrid arms. Could not determine whether another experiment in the same job writes rows into the same per-fold namespace first. If one did, those rows would count toward the 50% threshold.

### Other problems

- Early return discards finished work. If the rf pool lookup returns no recipe, run() returns only {'error': 'no_blueprint'} (n02_sample_weighting.py:709-712). By then conditions 1 and 2 have been scored for all five models. Their results never reach the file.
- That gate uses rf on every dataset (n02_sample_weighting.py:680-682). rf is approved on only 7 of the 35 datasets n02 runs on. A dataset whose approved models have recipes still loses every hybrid row when rf has none.
- A missing augmentation condition defaults to 'uncapped' (n02_sample_weighting.py:754, 869, 409, 432). If a pool entry carries no condition, its hybrid is rebuilt with augmentation features under 'uncapped'. Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 of 41 datasets.
- The neighbour settings include base_1_aug_uncapped and base_2_aug_uncapped (similarity_space.py:119-121). These append augmentation features per fold on every dataset with augmentation representations. Step 8 covers searches only, so whether this counts as augmentation under Step 8 is for her to say.
- Hybrid features are refit on each fold's training rows (n02_sample_weighting.py:947-973). Which representations a recipe with a representation count below 10 keeps is chosen from blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5262). Those scores come from the whole-dataset search.
- n02's importance sweep (lightgbm_gain, deeplift) is not a search setting. It only scales the distance used to find each molecule's neighbours (n02_sample_weighting.py:162, 286-292). Step 3 does not govern it.
- Pruning: the start-up searches run with the noise run's pruning schedule (noise_helpers.py:1838). A pool search built inside n02 uses adaptive_pruning=False (_shared.py:5889). Could not determine whether these two give the same stored search identity.
- The similarity-objective searches are not covered by any DECISIONS.md step. n02 builds up to three hybrids per model from them.
- R3 by dataset: no dataset gets its decided grid on every search n02 reads. humanness_therapeutic is the nearest. It keeps every budget, method, evaluator and representation count, and it has no augmentation representations (DATASET_REPS printed this session). There its predictive general and distance grids match Steps 2-8. Could not determine whether that also holds for its similarity-objective searches.
- R3: every other dataset of the 35 reads at least one budget its Step 2 or Step 7 row cuts. tcga_luad_vs_lusc keeps all budgets, but it carries 8 augmentation representations, so it reads uncapped and capped searches that Step 8 cuts.
- R3: flab_expression_koenig, logd, bindingdb_kd and kiba are on the code's fast list (dataset_policy.py:688-711). They are not on the DECISIONS fast-tier table (DECISIONS.md:352-363). So their general searches use the fast lists, not their decided methods.
- R1 by dataset: on all 35 datasets n02 fits at least three models outside the approved pair. On abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho it also lacks gp, one of the two approved models.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R4/R5: the 2 single representations and up to 6 hybrids per model are chosen once from whole-dataset searches and fitted unchanged on every fold. Nothing is selected per fold (n02_sample_weighting.py:514-521, 929-935; _shared.py:4876-4880).
- R3 on humanness_therapeutic: the general search the pool reads scores five downstream models (plus gp under 1,000 rows), not the decided pair xgboost+rf. Step 7's heading says downstream = decided pair. Whether Steps 2-6 also fix the model list is not stated in the record (DECISIONS.md:607; _shared.py:5891 _apply_dataset_search_speed).

## noise n06 (tests/experiments/noise/n06_bindingdb_ground_truth.py)

What it measures: For each noise estimator, it measures how well the estimator's per-molecule noise score matches real disagreement between repeat measurements. It then rank-correlates that ordering of estimators with the orderings n11 and n13 found under injected noise.

Datasets: n06 is queued on every dataset the noise suite runs: the 41 DATASET_REPS keys minus chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:211-213). Noise run_all puts n06 last (noise/noise_helpers.py:146-152). should_skip_experiment never skips it (n06 is in neither skip set, _shared.py:3672-3685). n06 stops before any search read unless a ground-truth source finds at least 50 groups of repeat measurements that disagree (n06:802-810; _ground_truth_providers.py:54). Three sources exist (_ground_truth_providers.py:779-783). drug_target_repeats needs drug and protein ids per row (_ground_truth_providers.py:164-198), which only the drug-target loaders supply. That is bindingdb_kd, and kiba, whose repeats n06's docstring says are absent (n06:56-57, not re-counted by me). cross_curator runs only on herg and herg_ki (_ground_truth_providers.py:62, 484-490). It needs Lhasa's hERG_lhasa_test.sdf; I could not determine whether that file is on the server. chembl_multi_document refuses unless a raw ChEMBL file with document ids exists (_ground_truth_providers.py:617-645); I could not determine whether one exists. So the datasets where n06 reads searches are bindingdb_kd, and herg and herg_ki if the Lhasa file is present. herg_ic50 also carries repeat groups (src/kirby/datasets/herg.py:606), but it is not in the submit roster.

### R1 models: NO

Code: n06 fits no downstream model. It builds spaces for each model in config['models'], filtered to the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS, and always adds rf. Noise run_all passes DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, which equals the five: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. So every dataset gets hybrid and single-representation spaces for all five models.

Decisions: Step 1: bindingdb_kd rf+dnn, herg lightgbm+xgboost, herg_ki svm+dnn. bindingdb_kd gets three extra models: xgboost, svm, lightgbm. herg gets rf, svm and dnn extra. herg_ki gets rf, xgboost and lightgbm extra. On herg and herg_ki, rf is added even when the caller's list omits it. knn and ridge are never used.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe and every single representation is chosen once, on the whole dataset. rf's lead recipe comes from get_best_search_for_downstream, which labels its own selection_scope 'whole_dataset'. The two-general-plus-one-distance set per model comes from get_rule_hybrids with no fold index. That ranks on the mean over all folds of searches run over every row. rf's two single representations come from noise_base_reps_by_model, which ranks on the stored search's whole-dataset mean. Inside each of n06's five folds, build_fold_hybrid refits only the selected features on that fold's training rows. n06 passes no fold-local allocation scores. So when a recipe uses fewer representations than the pool, the representations kept are chosen from blueprint.rep_scores, measured over every row. n06's own provenance note says the recipe is chosen once by a search over every row. That note is written only on the fallback path, not on the rule path that normally runs.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only. The whole-dataset search, re-read per fold or read once, does not comply.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: n06 reads whole-dataset searches with the default grid. general: FULL_BUDGETS, 10 to 2000 features (8 budgets). Distance: DISTANCE_BUDGETS 10-500, evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm, models with knn. bindingdb_kd and herg are run fast in code: lightgbm_gain only; performance_weighted, power_2, rank_exp_d0.3; counts 3 and all. herg_ki is run full: three importance methods, five allocation methods, counts 2, 3, 5 and all. n06 passes budget=None, so hybrids at any stored budget can be picked. Augmentation conditions come from _pool_conditions. The general search gets none, uncapped and capped; bindingdb_kd gets none and capped only.

Decisions: bindingdb_kd: budgets 250-2000; keep all three importance and all five allocation methods; four evaluators; cut counts 3 and 5. The code differs on bindingdb_kd in five ways at once. It allows budgets 10-100, lacks deeplift and treeshap, and lacks softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2. It runs count 3 and lacks count 2. It also reads capped augmentation. bindingdb_kd has no Step 7 row because no distance search is stored. herg: budgets 100-2000, distance 100-500, fast grid as stored. The code matches herg's fast grid but allows budgets 10, 25 and 50 on both searches. It also reads uncapped and capped augmentation. herg_ki: budgets 250-2000; cut deeplift; cut wglobal_power2; cut counts 2, 3, 5. Distance: 100-500 with the same three cuts. The code allows all of those, plus budgets 10-100 general and 10-50 distance, plus uncapped and capped augmentation. Step 8 cuts augmentation on all three datasets.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each of five models, n06 builds up to three hybrids per search family: the top 2 general and the top 1 distance. It reads two families, predictive and similarity, so a model can get up to 6 hybrids. Each model also gets its top 2 single representations. That is up to 8 spaces per model and up to 40 in total. The estimators then score every space. rf's two single representations come from one stored search, the one the pool returned. The other four models' come from the rule read, which takes the best over all augmentation conditions. So rf's single representations are chosen from a different set of searches than the other four models' are.

Decisions: Per each of the dataset's two models: the 2 best single representations and the 2 best hybrids. n06 differs by design in one respect. It fits no downstream model and scores noise estimators, so 'per model' only decides which model's ranking picks the spaces. The counts still differ from R4: 3 hybrids per family instead of 2, two families instead of one, and five models instead of two.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n06 never builds a per-fold search. It only reads whole-dataset searches through get_precomputed_search. Noise run_all builds two whole-dataset searches: predictive general and similarity general. It builds no distance search. So both distance reads go to disk; bindingdb_kd has no stored distance search at all. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH unset, a missing whole-dataset search is built inside the job on all rows. With it set and more than 500 configurations missing, find_best_hybrid raises. _iter_pool_searches then prints a warning and skips that search, and n06 records the empty slot in rule_missing and runs on.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment builds it itself. Refusing it or skipping it with a warning does not comply.

### Other problems

- n06's docstring says each fold's feature space is built from the other folds' rows, so no molecule helps choose the features its score is computed in (n06:59-62). That holds for the selected features only. The recipe and the single representations were chosen by searches that saw every row. When a recipe uses fewer representations than the pool, which ones it keeps was also chosen that way (_shared.py:5256-5286).
- The provenance note saying the recipe was chosen once over every row is written only on the fallback path, for a single winner per family (n06:945-953). The rule path that normally runs writes rule_entry_summary (n06:366-384), which carries no such note. So the usual result file does not say the recipe was chosen on all rows.
- rf's single representations and the other four models' are picked from different searches. rf's come from the one search the pool returned (n06:1047-1048). The others' come from the rule read, which keeps each representation's best score across augmentation conditions (n06:1059; _shared.py:6955-6963).
- rf is always added to the model list (n06:987-988). On herg (approved lightgbm+xgboost) and herg_ki (approved svm+dnn), rf's spaces are the ones the base_1, base_2 and hybrid_predictive names refer to. So the headline names belong to a model neither dataset approved.
- Noise run_all builds no distance search, predictive or similarity (noise_helpers.py:1826-1870). Every distance slot n06 asks for is read from disk. bindingdb_kd has no stored distance search (DECISIONS.md Step 7 header), so its distance slots are either built inside the job on all rows or refused and left empty.
- budget=None is what n06 receives from run_all (n06:840; noise_helpers.py:2063-2064). So a hybrid at 10 features can be chosen on bindingdb_kd and herg_ki, where Step 2 cuts everything below 250.
- Each estimator is fitted on all rows of the fold, training and held-out together; only held-out rows keep a score (n06:1203-1206, 1255-1256). The file says this is deliberate (n06:1291-1297). It is noted here because it differs from the per-fold fit used elsewhere.
- Could not determine whether rows in a similarity-objective search carry each downstream model's name. get_fold_pool_recipes keeps only rows whose model matches the requested model (_shared.py:6848-6850). So how many similarity hybrids each model gets is not known from the code alone.
- Could not determine whether Lhasa's hERG_lhasa_test.sdf exists on the server. Without it, herg and herg_ki find no repeat groups and n06 skips them before any search read.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- n06:1076-1079 writes provenance for rf's base_1 and base_2 saying they come from 'the same search that chose the hybrid recipe'. On the rule path, rf's hybrids come from get_rule_hybrids (n06:345-348), which ranks every pool search, general and distance, across augmentation conditions. That one search is the source of at most one of rf's six hybrid slots, so the sentence is wrong for the rest.
- n06:1093 writes 'ranked_in_which_search_family': winner_family for every model's single-representation space. For the four models other than rf, the ranking comes from rule['base_reps'], the first family that has any (_shared.py:7190-7194). So the family recorded and the family used are not necessarily the same.
- noise run_all's general precompute builds an uncapped search on bindingdb_kd. precompute_hybrid_searches adds 'uncapped' whenever augmentation representations exist (_shared.py:5543-5548). The pool reader drops 'uncapped' for bindingdb_kd (_shared.py:5989, 6036-6040). So a search is built that nothing in n06 reads, and Step 8 cuts augmentation on bindingdb_kd anyway (DECISIONS.md:666).
- n06:1286-1290 copies the docstring's claim into the result file: 'each fold's features are chosen on the other folds' rows, so no molecule helps choose the features'. As with n06:59-62, that holds only for the selected features. The recipe, the representations kept and the single representations were chosen on every row.
- Correction to the reported note about estimator rows. n06:1203 sets rows = train_idx + val_idx. Across folds those two together are every row in the dataset, not 'all rows of the fold'. The estimator is fitted on the whole dataset mapped into that fold's features, and only held-out rows keep a score (n06:1256).
- Could not determine whether the bindingdb_kd general search was stored with the full grid and then read under fast settings. DECISIONS.md:313 and :379 show three importance and five allocation methods stored for bindingdb_kd. dataset_policy.py:701-709 says it was added to the fast list on 2026-10-02. I did not check whether a fast-speed read matches those stored rows or starts a new search.


## noise n07 (tests/experiments/noise/n07_remediation.py)

What it measures: For each noise condition, it measures how much of the score lost to injected training-label noise each label-cleaning method wins back, under each downstream model, in hybrid features and in single representations.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. submit_everything.sh takes every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213) and queues the noise category on each (submit_everything.sh:95, 350-364). n07 is not in NUCLEOTIDE_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675) or LARGE_N_OOM_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS (_shared.py:3684-3685), so no dataset skips it. Inside one dataset it runs once per noise condition plus the recorded labels, via sweep_conditions (n07_remediation.py:2403-2407).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every dataset gets the same five downstream models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. That list comes from config['models'] or DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE. gp is never asked for. On top of that, every D-versus-D' row is fitted with rf and svm whatever the dataset. The single-representation block is random forest only. Ridge and knn are not used as downstream models.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two Step 1 models. Five datasets are approved with gp: abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn), ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn). On those five, n07 lacks gp entirely. On all 41 datasets it fits at least three models outside the approved pair. Examples: herg_ki is approved for svm+dnn, and n07 also fits rf, xgboost and lightgbm. The rf-only single-representation block runs even where rf is not approved, e.g. caco2 (dnn+svm).

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe comes from one search over all rows of the dataset. get_best_search_for_downstream reads it and labels it selection_scope 'whole_dataset'. get_rule_hybrids is called without fold_i, so the top 2 general and top 1 distance hybrids are ranked on the mean over all folds of that search. No held-out fold is left out, not even its scores. Each fold then rebuilds the recipe on its own training rows, which only refits the features. When a recipe uses fewer representations than were loaded, build_fold_hybrid chooses which ones from blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores were measured over all rows, because n07 passes no fold-local scores. The two base representations per model used for neighbour spaces come from the same whole-dataset search. The base representations the expensive cleanups run on come from rank_models_and_reps. It ranks on the held-out score of every fold, including the fold later scored.

Decisions: Every hybrid used on a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. n07 runs no per-fold search anywhere. It never calls search_on_fold, get_fold_best_search, run_nested_cv or nested_cv_evaluate.

### R3 same cuts: NO (partly)

Code: n07 fixes the budget at 100 features (kwargs default). It reads recipes at that budget from the general search and the distance search. It applies no filter on importance method, allocation method, internal evaluator or representation count. It takes whatever the stored whole-dataset search ranks best at 100 features. The start-up search it reads is built with FULL_BUDGETS and the engine's default lists. The 14 datasets in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS get the fast lists instead. The pool also reads the uncapped and capped augmented searches whenever the dataset loads augmentation representations. It also reads a general search under objective='similarity', which no Step covers.

Decisions: Step 2 budget range: 100 features is outside the decided range on 25 of 41 datasets. Those are abagym_EGFR, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, the five nt_* datasets, qm9 and tz_her2_multiclass. On the distance search, 100 is inside every Step 7 range. Steps 3-6 cut methods on many datasets; n07 can pick a cut method because it filters nothing. Step 3 importance cuts include herg_ki deeplift, buchwald_hartwig lightgbm_gain, and logd deeplift and treeshap. Step 4 cuts wglobal_power2 on caco2, ginkgo_acsins and herg_ki, and power_2 and wglobal_power2 on ddg_combined. Suzuki is held. Step 5 cuts include rf, lightgbm and dnn on abagym_VEGF. Step 6 cuts include representation counts 2, 3 and 5 on herg_ki, caco2 and kiba. Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 datasets; n07 reads uncapped and capped wherever augmentations load. Step 7 distance cuts are not applied either. Example: buchwald_hartwig cuts the dnn, knn and svm evaluators there.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Hybrids: for each of 5 models, it builds up to 6 hybrid feature spaces. That is general rank 1, general rank 2 and distance rank 1, for each of two search families (predictive and similarity). They are chosen once for the whole dataset, not per fold. Base representations: random forest is run on every loaded representation, typically 10. On regression datasets only, two models picked by n07's own ranking each run on that ranking's top 2 representations. On classification datasets that second block does not run. The top-2 lists in results['top2_base_reps'] and results['top2_hybrids'] are read from the stored search. Nothing is fitted on them.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n07 differs in two ways at once: it has 3 hybrids per model per family, not 2, and the choice is made once for the dataset, not per fold. Its base side is also not 2 per approved model. It is 10 under rf, plus 2 under each of two score-picked models.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: n07 never builds a per-fold search. A whole-dataset search missing from memory and disk goes to get_precomputed_search, which calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, that call raises when more than 500 configurations are missing. submit_everything.sh sets that variable by default. _iter_pool_searches catches the error, prints a warning and skips that pool member. With no member left, get_best_search_for_downstream returns (None, None). n07 then drops the model with 'no_search_metadata'. If every model drops, it returns {'error': 'no_blueprint'}. A missing rule slot is recorded in rule_missing_by_model and not built. Per DECISIONS, bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg have no stored distance search. On those three the distance rank-1 slot is built on all rows inside the job, or refused.

Decisions: When a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment builds it itself. n07 refuses or skips with a warning, and when it does build one, the search covers the whole dataset.

### Other problems

- The module docstring says n07 does not pass distance=True and that this is unchanged (n07_remediation.py:103-104). Since 2026-10-02, get_rule_hybrids reads the distance search for every model (n07:2533-2537, _shared.py:7130-7137). The docstring and the code disagree.
- The representation choice inside each fold's hybrid leaks. _fold_space calls build_fold_hybrid with no fold-local scores (n07:3442-3445). For a recipe using fewer representations than are loaded, the kept ones come from blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5286), which were measured on all rows.
- rank_models_and_reps ranks every model on every representation using held-out scores (n07:1290-1307). It uses the same cv_split folds that are later scored (n07:3911-3912). So the two cleanup models and their two representations are picked with each scored fold's held-out rows in view.
- The same recipe is rebuilt from two different sets of representations in one fold. _fold_space passes every loaded representation to build_fold_hybrid (n07:3398-3399, 3442). fold_similarity_spaces uses hybrid_for_fold, which keeps only the representations the recipe names (noise_helpers.py:1005-1012). Whether those sets differ depends on blueprint.reps. Not checked.
- The fold split may not match the stored search's split. n07 splits with cv_split using config['n_splits'] (n07:2441, 3387-3388). The rule read ranks over the stored search's own folds. With fold_i None this does not change which recipe is picked, but nothing checks the two splits match.
- The per-fold noise draws and cleanups use only the fold's training labels (n07:3389-3400, 3484-3491). The hybrid features are also re-chosen per fold from noisy training labels. Only the recipe choice and the representation choice come from all rows.
- Step 8 has an open check about noise experiments that read augmented spaces such as base_k_aug_uncapped (DECISIONS.md:654). n07 builds that space per fold from the top representation plus augmentation donors (n07:1712-1748; SWEPT_AUG_STRATEGIES = ('uncapped',) at similarity_space.py:119). On the 39 datasets where Step 8 cuts augmentation, this space is still built whenever augmentations load.
- Could not determine whether the stored searches on the server hold only the decided cut grid or the full default grid. That decides which cut methods n07 can actually pick. Either way, n07 itself applies no Step 3-7 filter.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R1: rank_models_and_reps fits every one of the five models on every loaded representation, once per fold. On herg_ki that is rf, xgboost and lightgbm too, not only svm and dnn. Regression datasets only (tests/experiments/noise/n07_remediation.py:1285-1307, 2845-2876).

- R1: the start-up searches score all five models plus gp on small datasets (_shared.py:1049-1080, 1084-1114). That is more models than each dataset's approved pair. Each extra model adds configurations to the search grid.


## noise n09 (tests/experiments/noise/n09_lnl_survey.py)

What it measures: It injects label noise into each fold's training labels and trains a neural network, plain and with each of 12 noisy-label methods, on two single representations, one hybrid and an importance-weighted copy of that hybrid; it records whether the hybrid changes which methods rank best.

Datasets: All 41 datasets in the noise roster. submit_everything.sh takes every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213) and queues the noise category on them (:95). n09 is in the default noise list (tests/experiments/noise/noise_helpers.py:63). It is in neither skip set, so nucleotide and large datasets run too (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3667-3685; the comment at :3670-3671 says n09 is kept on nucleotide). Each run sweeps every noise condition the task allows (n09_lnl_survey.py:254-258).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Every arm is the same neural network: the plain baseline and all 12 noisy-label methods. The per-fold search also fits only that network. No second model is fitted for the main arms. The distance_selection sweep writes extra rows that fit rf, svm and dnn on every dataset. The network was chosen because the noisy-label methods are neural networks, so this is partly a design choice.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models. dnn is one of the two on 25 datasets. On 16 datasets it is neither: abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, flab_binding_adams, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_acsins, herg, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, nt_promoter_tata, suzuki, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary, tz_her2_multiclass. On those 16 no approved model is fitted. On the other 25 the second approved model is never fitted. The sweep rows add rf and svm where they are not approved, e.g. rf on herg_ki (svm+dnn).

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: The hybrid arms follow the rule: each (level, fold, draw) runs a new search on that fold's training rows and noisy labels, then builds the winner on those rows. Four other inputs come from the whole-dataset search. The two single representations are ranked by the dnn's mean in that search. When the per-fold search scores no budget, the whole-dataset recipe replaces it. The per-fold search's augmentation condition is the whole-dataset winner's condition. The distance_selection sweep builds its 'hybrid' and 'hybrid__general2' neighbour spaces from whole-dataset recipes.

Decisions: Every hybrid and every choice made for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only. The single-representation arms differ from the hybrid arms in two ways at once: their selection saw every row, and it saw the clean labels. The hybrid arms saw neither. So base-versus-hybrid differences mix the representation with that selection advantage.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: One model (dnn) per fold. Two single representations, the dnn's top 2 from the whole-dataset search. One hybrid: the best of the per-fold search across its three budgets. A fourth arm is the same hybrid with each feature multiplied by its importance weight. Each of the four feature sets is trained plain and with each of 12 methods (10 on classification).

Decisions: Two models, and for each model per fold the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. The code has one model instead of two, and one hybrid instead of two. Its second 'hybrid' arm is a rescaled copy of the first, not the second-best recipe. The 2 base representations match in count, but are not chosen per fold.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: The per-fold search is built inside the job when missing. Its tier 'n09_noisy_search' is not one the cold-search refusal covers, so KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH never refuses it. But before any fold runs, the code needs a whole-dataset dnn recipe. If neither the pool read nor the rule read returns one, it returns error 'no_blueprint' for that condition and skips every fold. The rule read's distance slot reads a whole-dataset distance search that noise run_all never builds. Under the refusal it is refused and skipped with a printed warning; without it, it is built on all rows.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment, with no refusal or skip. The per-fold search complies. The skip at 'no_blueprint' stops the experiment because a whole-dataset search is missing, though the per-fold path does not need it.

### Other problems

- The comment at n09_lnl_survey.py:723-729 says KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH refuses the per-fold search. The code does not: 'n09_noisy_search' is not in _PRECOMPUTE_TIER_ROOTS (find_best_hybrid.py:598-605), so the refusal returns at :650-651. The comment and the code disagree.
- The comment at n09_lnl_survey.py:646-651 says the per-fold search uses rf as a proxy for the network. The code fits dnn (n09:690-692, 736). The comment is stale.
- The 'hybrid' neighbour space can pair one recipe with another recipe's augmentation condition. `bp` is replaced by the rule read's general1 recipe (n09:364-366). Its augmentation condition is still taken from the pool read's meta (n09:509-510). The two reads can pick different pool members.
- The per-fold search's augmentation condition is the one the clean-label, whole-dataset winner used (n09:750). So one choice on every fold was made on all rows and clean labels. With 'uncapped' chosen, the fold never searches 'none'.
- The fallback recipe `bp` is whole-dataset. When it is used, build_fold_hybrid picks which representations to keep from its rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5276), also whole-dataset. Folds that fell back are listed in 'recipe_sources' (n09:788-793).
- extract_top3_base_reps is called with its default model rf (n09:335; _shared.py:867). The result field 'top3_base_reps' is an rf ranking read from the dnn pool search. It is recorded only and feeds no arm.
- The weighted-hybrid arm (n09:850-876) uses the same recipe as the hybrid arm. It is counted as a separate arm but is not a second hybrid.
- On classification the two regression-only methods are dropped, so 10 methods run, not 12 (n09:295-297).

- n09_lnl_survey.py:318-319: the comment says that with no network recipe 'the fold says so'. The code does not work per fold. At :387-389 it returns 'no_blueprint' for the whole condition, and no fold runs.
- n09_lnl_survey.py:439-441: the comment says that with no stored DNN search 'the run does not reach this point'. It can reach it. When meta is None (:328), bp can still come from the rule read's general1 (:364-366). The run then continues with base_reps_search_model=None and no single-representation arms (:407-416). Whether the two reads can disagree in practice was not determined.
- R1 also applies to the whole-dataset search n09 reads. noise_helpers.py:1751 passes models=DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, which is list(DOWNSTREAM_MODELS) (_shared.py:857). So the start-up general search fits every downstream model, not each dataset's two from Step 1. The search list records this, but R1 was not flagged for it.
- R3 also applies to that start-up search. noise_helpers.py:1745-1752 passes FULL_BUDGETS (_shared.py:494: 10-2000 features, 8 budgets) and the default allocation, importance and evaluator lists on every dataset. n09 reads this search for its base ranking (n09:406-409), its fallback recipe (n09:342, 366) and its augmentation condition (n09:750).
- Fast-tier datasets in the per-fold search: find_best_hybrid is called directly at n09:732, not through get_precomputed_search, so _apply_dataset_search_speed (_shared.py:1015, applied at :5896) never runs. herg, qm9, the nt_ datasets, gb_human_enhancers_cohn and tz_her2_* therefore get the full lists (find_best_hybrid.py:8651-8669). The decided grid for those 10 datasets is the fast one (DECISIONS.md:352-363).


## noise n11 (tests/experiments/noise/n11_estimation_remediation_grid.py)

What it measures: For each noise level, it injects label noise into the training rows. It scores each training molecule's suspicion with ten-plus noise estimators in several feature spaces. Then it repairs the labels by weighting, smoothing or clipping, refits each downstream model on its own two single representations, and reports how much of the clean-to-noisy score gap the repair recovers.

Datasets: n11 is in the noise suite's default list (tests/experiments/noise/noise_helpers.py:64). The noise suite is queued on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213). That is the 41 datasets of DECISIONS Step 1. noise run_all calls should_skip_experiment before each experiment (noise_helpers.py:1988). That skips n11 on nucleotide datasets (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675, 3703). A dataset counts as nucleotide when its name starts with nt_ or gb_ (_shared.py:3557, 3641-3642). ### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Hybrid recipes come from get_rule_hybrids with no fold index. That ranks every stored recipe by its mean over all folds of the search, and the search ran on all rows. The two single representations per model are ranked by the same search's means. Inside each fold, n11 rebuilds the chosen recipes on that fold's noisy training labels. That refits the features, not the choice of recipe. The file's own header says the recipe was chosen on clean labels over all rows.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search run on that fold's training rows only. n11 runs no per-fold search. Its recipes and its single representations were both chosen with the held-out rows in view.

### R4 standard selection: by design

Code: For each model it takes 2 single representations, and the model is fitted only on those two. Hybrids are never the features a downstream model is fitted on. They are spaces where the noise estimators score suspicion, and where the sweep finds neighbours. Per model it reads up to 2 general + 1 distance hybrid for each of two search families (prediction-built and similarity-built). That is up to 6 hybrid detection spaces per model. Selection is once for the whole dataset, not per fold.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best single representations and the 2 best hybrids. n11 has the 2 single representations, chosen once on the whole dataset. It has 3 hybrids per family instead of 2, used for detection only.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: n11 builds no search itself. A missing pool member goes to get_precomputed_search. That either builds a search on all rows inside the job, or, under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, raises. DECISIONS says no distance search is stored for bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg. A missing hybrid slot is written to 'unavailable'. If the prediction-built read returns nothing, no model can rank its single representations. n11 then returns an error record and writes no results.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n11 never builds a per-fold search. It either builds an all-rows search, or skips with a warning, or stops with no results.

### Other problems

- One recipe is built two ways in the same run. n11's own detection space passes no model, all 10 representations and no representation count (n11:431-440). The sweep's 'hybrid' and 'hybrid__general2' spaces come from the same recipe (n11:1287-1317). Those go through build_fold_hybrid, which keeps the recipe's own representations (noise_helpers.py:1005-1011). It also cuts them to the recipe's representation count using whole-dataset scores (_shared.py:5256-5286), and passes the model (n07_remediation.py:1766-1773). So the two spaces built from one recipe differ in two ways at once, not one.
- The comment at n11:916-941 says that when the pool has no recipe, the run carries on in the single-representation spaces. Both the recipe and the single-representation ranking come from the same search (n11:908, 1139-1141). If that search is missing, every model is listed as missing (_shared.py:4909-4913). n11 then returns {'error': 'no_single_representation'} with no results (n11:1173-1179). So the comment and the code disagree.
- The single-representation ranking for every model reads the search that won for rf (n11:910, 1140; recorded as 'base_reps_search_model': 'rf' at 1205). That is the augmentation condition and family that scored best for rf, not for the model being ranked. Whether the single-representation scores differ between augmentation conditions: could not determine; I did not open the baseline code in find_best_hybrid.
- The distance-search hybrid (slot distance1) becomes a detection space in the main grid. It is not passed to the similarity sweep, because sim_recipes_by_model holds only general1, general2 and the similarity family (n11:1288-1317). similarity_sweep passes no extra_spaces (n07_remediation.py:2275-2281).
- n11 sets n_samples to the whole dataset's row count when building model factories (n11:812, 830-831), not the fold's training rows. The svm cap at 10,000 rows (find_best_hybrid.py:2812) is therefore checked against the full dataset.
- Whether a similarity-objective distance search (tier general_distance, objective similarity) is stored on any dataset: could not determine. Step 7 of DECISIONS covers only the prediction-built distance search.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- If the prediction-built search is missing and the similarity-built one is present, n11's single representations for every model are ranked by the similarity search's baselines. Those baselines store one geometry score per representation, copied to every model (find_best_hybrid.py:5910-5912). That score is the correlation between each held-out molecule's activity and what its five nearest neighbours predict. So every model gets the same two representations, chosen without fitting any model. The path: _shared.py:6359-6365 returns the only family present; n11:1139-1141 ranks from it. The same holds in every run with KIRBY_SIMILARITY_HYBRID_ONLY=1 (n11:901-905, pool subset 'similarity_only').
- On herg_ki the Step 7 distance budgets are 100-500 features (DECISIONS.md:636). The distance read ranks over 10-500 (_shared.py:495, 6774-6777). The first agent named the six distance budgets but gave no dataset where they break Step 7.
- Step 6 cuts representation counts 2, 3 and 5 on herg_ki (DECISIONS.md:589). get_fold_pool_recipes keeps every stored row for the model (_shared.py:6846-6853). So a recipe searched over 2, 3 or 5 representations can be chosen there. n11's own rebuild then ignores that count and uses all representations (n11:431-440, 1366).
- n11's own rebuild of a prediction-built recipe passes no model to create_hybrid (n11:431-440). create_hybrid takes a model for its capped and uncapped augmentation (hybrid.py:5660-5662). The sweep passes the model for the same recipe (n07_remediation.py:1764-1773). What create_hybrid does with an augmented recipe and model=None: could not determine, I did not read that branch.
- submit_everything.sh exports KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 by default (submit_everything.sh:93, 363). So on the cluster the refuse-or-small-search path is the normal path, not an exception. The noise start-up searches catch a refusal per augmentation condition and record it (noise_helpers.py:1829-1841; _shared.py precompute_hybrid_searches except at its lines 159-183 relative to 5452).


## noise n12 (tests/experiments/noise/n12_importance_weighted_distance.py)

What it measures: For each noise condition and level, it asks whether finding each molecule's neighbours in a feature space weighted by feature importance finds the corrupted labels better, and recovers more of the downstream score after down-weighting suspect molecules, than finding them in an unweighted space.

Datasets: 35 of the 41 datasets: every dataset in the submit roster except the six nucleotide ones (nt_H3K27me3, nt_H3K4me3, nt_H3K9ac, nt_H3K9me3, nt_promoter_tata, gb_human_enhancers_cohn). The roster is every DATASET_REPS key minus chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213). noise run_all calls should_skip_experiment before n12 (tests/experiments/noise/noise_helpers.py:1988). n12 is in NUCLEOTIDE_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675, 3703). The domain is nucleotide for names starting nt_ or gb_ (_shared.py:3557, 4284). n12 is not in the large-dataset skip list (_shared.py:3684-3685). The docstring says molecular datasets only (n12:5), but nothing in the code checks that, so it also runs on antibody, reaction, tcga and drug-target datasets.

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: Downstream models are config['models'] or DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. noise run_all sets config['models'] to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm. So every dataset fits five models. svm drops out above 10,000 rows. gp is never in the list. The similarity sweep inside n12 also fits rf and svm on every row it writes, whatever the dataset. rf alone picks the stored search that every model's two base representations are ranked from.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two Step 1 models. ridge is not used here, which agrees. knn is not a downstream model here, which agrees. On abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, gp is one of the two approved models, and n12 never fits it. On all 35 datasets n12 fits three models outside the approved pair (two on datasets above 10,000 rows, where svm drops).

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe comes from searches over all rows of the dataset. get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index, so recipes are ranked on the mean over all folds of the whole-dataset search. ### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per downstream model it takes 2 base representations and, per search family, 2 general hybrids and 1 distance hybrid. With both families (predictive and similarity) that is up to 6 hybrids per model, chosen once for the whole dataset, not per fold. By design the model is never fitted on a hybrid. Each hybrid is a space in which neighbours are found, and the model is always fitted on one of its two base representations. Each base rank carries 2 conditions (unweighted, importance-weighted); each hybrid carries 3 (unweighted, weighted by the recipe's importance method, weighted by the method being swept).

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n12 differs in three ways at once: up to 6 hybrids per model instead of 2, chosen once for the dataset instead of per fold, and used as neighbour spaces rather than model inputs. The last of those is the experiment's design.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n12 never builds a per-fold search. The general searches come from noise run_all at start-up, over all rows. noise run_all builds no distance search, and n12 does not fill data['precomputed_searches_distance']. So each distance read goes to get_precomputed_search, which calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH set and over 500 configurations unstored, that raises. The pool reader prints a warning and skips that member. The slot is recorded as missing and no space is built for it. With the variable unset, the whole-dataset search is built inside the n12 job. If rf gets no recipe at all, n12 returns {'error': 'no_blueprint'}. A failed rule read for a model drops all of that model's hybrid spaces.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n12 has no per-fold search to build. The searches it does read are whole-dataset, and a missing one is either refused and skipped or built on all rows. DECISIONS lists bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg as having no stored distance search.

### Other problems

- The base representations and the hybrids are ranked from different sources. The two base representations per model come from the one stored search rf's best recipe came from (n12:843-851, 980-982). The hybrids for each model are ranked across every pool member (get_rule_hybrids). So svm's base representations are ranked inside whichever augmentation member rf won.
- n12's own weighting sweep always uses lightgbm_gain and treeshap (n12:147). Step 3 cut lightgbm_gain from the search on buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer, and treeshap on bh_doyle_plates and logd. This is the experiment's own axis, not a search setting. Whether the cut applies to it is a decision, not a fault.
- When a recipe used fewer representations than the pool, build_fold_hybrid picks which ones from blueprint.rep_scores, measured on all rows (_shared.py:5256-5286). n12 passes no fold-local scores (n12:426-436). So the choice of representations on each fold also used that fold's held-out rows.
- The docstring says molecular datasets and synthetic noise only (n12:4-6). No code enforces the dataset half; the only skip is for nucleotide datasets (_shared.py:3703).
- The hybrid recipes are chosen on clean labels and rebuilt on noisy ones (n12:812-821). The file says so; the result is a best case for the hybrid conditions, not a held-out comparison.
- Each hybrid space is rebuilt once per (level, fold, draw) because the noisy labels change per draw (n12:1265-1268, 1333-1350). With up to 30 spaces, 3 draws and 5 folds, that is up to 450 hybrid builds per level. This is cost, not a rule break.
- The distance searches are not built by noise run_all (noise_helpers.py:1817-1903 builds general predictive and general similarity only). Unless another job filled the result store, every distance slot in n12 is either built on all rows inside the n12 job or refused and recorded missing.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Step 3 sets four non-nucleotide fast-tier datasets to 'lightgbm_gain only... do not extend to other methods': herg, qm9, tz_her2_binary and tz_her2_multiclass. n12 nevertheless sweeps treeshap on them (n12:147 IMPORTANCE_METHODS = ['lightgbm_gain','treeshap']; DECISIONS.md:323,334,338,339). The auditor listed the Step 3 conflict only for six other datasets.
- R1: the hybrid build's accept-or-reject step fits the recipe's own model on every pass. For xgboost, svm, dnn or lightgbm outside the approved pair, that is one more set of fits per space, besides the evaluation fits (n12:1338-1346).
- R1: precompute_hybrid_searches runs with models=None. On datasets under 1,000 rows _apply_small_dataset_models adds gp, so the stored general searches score six models, not the approved two (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5568, 1046-1079; dataset_policy.SMALL_DATASET_MAX_SAMPLES=1000, SMALL_DATASET_EXTRA_MODELS=('gp',)). The distance read asks for DISTANCE_MODELS including knn (_shared.py:6777, 568). Step 9 allows knn there, but the five non-approved models are also scored.
- R3: the general precompute adds an 'uncapped' member whenever augmentations exist, with no UNCAPPED_SKIP_DATASETS check (_shared.py:5543-5548). The pool reader drops 'uncapped' for those datasets (_shared.py:6029, 6041-6042). So the in-memory search is built but never read there; this is wasted search, not a cut violation.


## noise n13 (tests/experiments/noise/n13_noise_distributions.py)

What it measures: For many injected label-noise shapes and levels, it measures how 12 noise-handling training methods (Track A, DNN) and sample weights from noise detectors (Track B) change scores on single representations and on hybrids.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. submit_everything.sh queues the noise suite on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213, 350-364). n13 is in the noise suite's default list (noise_helpers.py:66). should_skip_experiment never skips n13: it is in neither the nucleotide list nor the large-dataset list (_shared.py:3672-3675, 3684-3685). Inside n13, only the two grouped noise conditions are dropped, on datasets with no SMILES (n13:558-565).

### R1 models: NO

Code: The model list is config['models'] or DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE. Both are rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. dnn is always added for Track A. The similarity sweep also fits rf and svm on every evaluation unit. gp is never in the list. svm drops out above 10,000 rows.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two Step 1 models. Five pairs include gp: abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho. ridge excluded; knn is not a downstream model here.

### Other problems

- The recipe is chosen on clean labels of every row, including each fold's validation rows. The noise is then injected on training rows only (n13:1502-1504). So the selection saw the clean labels the experiment later corrupts.
- The comment at n13:1476-1480 says a per-fold search was left out to keep the run inside a 7-day wall. That is a compute cut, which the owner's rules forbid without a stated reason of degenerate, broken or undefined.
- The headline clean and noisy scores are rf on its rank-1 representation (n13:1033, 1296, 1964). rf is not an approved model on most datasets.
- 'top3_base_reps' is rf's top 3 on the whole-dataset search (n13:616, 1089; _shared.py:867). That is three representations ranked by rf.
- The svm warning at n13:525-530 cannot print. get_model_factories already drops svm above 10,000 rows (_shared.py:3066-3069; find_best_hybrid.py:2812).
- The listed DECISIONS sections have no rows for searches under objective='similarity'. n13 reads that family on both the general and distance searches. Whether it is allowed at all is not in the record.
- The noise start-up searches run with a pruning schedule (noise_helpers.py:1867). The reader asks with adaptive_pruning=False (_shared.py:5889). Could not determine whether pruning is part of the stored search's identity, so whether the similarity read finds the start-up search is not determined.
- The similarity sweep can build augmented single-representation spaces per fold from data['augmentations'] (n07_remediation.py:1712-1723). Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 datasets and lists this as an open check.
- n13's own folds come from cv_split (n13:1213-1214). The recipe ranking uses the stored search's folds. Could not determine whether the two partitions are the same rows; n13 does not check.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- n13_noise_distributions.py:209-221 and 1652-1685: one fold's hybrid build is cached by _bp_sig. That key holds allocation method, importance method, budget, internal evaluator and augmentation condition. It leaves out rep_count, which is a searched setting (result_cache.py:121-127). Two rule recipes that differ only in representation count get one build. The second is scored on the first's features under its own name.
- n13:1652-1685 and _shared.py:5129-5132: the same cache key leaves out the model. For a prediction-built recipe the accept-or-reject step inside build_fold_hybrid fits the model passed in. A second model with the same recipe reuses features accepted by the first model's fits. This hits every model filled from the cross-model ranking (n13:810-813), which all get one identical blueprint.
- find_best_hybrid.py:9568-9572 says rep_scores are no longer fed to a labelled rebuild because they saw held-out rows. _shared.py:5257-5259 still feeds them to build_fold_hybrid on each fold's labelled training rows. The two disagree; n13 takes the second path (n13:1675-1681, no precomputed_alloc_scores).
- Pruning question from the report, partly answered: pruning settings are in the search pickle key (find_best_hybrid.py:827-848). They are not in the result_db row identity or row config (result_cache.py:46-111, 113-135). The noise start-up uses default_pruning with final_strategy_threshold 0.15 (_shared.py:688-699); the reader asks adaptive_pruning=False (_shared.py:5889). Could not determine which store the similarity read then hits; I did not trace the pickle-then-result_db fallback.
- Fold partition question from the report: cv_split uses seed 42 and GroupKFold or StratifiedGroupKFold (_shared.py:2114-2139), the same splitter the pool's docstring names (_shared.py:6666-6671). n13 ranks with fold_i=None, so fold alignment does not enter its selection either way. Whether n_folds is 5 in n13's run could not be determined from what I read.
- The predictive general read is served from the in-memory start-up search, data['precomputed_searches'] (_shared.py:6781-6792), which run_all filled over all rows with the full grid (noise_helpers.py:1829-1840). So the general predictive recipes come from a search with no Step 2-7 cuts even when a cut search exists on disk.


## noise n14 (tests/experiments/noise/n14_activity_cliff_landscape.py)

What it measures: It counts activity-cliff pairs (similar molecules whose labels differ by more than 2 log units) and the shape of the graph they form, and fits one LightGBM to measure residual spread; it scores no downstream model.

Datasets: The noise runner queues n14 on all 41 datasets (submit_everything.sh, per the helper map, not re-opened). n14 produces numbers on 7 of them only: adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, herg_ki, logd, qm9. Those are the molecular regression datasets in the registry (printed this session with registry_lookup). It skips the rest in three places. should_skip_experiment skips the six nucleotide datasets (_shared.py:3678-3681, n14 in NUCLEOTIDE_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS) and any dataset over 15,000 rows (_shared.py:3665, 3684-3685), called at noise_helpers.py:1988. n14 itself skips classification (n14:418-422), non-molecular domains such as antibody, reaction, dta and tcga (n14:423-427), and over 15,000 rows again (n14:428-432). I did not check the row counts of the 7, except herg_ki at 1,412 molecules (registry print).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: n14 trains no downstream model. It fits three other things on its own. First, a LightGBM on every representation concatenated, out-of-fold over 5 folds, to measure residual spread. Second, a random forest on all molecules, for the forest_proximity similarity. Third, importance fits (lightgbm_gain, treeshap, deeplift) on the two base spaces. It picks its two base representations by rf's ranking in the stored search. rf is not an approved model on any of the 7 datasets it runs on.

Decisions: Step 1 approves svm+dnn on adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm and herg_ki; dnn+svm on caco2 and logd; dnn+lightgbm on qm9. Any representation choice should come from those models.

### R2 per fold: by design

Code: n14 has no held-out fold. Every similarity graph is built over all molecules, and no score is reported on held-out rows. The one fitted number with folds, the residual spread, uses cv_split folds and no search. The two base representations are ranked on the whole-dataset search's mean over its own folds. No hybrid is used.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows. n14 uses no hybrid and has no fold, so there is no held-out row for the whole-dataset ranking to leak into.
