### Other problems

- The file gives two answers on fitting to every molecule's label. It refuses the hybrid spaces because a build 'chooses features from every molecule's label' (n14:318-323, 364-368). It still fits a random forest on all molecules' labels for forest_proximity (similarity_space.py:638). It also fits lightgbm_gain, treeshap and deeplift on all labels for the weighted base spaces (similarity_space.py:664). So hybrids are skipped for a reason that applies equally to two kinds of space it does build.
- The noise runner builds two whole-dataset searches, predictive and similarity-objective, before any skip check (noise_helpers.py:1829, 1858 versus 1988). n14 then skips 34 of the 41 datasets. On those 34, the searches are still built or read first in n14's own process.
- Which augmentation condition the base representations are read from is chosen by rf's best hybrid score at any budget, including budgets Step 2 cuts (n14:348, _shared.py:6292-6298). I could not determine whether base-representation scores differ between the none, uncapped and capped searches.
- The base representations are picked once by rf for the whole dataset. The base_1 and base_2 spaces therefore do not match what any other noise experiment uses for the approved models on the same dataset.
- The residual-spread LightGBM is fitted on every representation concatenated with no width cap: 16,405 features against 1,412 molecules on herg_ki, per the file's own comment (n14:531-547). That number was not re-measured this session.
- The augmentation sizes in the helper map (32 of 41 datasets carry augmentation representations, adme/caco2/herg_ki/logd/qm9 among them) were not re-counted by me.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Similarity weightings outside the search cuts (n14 via similarity_space.py:224-229, 661-664). base_1 and base_2 are each weighted by deeplift and treeshap, fitted on every molecule's label. Step 3 cut deeplift from herg_ki's search and deeplift and treeshap from logd's (DECISIONS.md:330, 334). This is not a search, so R3 may not cover it. Whether those two methods stay as similarity weightings on those datasets is the owner's call.
- Standalone and run_all can read different whole-dataset searches. Under run_all the start-up search passes the runner's pruning schedule (noise_helpers.py:1807-1809, 1838-1839). When n14 runs alone, get_precomputed_search builds or reads with adaptive_pruning=False (_shared.py:5889). So base_1 and base_2 can come from a different search depending on how n14 is launched. Whether the two land on the same stored file was not checked.
- The skip-check count needs one correction. Of the 41 datasets in DECISIONS.md, 8 are molecular regression by the registry, not 7: chembl_qsar is the eighth. submit_all_datasets.sh:62-64 says chembl_qsar cannot be loaded and is not submitted. So n14 runs on 7 in practice, as the report says, and chembl_qsar has no Step 1 row.


## noise n15 (tests/experiments/noise/n15_clean_vs_noisy_hybrid.py)

What it measures: For each noise level and model, n15 builds two sets of hybrids. One was searched on clean labels, the other on noisy labels. It trains both on the noisy training labels and reports the per-fold score gap on clean validation labels.

Datasets: Every dataset the noise job runs, which is all 41 Step 1 datasets. n15 is in the noise suite's default list (tests/experiments/noise/noise_helpers.py:54,68). Nothing skips it by domain or size: n15 is in neither skip set (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675, 3684-3685). submit_everything.sh queues the noise category on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). It runs only in the noise job that has no noise condition. n15 is not in HONOURS_NOISE_CONDITION (noise_helpers.py:1586-1588), so a job with a condition skips it (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_dataset.sh:343-345).

### R1 models: NO

Code: The models are config['models'], which noise run_all sets to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. get_model_factories drops a model only above its row limit (svm above 10,000 rows). Both searches are told to fit that same list. _apply_small_dataset_models also adds gp to the search on small datasets. n15 never builds a gp cell, because gp is not in its model list. knn and ridge are never downstream models here; knn appears only as an internal evaluator in the distance search.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two Step 1 models. Five pairs include gp: abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho.

The draw count is wrong. noisy_search_specs reads dataset_policy.noise_levels(None), which returns 7 regression levels: 0.0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5. That gives 1 + 6x3 = 19 draws on a regression dataset, not 16. A classification dataset gets 6 levels x 3 draws = 18. The 16 comes from n15's docstring at n15:63-69, which is out of date. Each of the 30 configurations is also rebuilt on every fold, so a 5-fold run makes 150 hybrid builds per draw.
  - noise_helpers.py:266-283: levels from _policy_levels(None, ...); level 0.0 gets one seed on regression, every other level gets the 3 seeds.
  - noise_helpers.py:236 NOISY_SEARCH_SEEDS = (0, 1, 2).
  - dataset_policy.py:406 _NOISE_LEVELS = {}; :429 default is (0.0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5); :471 classification is (0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40).
  - A python import printed noise_levels(None) = (0.0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5) and the classification grid = (0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4).
  - n15:722-733 and n15:764-773 build every arm on every fold.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: Clean arm: its searches are on tiers 'general' and 'general_distance', which the cold-search refusal covers. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1 (the default in submit_everything.sh), it is refused when under half the configurations are stored and more than 500 are left. The refusal is caught: the pool prints a warning and skips that search. If all are refused, _fetch_bp returns nothing and the model is named in models_unscored with no cell. A refused distance read becomes a 'distance1' entry in rule_missing. Noisy arm: its tier carries a noise suffix, so it is never refused and always built, on all rows. It is built before the clean result is checked, so a refused clean arm still pays for the noisy search. Whether tuned fast-grid rows exist on the server could not be determined.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search is built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- Dataset-level R3 breaks. Budgets: the general search runs all 8 budgets, and the distance search runs 10-500 features. Both include budgets Step 2 or Step 7 cut on every dataset except humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc (DECISIONS.md:209-249, 613-650).
- Dataset-level R3 breaks. Importance: n15 runs lightgbm_gain alone everywhere. On buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer, Step 3 cut lightgbm_gain, so n15 runs only a cut method (DECISIONS.md:314, 316, 327, 328). On the 20 or so full-tier datasets that keep deeplift or treeshap, those are missing.
- Dataset-level R3 breaks. Allocation: softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2 are never searched. Step 4 keeps them on most full-tier datasets, for example abagym_VEGF, bindingdb_kd and tcga_luad_vs_lusc. On suzuki the decision is held; n15 runs three of the five methods anyway.
- Dataset-level R3 breaks. Representation counts 3 and all: Step 6 cuts 3 on 15 datasets. On buchwald_hartwig both counts n15 runs (3 and all) are cut, and the kept count 2 is absent (DECISIONS.md:574).
- Dataset-level R3 breaks. Evaluators: the general search keeps rf, lightgbm and dnn everywhere, including where Step 5 cut them: abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_titer. The distance search keeps knn and svm on the 11 datasets where Step 7 cut an evaluator.
- Dataset-level R3 breaks. Augmentation: uncapped and capped are built on every dataset that has augmentation representations. Step 8 cuts both everywhere except ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, which keep uncapped only (DECISIONS.md:658-698).
- The 10 fast-tier datasets match the fast-tier table on allocation, importance and counts. Two exceptions: gb_human_enhancers_cohn and nt_promoter_tata cut count 3 in Step 6, and n15 still runs it.
- n15 forces tuning and its own pruning. tune=True and the aggressive schedule are hard-coded and ignore PRUNING_MODE (n15:227-237). The precompute stored neither, so the clean arm cannot read it; the file's own TODO says this is the owner's call (n15:193-204).
- n15's folds come from cv_split without task_type (n15:534, 764-765). The engine's splitter takes task_type (find_best_hybrid.py:4049-4070). On a classification dataset with float-typed labels the two fold sets differ. _reusable_caches checks only fold numbers, not rows (n15:330-334). So reused importance and allocation scores could include this fold's validation rows. Label dtypes per dataset were not checked.
- extract_top3_base_reps is imported and never used (n15:119).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Draw count is 19 on regression and 18 on classification, not 16 (noise_helpers.py:266-283, dataset_policy.py:406, 429, 471). n15's own docstring at n15:63-69 says 6 levels and 16 draws. That is out of date: the grid gained level 1.5 and changed 0.15 to 0.2 on 2026-09-21 (dataset_policy.py:411-416).
- Importance on the distance search also breaks Step 7. n15 runs lightgbm_gain alone there too. Step 7 cuts lightgbm_gain from the distance search on cdr_flexibility and ginkgo_pr_cho (DECISIONS.md:623, 634). So n15's distance search on those two runs only a cut method. The report raised this for the general search only.
- Representation counts on the distance search also break Step 7. n15 runs counts 3 and all there. Step 7 cuts 3 on 12 datasets, including abagym_VEGF, buchwald_hartwig, herg_ki and nt_promoter_tata (DECISIONS.md:615, 621, 636, 644). On buchwald_hartwig, Step 7 also cuts all, so the distance search keeps only count 2, and n15 never runs 2 (DECISIONS.md:621).
- Allocation on the distance search breaks Step 7. On ddg_combined, Step 7 cuts power_2 and performance_weighted from the distance search (DECISIONS.md:624). n15 runs both through the fast list (find_best_hybrid.py:3072).
- Corrected wording for the evaluator bullet: the 11 datasets with a Step 7 evaluator cut are abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ddg_combined, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_titer and qm9 (DECISIONS.md:613-645). Between them they cut lightgbm, rf, svm, dnn and knn. n15's distance read always uses all five (_shared.py:6775, 502).
- No distance search is stored for bindingdb_kd, kiba or lhasa_herg (DECISIONS.md:609, 750). Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, n15's clean distance read on those three is refused whenever more than 500 configurations are missing (find_best_hybrid.py:665-697). It then lands in rule_missing as distance1 (n15:409-411).
- n15 asks get_rule_hybrids for 3 general recipes (n_general=3, n15:385), not RULE_N_GENERAL=2 (_shared.py:7064). general1 and general2 are ranked two different ways. general1 is the pool winner by score_mean (n15:287-298). general2 comes from the reader's mean over every fold (_shared.py:6746-6748), after skipping whatever matches general1 (n15:396-401).


## noise n16 (tests/experiments/noise/n16_importance_under_noise.py)

What it measures: For each fold and noise level, it measures how the per-feature importance ranking of each base representation, and of one fixed hybrid, moves away from its ranking under clean labels; it trains no downstream model.

Datasets: Queued on all 41 datasets: submit_everything.sh builds the roster from every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213), and noise is one of its categories (:95). n16 is in the noise default list (noise_helpers.py:69). It is not in NUCLEOTIDE_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS or LARGE_N_OOM_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS (_shared.py:3672-3685). n16 skips classification datasets itself (n16:493-500). So it produces rows on the 26 regression datasets only. I printed task_type from src/kirby/registry.py DATASET_REGISTRY this session. Regression (runs): abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. Classification (writes a skip marker): cdr_flexibility, flab_binding_adams, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, herg, humanness_therapeutic, lhasa_herg, the five nt_ datasets, tcga_brca_pam50, tcga_luad_vs_lusc, tz_her2_binary, tz_her2_multiclass. The noise run_all still builds its two whole-dataset searches on those 15 before n16 skips (noise_helpers.py:1829-1870).

### R1 models: NO

Code: n16 fits no downstream model on the held-out rows. It uses rf twice. First, it picks the hybrid recipe as rf's best configuration (n16:591-597, downstream_model='rf'). Second, it hands an rf instance to build_fold_hybrid, which uses it to score which features are admitted (n16:612-615, 921-928). The search it reads scores five models: rf, lightgbm, dnn, xgboost, svm (precompute_hybrid_searches passes models=None, _shared.py:5574; noise run_all passes no models, noise_helpers.py:1829-1841). The importance scorers (deeplift, lightgbm_gain, treeshap) fit their own estimators inside compute_feature_importance (n16:317-320).

Decisions: Only each dataset's two approved models from Step 1. ridge nowhere; knn only where Step 9 allows.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: One recipe is read from the whole-dataset general search that noise run_all built on every row (noise_helpers.py:1829-1841, precompute_hybrid_searches on unsliced labels, _shared.py:5569-5593). The same recipe is used on every fold and every noise level. Its own metadata says selection_scope 'whole_dataset' (_shared.py:6430). Each fold refits the features on that fold's training rows (n16:821-824, 921-928). But build_fold_hybrid also picks WHICH representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores when rep_count is below the pool size (_shared.py:5256-5286). Those scores are each representation's best baseline over every row the search ran on (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593). n16 subsets to bp.reps first (n16:756-767), but bp.reps lists the whole pool, not the rep_count chosen (find_best_hybrid.py:1523-1530). So that subset narrows nothing.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### Other problems

- The recipe chooses which representations to keep from whole-dataset scores. n16 hands build_fold_hybrid every representation in bp.reps (n16:756-767). bp.reps is the whole pool, not the rep_count used (find_best_hybrid.py:1523-1530). build_fold_hybrid then keeps the top rep_count by blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5286). Those are best-over-all-models baselines on every row (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593). The comment at n16:748-753 says the subset restricts to 'the representations the recipe scored'. It does not narrow anything.
- The comment at n16:151-155 says the three importance methods are 'the three the engine can actually pick'. After Step 3 that is not true per dataset. Example: Step 3 cuts deeplift on herg_ki, and keeps only lightgbm_gain on qm9. n16 still measures drift under all three on every dataset (n16:155, 517). This is the measured quantity, not a search axis, so it is listed here and not under R3.
- The docstring argues the clean-label whole-dataset recipe is a control, not a leak, because no performance number is reported (n16:44-53, 643-653). A recipe from a clean search on each fold's training rows would also be held fixed across noise levels. So the stated reason does not require the whole-dataset search.
- On 19 of the 26 regression datasets rf is not an approved model. It still picks the recipe and scores feature admission. rf is approved on bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_titer, kiba, suzuki (DECISIONS.md Step 1). Even there, only one of the two approved models is used.
- The comment at n16:583-585 cites noise_helpers.py:351-367 for the precompute. The precompute call is now at noise_helpers.py:1829-1841. The line reference is stale.
- On the 15 classification datasets n16 only writes a skip marker (n16:493-500). The noise run_all still builds the two whole-dataset searches there first (noise_helpers.py:1829-1870). Other noise experiments may need them; for n16 they are unused.
- The pool reader asks for 'capped' on the general tier (_shared.py:6044) on every augmented dataset, including ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, where Step 8 keeps uncapped only.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R1: rf enters a third way. If the recipe's internal evaluator is 'match', the rebuild resolves 'match' to rf. This is because n16 hands create_hybrid an rf instance (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5870-5874; tests/experiments/noise/n16_importance_under_noise.py:614-615, 921-928).
- R2: the comment at n16:748-753 says build_fold_hybrid does not subset representations by itself. It now does, by rep_count from blueprint.rep_scores (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5256-5286). The comment is out of date, and the n16 subset at n16:756-767 changes nothing because bp.reps is the whole pool (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:5389-5398).
- R3, could not determine: the two ways of building the search set pruning differently, and I did not check whether they share a stored key. noise run_all builds it with adaptive_pruning_schedule from 'default_pruning' (noise_helpers.py:1838). That schedule prints as final_strategy_threshold 0.15 this session. get_precomputed_search builds it with adaptive_pruning=False (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5889). In a standalone run, that second path is the only one used (n16:1258).
- R3: the recipe can carry a budget that Step 2 cuts. budget=None takes rf's best across all 8 budgets, 10 to 2000 features (tests/experiments/_shared.py:7517-7523). That chosen budget is then used on every fold and every noise level (n16:917-928).


## noise n17 (tests/experiments/noise/n17_replicate_removal.py)

What it measures: It measures whether removing or relabelling training molecules helps when the label noise is real disagreement between laboratories. Each entity trains on one real measurement and is graded on the mean of its other measurements.

Datasets: n17 has no dataset list of its own. It runs on every dataset the noise runner is given and skips most of them. It skips any dataset that is not regression (n17_replicate_removal.py:714-720). It also skips any dataset with no repeat-measurement grouping (n17_replicate_removal.py:726-734). That grouping comes from build_replicate_groups (noise/_ground_truth_providers.py:164-198). It finds one in two places. The first is data['replicate_groups'], which only the herg_ic50 loader sets (_shared.py:4611-4616, 4727-4731). The second is metadata drug_ids/protein_ids, which the drug-target loader sets (src/kirby/datasets/dta.py:353-360) for davis, kiba and bindingdb_kd (_shared.py:3559). A dataset with fewer than 30 entities measured 3 or more times is skipped too (n17_replicate_removal.py:880-884). submit_everything.sh queues the noise jobs on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213). So in the full submission n17 can only produce numbers on bindingdb_kd and kiba. herg_ic50 runs only when it is named by hand. It has no DATASET_REPS entry of its own and borrows herg_ki's representations (noise/noise_helpers.py:1640, 1653-1660). It also has no row in DECISIONS.md. Could not determine whether kiba has 30 entities measured 3 or more times; I did not load the data.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Models are config['models'], or DOWNSTREAM_MODELS if that is empty. The noise runner sets them to rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. svm drops out above 10,000 rows. The drug-target sets are cut to 30,000 rows, so svm drops out on bindingdb_kd and kiba. Every arm is then fitted with rf, xgboost, dnn and lightgbm. ridge is never used, and knn is never a downstream model here.

Decisions: bindingdb_kd: rf+dnn. kiba: dnn+rf. On both, n17 also fits xgboost and lightgbm, so each runs two models the record excludes. herg_ic50 has no Step 1 row, so it has no approved pair to check against. Step 9 keeps knn in the distance search on both datasets. n17 reads that search but fits no knn.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe is fetched once, before any fold, from searches over all rows of the dataset. The lookup gets the row-level representations, labels and groups. get_rule_hybrids is called without fold_i, so it ranks on the mean over all of the stored search's folds. get_best_search_for_downstream labels its own pick 'whole_dataset'. The same recipe is then rebuilt on each fold's training entities. If a recipe used fewer representations than the full set, the rebuild picks which ones from blueprint.rep_scores, which also come from the whole-dataset search. The main arms run every loaded base representation, so no base representation is picked there. The similarity-axis base_1/base_2 and the top-2 extra block are ranked on the whole-dataset search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used in a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows. In n17, the recipe chooser saw the held-out entities' rows. Their labels are the same measurements that are averaged into those entities' grading labels. The rebuild per fold fixes the feature weights, not the choice of recipe.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: bindingdb_kd and kiba are both on the code's fast list, so every search on them uses the fast lists. General searches have all 8 budgets (10-2000 features). n17 asks with budget=None, so a recipe at 10-100 features can win. The distance searches use budgets 10-500, evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm, and models including knn. The noise runner builds uncapped and capped general searches whenever augmentation representations are passed. The pool then reads general 'none' and 'capped' on these two datasets. The similarity sweep also builds an uncapped augmented feature set for each model's top two base representations.

Decisions: bindingdb_kd: budgets 250-2000, all three importance methods, all five allocation methods, all four evaluators, representation counts 2 and all (3 and 5 cut), augmentation cut. The code differs on five axes: it adds budgets 10/25/50/100, lacks deeplift and treeshap, lacks softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2, runs count 3 and lacks 2, and builds augmented searches. Only the evaluators match. kiba: budgets 250-2000, all three importance methods, four stored allocation methods (softmax_T1, power_2, performance_weighted, rank_exp_d0.3), all four evaluators, count all only, augmentation cut. The code also differs on five axes for kiba: budgets, importance, softmax_T1 missing, count 3 kept, augmentation built. Step 7 has no decision for either dataset, because no distance search is stored. Yet n17 reads one with the same lists as every other dataset. herg_ic50 has no rows at all.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each model, every arm is measured in every loaded base representation (10 on these datasets). By design it also runs up to six hybrid feature sets: 2 general and 1 distance from the prediction-built search, and the same three from the similarity-built search. One set is chosen for the whole dataset, not one per fold. It also writes each model's top 2 base representations and top 2 hybrids from the stored search as a side record, with no fits. The similarity sweep uses each model's top 2 base representations and three hybrid feature sets.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n17 runs 10 base representations instead of 2 and up to 6 hybrids instead of 2, chosen once on all rows instead of per fold. Running every base representation is stated as deliberate in the docstring. The hybrid count comes from the shared top-2-general-plus-1-distance rule.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n17 never builds or requests a search on one fold's training rows. When a stored member is missing, get_precomputed_search runs find_best_hybrid on all rows inside the job. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH that search is refused if more than 500 configurations are unstored. The refusal is caught, printed as a warning, and that member is skipped. With no usable member, the lookup prints a warning and returns nothing. n17 then runs base representations only, or gives that model no hybrid.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n17 has no per-fold search path at all. Its fallback is a whole-dataset build, or a refusal and a skip.

### Other problems

- The result file writes hybrid_sees_grading_labels=False and says the consensus labels never reach any feature ranking (n17_replicate_removal.py:95-99, 852-857). The recipe was chosen by a search over every measurement row (n17_replicate_removal.py:903-909). Those rows include the measurements that are averaged into the held-out entities' grading labels. So the stored claim is true of the per-fold rebuild and false of the recipe choice.
- The hybrid rebuild passes no augmentation matrices (n17_replicate_removal.py:1381-1389). On bindingdb_kd and kiba the general pool includes the 'capped' search (_shared.py:6040-6046). A capped recipe is therefore rebuilt without the augmentation features its search used; hybrid_for_fold's own docstring warns of this (noise_helpers.py:982-985). Could not determine whether the build then narrows silently or fails; I did not read create_hybrid.
- On bindingdb_kd and kiba the start-up search builds an 'uncapped' general search (_shared.py:5543-5548) that the pool never reads, because _pool_conditions leaves uncapped out for these two (_shared.py:5989, 6042-6043). The comment at _shared.py:5969-5984 says uncapped general/none alone measured about 4 days on bindingdb_kd.
- herg_ic50 is the dataset this file was built for (comments at n17_replicate_removal.py:181-191, 521-527), but it has no row in DECISIONS.md. Step 1 names no approved pair for it, and Steps 2-9 have no cuts for it.
- The cost comment counts two hybrid spaces and 5,400 fits (n17_replicate_removal.py:116-121). The rule read now gives up to six hybrid spaces per model (_shared.py:6508-6535), so that count is out of date.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The code's fast list and the record disagree for bindingdb_kd and kiba. dataset_policy.py:701-708 added both to the fast list on 2026-10-02. The record's fast-tier table (DECISIONS.md:350-363) lists ten other datasets. The record also shows all three importance methods stored for both (DECISIONS.md:313, 332). Every setting in the fast lists is part of the search's cache key (find_best_hybrid.py:3059-3061). So n17's start-up search may not match the stored one. I could not determine whether the stored rows are enough to avoid a new whole-dataset search or a refusal.
- Two start-up search settings may not match what the readers ask for. The noise start-up search passes the runner's pruning schedule (noise_helpers.py:1838, 1867). get_precomputed_search, which the readers use, sets adaptive_pruning=False (_shared.py:5889). For the predictive family this does not matter, because the reader takes it from memory (_shared.py:6084-6085). The similarity family is always read from disk (_shared.py:6081-6085). If the cache key includes the pruning settings, that read misses the search the start-up just built. I did not confirm that the key includes them.
- With fold_i=None, the rule read labels its own result wrongly. It sets selection_scope 'other_folds_of_pool_search' and the note 'fold None contributed nothing to the ranking' (_shared.py:7037-7042). In fact every fold went into the ranking.
- The agent's list of search calls marks the per-fold rebuild (n17_replicate_removal.py:1381-1389) and the similarity-sweep builds (_sim_axis_n15_n22.py:242-253, 270-279) as 'whole dataset'. Both builds are fitted on each fold's training entities. Features are ranked and the budget is split on those rows (_shared.py:5345-5356). What comes from the whole dataset is the choice of recipe, of base_1/base_2, and of which representations a rep_count recipe keeps.
- In the similarity sweep, the augmented sets for base_1 and base_2 use uncapped augmentation on bindingdb_kd and kiba (similarity_space.py:119, _sim_axis_n15_n22.py:229-253). Step 8 cuts augmentation on both datasets (DECISIONS.md:666, 685). DECISIONS.md:654 says this conflict with noise base_k_aug_uncapped is an open check. So the sweep differs from Step 8 even though no search is involved.


## noise n18 (tests/experiments/noise/n18_clean_the_real_labels.py)

What it measures: Per fold, it compares a model trained on the labels as loaded with the same kind of model trained after each of seven label cleanups, and counts the folds the cleaned model wins.

Datasets: All 41 datasets in DECISIONS Step 1. n18 is in the noise list SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (noise/noise_helpers.py:79). It is not in either skip list (_shared.py:3672-3675 nucleotide, 3684-3685 over 15,000 rows). submit_everything.sh queues noise on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:207-213). It does not run in the jobs that inject a noise condition, because it is not in HONOURS_NOISE_CONDITION (noise_helpers.py:1586-1588, 1768-1770).

### R1 models: NO

Code: It fits config['models'] or DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. Both are rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. gp is never named, so it is never fitted. svm is dropped above 10,000 rows. knn and ridge are never fitted as downstream models. The cleanups fit their own models inside the method (LightGBM, a Gaussian process, a quantile forest), but these are not downstream models.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two approved models from Step 1. knn is not allowed downstream here, and ridge is excluded.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each of five models, it scores 2 base representations and up to 6 hybrids. Those are ranks 1 and 2 from the general searches and rank 1 from the distance searches, each taken for the predictive and the similarity search. The same set is used on every fold. It is not re-picked per fold.

Decisions: For each of the dataset's two models, on each fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### R5 noise 8 configurations: NO

Code: Each model gets 2 base representations and up to 6 hybrids, so up to 8 feature spaces per model. With five models that is up to 40 feature spaces, and every cleanup is scored in each one. With only the two approved models it would still be 16, not 8.

Decisions: Two models, each with its 2 best base representations and 2 best hybrids: 8 configurations in total.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n18 never builds a per-fold search. A missing stored search goes to get_precomputed_search, which builds it over all rows. If KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is set and more than 500 configurations are missing, the build is refused instead. submit_everything.sh sets that variable by default. The refusal is caught, a warning is printed, and that pool member is skipped. The missing slot is recorded and the run carries on without it. A model with no general search loses its hybrids and also its two base representations.

Decisions: The experiment must build any per-fold search it needs itself. It must not refuse or skip.

### Other problems

- Augmented recipes are rebuilt without their augmentation features. The pool reader can return a recipe chosen under uncapped or capped and stamps that condition on it (_shared.py:6992-6996). n18 calls the per-fold build with no augmentation features (n18:1283-1288; hybrid_for_fold default None, noise_helpers.py:951). create_hybrid adds augmentation only when augmentation features are passed (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5984). So the matrix scored differs from the recipe the search scored, under that recipe's name.
- The file's docstring says the held-out labels reach no feature ranking and no budget split (n18:65-69). The recipe itself was chosen with those rows. Under a representation count below the pool size, which representations are kept also comes from whole-dataset scores (_shared.py:5256-5286).
- Noise run_all builds no distance search (noise_helpers.py:1817-1903). The distance hybrids n18 reads therefore come from disk, a build over all rows inside the job, or nothing. DECISIONS records no stored distance search for bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg (DECISIONS.md:750).
- On the five datasets whose approved pair includes gp, n18 lacks gp and fits four unapproved models: abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho (DECISIONS.md:11,13,30,32,33). On the other 36 datasets it fits three unapproved models.
- Four datasets run the fast grid in code, but DECISIONS does not list them as fast: flab_expression_koenig, logd, bindingdb_kd, kiba (dataset_policy.py:688; DECISIONS.md:352-363). On flab_expression_koenig, bindingdb_kd and kiba, Step 3 keeps all three importance methods, and the fast grid searches lightgbm_gain only (find_best_hybrid.py:3674).
- R3 by dataset: every dataset except humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc keeps fewer than all 8 general budgets in Step 2. So the read grids include budgets she cut on 39 of 41 datasets. Augmentation is cut on 39 datasets, but uncapped and capped are read wherever augmentation features are loaded. Unverified: that tcga_luad_vs_lusc carries augmentation features. If it does, humanness_therapeutic is the only dataset whose read grid matches Steps 2-8.
- The similarity sweep adds an augmented space for each of the two base representations (base_1_aug_uncapped, base_2_aug_uncapped) on every dataset with augmentation features (_sim_axis_n15_n22.py:229-260; similarity_space.py:119-121). Step 8 cuts augmentation on all datasets except ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, and its open check names this space.
- Could not determine whether the similarity search n18 asks for from disk has the same stored identity as the one run_all builds. run_all passes its pruning schedule (noise_helpers.py:1867); get_precomputed_search forces adaptive_pruning=False (_shared.py:5889). If the two differ, n18 builds or refuses a second whole-dataset search.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R1 at the search level. The general search n18 reads names rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm, and gp on small datasets. The distance read names those five plus knn. Step 1 and Step 7 say each search's downstream models are the dataset's decided pair, with knn added in the distance search by Step 9. So the stored searches n18 needs score three or four models outside the pair. Evidence: tests/experiments/_shared.py:1074-1078, 1112; tests/experiments/_shared.py:6774-6777; scratchpad/precompute_cuts/DECISIONS.md:607.
- R3, augmentation detail. Step 8 keeps uncapped only, on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, and cuts capped everywhere. The general pool still reads capped wherever augmentation features are loaded, those two datasets included. Evidence: tests/experiments/_shared.py:6040-6046; scratchpad/precompute_cuts/DECISIONS.md:677-678.
- R3, the noise start-up search adds uncapped for any dataset with augmentation features. It does not apply UNCAPPED_SKIP_DATASETS (bindingdb_kd, kiba). The pool reader does apply it. So on those two datasets run_all can build an uncapped search that n18 never reads. Evidence: tests/experiments/_shared.py:5543-5548 vs 5989 and 6022.
- R3, evaluator cuts on the distance search. Step 7 cuts the knn evaluator on buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic. It also cuts svm, lightgbm, rf or dnn on several other datasets. The distance read sets DISTANCE_EVALUATORS for every dataset. Evidence: tests/experiments/_shared.py:502, 6774-6777; scratchpad/precompute_cuts/DECISIONS.md:617-645.
- R3, representation counts. Step 6 cuts count 3 on gb_human_enhancers_cohn and nt_promoter_tata. The fast lists those datasets run keep counts 3 and all. Evidence: src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:3070; scratchpad/precompute_cuts/DECISIONS.md:584, 600.


## noise n19 (tests/experiments/noise/n19_measurement_count.py)

What it measures: Whether weighting, relabelling or adding a feature from each molecule's measurement count and measurement spread improves held-out scores over training on the labels untouched.

Datasets: n19 runs only where the loader keeps one row per measurement. It skips non-regression datasets (n19:791-795). It skips datasets with no repeat structure, where build_replicate_groups returns None (n19:797-802; _ground_truth_providers.py:178-198). It also skips datasets with fewer than 30 molecules measured 3 or more times (n19:933-938). Repeat structure comes from two loaders. herg_ic50 sets replicate_groups (_shared.py:4612-4616, 4727-4731). The three DTA datasets, davis, kiba and bindingdb_kd, carry drug_ids and protein_ids metadata (_shared.py:3559, 4513-4526). submit_everything.sh queues noise on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:211-213). herg_ic50 has no DATASET_REPS key; it borrows herg_ki's representations (noise_helpers.py:1640, 1653-1657). So the default roster gives n19 real work on bindingdb_kd only. kiba is in the roster too. Could not determine whether kiba has 30 molecules measured 3+ times; I did not load it. herg_ic50 runs only when named explicitly, and it has no DECISIONS.md row. bindingdb_kd's DECISIONS rows: Step 1 rf+dnn (line 19), Step 2 v3 250-2000 (217), Step 3 v2 keep all three (313), Step 4 keep all five (379), Step 5 v3 keep all four (524), Step 6 cut 3/5 (573), Step 7 no row because no distance search is stored (609), Step 8 cut (666), Step 9 knn run (716).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Downstream models come from config['models'] (n19:841-842). noise run_all sets that to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE (noise_helpers.py:1751), a copy of rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm (_shared.py:565, 857). get_model_factories drops svm above 10,000 molecules (_shared.py:3066-3069; find_best_hybrid.py:2812). By the loader's own comment, bindingdb_kd has about 30,000 rows and 2,017 repeated pairs over 5,480 rows (_shared.py:4457-4458). That puts it well above 10,000 molecules, so svm is dropped (my arithmetic, not run). On bindingdb_kd that leaves rf, xgboost, dnn and lightgbm. Beside them, n19 always fits six extra learners by default (n19:300-302, 854-855). Those are ngboost, a gp on up to 1,000 training molecules (n19:309, 864-868), and an xgboost survival:aft model (n19:869-872). No ridge and no knn are fitted.

Decisions: bindingdb_kd: rf and dnn only (DECISIONS.md:19). herg_ic50 has no Step 1 row; herg_ki, whose representations it borrows, is svm+dnn (DECISIONS.md:36).

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every recipe and every base representation is chosen once, from searches over all rows of the dataset. The pool reader is handed the row-level reps, labels and groups, unsliced (n19:951-957). get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index (noise_helpers.py:1414-1422), so it ranks on the mean over all folds (_shared.py:7082-7084). get_best_search_for_downstream marks its own pick 'whole_dataset' (_shared.py:6430). The top 2 base representations are ranked off that same stored search (n19:995-997). That ranking is the search's mean over its own folds on all rows (_shared.py:4876-4880). n19 then rebuilds each recipe's features on each fold's training molecules (n19:1464-1483). But the recipe, its representations and the base ranking were picked with the held-out molecules in view. Those include the very measurements that form each held-out molecule's grading label. build_fold_hybrid also takes blueprint.rep_scores to pick which representations to keep when the recipe's representation count is below the pool size (_shared.py:5256-5262).

Decisions: Every hybrid and base representation for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: The rule read ranks every stored configuration the model scored, at every budget, because budget=None is passed (n19:954; _shared.py:6848-6858). No Step 2-7 filter is applied to the candidates. The general pool reads 'none' and 'capped' on bindingdb_kd. uncapped is skipped there (_shared.py:5989, 6040-6044). The distance pool reads 'none' only on bindingdb_kd, because it has over 10,000 rows (_shared.py:6030-6037). Distance reads use budgets 10-500 and evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm on every dataset (_shared.py:495, 502, 6774-6777). A missing search is built with the fast grid on bindingdb_kd (dataset_policy.py:708; _shared.py:5895, 1049-1053). The fast grid is lightgbm_gain only, 3 allocation methods, and representation counts 3 and all (find_best_hybrid.py:3071-3072, 3674).

Decisions: bindingdb_kd general search: budgets 250-2000 (DECISIONS.md:217). Keep deeplift, lightgbm_gain and treeshap (313). Keep all five allocation methods (379). Keep all four evaluators (524). Representation counts: cut 3 and 5, keep 2 and all (573). Distance: no Step 7 row, since nothing is stored (609). Augmentation: cut (666). So the read and the decision differ in three ways at once. Budgets 10, 25, 50 and 100 enter the ranking. Representation counts 3 and 5 enter it. The capped searches enter it. If the search is built in the job instead, it lacks deeplift, treeshap, softmax_T1, wglobal_power2 and count 2. It also runs count 3, which the record cuts. herg_ic50 has no rows to compare against.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each downstream model, n19 builds the top 2 base representations as spaces base_1 and base_2 (n19:995-1002, 1427-1448). The hybrids come from the rule read: per search family, 2 general hybrids plus 1 distance hybrid (_shared.py:7064-7066). n19 asks for two families, predictive and similarity (n19:344; _shared.py:5937). Each slot becomes its own space: hybrid, hybrid__general2 and hybrid__distance1, then the same three for hybrid_similarity (_shared.py:6508-6535). So each model gets 2 base representations and up to 6 hybrids, not 2. The extra learners are fitted only in the first model's features (n19:1007-1010, 1489-1490). The comment at n19:1115-1118 still says the hybrid is one recipe fetched for the first model. Lines 948-957 fetch one per model, so the comment and the code disagree.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids, chosen on that fold.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n19 builds no per-fold search anywhere. Every pool member goes through get_precomputed_search. That function returns the in-memory whole-dataset search first (_shared.py:5841-5843). Otherwise it calls find_best_hybrid on all rows with cache=True (_shared.py:5863-5896). noise run_all fills only the general dicts (noise_helpers.py:1826-1870). So every distance read goes to disk, and bindingdb_kd has no stored distance search (DECISIONS.md:609, 750). Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, a search that is not exempt is checked by _refuse_cold_search (find_best_hybrid.py:9355-9369). A refusal is caught, printed as a warning, and that pool member is skipped (_shared.py:6108-6114). The missing slot is then recorded and the run continues without it (_shared.py:7171-7178; n19:1019-1029). Without the variable, the missing search is built over all rows inside the job.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, on that fold's training rows.

### Other problems

- The grading labels and the recipe disagree about who saw what. Each held-out molecule is graded on the mean of its measurements not used for training (n19:17-20). The whole-dataset search trained and scored on every measurement row, including those same measurements (n19:951-957).
- n19's folds are not the pool's folds. n19 splits one row per molecule with cv_split (n19:1363-1365). The pool's fold scores are over measurement rows. With fold_i=None this does not change the ranking, but no fold-level match exists either.
- results['spaces'] is written as the four names in SPACES (n19:888, 322-323). The spaces actually run can be up to eight, recorded only in 'spaces_run' (n19:1112).
- The module docstring says one hybrid per search family (n19:163-172). The code builds up to three per family per model through the rule read (_shared.py:6508-6535).
- On bindingdb_kd the runner's start-up search builds 'uncapped' (_shared.py:5543-5548). The pool read never asks for it (_shared.py:5989, 6042). So the runner pays for searches n19 does not read.
- On every dataset without repeat structure, noise run_all still builds both whole-dataset start-up searches before n19 skips (noise_helpers.py:1826-1870; n19:797-802).
- The extra learners (ngboost, gp, xgboost survival:aft) are always fitted in the first downstream model's features only (n19:1007-1010). On bindingdb_kd that model is rf.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Which predictive general search n19 actually reads. The in-memory search is served before anything on disk (_shared.py:5840-5843). get_fold_pool_recipes uses data['precomputed_searches'] for it when data is passed (_shared.py:6777-6788). n19 passes data (n19:953-956). That in-memory search is the one noise run_all builds at start-up under 'default_pruning' (noise_helpers.py:1706, 1808-1842). default_pruning drops allocation methods after fold 0, with final_strategy_threshold 0.15 (_shared.py:688-697). The precompute default is no pruning (_shared.py:666-686). So the stored precompute and n19's read differ in the allocation methods searched. The read also chose its candidates using fold 0's scores. Unverified whether the pruning schedule is part of the search cache key.
- Speed is part of the search cache key (find_best_hybrid.py:3059-3061). bindingdb_kd was added to FAST_SPEED_DATASETS on 2026-10-02 (dataset_policy.py:699-708). The stored bindingdb_kd general search that DECISIONS.md describes holds deeplift, treeshap and five allocation methods (DECISIONS.md:313, 379), which is the full grid. Every n19 call on bindingdb_kd asks for the fast grid (_shared.py:1046-1053, 5895). So the stored full-grid search cannot answer n19's read. The fast search is either built over all rows inside the noise job, or refused under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH. Could not determine whether a fast-grid bindingdb_kd search is already on disk.
- herg_ic50 is one of the two datasets the n19 docstring names (n19:10-11, 210). It has no row in any Step 1-9 table (grep of DECISIONS.md for herg_ic50 returns nothing). So it has no approved models, budgets or other cuts to follow.


## noise n20 (tests/experiments/noise/n20_clean_before_search.py)

What it measures: For each outer fold, it measures whether choosing the hybrid's features from cleaned training labels beats choosing them from the labels as they are, with each model scored on untouched held-out labels.

Datasets: All 41 datasets. submit_everything.sh queues the noise category on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:95, :207-213, :350-374). n20 is in the noise list (noise_helpers.py:86). It is in neither skip list (_shared.py:3672-3675 nucleotide, :3684-3685 over 15,000 rows), so it also runs on the six nucleotide datasets and on kiba and bindingdb_kd. It takes a noise condition (noise_helpers.py:1586); its default is outlier_p10 (n20:393, :887).

### R1 models: NO

Code: The model list is config['models'] (n20:923-924). The noise runner sets it to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, which is rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset (noise_helpers.py:1751; printed this session). svm is dropped from that list when the whole dataset has more than 10,000 rows (_shared.py:3066-3069, n20:925-927). gp is never added: n20 does not call _apply_small_dataset_models. knn and ridge are never in the list. On the six nucleotide datasets the engine skips xgboost inside the search (printed: _applied_skips gives ['xgboost'] for nt_H3K27me3 and gb_human_enhancers_cohn). n20 keeps xgboost because its factory exists. get_best_for_downstream with budget=None then falls through to the best recipe of any model (_shared.py:7537-7545). So xgboost is fitted on another model's recipe under its own name (n20:1442, :1891). The two single representations the cleaning runs in are ranked by rf on every dataset (n20:424, :1507-1509). The similarity sweep also uses rf's recipes (n20:1285-1293).

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models; knn only where Step 9 allows; no ridge.

### R2 per fold: yes

Code: Every search is built inside the fold loop. The representations are sliced to the fold's training rows (n20:1416-1419). The labels are labels[train_idx], or those rows after injection (n20:1401-1414). The groups are groups[train_idx] (n20:1396). The uncleaned search runs on those rows (n20:1425-1431); each cleaned search runs on the same rows or the kept subset (n20:1671-1705, :1751-1759). The two hybrids per model and the two single representations are read from that fold's own search (n20:1442, :1464, :1507). Each hybrid is rebuilt on the fold's training rows with build_fold_hybrid (noise_helpers.py:1002-1024). Its representation scores come from the same per-fold search. Held-out rows are graded on labels[val_idx] (n20:1395). n20 never reads the whole-dataset searches the noise runner builds at start-up.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold comes from a search on that fold's training rows only.

Representation count 3 is run where Step 6 cuts it on 15 datasets. buchwald_hartwig keeps only count 2, and the fast list has only 3 and all, both cut there. Augmentation 'none' agrees with Step 8 for a general search.

Decisions: Each dataset's Step 2 budget range, Step 3 importance methods, Step 4 allocation methods, Step 5 evaluators, Step 6 representation counts, the fast-tier table for its ten datasets, and Step 8 augmentation.

Code: n20 calls find_best_hybrid itself on every fold, with cache on (n20:543-562). The cold-search refusal does not apply to it. A failed cleaned search is printed but writes no '_errors' entry; its two arms are left empty (n20:1751-1759, :1889-1890).

### Other problems

- On the six nucleotide datasets, xgboost's results are another model's recipe filed under xgboost. n20 keeps xgboost because get_model_factories has no domain skip (_shared.py:3060-3075). The search skips it (dataset_policy.py:35). get_best_for_downstream with budget=None then returns the best recipe of any model (_shared.py:7537-7545). xgboost's rank-2 slot is empty and recorded as an error, because top_hybrids has no cross-model fallback (_shared.py:7925-7927, n20:1464-1470).
- The comment at n20:938-940 cites an owner decision of 2026-09-30: every experiment that builds its own search runs the fast grid. DECISIONS.md sets per-dataset grids on 2026-10-03. The two disagree, and the code follows the earlier one. I did not verify the 2026-09-30 decision itself.
- The docstring says both searches use the aggressive pruning schedule (n20:144-148, :433-434). The default is calibrated (n20:941-942). The two disagree.
- The calibrated schedule can delete members of the allocation, evaluator and representation-count axes inside each per-fold search after folds 0 and 1 (find_best_hybrid.py:3789-3890, per the helper map; not re-read). The docstring at n20:167-169 says the representation-count and allocation axes must keep more than one value. Nothing checks that after pruning.
- The comments at n20:636-641 and n20:2313-2318 say stored configurations never re-enter all_results. The engine appends every stored row this call asked for to the results list (find_best_hybrid.py:7536-7555). The two disagree. This affects how the candidate count in the identity check is read, not which recipe is chosen.
- noise run_all's pruning_mode argument is not forwarded to n20 (noise_helpers.py:2031-2047). n20 always runs calibrated unless a caller passes pruning_mode itself.
- Both searches tune hyperparameters (tune=True, 20 iterations). Whether the stored rows behind DECISIONS.md were tuned: could not determine, I did not check.
- Whether any dataset with svm in its approved pair has more than 10,000 rows, which would drop svm here: could not determine, I did not look up dataset sizes.
- A failed cleaned search is printed but not written to '_errors' (n20:563-566, :1751-1759, :1889-1890). Its two arms are left empty with no recorded reason.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R1: on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho, Step 1 approves gp. n20's model list has no gp, so one of the two approved models is never fitted on those five datasets. Evidence: DECISIONS.md:12,14,30,32,33; _shared.py:857; n20:923-924.
- Cleaned side: when the cleaned search has no rank-2 recipe for a model, the arm is skipped with no '_errors' entry (n20:1891-1893). The uncleaned side records the same case (n20:1464-1470).
- R3 / Step 8: the similarity sweep builds neighbour spaces with augmentation features on every dataset that supplies them (n20:1231, :1295-1306). Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 datasets. It also lists noise's base_k_aug_uncapped as an open check (DECISIONS.md:654), so this is unsettled, not a confirmed break.
- The similarity sweep never passes a similarity-objective recipe ('hybrid_similarity'), so that neighbour space is always unavailable (n20:1213, :1287-1293). No per-fold distance search is built, so nothing under Step 7's cuts is run or read.
- Rank 2 is chosen with _bp_key, which includes step_size (n20:584-592). Two recipes that differ only in step_size count as distinct. Rank 2 can then be the rank-1 configuration at another step. Not run, read from code only.


## noise n21 (tests/experiments/noise/n21_neighbour_distance.py)

What it measures: For molecules whose training labels were deliberately corrupted, it measures how well each of several distances finds them through nearest-neighbour label disagreement, and how much a repair weighted by that disagreement recovers.

Datasets: Every dataset the noise suite is queued on. submit_everything.sh builds the list from every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213), and queues noise on all of them (CATEGORIES, :95). n21 is in the noise default list (noise_helpers.py:98). It is in neither skip set, so no dataset is skipped by size or by the nucleotide rule (_shared.py:3672-3675, 3684-3685). The six nucleotide datasets therefore run it. Within a dataset it sweeps every condition in DETECTION_IS_DEFINED (n21_neighbour_distance.py:771-775, 794-800; noise_helpers.py:598-603, 1602). The grouped conditions are dropped on a dataset with no scaffold groups (noise_helpers.py:1148-1160).

### R1 models: NO

Code: It fits config['models'], or DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE when none is given. Both are rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm, on every dataset. It never fits gp, knn or ridge. The first model in that list, rf, also ranks the two single representations that every model is fitted on. rf also chooses the recipes for the shared similarity sweep.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two approved models (Step 1). knn is never one of the two. ridge is excluded.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe comes from get_rule_hybrids called with no fold index. It ranks configurations by their mean over all folds of the whole-dataset search. The two single representations come from top_base_reps with rule='whole_dataset' on that same search. Each recipe is then rebuilt per fold on the training rows under the corrupted labels. That rebuild fits feature weights only. When the recipe uses fewer representations than the pool, build_fold_hybrid picks which ones from blueprint.rep_scores, which the whole-dataset search measured. The file records this itself as 'not a leak-free comparison'.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: It reads stored searches and ranks every stored configuration. The only filters are the downstream model, and the budget when one is named. n21 names no budget (budget=None), so every stored budget is eligible. A missing search is built with FULL_BUDGETS (8 budgets) or DISTANCE_BUDGETS (6 budgets). Allocation, importance, evaluator and representation-count lists are the engine defaults, or the fast lists on 14 datasets. Distance reads use evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm on every dataset. Augmentation conditions come from _pool_conditions. That adds uncapped and capped to the general search whenever augmentation representations are passed. It adds uncapped, and capped under 10,000 rows, to the distance search. The per-fold rebuilds also pass the augmentation representations. The shared similarity sweep builds an uncapped augmented space for each single representation.

Decisions: Steps 2-7 set budgets, importance methods, allocation methods, evaluators and representation counts per dataset. Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 of 41 datasets. It keeps uncapped only on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, on the distance search.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Single representations: rf's top 2 are used for every model. Each model's own ranking is recorded but not used. Hybrids are per model. For each of the two search families (prediction and similarity), it takes the top 2 general hybrids and the top 1 distance hybrid. That is up to 6 hybrids per model. By design the hybrids are never model inputs. Each one is a feature space where neighbours are found. Every fit (clean, corrupted, repaired) is on one of the two single representations. A record-only block at the end also lists 2 base representations and 2 hybrids per model from the whole-dataset searches, with no fits.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: n21 runs no per-fold search at all. A missing stored search is built over all rows by get_precomputed_search. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH set, a search with more than 500 configurations left is refused with RuntimeError. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that pool member. The missing hybrid slot is listed in hybrid.unavailable and the run goes on without it. If rf gets no single representation, the whole condition returns 'skipped': 'no_single_representation'.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

- tests/experiments/_shared.py:5845-5896 (cold build over the rows passed, which are all rows)

- tests/experiments/noise/n21_neighbour_distance.py:900-907, 935 (missing slots recorded)
- tests/experiments/noise/n21_neighbour_distance.py:984-995 (condition skipped without single representations)

Second agent (partly right): The refusal condition is stated incompletely. KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH refuses only when two things are both true. Fewer than half of the configurations this call would score are stored (threshold 0.5). And more than 500 configurations are left (KIRBY_COLD_SEARCH_MAX_CONFIGS). Below 500 left, the search runs inside the job, but over all rows, not per fold. The rest holds: _iter_pool_searches prints and skips a failed member, missing slots go to hybrid.unavailable, and no single representation for rf returns 'skipped'. COLD_REFUSAL=1 is the default in submit_everything.sh.

### Other problems

- The model fitted inside each per-fold hybrid rebuild is the downstream model that owns the recipe. On 33 of 41 datasets rf is not approved, yet rf chooses the single representations and the shared sweep's recipes (n21:969, 1165-1168; DECISIONS.md:11-51).
- The docstring says n21 runs under five conditions (n21:34-41), and so does the --noise-condition help (n21:2001-2002). The default sweep is all of DETECTION_IS_DEFINED (n21:774). That tuple also holds outlier_only_*, shift_only_* and the sparse_dprime conditions (noise_helpers.py:598-603).
- The --levels help says the default grid excludes 0.0 (n21:2004-2005). The code includes 0.0 by the owner's decision (n21:817-829).
- The distance reads name DISTANCE_MODELS, which includes knn (_shared.py:6777). n21 runs on the six nucleotide datasets. Step 9 says the knn distance precompute is not run there (DECISIONS.md:726, 738-742). Whether that read then refuses or builds there: could not determine.
- noise run_all builds no distance search at start-up (noise_helpers.py:1817-1884). get_rule_hybrids still asks for one distance hybrid per family (_shared.py:7130-7137). So the distance slots come from disk, a whole-dataset cold build inside the job, or a refusal.
- n21's own importance-weighted distances use lightgbm_gain and treeshap on every dataset (n21:169). The shared sweep's weightings add deeplift (similarity_space.py:133). Step 3 cuts these per dataset for the search. Whether it also governs these distance weightings is not stated in the record.
- Step 8's open check names the noise base_k_aug_uncapped spaces (DECISIONS.md:654). n21 builds exactly those through the shared sweep on every dataset with augmentation donors (_sim_axis_n15_n22.py:229-253).
- svm is dropped by get_model_factories above its _max_samples (_shared.py:3066-3069). Which approved svm pairs that removes: could not determine without dataset sizes.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The 'other problems' items I checked hold: rf is approved on 8 of 41 datasets, so 33 lack it (DECISIONS.md:11-51). The docstring and the --noise-condition help say five conditions (n21:34-41, n21:1998-2001). DETECTION_IS_DEFINED holds ten conditions plus the sparse_dprime ones (noise_helpers.py:598-603). The --levels help says 0.0 is excluded (n21:2002-2004), but the code includes it (n21:817-829).
- gp is an approved model on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho (DECISIONS.md:11, 13, 30, 32, 33). n21's model list never contains gp (n21:839-843; _shared.py:565, 857). On those five datasets, one approved model is never fitted.
- The noise start-up search ignores config's budget, allocation, importance and evaluator lists. run_all puts them in config (noise_helpers.py:1745-1752). precompute_hybrid_searches uses budgets=None -> FULL_BUDGETS (_shared.py:5513-5514). It never reads the other three lists (_shared.py:5536-5556).
- svm limit: _max_samples is 10,000 rows (find_best_hybrid.py:2812). Eight of the 18 datasets where svm is approved have a row count in dataset_policy.py, and all eight are under 10,000. nt_promoter_tata is the largest at 5,274. The other ten carry no n_samples there, so whether svm is dropped on them: could not determine.
- Whether n21 actually runs on the six nucleotide datasets: could not determine. I found no noise-side nucleotide skip. submit_dataset.sh:38-39 implies noise jobs run on nt_* and gives them 128G. I did not trace the dataset list end to end.


## noise n22 (tests/experiments/noise/n22_curator_flag.py)

What it measures: For each label-noise detector, it scores how well its suspicion ranking finds the hERG IC50 records that ChEMBL curators marked suspect. It reports average precision, plus precision and recall in the top k records.

Datasets: herg_ic50 only. The name is fixed at n22_curator_flag.py:158, and every other dataset returns a skip before any search of its own (n22_curator_flag.py:174-178, 314-319). herg_ic50 has no DATASET_REPS entry; it borrows herg_ki's representations (noise_helpers.py:1640, 1653-1656). Its augmentation list comes back empty, so augmentations is None (noise_helpers.py:1683-1700). submit_everything.sh builds its default dataset list from DATASET_REPS (submit_everything.sh:207-213), so herg_ic50 is not in it. herg_ic50 is reached only when named with --datasets or run by hand. n22 is in the noise run_all list (noise_helpers.py:92), so on the 41 listed datasets it runs and skips. Those jobs still build the whole-dataset start-up searches first (noise_helpers.py:1826-1870). herg_ic50 has no row in any DECISIONS.md step; a grep for herg_ic50 in DECISIONS.md finds nothing.

### R1 models: NO

Code: It reads hybrids and single representations for five downstream models: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm. rf is the main model. Its rule read gives the rf spaces, base_1 and base_2. The other four get spaces named '<space>@<model>'. n22 trains no downstream model to make predictions. Each model decides which feature spaces the detectors run in. The similarity rebuild also uses each of the five models to accept or reject features. svm is dropped from any search over more than 10,000 rows, the n22 docstring says herg_ic50 has 12,008 records, and I did not load the data to check. So svm's slots are probably empty. knn is never asked for. ridge is not used.

Decisions: Two approved models per dataset (Step 1). herg_ic50 has no Step 1 row. It borrows herg_ki's representations, and herg_ki's two approved models are svm and dnn. Under that reading, rf, xgboost and lightgbm are extra. rf is also the model that picks the main spaces.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe and both single-representation rankings come from searches over all rows of herg_ic50. get_best_search_for_downstream says so in its own metadata (selection_scope 'whole_dataset'). get_rule_hybrids is called without fold_i, so it ranks on the mean over every fold of the whole-dataset search. Inside each of n22's 5 folds, only the feature weights are refit on the training rows. When a recipe uses fewer than all representations, which ones it keeps comes from blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores are whole-dataset, because _fold_hybrid_pair passes no precomputed_alloc_scores. So a flagged record's own label helped choose the recipe, the budget and the representations of the space it is scored in.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

The distance search should use budgets 100 to 500, with the same three cuts. Augmentation is cut. Taking herg_ki's rows, the general search differs in four ways at once: budgets, importance, allocation and representation count. The distance search differs in the same four. Evaluators and augmentation match only because herg_ki keeps all four evaluators and herg_ic50 loads no augmentation representations.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, not refused or skipped.

### Other problems

- The docstring and the result file both say features are chosen inside each fold, on the other folds' rows (n22_curator_flag.py:62-63, 1136-1139). That holds for the feature weights only. The recipe, the budget, the representations kept, and base_1 and base_2 were all chosen by searches that saw every record's label, the flagged records included. The file does not say this.
- _fold_hybrid_pair passes no precomputed_alloc_scores to build_fold_hybrid (n06_bindingdb_ground_truth.py:529-532). So a recipe with fewer representations than the pool keeps whichever representations score best in whole-dataset scores (_shared.py:5256-5286).
- run_all passes only noise_condition and force_rerun to an experiment (noise_helpers.py:2031-2046). So n22 always gets budget=None, and every recipe is picked across all budgets.
- svm is skipped by any search over more than 10,000 rows (find_best_hybrid.py:2812, 3229-3232). The n22 docstring says herg_ic50 has 12,008 records (n22_curator_flag.py:12-13); I did not load it. svm is one of herg_ki's two approved models, so it would get no spaces here.
- The noise start-up builds no distance search (noise_helpers.py:1826-1870). The distance hybrids for herg_ic50 are therefore built over all rows inside an experiment's pool read, or refused and skipped under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH.
- herg_ic50 is not in the submit_everything.sh default list (submit_everything.sh:207-213), and no precompute covers it. In the default submission, n22 writes a skip on all 41 datasets and is never run on herg_ic50.
- The similarity rebuild builds each model's hybrids with that model in the accept-or-reject step (n22_curator_flag.py:875-877, _sim_axis_n15_n22.py:270-273). Each detector space's similarity version is therefore built with all five models, not two.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The 'other problems' item says each similarity rebuild is built with all five models. It is partly right. _sim_axis_n15_n22.py:270-273 passes the model only for a recipe that is not a similarity-objective recipe. A similarity-objective recipe is rebuilt with no model at all.
- The similarity rebuild also puts each fold's neighbour spaces through whole-dataset recipes. It rebuilds rf's and each model's hybrids per fold through cached_hybrid_for_fold (_sim_axis_n15_n22.py:262-279), using the blueprints read with fold_i=None (n22_curator_flag.py:881-893). That is a second place R2 fails, beside the main detector loop.
- The 'other problems' item says n22 writes a skip on all 41 datasets in the default submission. The count is confirmed: DATASET_REPS minus chembl_qsar and davis is 41 (submit_everything.sh:207-211; counted by import). n22 is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (noise_helpers.py:92), and _flag_for_rows skips any dataset that is not herg_ic50 (n22_curator_flag.py:174-178). But run_all's two whole-dataset start-up searches run before that skip (noise_helpers.py:1826-1870, 1926-2047).
- The R1 evidence implies a downstream model decides each detector space. That holds for the hybrid spaces. But no downstream model is trained, and each detector is fitted on the space itself (n22_curator_flag.py:1052-1087). So the R4/R5 'configurations' are detector feature spaces, as the report says. That is a design difference, not a defect.


## noise n23 (tests/experiments/noise/n23_uncertainty_cleaning.py)

What it measures: Whether dropping or moving the training labels a model's own per-molecule uncertainty marks as noisy improves the held-out score, scored against untouched held-out labels.

Datasets: All 41 datasets that submit_everything.sh queues for the noise category: every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213, categories at :95). n23 is in the noise SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS list (tests/experiments/noise/noise_helpers.py:99). It is in neither skip list, so it also runs on the nucleotide datasets and on kiba and bindingdb_kd (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675, 3684-3685). Inside each dataset it sweeps the conditions in DETECTION_IS_DEFINED (n23:934, run at n23:1196-1200). The grouped conditions are skipped on datasets that load no SMILES (noise_helpers.py:1148-1160).

### Other problems

- Under injection, the recipes and the two base representations were chosen on the clean labels of every molecule, held-out ones included. n23 passes no label_noise, though get_best_search_for_downstream's docstring says noise experiments should (_shared.py:6155-6159; n23:1389-1395).
- The per-fold hybrid rebuild passes no augmentation arrays (n23:1776-1782). A recipe the search picked under 'uncapped' or 'capped' carries that condition (_shared.py:6992-6996). hybrid_for_fold's docstring says such a recipe then rebuilds a narrower feature space (noise_helpers.py:982-985). I did not trace create_hybrid to confirm.
- Two things disagree about how many hybrids n23 uses. The docstring says one hybrid per search objective (n23:168-170). The rule read gives up to three per objective, six in all (_shared.py:7064-7066, 6508-6535).
- The similarity sweep offers three hybrid spaces as neighbour spaces: hybrid, hybrid__general2 and hybrid_similarity (similarity_space.py:126). Three more are fitted as model inputs but never offered: hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1.
- ensure_dprime_models adds rf and svm to any model list a caller passes (n23:298-308). So even a run narrowed to a dataset's approved pair fits rf and svm where that pair lacks them.
- gp is approved on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho (DECISIONS.md:11,13,30,32,33). n23 never fits gp, so on those five one approved model is missing entirely.
- Step 8 records an open check: noise base_k_aug_uncapped may break if augmentation is cut (DECISIONS.md:654). n23 builds that space on every dataset with augmentation representations (n23:634-663).
- When rep_count is below the pool size, build_fold_hybrid picks which representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5286). A whole-dataset recipe makes that choice from whole-dataset scores. Whether bp.reps already names the subset, which would skip this, could not be determined.
- The distance read happens on the nucleotide datasets too. Its stored search scores knn there, where Step 9 says knn is not needed (DECISIONS.md:726, 738-742; _shared.py:6774-6777). n23 itself fits no knn.
- Could not determine which datasets exceed 10,000 rows. On those, svm is dropped (find_best_hybrid.py:2812). nt_promoter_tata's approved pair is lightgbm+svm, so it would lose an approved model there if it is that large.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The open question about rep_count has an answer. A stored recipe's reps field lists the whole pool: rep_names = list(base_reps.keys()) (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:5388, 5397-5398). So when rep_count is below the pool size, build_fold_hybrid picks which representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5256-5286). Those scores are each representation's best score across all models, measured on every row (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:5563-5593). hybrid_for_fold passes no fold allocation scores (tests/experiments/noise/noise_helpers.py:1013-1020). So which representations enter each fold's hybrid is chosen with the held-out molecules in view.
- The augmentation question has an answer too. n23 rebuilds each hybrid with no augmentation arrays (n23_uncertainty_cleaning.py:1776-1782, defaults None at 828-830). create_hybrid runs its augmentation step only when augmentations is not None (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5984). So a recipe the search picked under 'uncapped' or 'capped' is rebuilt per fold without any augmentation features, and nothing raises. The fold's features then differ from the configuration that won the search.
- The report's worry about nt_promoter_tata losing svm is wrong. It has 5,274 rows (tests/experiments/dataset_policy.py:321). The svm drop applies above 10,000 rows. The datasets above 10,000 rows in Step 1 are nucleotide sets and gb_human_enhancers_cohn, whose approved pairs are dnn+lightgbm (DECISIONS.md:19, 31-34).
- n23 passes no label_noise anywhere in the file (grep for label_noise in n23_uncertainty_cleaning.py returns nothing). get_fold_pool_recipes reads data['precomputed_searches_noisy'] only when label_noise is given (tests/experiments/_shared.py:6784-6786). So under injection both the hybrids and the two base representations come from the search on clean labels.


## noise n24 (tests/experiments/noise/n24_delete_or_keep.py)

What it measures: After injecting label noise into each fold's training rows, it compares deleting the molecules a detector flags against rewriting or down-weighting them. Each arm is scored against no cleaning and against deleting the same number of molecules at random.

Datasets: All 41 datasets in the noise job roster. n24 is in the default noise list (noise/noise_helpers.py:105). It is not in either skip set (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3675 for nucleotide, 3684-3685 for over 15,000 rows), so it runs on the nucleotide datasets and on kiba and bindingdb_kd too. submit_everything.sh:211-213 builds the roster: every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis. It queues noise on all of them (submit_everything.sh:95). With no NOISE_CONDITION, n24 runs outlier_p10 (n24:250, 706). Under a condition outside DETECTION_IS_DEFINED, run_all writes a skip instead (noise_helpers.py:1602-1604, 2012-2025). A grouped condition on a dataset with no scaffold groups raises (n24:739-746).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: n24 fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. The list comes from config['models'], which noise run_all sets to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. ensure_dprime_models then adds rf and svm, which are already there. gp is never fitted, because nothing in n24 adds it. svm is dropped on any dataset over 10,000 molecules. ridge and knn are never fitted as downstream models.

Decisions: Step 1 allows two models per dataset. On every dataset n24 fits three models that are not in the approved pair. Five datasets are approved with gp: abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn) and ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn). On those five, n24 fits three unapproved models and lacks one approved model. Some datasets are approved with svm and may be over 10,000 molecules, such as nt_promoter_tata (lightgbm+svm). On those, svm would be missing. I could not determine their molecule counts. ridge and knn: complies.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: n24 runs no per-fold search. For each model it calls get_best_search_for_downstream and get_rule_hybrids with the full reps and labels. Those read the whole-dataset searches. get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index, so each recipe is ranked by its mean over all folds of that search. The same hybrid recipes and the same two base representations serve every fold. Each fold rebuilds the features on its own training rows, using the noisy training labels. A recipe searched over fewer representations than the pool picks which ones to keep from blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores are each representation's best score over every row of the dataset. The recipes were also chosen on the clean labels of every row, because label_noise is not passed.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only. Here both the choice of recipe and the choice of the two base representations saw the held-out molecules. The engine's own metadata says so: selection_scope 'whole_dataset'. get_fold_pool_recipes says it 'holds out the fold's SCORES, not its rows', and n24 does not even hold out the scores.
