### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: The general reads and the distance reads rank every stored configuration for the model. Neither filters on any Step 2-7 axis. budget=None ranks over every budget. The distance read also adds the global DISTANCE_EVALUATORS, DISTANCE_BUDGETS (10-500) and DISTANCE_MODELS. Augmentation conditions come from _pool_conditions. On the general search those are none, uncapped and capped. On the distance search they are none, uncapped, and capped under 10,000 molecules. kiba and bindingdb_kd get no uncapped. Separately, the similarity sweep builds an uncapped augmented copy of each base representation (base_k_aug_uncapped) on every dataset that loads augmentation representations. The sweep is on by default.

Decisions: Steps 2-7 decide budgets, importance methods, allocation methods, internal evaluators and representation counts per dataset. Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 of 41 datasets. It keeps only uncapped, on the distance search, for ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic. n24 can pick a recipe at a cut budget on any dataset whose Step 2 range excludes stored budgets. Example: herg_ki is decided 250-2000 features, and nothing stops a 10-feature recipe. It can also pick a cut importance method, allocation method, evaluator or representation count (Steps 3-7). It reads capped and uncapped searches that Step 8 cut. The only dataset with no cut on any of Steps 2-7 is humanness_therapeutic. According to the helper map, which I did not re-check, it also loads no augmentation representations. Every other dataset can break the rule. DECISIONS.md:654 names base_k_aug_uncapped as an open check under Step 8.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each of the five models it uses two base representations, base_1 and base_2. It also uses up to six hybrids, from the owner's rule of 2 general plus 1 distance per search family. There are two families here, predictive and similarity: hybrid, hybrid__general2, hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1. One set is chosen for the whole dataset and reused on every fold.

Decisions: R4 wants, per approved model and per fold, the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n24 differs in three ways at once. It covers five models, not two. It uses up to six hybrids per model, not two. It picks one set for all folds, not one per fold. The design reason in the file covers the base side only: 'each model's top 2 base representations' (owner decision 2026-09-25). Nothing in the file explains why it uses more than 2 hybrids, beyond the 2026-10-02 rule written in _shared.py.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n24 never builds a per-fold search. When a whole-dataset search is missing, get_precomputed_search calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH (on by default in submit_everything.sh), the cold-search refusal decides. It builds the search when 500 or fewer configurations are left. Otherwise it raises. _iter_pool_searches catches the error, prints a warning and skips that search. n24 then records that model's hybrid space as unavailable. The run continues on whatever spaces are left, and on the base representations only if no hybrid is left.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n24 has no per-fold path at all. Its only fallback builds a whole-dataset search, or skips with a warning.

### Other problems

- Two different 'top 2 base representations' exist for each model. n24 ranks its base_1 and base_2 from the search get_best_search_for_downstream returned (n24:878-880). That search is the best (tier, augmentation condition) for the model, so it can be an uncapped or capped search. get_rule_hybrids also computes a top-2 base list from the general read (_shared.py:7183-7185, 7190-7194), and n24 ignores it. The two lists can name different representations. I could not determine whether they differ in practice.
- Recipes searched over fewer representations than the pool choose which ones to keep from blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5286). Blueprint.reps is the whole pool (find_best_hybrid.py:5388-5399), so this path runs for every recipe with a representation count below all. rep_scores are filled after the search aggregates (find_best_hybrid.py:9593). If a recipe read back from result_db lacks them, build_fold_hybrid raises (_shared.py:5263-5272). n24 records that as 'the hybrid could not be built on this pass' (n24:1105-1109). I could not determine whether stored recipes carry rep_scores.
- The similarity sweep hands model_similarity_spaces the hybrid matrices of every hybrid space n24 built. But similarity_space.HYBRID_SPACES lists only hybrid, hybrid__general2 and hybrid_similarity (similarity_space.py:126). So hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1 are never used as neighbour spaces.
- get_best_search_for_downstream's docstring says an experiment that injects label noise should pass label_noise. Otherwise the hybrid enters the comparison already built from the very labels the experiment then corrupts (_shared.py:6155-6159). n24 injects noise and does not pass it (n24:844-850). Each fold rebuilds the features on the noisy training labels, but the recipe was chosen on the clean labels of every row.
- Because the recipe set is chosen once over all folds, n24's own folds (cv_split, n24:840-841) need not be the same partition as the stored search's folds. n24 never checks this. The mismatch matters only once per-fold selection is added.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Augmented recipes are rebuilt without their augmentation features. n24 passes no augmentations_train or augmentations_val to cached_hybrid_cell (n24_delete_or_keep.py:1099-1104), so both default to None (n23_uncertainty_cleaning.py:828-830). create_hybrid adds augmentation features only when augmentations is not None (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5984, 6403). Nothing in build_fold_hybrid raises on this (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5190-5230). So a recipe picked from an uncapped or capped search is scored as a narrower, unaugmented hybrid under that recipe's name. The recipe choice saw augmented scores, and the fold build uses none. Two things differ at once, not one.
- Noise run_all start-up builds the uncapped and capped general searches on every dataset that loads augmentation representations, kiba and bindingdb_kd included (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5543-5548). The pool read skips uncapped on those two (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5989, 6041-6043), so the start-up builds a search nothing reads. Step 8 cuts augmentation on both (DECISIONS.md:663, 681).
- The start-up searches use pruning from run_all's pruning_mode (noise_helpers.py:1808-1810, 1840-1841). get_precomputed_search asks for adaptive_pruning=False (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5888). I could not determine whether the two hit the same stored search or the reader rebuilds on a miss.
- The distance read asks for a search whose models include knn (tests/experiments/_shared.py:6777, 568). n24 reads only its own model's rows from it, so this is not a knn downstream fit. It does tie n24 to the knn distance precompute that Step 9 marks 'not needed' on the six nucleotide datasets (DECISIONS.md:726, 739-743). On those, a missing knn distance search would go through the refusal path in R6.


## noise n25 (tests/experiments/noise/n25_cliff_exemption.py)

What it measures: On each fold it injects label noise and runs each cleanup once. It then fits the cleaned training set three ways: as cleaned, with the activity-cliff molecules put back, and with as many random non-cliff molecules put back. It counts how many folds the cliff version beats the plain cleanup.

Datasets: n25 is one of the noise experiments (noise_helpers.py:106). The noise jobs are queued on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213), which is the 41 datasets of DECISIONS Step 1. n25 is not skipped on the nucleotide datasets: it is absent from NUCLEOTIDE_SKIP_EXPERIMENTS (_shared.py:3672). It is skipped on any dataset over 15,000 molecules (_shared.py:3665, 3684, 3713). The record says kiba and bindingdb_kd are over 15,000 (DECISIONS.md:716, 735); I did not load the datasets to count, so other skips are unverified. It runs only under the five noise conditions in DETECTION_IS_DEFINED (noise_helpers.py:1604; n25:955-962). Its default is outlier_only_p05 (n25:399).

### R1 models: NO

Code: The downstream models are config['models'], or DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, plus rf and svm if missing. Under run_all that is rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. get_model_factories only drops a model above its size limit. gp is never added, because n25 does not call _apply_small_dataset_models. knn and ridge are never fitted downstream.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two Step 1 models. For example herg_ki is svm+dnn, ginkgo_hic is gp+dnn, and abagym_Ang2 is gp+svm.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: It never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search goes through get_precomputed_search to find_best_hybrid on all rows. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH unset, it builds that whole-dataset search inside the job. With it set, which is submit_everything.sh's default, the search is refused when over 500 configurations are missing. _iter_pool_searches catches the refusal, prints a warning and skips it. The rule records the slot as missing. If no model gets a recipe, n25 runs the base representations only. A failed per-fold hybrid build is logged and that space is skipped for that fold. noise run_all never builds the distance search, so the distance hybrid relies on what is stored on disk.

Decisions: If the per-fold search a fold needs does not exist, the experiment builds it itself.

### Other problems

- The recipes were picked on the clean labels of every row. n25 then corrupts the training labels and rebuilds the features on the noisy ones. get_best_search_for_downstream's docstring says a noise-injecting experiment should pass label_noise to read the noisy search (_shared.py:6155-6159). n25 passes none (n25:1117-1121). Its own note says no cleanup reaches the feature choice (n25:1087-1093). Only the feature rebuild is noisy; the recipe was chosen on clean labels.
- gp is approved on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho (DECISIONS.md:11,13,30,32,33). n25 never fits gp on any of them. So on those five datasets one of the two approved models is missing, and four unapproved ones run.
- On each dataset the general and distance searches differ in two ways. The distance search adds knn as a scored model and uses its own evaluator list (_shared.py:6774-6777). The general search has neither.
- The similarity sweep builds uncapped augmented feature matrices on every dataset with augmentation representations (n23:634-663). Step 8 keeps augmentation on two datasets only. Step 8 itself names noise base_k_aug_uncapped as an open check (DECISIONS.md:654).
- noise run_all never builds the distance search, but n25's rule asks for one distance hybrid per family (noise_helpers.py:1820-1870; _shared.py:7130-7137). Under the default cold refusal, that slot is missing wherever the distance search is not already stored with over half its configurations. The record says the distance search is not stored for bindingdb_kd, kiba and lhasa_herg (DECISIONS.md:750).
- The cleanups and detectors fit models of their own: cross_val, activity_cliff_aware and the oof_smooth and gp_smooth targets. Those come from n07 and are not downstream models. I did not open n07 to list them.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The code and the record disagree on which datasets use the fast grid. The code puts 14 datasets on it (dataset_policy.FAST_SPEED_DATASETS, printed this session; applied at _shared.py:1014-1081). The record's fast-tier table lists 10 (DECISIONS.md:350-363). The four extra are bindingdb_kd, flab_expression_koenig, kiba and logd. On those four the code reads the fast allocation, importance and representation-count lists. The record expects the Step 3-6 decisions instead.
- noise run_all's start-up searches ignore everything in config except where it is passed explicitly. precompute_hybrid_searches never reads config's models, allocations, importance_methods or internal_evaluators (_shared.py:5452-5599). It also takes FULL_BUDGETS whatever config holds (_shared.py:5515-5516). So no setting in run_all's config (noise_helpers.py:1745-1752) can carry a Step 2-7 cut into these searches.
- The general search's evaluators are never set for n25. get_precomputed_search passes no internal_evaluators for the general tier (_shared.py:5863-5896). The engine default list is used, not the Step 5 v3 decision for each dataset.


## noise n26 (tests/experiments/noise/n26_noise_variance_from_repeats.py)

What it measures: It measures how large the label noise is from repeat measurements of the same molecule, and puts each model's out-of-fold error beside it.

Datasets: n26 does real work only where build_replicate_groups returns molecule ids. That happens when the loader gives replicate_groups, or drug_ids and protein_ids (_ground_truth_providers.py:178-198). Every other dataset writes {'skipped': 'no_replicate_structure'} (n26:394-398). Classification datasets are skipped earlier (n26:389-392). Three datasets get through. herg_ic50 does, through its molecule grouping (_shared.py:4611-4616). bindingdb_kd and kiba do, because every DTA dataset carries drug_ids and protein_ids in metadata (_shared.py:3559, 4430-4525). The docstring names herg_ic50 and bindingdb_kd only (n26:20-23); kiba is missing from it. herg_ic50 has no DATASET_REPS entry (noise_helpers.py:1640, 1653-1656). The cluster roster is the DATASET_REPS keys minus chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:207-213). So herg_ic50 runs only by hand. On the cluster, n26 measures something on bindingdb_kd and kiba only. should_skip_experiment does not skip n26 on either (_shared.py:3672-3686). herg_ic50 has no row in DECISIONS.md, so R1 and R3 are judged on bindingdb_kd and kiba.

### R1 models: NO

Code: The model list is kwargs models, else config models, else DOWNSTREAM_MODELS (n26:439-440). Under noise run_all, config models is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. get_model_factories drops any model above its sample cap (n26:441-443). svm's cap is 10,000. On bindingdb_kd, the loader comment's counts give about 26,500 molecules after the 30,000-row draw. That figure is derived, not measured. So svm is dropped there. kiba's molecule count could not be determined without loading it. So n26 fits rf, xgboost, dnn and lightgbm on bindingdb_kd. On kiba it fits the same four, plus svm if kiba has 10,000 molecules or fewer. The estimator check refits downstream_models[0] only, which is rf (n26:716-734). knn and ridge are never fitted downstream.

Decisions: Step 1 approves rf+dnn for bindingdb_kd and dnn+rf for kiba. herg_ic50 has no Step 1 row. ridge is excluded everywhere. Step 9 allows knn in the distance search on both datasets, but n26 fits no knn.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Each hybrid recipe comes from whole-dataset searches. The search inputs are bound to every measurement row (n26:498-504). pool_recipe_per_downstream_model then calls get_rule_hybrids with no fold index (noise_helpers.py:1414-1422). With fold_i=None, the ranking is the mean over every fold of the stored search (_shared.py:7082-7084, 6746-6748). That search ran over every row (_shared.py:7038-7042). The fallback single recipe also comes from get_best_search_for_downstream, which records selection_scope 'whole_dataset' (_shared.py:6422-6432). The two base representations per model come from noise_base_reps_by_model. It ranks by the whole-dataset search's own mean (_shared.py:4876-4880, 4917-4921). Each hybrid is refitted per fold on that fold's training molecules (n26:623-631). That refits the feature weights only. The choice of recipe and of base representations saw every row.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. Reading the whole-dataset search and picking from it does not comply.

### R3 same cuts: NO (partly)

Code: n26 reads general searches built at noise start-up with FULL_BUDGETS, 10 to 2000 features (_shared.py:5518-5519). get_rule_hybrids passes budget=None, so it ranks over all eight budgets (n26:501, _shared.py:6855). bindingdb_kd and kiba are in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS (dataset_policy.py:688-711). So their searches use the fast lists (find_best_hybrid.py:8651-8669). Those are lightgbm_gain only; performance_weighted, power_2 and rank_exp_d0.3; evaluators rf, match, dnn, lightgbm; representation counts 3 and all (find_best_hybrid.py:3063-3072, 3674). The distance read uses DISTANCE_BUDGETS 10-500 and DISTANCE_EVALUATORS knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm (_shared.py:6774-6777). It also uses the same fast lists. Augmentation: load_noise_data sets three protein augmentation representations on both datasets (noise_helpers.py:1680-1695). So the general pool reads 'none' and 'capped' (_shared.py:6040-6046). The start-up search builds 'none', 'uncapped' and 'capped' (_shared.py:5543-5548).

Decisions: bindingdb_kd: budgets 250-2000; all three importance methods; all five allocation methods; all four evaluators; representation counts 2 and all (3 and 5 cut); augmentation cut. kiba: budgets 250-2000; all three importance methods; the four stored allocation methods (no wglobal_power2 stored); all four evaluators; representation count all only (2, 3 and 5 cut); augmentation cut. Step 7 has no rows for either dataset, so there is no distance decision to compare against. On bindingdb_kd the general search differs from the record in five ways at once. It has budgets 10-100, which are cut. It lacks deeplift and treeshap. It lacks softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2. It has count 3, which is cut, and lacks 2. It reads the 'capped' search, which is cut. On kiba it differs in the same five ways, except the allocation gap is softmax_T1 alone and the count gap is 3 present where only all is kept. Evaluators match on both.

Which of the two happens depends on the environment variable.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment must build it itself. It must not refuse or skip with a warning.

### Other problems

- The hybrid rebuild passes no augmentation features (n26:627-631 calls cached_hybrid_cell without augmentations_train or augmentations_val). On bindingdb_kd and kiba the pool includes the 'capped' search, so a winning recipe can name capped augmentation (_shared.py:6040-6046, 6996). hybrid_for_fold's docstring says such a recipe then rebuilds a narrower feature space than the one the search chose (noise_helpers.py:982-985). Not run, so whether it raises or builds narrower was not checked.
- The docstring lists two datasets, herg_ic50 and bindingdb_kd (n26:20-23). The code also runs on kiba, because every DTA loader returns drug_ids and protein_ids (_shared.py:3559, 4525; _ground_truth_providers.py:182-198). Whether kiba has any pair measured twice could not be determined. If it has none, every 1/count fit records 'every molecule has the same measurement count', but all models are still fitted.
- The docstring says one hybrid per search family (n26:85-93). The code builds up to three per family: general1, general2 and distance1 (_shared.py:6508-6547).
- The search ran on measurement rows with its own 5 folds. n26 splits molecules into its own folds (n26:566-567). The two fold sets are different rows. This does not change R2, because the ranking uses every fold anyway.
- build_fold_hybrid picks which representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores when the recipe's rep_count is below the number of representations passed (_shared.py:5256-5286). Those scores come from the whole-dataset search. hybrid_for_fold first cuts the representations to bp.reps (noise_helpers.py:1005-1012). Whether bp.reps already holds only rep_count representations could not be determined, so whether this second leak applies is open.
- The code makes bindingdb_kd and kiba fast datasets, citing an owner's decision of 2026-10-02 (dataset_policy.py:702-709). DECISIONS.md, dated 2026-10-03, keeps all three importance methods and more allocation methods on both. The two records disagree, and n26 follows the code.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- herg_ic50 is not in any dataset list in tests/slurm_scripts/submit_all_datasets.sh:34-55. Its only DTA list is kiba and bindingdb_kd (line 38). So the submitted noise sweep runs n26 only on kiba and bindingdb_kd. herg_ic50 runs only when someone starts it by hand. n26's docstring (n26:20-23, 104-105) names herg_ic50 and bindingdb_kd, and leaves out kiba.
- kiba does reach n26's measurement and is not skipped. The 30,000-row draw reads metadata['drug_ids'] and metadata['protein_ids'] for every DTA dataset (_shared.py:4462-4467), so kiba carries both. build_replicate_groups then returns a grouping (_ground_truth_providers.py:182-198). Whether any kiba pair is measured twice could not be determined without loading the data.
- On bindingdb_kd and kiba, n26's molecule is a (drug, protein) pair, not a molecule. build_replicate_groups keys on drug|protein (_ground_truth_providers.py:194). The output still labels these 'molecules' (n26:457-462, 475-477).
- The estimator check refits rf, which is downstream_models[0] (n26:716). rf is approved on both datasets, but dnn, the other approved model, never gets the check.
- The hybrid rebuild passes no augmentation features, confirmed. cached_hybrid_cell takes augmentations_train and augmentations_val as optional (n23_uncertainty_cleaning.py:828-830). n26 calls it with ten positional arguments and neither of those two (n26:627-631).


## noise n27 (tests/experiments/noise/n27_removal_cost_and_propagation.py)

What it measures: On each outer fold, it measures how much the held-out score drops when the downstream model trains on a random share of the training molecules, and how much injected or prediction-moved training-label error reaches the held-out mean squared error.

Datasets: n27 runs on every dataset the noise job is given, and skips classification datasets itself (n27:326-329). submit_everything.sh queues the noise category on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis, which is 41 datasets (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213, 350-374). n27 runs only in the noise job with no noise condition (noise_helpers.py:1572-1574, submit_dataset.sh resolve_experiments loop). should_skip_experiment never skips it: n27 is in neither skip list (_shared.py:3672-3675, 3684-3685). By the task type in DATASET_REGISTRY_DATA (dataset_policy.py:230 onward), 26 of the 41 are regression and run: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. The other 15 write a skip. The registry's task type was printed this session; the task type load_data returns, which n27 actually checks, was not checked. The docstring says it was written for herg_ki, caco2, logd and flab_thermo_tresanco (n27:75-78), but nothing in the code limits it to those four.

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: n27 fits the models in config['models'], with rf and svm added if missing. In a noise job config['models'] is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. That is five models on every regression dataset. gp is never fitted, because get_model_factories builds only the names it is given. svm is dropped on kiba and bindingdb_kd, which are over its 10,000-row limit. The relabelled part also fits a LightGBM on every dataset to make the out-of-fold prediction the labels are moved toward; that is not a downstream model.

Decisions: Step 1 gives each dataset two approved models, and ridge and knn are excluded. All 26 regression datasets break the rule. On 21 of them n27 fits both approved models plus three others. On kiba and bindingdb_kd (approved dnn+rf) it fits both plus xgboost and lightgbm. On the five datasets whose approved pair includes gp (abagym_Ang2 gp+svm, abagym_VEGF gp+svm, ginkgo_acsins lightgbm+gp, ginkgo_hic gp+dnn, ginkgo_pr_cho gp+dnn), gp is never fitted. So those five have one approved model and four unapproved ones. ensure_dprime_models forces rf and svm in by an owner decision of 2026-09-25. That disagrees with Step 1 wherever rf or svm is not approved, which is most datasets. ridge and knn are never fitted, which agrees with R1.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe and every base representation is chosen once, before the fold loop, from whole-dataset searches. The hybrid recipes come from get_rule_hybrids with no fold index, which ranks on the mean over all folds of a search run on every row. The two base representations per model come from noise_base_reps_by_model, which ranks on the same whole-dataset search. Inside each fold the chosen recipe is rebuilt on that fold's training rows. When a recipe uses fewer representations than the pool, the rebuild picks which ones from blueprint.rep_scores, which are whole-dataset scores.

Decisions: Every hybrid used on a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. n27 runs no per-fold search. The held-out rows of every fold were among the rows that chose the recipe, the two base representations, and, for reduced representation counts, which representations the rebuild keeps. Rebuilding on the training rows refits the feature selection only. Its own pool reader says so: selection_scope 'whole_dataset' and the note that only the features are refit.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: n27 reads hybrids at budget=None, so it ranks over every budget the stored search holds. The general searches it reads use all 8 budgets, 10 to 2000 features. The distance searches use 6 budgets, 10 to 500 features, evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm, and models rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm, knn. Importance, allocation, evaluator and representation-count lists are the engine defaults. On 14 fast datasets they are the fast lists instead. Nothing filters the stored configurations by any Step 2-7 cut. Augmentation: whenever the dataset carries augmentation representations, the general read includes uncapped and capped searches. The distance read includes uncapped, and capped under 10,000 rows. kiba and bindingdb_kd get no uncapped. Nothing reads DECISIONS.md.

Decisions: Each search must use the dataset's decided budgets, importance methods, allocation methods, evaluators and representation counts from Steps 2-7, and augmentation per Step 8. All 26 regression datasets break this. Budgets: every one except humanness_therapeutic and tcga_luad_vs_lusc has a decided general range narrower than 10-2000, and neither of those two runs here. The fast lists are applied to four regression datasets the fast-tier table does not name: flab_expression_koenig, logd, kiba and bindingdb_kd. On flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd that drops deeplift and treeshap, which Step 3 keeps. Augmentation: 22 of the 26 carry augmentation representations, so n27 reads augmented hybrids on them. Step 8 cuts augmentation on all 22 except ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, where only uncapped on the distance search is kept. The four with none are abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF and abcov_kd.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each downstream model n27 builds up to 8 feature spaces. Two are base representations: base_1 and base_2, the model's top 2 by the whole-dataset search. Up to six are hybrids: for each of the two search families, the top 2 general hybrids and the top 1 distance hybrid. The families are features chosen for prediction and features chosen under objective='similarity'. The space names are hybrid, hybrid__general2, hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1. The same set is used on every fold.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold, the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n27 matches on the base representations: two per model. It differs on the hybrids in two ways at once: up to six per model instead of two, and one set for the whole dataset instead of one set per fold. It also applies this to five models, not two. Nothing in the file says the six-hybrid shape is by design for this experiment; the result file calls it the owner's set of 2026-10-02.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n27 never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search is handled by get_precomputed_search, which calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. Without KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH it builds the whole-dataset search inside the job. With it set, which submit_everything.sh does by default, the search is refused when more than 500 configurations are missing. _iter_pool_searches then prints a warning and skips that pool member. A model left with no recipe gets no hybrid space; it is never handed another model's. If no model gets a recipe, every part runs on the base representations only. The reason is written to the result file. The noise runner's start-up searches catch the same refusal and store None.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment must build it itself. n27 does not ask for a per-fold search at all. The search it does ask for is the whole-dataset one, and under the default submit setting that one is refused and skipped with a warning when over 500 configurations are missing. Neither is the per-fold build R6 requires.

### Other problems

- The injected part rebuilds each hybrid on the noisy training labels (n27:712-724). The recipe it rebuilds was still chosen by a search on every row's correct labels. So which budget, allocation, importance and evaluator are used was decided with the correct labels of the held-out molecules and the noisy training molecules in view.
- n27 passes no per-fold allocation scores to the rebuild (n27:295-306 -> noise_helpers.py:1017-1024). For a recipe with fewer representations than the pool, build_fold_hybrid keeps the top ones by blueprint.rep_scores, which are whole-dataset scores (_shared.py:5256-5286).
- The base representations and the hybrids are ranked by two different readers. The base pair comes from the one SearchResult get_best_search_for_downstream returned for the model (n27:447-450). The rule reader also ranks base representations across every pool member (_shared.py:7183-7185), and n27 does not use that ranking. The two can name different representations; not checked on any dataset.
- On kiba and bindingdb_kd the general searches are run on the fast lists, because both are in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS (dataset_policy.py:688-711). The fast-tier table in DECISIONS.md does not list them, and Step 3 keeps deeplift and treeshap on both. logd and flab_expression_koenig are in the same position.
- The docstring names four target datasets (n27:75-78), but the job runs n27 on all 26 regression datasets in the submit roster. That includes kiba and bindingdb_kd at about 100,000 rows each, with 20 random draws at 5 shares per fold, per space and per model (n27:137-140, 582-602).
- The out-of-fold prediction the relabelled part moves labels toward is a fixed LightGBM on every dataset (noise_cache.py:403-423). It is fitted in each space's feature matrix, so each space gets its own target.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3: the general read also uses evaluators that Step 5 (v3) cut. abagym_EGFR cuts rf, abagym_VEGF cuts rf/lightgbm/dnn, buchwald_hartwig cuts dnn, ginkgo_colloidal cuts dnn, ginkgo_titer cuts lightgbm (DECISIONS.md:517-539). n27 reads with the engine default of match, rf, lightgbm, dnn (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:3700), and nothing filters the stored configurations by evaluator.
- R3: on kiba the fast representation-count list is [3, whole pool] (find_best_hybrid.py:3071). Step 6 cuts 2/3/5 on kiba (DECISIONS.md:592), so n27 reads a count Step 6 cut. On flab_expression_koenig, Step 6 also cuts 3 (DECISIONS.md:581), and the fast list runs it. On kiba, Step 4 keeps softmax_T1 (DECISIONS.md:398), and the fast allocation list drops it (find_best_hybrid.py:3072).
- R6: DECISIONS.md:609 and :750 say no distance search is stored for kiba or bindingdb_kd. That is a dated document, not checked on the server. If it is true, n27's distance read for both builds the whole-dataset distance search inside the job. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH it is refused if over 500 configurations are missing. Then the __distance1 spaces are absent there (_shared.py:6108-6114, tests/experiments/noise/n27_removal_cost_and_propagation.py:422-433).
- R2: the pool reader chooses each model's search by best score across every pool member (_shared.py:6320-6340). Members are both families (prediction and objective='similarity') and every augmentation condition. So the base pair for a model may be ranked from an augmented or similarity-family search. That is a whole-dataset search either way. I did not check which member wins on any dataset.


## noise n29 (tests/experiments/noise/n29_document_bias.py)

What it measures: On herg_ic50, it fits one offset per ChEMBL document to the per-measurement labels, removes it from the training labels in seven ways, and scores each against training on each molecule's mean label, per fold.

Datasets: herg_ic50 only. Every other dataset returns {'skipped': 'no_record_documents'} because n29 needs one ChEMBL document per measurement (n29_document_bias.py:598-603). Only the herg_ic50 loader sets that (tests/find_best_hybrid_molecular.py:441-453, passed on at tests/experiments/_shared.py:4733-4734). herg_ic50 has no row in any DECISIONS.md step (grep for 'herg_ic50' in DECISIONS.md finds nothing). It is not a DATASET_REPS key (printed False this session); it borrows herg_ki's representations (noise/noise_helpers.py:1640, 1653-1656). No .sh file under tests/slurm_scripts names herg_ic50, and submit_everything.sh builds its dataset list from DATASET_REPS keys (submit_everything.sh:207-214). So on the cluster n29 runs on 41 datasets and skips on all 41. It produces a result only when run by hand on herg_ic50.

### R1 models: NO

Code: Downstream models are kwargs models, else config models, else DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. ensure_dprime_models then adds rf and svm if missing. Every arm is fitted with every model in each feature space. within_document_rank is fitted with xgboost whenever xgboost is in the list. The document offsets are always fitted with LightGBM (oof_predict), whatever the models. The known-bias check uses the first model, rf by default.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two approved models (Step 1). herg_ic50 has no Step 1 row, so no pair is approved for it. If herg_ki's row is meant (herg_ic50 borrows its representations), the pair is svm+dnn. Then rf, xgboost and lightgbm are three extra models, and within_document_rank runs only on an unapproved model.

Distance 100-500 features with the same importance, allocation and count cuts. Augmentation cut. Against those, the code runs four extra general budgets (10-100), deeplift, wglobal_power2 and counts 2, 3 and 5. Augmentation 'none' only would match.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per downstream model: 2 base representations (spaces base_1, base_2) ranked once on the whole-dataset search, the same two in every fold. Hybrids per model: up to 6. That is 2 general and 1 distance, for each of two families: features chosen for prediction ('hybrid') and features chosen under objective='similarity' ('hybrid_similarity'). The slots are named hybrid, hybrid__general2, hybrid__distance1 and the same for hybrid_similarity. Every one of the seven arms is then fitted in each of these spaces. The seven arms are the design of the experiment; the space selection is not.

Decisions: Per each of the dataset's two models, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n29 builds no per-fold search. When a whole-dataset search is missing, get_precomputed_search builds it on all rows inside the job. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH a large missing search raises instead. _iter_pool_searches then prints a warning and skips that search, and the model's hybrid spaces are listed as unavailable. The noise start-up builds no distance search, and nothing precomputes herg_ic50. So the distance slot is either built over all rows inside the job or refused.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment builds it itself, per fold.

### Other problems

- n29 never runs on the cluster. Its only dataset, herg_ic50, is not a DATASET_REPS key, and submit_everything.sh lists datasets from those keys (submit_everything.sh:207-214). No .sh file under tests/slurm_scripts names herg_ic50. On the 41 submitted datasets n29 writes a skip (n29_document_bias.py:598-603).
- The searches n29 reads are built on herg_ic50's per-measurement labels (n29_document_bias.py:608, 705). The hybrids are rebuilt per fold on each molecule's mean label (n29_document_bias.py:868). So the recipe was chosen for one label set and is fitted on another.
- n29 splits folds over molecules with cv_split (n29_document_bias.py:643-644). The stored search split its own folds over measurement rows. The two partitions are not the same rows. With fold_i=None this does not change which recipe is picked, but no fold of the stored search lines up with an n29 fold.
- herg_ic50 has no row in any DECISIONS.md step, so neither its two models nor its search cuts are decided. Whether herg_ki's rows (the representation donor) are meant to apply could not be determined from the record.
- The base representations are ranked once per model on the whole-dataset search, so base_1 and base_2 are the same in every fold (n29_document_bias.py:719-722, _shared.py:4876-4880).
- The document offsets are always fitted with an out-of-fold LightGBM prediction (n29_document_bias.py:83-86, 441-444), and within_document_rank always uses xgboost (n29_document_bias.py:931). Neither follows the dataset's models. The file says the first is by design, so all models in one space see the same corrected labels.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Run on its own through main(), n29 loads representations with load_data(args.dataset, rep_preset=args.reps), and --reps defaults to 'fast' (n29_document_bias.py:1229, _shared.py:9264). Only run_all's load_noise_data gives herg_ic50 herg_ki's ten representations (noise_helpers.py:1640, 1656). So the two entry points search and rank different representation sets.
- On the main() path data has no 'precomputed_searches' and no 'augmentations' key (n29_document_bias.py:1229-1237). Every general and distance search n29 reads is then built inside the job by find_best_hybrid on all per-measurement rows (_shared.py:5863-5896), or refused under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH above 500 configurations left (find_best_hybrid.py:700-750).
- The other agent's 'OTHER PROBLEMS' were spot-checked and hold. herg_ic50 is not a DATASET_REPS key (checked by import: False; 41 datasets submitted). submit_everything.sh:207-214 takes datasets from those keys. grep finds no herg_ic50 under tests/slurm_scripts. Searches use per-measurement labels (n29:608, 705); the hybrid is refitted on molecule means (n29:868).


## noise n30 (tests/experiments/noise/n30_censored_likelihood.py)

What it measures: When training labels above a limit are clipped to that limit, it measures how much of the lost score each label treatment (lift, drop, winsorise) or model change (censored-likelihood xgboost, absolute-error forest, Huber lightgbm) recovers, per fold, against untouched held-out labels.

Datasets: Every dataset the noise job is queued for: submit_everything.sh takes every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213). n30 runs in the job with no noise condition (tests/slurm_scripts/queue_noise_conditions.py:15-18; tests/experiments/noise/noise_helpers.py:112-117). should_skip_experiment does not list n30 (tests/experiments/_shared.py:3672-3685). n30 itself writes a skip on any classification dataset (n30_censored_likelihood.py:435-440). So it measures only the regression datasets. Inferred from the metric column of DECISIONS.md Step 1 (rmse, spearman, ci), not from the loaders, these are 26: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. The 15 classification datasets get a skip file.

On top of these it fits three more models: rf_l1 in rf's features, lightgbm_huber in lightgbm's, and xgboost_aft in xgboost's. gp is never asked for.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: The hybrid recipes and the two base representations are picked once per dataset, before the fold loop. They come from the whole-dataset searches. get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index. So it ranks on the mean over every fold of a search that ran on all rows, the held-out fold included. Each fold then rebuilds that fixed recipe on its own training rows with the clipped labels. The rebuild sets the feature weights, not the choice of recipe. Base representations are ranked by top_base_reps rule='whole_dataset' on the same stored search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used on a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. n30 runs no per-fold search. Its own pool metadata says selection_scope 'whole_dataset'. Its base-representation helper says the two were picked with the held-out molecules in view.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: Nothing reads the per-dataset cuts. The start-up searches use FULL_BUDGETS (8 budgets, 10 to 2000 features) and engine default lists. Those are 5 allocation methods, 3 importance methods, evaluators match/rf/lightgbm/dnn, and representation counts 2/3/5/all. On five regression datasets the fast lists apply instead: flab_expression_koenig, logd, qm9, bindingdb_kd, kiba. The distance read uses budgets 10 to 500, evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm and six models. n30 passes budget=None, so its ranking takes every stored budget. Augmentation conditions none, uncapped and capped are read on every dataset with augmentation representations.

Decisions: Step 2: every one of the 26 regression datasets has a decided range narrower than 10-2000; n30 ranks over all stored budgets on each. Step 3: importance cuts are ignored, e.g. deeplift on herg_ki and ddg_combined, lightgbm_gain on buchwald_hartwig. Step 3 and the fast-tier table also disagree with the code on flab_expression_koenig, bindingdb_kd and kiba. The record keeps deeplift, lightgbm_gain and treeshap there; the code's fast grid searches lightgbm_gain only. Step 4: wglobal_power2 is cut on caco2, ginkgo_acsins and herg_ki, and power_2 plus wglobal_power2 on ddg_combined; the default searches them. Step 5: cut evaluators still run on abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_titer. Step 6: cut counts still run, e.g. 2/3/5 on herg_ki, caco2, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm. kiba keeps only 'all', but fast gives 3 and all. bindingdb_kd keeps 2 and all, but fast gives 3 and all. Step 7: distance budgets 10, 25 and 50 are read on every regression dataset whose range starts at 100. Step 8: augmentation is cut on 24 of the 26 regression datasets. n30 reads uncapped and capped wherever augmentation representations exist. On ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic it also reads capped, and uncapped on the general search. suzuki allocation is HELD and the default runs all five.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per model it takes the top 2 base representations, which matches. For hybrids it takes the owner's 2026-10-02 rule set: top 2 general plus top 1 distance hybrid. It does this for each of two search families, predictive and similarity (pool subset 'predictive_and_similarity'). That is up to 6 hybrid feature spaces per model: hybrid, hybrid__general2, hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1. The set is chosen once for the whole dataset, not per fold.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: 2 best base representations and 2 best hybrids. n30 gives 2 base representations and up to 6 hybrids per model, chosen once. It differs in two ways at once: the hybrid count (6 against 2) and the selection being whole-dataset rather than per fold. The design reason given in the file is the 2026-10-02 rule, not anything specific to censoring.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: n30 builds no per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search goes through get_precomputed_search. Without KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH it builds that search on all rows inside the job. With it, which submit_everything.sh sets by default, a search with more than 500 configurations unstored is refused with RuntimeError. _iter_pool_searches catches the error, prints a warning and skips that member. A missing rule slot is printed and recorded as missing. If no recipe comes back for any model, every label treatment runs on single representations only.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n30 never asks for one. Its fallback for a missing search is a whole-dataset build, or a refusal with a warning and a skipped slot. bindingdb_kd and kiba have no stored distance search (DECISIONS.md:750), so their distance slot meets this path.

### Other problems

- The per-fold hybrid build is not given the augmentation representations. cached_hybrid_cell is called without augmentations_train or augmentations_val (n30_censored_likelihood.py:741-746). The recipe can be the winner of an uncapped or capped search, and its augmentation_strategy is set to that condition (_shared.py:6040-6046, 6996). create_hybrid adds augmentation only when augmentations are passed (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5984). So an augmented recipe is rebuilt from the base representations alone, under the augmented recipe's name.
- get_rule_hybrids runs with fold_i=None, so the held-out fold's own stored score is inside the ranking that picks its hybrids (_shared.py:6746-6748, 6877). n_outer_folds is not passed, so the check that the caller's folds match the pool's folds never runs (_shared.py:6970-6975).
- The three swap models only run where their parent model is fitted (n30_censored_likelihood.py:466-475). rf, lightgbm and xgboost are outside the approved pair on most regression datasets. On herg_ki (svm+dnn), all three swaps are fitted in feature spaces built for unapproved models.
- noise run_all builds no distance search at start-up (noise_helpers.py:1817-1903). get_fold_pool_recipes reads data['precomputed_searches_distance'] for the distance lineage (_shared.py:6789-6790), and noise run_all never sets it. So every distance slot is read from disk or built during n30.
- Could not determine whether the similarity-family searches read through get_precomputed_search match the ones noise run_all built. The reader asks with adaptive_pruning=False and no schedule (_shared.py:5889). The start-up passes the 'default_pruning' schedule (noise_helpers.py:1838, 1868). I did not check whether the schedule enters the stored-search identity.
- The regression and classification split of the 41 datasets is inferred from the DECISIONS.md Step 1 metric column, not from the loaders.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3: n30's start-up search runs the uncapped condition on bindingdb_kd and kiba. Augmentation is cut on both in Step 8. The reader leaves uncapped out for these two (_shared.py:5989, 6041-6043). The start-up adds it whenever augmentation representations exist (_shared.py:5543-5549). So that search is built and never read. Whether these two datasets load augmentation representations: could not determine without running the loader.
- R3: the fast lists also cut allocation methods that the record keeps. Fast searches performance_weighted, power_2 and rank_exp_d0.3 only (find_best_hybrid.py:3072). Step 4 keeps softmax_T1 on kiba and flab_expression_koenig. It keeps softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2 on bindingdb_kd (DECISIONS.md:388, 381, 393).
- R3: the distance read ranks over every stored distance configuration (_shared.py:6830-6853). It ignores Step 7's importance, allocation, evaluator and representation-count cuts, not only its budgets. Example: herg_ki's distance search cuts deeplift, wglobal_power2 and counts 2/3/5 (DECISIONS.md:636). ddg_combined's cuts deeplift, three allocation methods, the lightgbm evaluator and counts 2/3 (DECISIONS.md:623).
- Augmentation on the distance search: n30 reads capped on ginkgo_hic under 10,000 rows (_shared.py:6036-6037). Step 8 says 'keep uncapped only' for ginkgo_hic (DECISIONS.md:676).
- Report item 'could not determine' on the pruning schedule: neither the row-store identity columns nor its configuration columns hold a pruning schedule (src/kirby/result_cache.py:46-135). So the schedule does not separate stored rows. I did not check the search file's own metadata, so whether the reader is served the start-up search is still undetermined.


## noise n31 (tests/experiments/noise/n31_regime_and_breakeven.py)

What it measures: n31 injects noise into each fold's training labels. It then compares the AUROC the report's formulas predict for a residual detector with the AUROC measured. Last, it finds the flag precision at which removing, downweighting, rewriting or shrinking the flagged labels starts to beat the noisy fit.

Datasets: It runs on the 26 regression datasets of the 41 that submit_everything.sh queues for noise. submit_everything.sh sets no noise condition, so the job runs n31 (submit_everything.sh:350-371; noise_helpers.py:119-123). n31 itself returns 'skipped' for any classification dataset (n31:457-460). Registry task types were printed this session. The 26 are abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9 and suzuki. should_skip_experiment does not list n31 (_shared.py:3672-3675).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Downstream models are kwargs models, else config models, else DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. ensure_dprime_models then adds rf and svm. Under run_all, config models are the five: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. All five are fitted in every space on every regression dataset. get_model_factories can drop a model above its row limit. gp is never named, so it is never fitted. knn and ridge are never fitted. A LightGBM also gives the out-of-fold residual that the detector ranks. That is the measurement itself, not a downstream model.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models. On 21 of the 26 regression datasets both approved models are among the five. Those 21 each get three extra models. abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn) and ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn) are the other five. On those, gp is never fitted and four unapproved models are. rf and svm are forced by an owner decision of 2026-09-25 (n23:298-308). That conflicts with Step 1 (2026-10-03) on every dataset whose pair lacks rf or svm.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Each model's hybrid recipes come from get_rule_hybrids. It is called with no fold index, so it ranks every stored configuration by its mean over all folds of a whole-dataset search. The base representations come from noise_base_reps_by_model, which uses the whole-dataset mean (rule='whole_dataset'). One recipe set and one base pair serve every fold. Only the hybrid's features are refitted per fold, on that fold's noisy training labels. The searches behind the recipes ran over every row of the dataset.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. n31 reads the whole-dataset search. It does not even hold out the fold's scores (fold_i=None). Its own metadata says selection_scope 'whole_dataset'. The base pair was picked with the held-out molecules in view (_shared.py:4876-4880).

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: n31 reads searches built with global lists. The general search is the run_all precompute: FULL_BUDGETS (8 budgets, 10-2000 features) and the engine default allocation, importance, evaluator and representation-count lists. The fast lists replace those on the 14 code-fast datasets. The distance read uses DISTANCE_BUDGETS (10-500), DISTANCE_EVALUATORS (knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm) and DISTANCE_MODELS. n31 passes budget=None. So every budget the search holds is ranked, and nothing filters it to the decided range. Augmentation members come from _pool_conditions. The general search gets none, uncapped and capped. The distance search gets none, uncapped, and capped under 10,000 rows. kiba and bindingdb_kd never get uncapped.

Decisions: The dataset's Step 2-7 cuts and the Step 8 augmentation rule on every search read. None is applied. Budgets break on all 26 regression datasets, because each has at least one cut budget. Example: herg_ki is decided 250-2000 features, but a 10-feature hybrid can be chosen. flab_expression_koenig, bindingdb_kd and kiba run the fast grid. That grid uses lightgbm_gain only, where the record keeps deeplift, lightgbm_gain and treeshap. Step 8 cuts augmentation on 24 of the 26. n31 reads uncapped and capped members wherever the data carries augmentation representations. The Step 3-6 cuts (e.g. herg_ki: deeplift, wglobal_power2, counts 2/3/5) are not applied on any dataset.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Each model gets two base representations, base_1 and base_2, ranked on the whole dataset. It also gets up to six hybrids: 2 general and 1 distance in each of two search families. The predictive family chose features to predict the label. The similarity family chose features so each molecule's five nearest neighbours predict its activity. The pool subset is 'predictive_and_similarity'. One set is chosen for the whole dataset and reused on every fold. It is not chosen per fold.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n31 matches on base representations but not on fold. It has up to six hybrids per model, not two. It picks once, not per fold. The six include a distance hybrid and three hybrids from the similarity family. No docstring line says the six are a deliberate design choice for n31. The comment at 588-590 cites the owner's 2026-10-02 set of 2 general + 1 distance per model and family.

### R5 noise 8 configurations: NO

Code: Each pass has five models. Each model has 2 base representations and up to 6 hybrids. That is up to 8 feature spaces per model and up to 40 (model, feature space) configurations per pass. Two similarity-family hybrids can share one feature matrix across models when their recipes are equal. That changes build count, not configurations.

Decisions: Two models, each with 2 base representations and 2 hybrids: 8 configurations. n31 has up to 40, from two things at once. It fits five models, not two. It uses up to six hybrids per model, not two.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n31 never runs a per-fold search. Each missing pool member goes to get_precomputed_search, which calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. Without KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, that builds a whole-dataset search inside the job. With it set, the default in submit_everything.sh, the call is refused when more than 500 configurations are unstored. _iter_pool_searches catches the error, prints a warning and skips that member. get_rule_hybrids then reports the slot missing. n31 writes it to hybrid_spaces_unavailable and runs without that space. A model with no stored search gets no base representations and no hybrids. noise run_all builds no distance search at start-up, so the distance slot always goes through this path.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n31 builds a whole-dataset search instead, or refuses it and skips the space with a warning.

### Other problems

- Hybrids are rebuilt without augmentation features. n31 passes no augmentations_train or augmentations_val to cached_hybrid_cell (n31:727-732). A recipe can come from an uncapped or capped search. hybrid_for_fold's docstring says such a recipe then rebuilds a narrower feature space than the search chose (noise_helpers.py:982-985). The feature space scored and the recipe it is filed under can then differ.
- The base representations and the hybrids come from two different reads. The base pair is ranked inside the one stored search that get_best_search_for_downstream returned for that model: one augmentation condition, the predictive family (n31:569-571; _shared.py:6392). The hybrids come from get_rule_hybrids, ranked across every pool member. get_rule_hybrids also returns its own top-2 base list, and n31 does not use it (_shared.py:7183-7185, 7190-7194).
- Whether the per-fold rebuild picks representations with whole-dataset scores could not be determined. build_fold_hybrid uses blueprint.rep_scores when the recipe's representation count is below the representations passed (_shared.py:5256-5286). hybrid_for_fold first cuts the representations to bp.reps (noise_helpers.py:1005-1012). I did not establish whether bp.reps already holds only the counted subset.
- The rf and svm forcing (owner decision 2026-09-25, n23:298-308) conflicts with Step 1 of 2026-10-03. Both rules exist in the code and the record, and neither mentions the other.
- The per-fold split comes from cv_split(groups, n_folds, ..., mode) (n31:532-533). The pool's fold numbering does not enter n31, because it reads with fold_i=None. So no fold mismatch arises, but nothing is held out either.
- The module docstring (n31:103-112) describes one recipe per downstream model plus two base representations. The code builds up to six hybrid spaces per model (n31:574-583; _shared.py:6508-6547).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The other agent marked this 'could not determine'. The code answers it: the per-fold rebuild picks which representations go in by whole-dataset scores. A configuration searched on the top N representations stores Blueprint.reps as the whole pool: rep_names = base_reps keys (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:5389-5398). The top-N cut applies to train_reps only (find_best_hybrid.py:4963-4984). build_fold_hybrid then ranks by blueprint.rep_scores (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5256-5286), because n31 passes no fold allocation scores. rep_scores is each representation's best baseline over every row (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593). So for any recipe with a representation count, which representations enter a fold's hybrid was decided with that fold's held-out molecules in view. hybrid_for_fold's cut to bp.reps (noise_helpers.py:1005-1012) removes nothing, because bp.reps is the whole pool.
- Step 8 on the two regression datasets that keep augmentation: ginkgo_hic is 'keep uncapped only' and ginkgo_colloidal is 'keep uncapped' (DECISIONS.md:673-674). n31 also reads the capped member for both: the general search at _shared.py:6040-6046, the distance search under 10,000 rows at _shared.py:6036-6037. So augmentation disagrees with the record on all 26 regression datasets wherever augmentation representations load, not on 24. The record leaves open whether the kept augmentation applies to the general search (DECISIONS.md:654).
- The 'two different reads' item is confirmed, with one more difference. noise_base_reps_by_model ranks inside the one SearchResult returned for the model: one augmentation condition and the first family (_shared.py:6392-6395, 4904-4921). get_fold_pool_recipes keeps the better score per representation across every pool member and condition (_shared.py:6955-6962). So the two lists can name different representations even before folds come in.


## noise n32 (tests/experiments/noise/n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py)

What it measures: Under injected label noise, n32 measures how well six detectors find the damaged training molecules. It also measures how much of the clean-label score trimming, two-learner exchange and flagged-only shrinking recover, each set against random removal.

Datasets: n32 is in the noise suite's default list (noise_helpers.py:124). submit_everything.sh queues the noise suite on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). should_skip_experiment never skips n32: it is in neither skip list (_shared.py:3672-3675, 3684-3685). n32 itself returns a skip on any dataset whose task is not regression (n32:1273-1274, 1300-1304). So n32 runs on the regression datasets. Judged by the metric column of DECISIONS Step 1 (rmse, spearman or ci), there are 26 of them: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9 and suzuki. I did not check each dataset's task_type field; the list is taken from the metric column. Within each dataset, n32 sweeps every condition in DETECTION_IS_DEFINED (n32:1283-1286).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: downstream_model_list takes config['models'] and appends rf and svm if they are missing. noise run_all sets config['models'] to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of DOWNSTREAM_MODELS: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. Every arm is fitted with all five models in every feature space. gp is never fitted. The detectors and the two exchange learners (lightgbm, svm) are fixed on every dataset. They are part of the cleaning methods, not downstream models.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two approved models. On abagym_Ang2 and abagym_VEGF the pair is gp+svm. On ginkgo_acsins it is lightgbm+gp. On ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho it is gp+dnn. On every regression dataset n32 fits three models outside the approved pair. On those five gp datasets it also never fits gp, so one approved model is missing. All 26 regression datasets break the rule. knn and ridge are never fitted, which agrees with the rule.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: For each model, n32 reads the recipes once, before the fold loop. They come from searches run over every row of the dataset. The rule read calls get_rule_hybrids with no fold index, so it ranks on the mean over all the stored search's folds. get_best_search_for_downstream records selection_scope 'whole_dataset'. The two base representations come from noise_base_reps_by_model, which ranks on the same whole-dataset search. Its own comment says the held-out molecules were in view. Each fold then rebuilds the chosen recipe on that fold's training rows with the noisy labels. That fixes the features, not the choice of recipe.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. n32 has no per-fold search anywhere. The rows it later holds out helped choose every recipe and both base representations.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: The general searches it reads were built at noise start-up. They used FULL_BUDGETS (8 budgets, 10 to 2000 features) and the engine's default axes, with no models passed. The rule's distance read uses DISTANCE_BUDGETS (10 to 500 features) on every dataset. It also uses DISTANCE_EVALUATORS (knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm) and DISTANCE_MODELS. budget=None, so the ranking covers every stored budget. Augmentation conditions come from _pool_conditions. The general tier gets none, uncapped and capped; the distance tier gets none, uncapped, and capped under 10,000 rows. Only kiba and bindingdb_kd drop uncapped. Every fold also builds base_k_aug_uncapped spaces from the c21 recipe on every dataset that carries augmentation representations.

Decisions: Each dataset's decided budget range (Step 2), importance methods (Step 3), allocation methods (Step 4), evaluators (Step 5 v3) and representation counts (Step 6) on the general search, and Step 7's five axes on the distance search. Step 8 also cuts augmentation everywhere except uncapped on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, on the distance search. Every one of the 26 regression datasets breaks Step 2: none of them keeps all 8 general budgets, yet n32 can pick a recipe at any of them. Every regression dataset with a distance decision breaks Step 7's budgets, because 10 features is read everywhere and no regression dataset's Step 7 range starts at 10. The per-dataset gaps in importance, allocation, evaluators and representation counts are the ones the shared helper map lists for the default grid; I did not recount them. On augmentation, the regression datasets that carry augmentation representations read uncapped and capped searches that Step 8 cuts. They also get base_k_aug_uncapped spaces. Step 8's open note names that exact space.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per model, n32 takes the top 2 base representations (base_1, base_2). It takes every hybrid the rule returns. The rule is read with pool_subset 'predictive_and_similarity', so each family gives 2 general hybrids and 1 distance hybrid. That makes up to six hybrid feature spaces per model: hybrid, hybrid__general2, hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1. All of them are picked once for the whole dataset, not per fold.

Decisions: For each of the dataset's two models, in each fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n32 matches on base representations, 2 per model, but picks them on the whole dataset. It differs in three ways: up to 6 hybrids per model instead of 2, five models instead of 2, and one pick for all folds instead of one per fold.

### R5 noise 8 configurations: NO

Code: Each model gets up to 8 feature spaces (2 base + up to 6 hybrids). With five models that is up to 40 combinations of model and feature space, each fitted under every cleaning arm.

Decisions: 2 models × (2 base representations + 2 hybrids) = 8 configurations. n32 uses up to 40. It has three more models than the rule allows and up to four more hybrids per model.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: n32 never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search goes to get_precomputed_search, which calls find_best_hybrid on all rows. noise run_all never builds the distance tier, so the rule's distance read always lands there. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, a search with more than 500 configurations still to score raises. The resulting RuntimeError is caught in _iter_pool_searches, which prints a warning and skips that search. The rule then lists the empty slot as missing. If no recipe comes back for any model, n32 runs only the single representations.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n32 builds a whole-dataset search inside the job, or skips it with a warning. Neither is a per-fold search.

### Other problems

- Hybrid recipes searched with augmentation are rebuilt without it. get_fold_pool_recipes stamps each recipe with its condition, 'uncapped' or 'capped' (_shared.py:6992-6997). n32's cached_hybrid passes no augmentation representations to the fold build (n32:332-344, 1604-1607). create_hybrid adds augmentation features only when augmentations is not None (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5983). So a recipe that won with augmentation features is scored without them, under the same name. I read create_hybrid only up to that line.
- The module docstring says the recipe was 'searched on clean labels' (n32:121-124). That is the clean labels of every row, the held-out rows included. Each fold then injects noise only into its own training rows.
- The knn_shapley similarity sweep covers three hybrid spaces: hybrid, hybrid__general2 and hybrid_similarity (similarity_space.py:126). n32 scores up to six hybrid spaces (n32:1472-1480). For hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1, knn_shapley runs only on the model's own feature matrix, not under the other similarity settings.
- For the relative conditions, the residual SD is measured in one representation: the first model's rank-1 base representation. n32's own comment says this is not signed off by the owner (n32:1459-1471).
- The base representations come from the search the pool picked for each model, through noise_base_reps_by_model (n32:1454-1456). get_rule_hybrids also returns its own top-2 base representations (_shared.py:7183-7198), and n32 does not use them. Both are whole-dataset rankings. When the pool's chosen search is not the rule's general search, the two can name different representations. I did not check whether they differ on any dataset.
- build_fold_hybrid uses blueprint.rep_scores, which are whole-dataset scores, to choose the representations when the recipe's rep_count is below the number of representations passed (_shared.py:5256-5286). hybrid_for_fold first restricts the representations to bp.reps (noise_helpers.py:1005-1012). Could not determine whether bp.reps lists only the restricted representations. That decides whether this path is reached.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R2: the representations inside each fold's hybrid are picked with whole-dataset scores, not only the recipe. Every Blueprint lists the whole pool as its representations (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:5389-5398). So any recipe with rep_count below the pool size reaches build_fold_hybrid's rep_scores path (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5256-5286). rep_scores are each representation's best baseline over every row (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593).
- R3: the noise start-up precompute builds uncapped and capped searches for every dataset that has augmentation representations, kiba and bindingdb_kd included (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5540-5548). _pool_conditions never reads the uncapped one on those two (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5989, 6036-6040). Step 8 cuts both on both datasets.
- R3: the per-fold base_k_aug_uncapped build uses a fixed recipe: performance_weighted, lightgbm_gain, evaluator 'match', full base width. These come from c21, not from Steps 2-6 (tests/experiments/noise/n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:700-702; settings as reported by the first agent from similarity_space.base_aug_blueprint, not re-opened here).
- R1: the start-up precompute passes models=None to find_best_hybrid (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5568-5571), although run_all's config carries 'models' (noise_helpers.py:1751). So the stored search's model list is the engine default, not the dataset's approved pair.


## noise n33 (tests/experiments/noise/n33_robust_training.py)

What it measures: Under each injected regression label-noise condition, it measures whether a target transform, a weighting, C-Mixup, label-noise bagging, a robust teacher, or a robust loss recovers held-out accuracy lost to the noise, scored against untouched labels.

Datasets: The 26 regression datasets: herg_ki, caco2, logd, qm9, adme_hlm, adme_rlm, adme_mdr1, flab_thermo_tresanco, abcov_kd, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_koenig, flab_expression_adams, abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, suzuki, buchwald_hartwig, bh_doyle_plates, kiba, bindingdb_kd. submit_everything.sh queues noise on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (tests/slurm_scripts/submit_everything.sh:207-213, 95). n33 is in the default noise list (noise/noise_helpers.py:125). n33 returns a skip on the 15 classification datasets (n33_robust_training.py:494-498, 518-519). The regression/classification split was printed this session from kirby.registry.

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: It fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every regression dataset. The list comes from config['models'], which noise run_all sets to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of the five. downstream_model_list appends rf and svm if absent; both are already there. gp is never fitted. It also fits loss-changed copies of lightgbm, xgboost, rf and dnn, plus an NGBoost pair, as comparators. knn and ridge are never fitted.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models. On 21 of the 26 regression datasets both approved models are among the five, so three unapproved models are fitted. On abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn) and ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn), gp is approved and never fitted. Those five get one approved model and four unapproved ones.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Per model it uses the top 2 base representations, chosen once for the whole dataset. Per model it uses up to 6 hybrids, also chosen once. Those are 2 general plus 1 distance under the predictive objective, and 2 general plus 1 distance under the similarity objective. The same set is used in every fold. If the rule read raises for a model, it falls back to one hybrid per objective, so 2. The label arms and loss changes are applied inside each of these feature spaces by design.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n33 has the base side right in count but not per fold. It has up to 6 hybrids per model instead of 2, and none is chosen per fold.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: It never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search is built inside the job on all rows when cold refusal is off. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, the default in submit_everything.sh, a search with more than 500 configurations missing raises. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that search. get_rule_hybrids reports the slot as missing. If no recipe comes back at all, n33 runs the base representations only.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search that does not exist must be built by the experiment itself. n33 asks for no per-fold search, and for a missing whole-dataset search it either builds one on all rows or skips with a warning.

### Other problems

- The per-fold rebuild passes no augmentation representations. cached_hybrid calls cached_hybrid_for_fold without augmentations_train or augmentations_val (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:340-344). create_hybrid then skips the augmentation step (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5984). So a recipe picked from an uncapped or capped search is rebuilt without its donor features, under that recipe's name.
- Two different rankings pick base representations. get_rule_hybrids ranks them across every pool member (_shared.py:7183-7185). n33 ignores that list. It ranks from the one search get_best_search_for_downstream returned (n33_robust_training.py:648-650). The two lists can name different representations.
- The number of hybrids per model varies by run. If get_rule_hybrids raises for a model, the error is printed and the model falls back to one hybrid per objective (noise_helpers.py:1419-1428; _shared.py:6549-6588). So a model gets 6 hybrids or 2.
- Recipes are chosen on clean labels, while features are refitted per fold on the noisy training labels (n33_robust_training.py:113-115, 776-779). This is stated in the docstring as the design.
- build_fold_hybrid picks which representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores when the recipe's representation count is below the representations passed (_shared.py:5256-5262). Those scores come from the whole-dataset search. hybrid_for_fold first cuts to bp.reps (noise_helpers.py:1005-1009). Could not determine whether bp.reps already holds only the counted representations, so whether this extra choice happens is undetermined.
- Every pool member that is missing is built inside the job on all rows when KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH is unset (_shared.py:5845-5896). That includes the distance searches, which noise run_all never builds at start-up (noise_helpers.py:1826-1885).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3, three datasets on the fast list: flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd are in dataset_policy.FAST_SPEED_DATASETS. So every read for them asks for the fast lists. Fast allocation is performance_weighted, power_2 and rank_exp_d0.3. Step 4 keeps softmax_T1 on all three, and wglobal_power2 too on bindingdb_kd, so those methods are missing. Fast representation counts are 3 and all. Step 6 cuts 3 on all three datasets, so a cut count is read. bindingdb_kd also keeps count 2, which the fast list does not hold. The first agent named only the missing importance methods. Evidence: tests/experiments/dataset_policy.py:688-711; FAST_REP_COUNTS [3, None] and FAST_ALLOCATION_METHODS (printed from find_best_hybrid this session); find_best_hybrid.py:8652-8668; DECISIONS.md:348-363 (these three are not in the decided fast-tier table); DECISIONS.md Step 4 rows for flab_expression_koenig, kiba, bindingdb_kd; DECISIONS.md Step 6 rows for the same three.
- R3, representation counts were not listed: the code reads counts 2, 3, 5 and all on every regression dataset outside the fast list. Step 6 cuts at least one count on 16 regression datasets (see the R3 correction). Evidence: find_best_hybrid DEFAULT_REP_COUNTS [2, 3, 5, None]; DECISIONS.md:559-605.
- R3, distance search cuts were not listed: the code reads distance budgets 10 to 500. Every regression row in Step 7 has a decided range starting at 25, 50 or 100, so budget 10 (and often 25 and 50) is a cut budget that is read. Step 7's importance, allocation, evaluator and count cuts on the distance search are ignored too. That includes the knn evaluator cut on buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic.
