## noise n34 (tests/experiments/noise/n34_group_random_effects.py)

What it measures: Under injected scaffold-group label noise, it measures whether subtracting each group's mean out-of-fold residual from the training labels helps more than subtracting a shrunk random-intercept offset. Each method is scored against leaving the labels as they are, on held-out molecules graded against clean labels.

Datasets: It is queued on all 41 datasets but runs on 7: adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, herg_ki, logd, qm9. submit_everything.sh:207-213 lists every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis. Noise is one of the queued suites (submit_everything.sh:95), and n34 is in the default noise list (noise_helpers.py:126). n34 skips any dataset whose task is not regression (n34:387-390). It also skips any dataset with no SMILES (n34:391-395, via dataset_policy.noise_groups_for at dataset_policy.py:534-536). load_data sets data['smiles'] only in its last branch, the plain molecular one (_shared.py:4718; the tcga, antibody, nucleotide, reaction, dta and cdr_flexibility branches open at 4107-4528). It also sets it for lhasa_herg (4101), which is classification. I classified the 41 names with a small import this session. Seven are molecular regression datasets. herg and lhasa_herg are molecular but classification, so they are skipped. I did not load qm9 to confirm that its regression label carries SMILES; its metric in DECISIONS is rmse.

### R1 models: NO

Code: It fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. config['models'] is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. downstream_model_list adds rf and svm only if they are missing, and both are already in the list. No knn, gp or ridge is fitted. The out-of-fold model that estimates the offsets is always lightgbm, whatever the downstream model is.

Decisions: Step 1 approves two models per dataset. adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm and herg_ki get svm+dnn. caco2 and logd get dnn+svm. qm9 gets dnn+lightgbm. On all seven datasets n34 fits three models that are not approved: rf, xgboost and lightgbm on the six svm+dnn datasets, and rf, xgboost and svm on qm9.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: Every hybrid recipe and both base representations come from searches over all rows of the dataset, read once before the fold loop. The general searches are built at start-up by noise run_all, which calls precompute_hybrid_searches on the full labels. Two searches are built: one predictive, one under objective='similarity'. The distance searches are read from disk or built on all rows by get_precomputed_search. n34 then reads them through get_rule_hybrids with no fold index, so recipes are ranked on the mean over every fold of the whole-dataset search. The two base representations come from noise_base_reps_by_model, which ranks on the whole-dataset search. Inside the fold loop, each chosen recipe is rebuilt on that fold's training rows and noisy labels. That refits the features, but which recipe and which representations to use were chosen with every row in view, held-out molecules included.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only. One search over all rows, then reused in every fold, leaks.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: The searches n34 reads use the same lists on every dataset. The general searches use budgets 10 to 2000 features (8 budgets). On logd and qm9 they use the fast grid: lightgbm_gain, three allocation methods, representation counts 3 and all. Elsewhere they use the full engine defaults: deeplift, lightgbm_gain and treeshap; five allocation methods; evaluators match, rf, lightgbm and dnn; representation counts 2, 3, 5 and all. The distance searches use budgets 10 to 500 features (6 budgets) and evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm. n34 asks with budget=None, so recipes are ranked over every stored budget. Both families read augmentation conditions none, uncapped and capped, because all seven datasets load augmentation representations.

Decisions: General budgets (Step 2): 500-2000 on adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, logd and qm9; 250-2000 on herg_ki. So 10, 25, 50, 100 and 250 should not be read, except 250 on herg_ki. Importance (Step 3): herg_ki cuts deeplift; logd and qm9 run lightgbm_gain alone. Allocation (Step 4): caco2 and herg_ki cut wglobal_power2. Evaluators (Step 5 v3): all four are kept on all seven. Representation counts (Step 6): adme_hlm cuts 2 and 3. adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2 and herg_ki cut 2, 3 and 5. Distance (Step 7): 100-500 on all seven. It also cuts deeplift on adme_hlm and herg_ki, treeshap on caco2, wglobal_power2 on herg_ki, and the svm evaluator on qm9. Its representation-count cuts are 2 and 3 on the three adme sets and caco2, and 2, 3 and 5 on herg_ki. Augmentation (Step 8): cut on all seven.

### R4 standard selection: NO

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n34 never builds a per-fold search. When a whole-dataset pool search is missing, get_precomputed_search builds it on all rows with find_best_hybrid inside the job. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, a search with more than 500 configurations left is refused with RuntimeError. _iter_pool_searches catches that, prints a warning and skips that pool member. The slot then shows as missing, and n34 writes the reason to hybrid_spaces_unavailable. noise run_all builds no distance search. So both distance families come from disk, from a build on all rows, or are refused.

Decisions: If a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment must build it itself, on that fold's training rows. It must not refuse or skip.

### Other problems

- The module docstring says each model is scored in 'its own top 2 single representations and both hybrid spaces' (n34:43-44). The code builds up to six hybrid spaces per model: two general and one distance per family, in two families (_shared.py:6504-6535, 7064-7066). The docstring describes two hybrids per model and the code builds up to six.
- Augmented recipes are rebuilt without their augmentation representations. The pool reads uncapped and capped searches, and get_fold_pool_recipes stamps the recipe with that condition (_shared.py:6996). n34 calls cached_hybrid with no augmentation arguments (n34:639-642), and cached_hybrid passes none on (n32:332-344). hybrid_for_fold's docstring says such a recipe 'rebuilds a narrower feature space than the one the search chose' (noise_helpers.py:982-985). I did not read create_hybrid to confirm whether it raises or builds without the augmentation features.
- The recipes are ranked with fold_i=None, so each fold's own stored score helps choose the recipe used on that fold (_shared.py:7082-7084, 6746-6748). This is in addition to the search having seen every row.
- The base representations come from the SearchResult that get_best_search_for_downstream picked for each model. Ties go first to 'none', then uncapped, then capped (_shared.py:6332-6339). I could not determine whether the stored baselines differ between those augmentation conditions.
- The rep_count leak in build_fold_hybrid (_shared.py:5256-5286) applies only when the fold's representations outnumber blueprint.rep_count after hybrid_for_fold cuts them to bp.reps (noise_helpers.py:1005-1012). I could not determine from the code alone whether stored blueprints list only the rep_count representations.
- The offsets every arm subtracts come from an out-of-fold lightgbm fitted in the space being scored (n34:663-671). This is a model choice inside the experiment's method, and it is the same on every dataset. It is not one of the approved downstream models on adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2, herg_ki or logd.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R6/R4: a silent fall-back from six hybrids to two. If the rule read (get_rule_hybrids) raises anything other than StaleResultDB, pool_recipe_per_downstream_model prints one line and continues (noise_helpers.py:1424-1428). pool_recipes_by_family then builds one hybrid per family from best_config (_shared.py:6549-6589). The result file does not record that general2 and distance1 were never attempted; only the printed line says so.
- R3: the two entry points read different pools. Under noise run_all, all seven datasets load augmentation representations (noise_helpers.py:1680-1698), so none, uncapped and capped are read. Under n34's standalone main(), load_data returns 'augmentations': None (_shared.py:4725), so only 'none' is read (_shared.py:6030-6046). Both read augmentation conditions that Step 8 cut on all seven datasets.
- R1: the hybrid rebuild inside each fold also fits each of the five downstream models as its accept/reject model (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:338-339, noise_helpers.py:1016-1022). So the unapproved models are fitted in the feature build as well as in scoring.
- R2: no per-fold search path (search_on_fold, get_fold_best_search, run_nested_cv, nested_cv_evaluate) is imported or called anywhere in n34 (imports at n34:122-145; fold loop n34:549-721).


## noise n35 (tests/experiments/noise/n35_near_duplicate_disagreement.py)

What it measures: For pairs of nearly identical training molecules, it measures how far their recorded labels disagree as a noise estimate, then tests whether weighting both molecules of a disagreeing pair at 0.25 improves held-out scores under injected gaussian noise.

Datasets: It is queued on all 41 datasets through the noise job. submit_everything.sh:207-213 takes every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis. n35 is listed in noise_helpers.py:127 and runs only in the job with no noise condition (noise_helpers.py:121-127, 1577-1579). It writes a skip on any dataset whose task is not regression (n35:439-442). By the metric in DECISIONS Step 1, 26 datasets are regression: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. I did not print data['task_type'] per dataset, so that split is inferred from the metric, unverified. On bindingdb_kd and kiba every fold is refused: over 12,000 training rows means no distances and no arm (n35:170, 671-683). dataset_policy.py:702-703 says both are about 100,000 rows. n35 is not in either skip list of should_skip_experiment (_shared.py:3672-3685).

### R1 models: NO

Code: Under the noise job it fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. config['models'] is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. downstream_model_list appends rf and svm only if missing, and both are already there. gp is never fitted, because nothing names it. knn and ridge are never fitted.

Decisions: Two approved models per dataset (Step 1). On 21 regression datasets both approved models are among the five. So n35 fits three extra models there. On abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn) and ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn), gp is approved. n35 never fits gp there, and it fits four unapproved models. All 26 regression datasets break the rule.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: The hybrid recipes come from the whole-dataset stored searches. They are ranked by the mean over all of that search's folds, because get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index. Each fold then rebuilds those recipes on its own training rows with the noisy training labels. The two single representations per model are ranked from the same whole-dataset search's own mean (rule='whole_dataset'). n35's own docstring says the recipes were read from the pool searched on clean labels.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. Here the recipe and the choice of the two single representations were both made with every row, including the fold's held-out molecules. Only the features are refitted per fold.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each of the five models, the comparison has 2 single representations (base_1, base_2). The 6 spaces are hybrid, hybrid__general2, hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1. Each space is a model input under 3 weighting arms, plus one arm per similarity setting swept.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: the 2 best single representations and the 2 best hybrids. n35 has the 2 single representations right. It scores up to 6 hybrids per model instead of 2. The method arms (untouched, downweight in this space, downweight by forest proximity) are its own design, layered on top of each feature space.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n35 never builds a per-fold search. If a stored whole-dataset search is missing, get_precomputed_search builds it over all rows inside the job. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, a search with more than 500 configurations left raises. _iter_pool_searches catches that, prints a warning and skips that member. The empty slot is written to hybrid_spaces_unavailable. With no recipe at all, every arm runs on the single representations only. submit_everything.sh turns the refusal on by default.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. Here the search is whole-dataset when built, and is skipped with a warning when refused.

### Other problems

- Hybrids found under an augmented condition are rebuilt without augmentation features. get_fold_pool_recipes sets the recipe's augmentation_strategy to 'uncapped' or 'capped' (_shared.py:6992-6996). n35 builds through cached_hybrid, which passes no augmentation matrices (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:332-344, n35:791-794). create_hybrid adds augmentation features only when matrices are passed (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5984, 6403). So the feature space fitted is narrower than the one the search scored, under the same space name.
- The docstring says the forest proximity is refused above n07.PROX_SMOOTH_MAX_ROWS (n35:34-36). That constant is None (n07_remediation.py:340), so the check at n35:731 never fires and the forest proximity is never refused.
- On bindingdb_kd and kiba every fold stops at MAX_PAIR_ROWS=12,000 training rows (n35:170, 671-683). The whole-dataset recipe lookups at n35:522-528 still run before the fold loop. If those searches are missing, they can be built for a run that then scores nothing.
- The two single representations per model are ranked from whichever search get_best_search_for_downstream returned for that model (n35:556-558). That can be an uncapped or capped search, not the 'none' search. Which one is used is not recorded beside base_reps_by_model.
- n35 splits with cv_split (n35:519-520) and ranks recipes with fold_i=None. It never checks that its folds match the stored search's folds. With no fold held out of the ranking, every fold's held-out molecules shaped every recipe and every single-representation choice.
- If the recipe asks for fewer representations than the pool holds, build_fold_hybrid picks which ones by blueprint.rep_scores when no fold scores are passed (_shared.py:5256-5286). Those scores come from the whole-dataset search. I could not determine whether bp.reps is already cut to that subset before this point (noise_helpers.py:1005-1012).

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R3: the start-up precompute builds the uncapped search on every dataset with augmentation representations, including bindingdb_kd and kiba. The read side leaves uncapped out for those two (UNCAPPED_SKIP_DATASETS, _shared.py:5989, 6033). precompute_hybrid_searches has no such check (_shared.py:5543-5548). I could not determine whether those two datasets carry augmentation representations.
- R3: on small datasets the start-up searches add gp to the search's model list through _apply_small_dataset_models (_shared.py:1016-1018, 1080). n35 never fits gp downstream. So those searches score a model this run does not use, while not scoring by the approved pair alone.
- R2: the representations inside a hybrid built from a 2-, 3- or 5-representation recipe are picked by each representation's best score over ALL models in the whole-dataset search, not the downstream model's score (find_best_hybrid.py:9574-9581). The comment at find_best_hybrid.py:9568-9572 says these scores are no longer fed to a labelled rebuild. build_fold_hybrid still uses them that way (_shared.py:5258-5260).
- R6: three more warning-and-skip places beyond _iter_pool_searches: get_rule_hybrids (_shared.py:7132-7140), pool_recipe_per_downstream_model (noise_helpers.py:1423-1430), and the start-up precompute (_shared.py:5614-5623).


## noise n36 (tests/experiments/noise/n36_remeasure_priority.py)

What it measures: Some training molecules were measured more than once. It measures whether ranking them by model disagreement, leverage or neighbour distance does better than random at choosing which ones get a second measurement.

Datasets: It runs only where the loader keeps repeat measurements. Other datasets write a skip (n36:309-313), and so does any dataset with fewer than 10 repeated molecules (n36:345-349). build_replicate_groups returns groups when data carries 'replicate_groups' or metadata drug_ids and protein_ids (_ground_truth_providers.py:178-198). Two loaders supply them. herg_ic50 supplies replicate_groups (_shared.py:4612-4616, 4727-4731). The three DTA datasets davis, kiba and bindingdb_kd supply drug and protein ids (_shared.py:3559, 4441-4445, 4517-4529). The docstring names herg_ic50 and bindingdb_kd (n36:16-18). davis is not in the submit roster. kiba gets through build_replicate_groups too. Whether kiba has 10 or more repeated (drug, protein) pairs could not be determined without loading it. herg_ic50 appears in no launcher: a grep of tests/slurm_scripts, run_dataset.py, dataset_policy.py and precompute_hybrids.py finds nothing. herg_ic50 also has no row anywhere in DECISIONS.md. It borrows herg_ki's representations (noise_helpers.py:1640, 1657). n36 is registered in the noise run_all list (noise_helpers.py:128).

### R1 models: NO

Code: It fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. The list is config['models'], which is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of the five DOWNSTREAM_MODELS. rf and svm are added if missing. svm is dropped when there are more than 10,000 molecules. bindingdb_kd and kiba are subsampled to 30,000 pairs, so svm probably drops there; the molecule count was not printed. No knn and no ridge are fitted.

Decisions: bindingdb_kd: rf+dnn. kiba: dnn+rf. Both datasets also score xgboost and lightgbm, plus svm if under 10,000 molecules. herg_ic50 has no Step 1 row. herg_ki, whose representations it borrows, is approved for svm+dnn. On herg_ic50 the code also fits rf, xgboost and lightgbm.

Code: Nothing reads DECISIONS.md. bindingdb_kd and kiba are in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS, so the general searches use the fast grid. That grid is lightgbm_gain only, three allocation methods, representation counts 3 and all, and evaluators match/rf/lightgbm/dnn. It runs all 8 budgets from 10 to 2000 features. The start-up builds none, uncapped and capped. The general pool read asks for none and capped. The distance read uses 6 budgets (10-500), evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm and six models. herg_ic50 is not fast, so it gets the full engine defaults.

Decisions: bindingdb_kd: budgets 250-2000, all three importance methods, all five allocation methods, all four evaluators, counts 2 and all, no augmentation. kiba: budgets 250-2000, all three importance methods, its four stored allocation methods (no wglobal_power2), all four evaluators, count all only, no augmentation. Step 7 has no distance row for either; both are listed as distance searches not yet stored. On bindingdb_kd the code differs in five ways at once. It has four extra budgets (10, 25, 50, 100) and lacks deeplift and treeshap. It lacks softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2, adds count 3 and lacks count 2, and builds augmented searches. kiba differs in the same five ways. The only differences are that kiba lacks softmax_T1 alone among allocation methods and has count 3 as its only extra count. herg_ic50 has no decision to compare against.

The selection is made once for the whole dataset, not per fold.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: It never builds a per-fold search. A missing stored search goes through get_precomputed_search, which builds a whole-dataset search inside the job. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH=1, the default in submit_everything.sh, that build is refused when more than 500 configurations are missing. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that search. The distance searches are not built by noise run_all at start-up, and DECISIONS lists them as not stored for bindingdb_kd and kiba. So under the refusal those hybrid slots are reported missing. herg_ic50 has no precompute in any launcher. There the start-up search is refused too and stored as None. The pool then returns nothing, so no base representations and no hybrids are available.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself.

### Other problems

- The whole-dataset searches were run on measurement rows, so they saw every candidate's held-back second measurement. They also saw every measurement of every held-out molecule. The recipe and the two base representations were chosen with exactly the labels this experiment then hands out or grades on (n36:408-414, 454-456, 523-524; noise_helpers.py:1829-1840).
- herg_ic50 is the experiment's first-named dataset (n36:86). No launcher submits it, and DECISIONS.md has no row for it. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH on, its start-up search is refused. n36 would then run with no base representations and no hybrids.
- Step 7 says no distance search is stored for bindingdb_kd or kiba (DECISIONS.md:609, 750). n36 asks for the distance slot on both. That slot is either built on all rows inside the job or reported missing (_shared.py:7130-7137, 7171-7202).
- FoldSimilarity's docstring lists a similarity setting 'base_k_aug_uncapped' built from augmentation features (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:631-636). n36 uses FoldSimilarity for its neighbour rules (n36:562-569, 600). On bindingdb_kd and kiba, Step 8 cut augmentation. This build was not followed into similarity_space.py, so whether it runs on these two datasets was not determined.
- The hybrid is rebuilt per fold from a stored recipe. hybrid_for_fold first restricts to the recipe's representations (noise_helpers.py:1005-1009). If the recipe's rep_count is still below that number, build_fold_hybrid picks representations by blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores come from the whole-dataset search (_shared.py:5256-5286). Whether blueprint.reps already holds only rep_count representations was not determined.
- The noise run_all start-up searches use the pruning schedule from run_all's pruning_mode (noise_helpers.py:1838). get_precomputed_search, which builds missing searches, forces adaptive_pruning=False (_shared.py:5889). So a search built on a miss can differ from the start-up one on that axis.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The hybrids are rebuilt without their augmentation features. n36 builds each hybrid through n32.cached_hybrid (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:332-344), which passes no augmentations_train. noise_cache.cached_hybrid_for_fold defaults it to None (noise_cache.py:661). create_hybrid then skips augmentation whenever augmentations is None (hybrid.py:5984). build_fold_hybrid has no check for this (_shared.py:5091-5300). The general pool read on bindingdb_kd and kiba includes the capped search (_shared.py:6040-6046). So the stored recipe adds augmentation features, and the per-fold rebuild in n36 does not. Whether a capped recipe actually wins a slot on either dataset could not be determined without the stored results.
- One open item in the first audit is answered. The first audit could not say whether blueprint.reps holds only rep_count representations. It holds the full pool: Blueprint(reps=rep_names) with rep_names = list(base_reps.keys()) (find_best_hybrid.py:5388-5398). rep_scores is each representation's best score across models over every row the search ran on (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593). build_fold_hybrid uses those scores to pick which rep_count representations to keep (_shared.py:5262-5286). n36 passes no per-fold allocation scores. So on a recipe with count 3 (fast grid) or 2, which representations enter a fold's hybrid is decided by whole-dataset scores. Unverified: whether a blueprint loaded back from result_db carries rep_scores. If it does not, build_fold_hybrid raises, and n36 records 'the hybrid could not be built on this fold' (n36:550-553).
- Another open item in the first audit is answered. The augmented similarity spaces are built by default. With KIRBY_SIMILARITY_SETTINGS unset, enumerate_settings loops over every FEATURE_SPACES entry (similarity_space.py:219-228). FEATURE_SPACES contains base_1_aug_uncapped and base_2_aug_uncapped (similarity_space.py:117-127). n36 hands FoldSimilarity the augmentations (n36:486-488, 562-569). On bindingdb_kd and kiba, which carry augmentation representations (complexity_helpers.py:618, 637), n36 therefore builds augmented neighbour spaces per fold. Step 8 cut augmentation on both (DECISIONS.md:666, 685).
- The start-up search in noise run_all builds 'uncapped' on bindingdb_kd and kiba. precompute_hybrid_searches adds uncapped whenever augmentations exist, with no UNCAPPED_SKIP_DATASETS check (_shared.py:5541-5548). The pool reader skips uncapped on those two (_shared.py:6040-6043). So the start-up search builds a search that no reader asks for. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH that build is refused and stored as None.
- The disagreement rule fits LightGBM out-of-fold inside each training fold (n36:34-37, 578-581). LightGBM is not an approved model on bindingdb_kd or kiba. It only ranks candidates and is never scored, so R1 may not cover it. It is listed here for her to decide.


## noise n37 (tests/experiments/noise/n37_noise_budget.py)

What it measures: On clean labels, it estimates the label-noise variance in each feature space with the Gamma test. It divides that estimate by each model's held-out mean squared error. It adds a SIMEX sensitivity curve and residual tail statistics.

Datasets: All 41 datasets are queued for noise. n37 exits on any dataset whose task is not regression (n37_noise_budget.py:309-312). That leaves 26 regression datasets: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9 and suzuki. The 26 are the datasets whose DECISIONS.md Step 1 metric is rmse, spearman or ci. kiba and bindingdb_kd are registered as regression at dataset_policy.py:334-335. n37 is in the default noise list at noise_helpers.py:135. It is not in HONOURS_NOISE_CONDITION (noise_helpers.py:1586-1588), so it runs only in the job with no noise condition. On kiba and bindingdb_kd every fold is refused, because a fold has more than MAX_PAIR_ROWS=12000 training rows (n37:556-561, n35_near_duplicate_disagreement.py:170). The whole-dataset pool is still read for them first.

On those five, n37 lacks gp and fits four models the record does not approve. So on those five it differs in two ways at once.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: For each model it reads the hybrid recipes once, before the fold loop. They come from get_rule_hybrids with no fold index. That ranks every stored configuration by its mean over all folds of a search run on every row. The top two base representations come from that same whole-dataset search, by top_base_reps' default rule='whole_dataset'. Inside each fold only the features are refitted, on that fold's training rows. When a recipe uses fewer representations than the pool, build_fold_hybrid picks which ones from blueprint.rep_scores. Those are whole-dataset scores. So the choice of representations leaks as well.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. n37 makes one choice for the whole dataset, with every held-out molecule's rows inside the search that ranked it.

### R3 same cuts: NO (partly)

Code: Every search n37 reads uses one global grid for all datasets. General search: budgets 10 to 2000 (8 budgets). Distance search: budgets 10 to 500, evaluators knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm, models the five plus knn. The engine defaults set allocation (5 methods), importance (deeplift, lightgbm_gain, treeshap), evaluators (match, rf, lightgbm, dnn) and representation counts (2, 3, 5, all). Exception: the fast list in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS gives 3 allocation methods, lightgbm_gain only and counts 3 and all. When n37 ranks recipes it takes every stored row for the model, with budget=None. So no budget, importance, allocation, evaluator or representation-count cut is applied when the recipe is chosen.

Decisions: Steps 2-7 cut each axis per dataset, and the cuts differ between datasets. All 26 regression datasets break R3. On the general search, all 26 have budgets Step 2 cuts. For example, adme_hlm keeps 500-2000 and the general search runs 10-2000. On the distance search, all 26 have budgets Step 7 cuts. Examples: herg_ki keeps 100-500 and abcov_kd keeps 25-500. Importance methods Step 3 cuts are run on abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco and herg_ki (deeplift), on buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer (lightgbm_gain), and on bh_doyle_plates (treeshap). Allocation methods Step 4 cuts are run on caco2, ginkgo_acsins and herg_ki (wglobal_power2) and on ddg_combined (power_2, wglobal_power2). On suzuki, the allocation decision is HELD and all five methods run. flab_expression_koenig, bindingdb_kd and kiba are fast in the code and full in the record. The code gives them lightgbm_gain only, where the record keeps all three importance methods. abagym_EGFR (rf), abagym_VEGF (rf, lightgbm, dnn), buchwald_hartwig (dnn), ginkgo_colloidal (dnn) and ginkgo_titer (lightgbm) keep evaluators Step 5 cut. Counts Step 6 cut are run on 14 of the 26.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: Each model gets its top 2 base representations, which matches. On hybrids, it reads the general and distance searches for two search families. The predictive family chooses features for predicting the label. The similarity family chooses features so that each molecule's activity is predicted from its five nearest neighbours. Each family gives 2 general hybrids and 1 distance hybrid per model. That is up to six hybrid spaces per model: hybrid, hybrid__general2, hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1. If the rule read fails, it falls back to one winner per family. All of this is chosen once for the whole dataset, not per fold.

Decisions: Per model, per fold: 2 best base representations and 2 best hybrids. n37 has 2 base representations, which matches. It has up to 6 hybrids instead of 2, and the choice is made once, not per fold. So it differs in two ways at once. The study is a diagnostic, but nothing in the file says the six-hybrid set was chosen on purpose.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: n37 builds no per-fold search. A missing pool search goes through get_precomputed_search. That builds one find_best_hybrid search on all rows of the dataset. With KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH set, a search with more than 500 configurations left is refused with RuntimeError. _iter_pool_searches then prints a warning and skips that search. A model with no recipe gets no hybrid space, and a reason is written to hybrid_unavailable_by_model. A model with no stored search gets no base representations (base_reps_missing). Noise run_all builds no distance search at start-up, so the distance read always goes to disk, a whole-dataset build, or a refusal.

Decisions: Build the needed per-fold search inside the experiment. n37 instead builds a whole-dataset search, or refuses and skips with a warning.

### Other problems

- Recipes can come from an augmented pool search (uncapped or capped), but n37 rebuilds every recipe with no augmentation features passed. cached_hybrid hands none to noise_cache.cached_hybrid_for_fold (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:340-344). That function forwards None (noise_cache.py:720-723). hybrid_for_fold's docstring says such a recipe then builds a narrower feature space than the one the search chose (noise_helpers.py:982-985). I did not open create_hybrid, so I could not determine whether that build raises or drops the augmentation block.
- Step 8 cuts augmentation on 20 of the 22 regression datasets that carry augmentation representations. abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF and abcov_kd carry none (checked with a DATASET_REPS import this session). n37 still lets uncapped and capped searches compete for every recipe slot. On ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic it also admits capped, which Step 8 does not keep.
- The similarity sweep inside the Gamma test (_sim_gamma, n37:519-540) can compute distances in base_k_aug_uncapped spaces. FoldSimilarity builds those from a fixed uncapped augmentation recipe on every dataset with augmentation representations (n32:686-717, similarity_space.py:113-121). This is augmentation outside Step 8. DECISIONS.md:654 lists this exact space as an open check.
- kiba and bindingdb_kd compute nothing: every fold has more than 12,000 training rows and is refused (n37:556-561; n35:170). The pool reads and any whole-dataset search build before the fold loop still run.
- gamma_reference_rep is the rank-1 single representation of the first downstream model that has one, which is rf under the default order. The noise estimate, the check and SIMEX all read it. The file says the owner has not signed this choice off (n37:84-88, 450-461).
- If the rule read raises, it prints a line and continues (noise_helpers.py:1423-1428). The model then gets one recipe per family from get_best_search_for_downstream, not the rule's set. The result file does not say which of the two happened, apart from the slot field being absent.
- The module docstring says each model's recipe is read from the precomputed pool, and each fold rebuilds the hybrid from that fold's training labels (n37:76-78). The code matches that, but the docstring does not say that the recipe and the base representations were chosen on all rows. get_best_search_for_downstream records that in its metadata (selection_scope 'whole_dataset', _shared.py:6430). n37 does not copy that field into its results (n37:465-480).

## noise n38 (tests/experiments/noise/n38_noise_relative_to_model_error.py)

What it measures: It injects label noise sized in units of lightgbm's out-of-fold residual SD on each fold's training labels, on real and semi-synthetic labels. It then measures how well the corrupted molecules are found and how much each cleaning method recovers on held-out molecules.

Datasets: It runs on regression datasets only. run() and _run_one_condition return a skip for any other task type (n38:337-338, 362-365). Noise jobs are queued on all 41 datasets (shared map, submit_everything.sh). n38 is listed in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (noise_helpers.py:136). It is not in HONOURS_NOISE_CONDITION (noise_helpers.py:1590-1592), so it runs only in the noise job that names no condition. should_skip_experiment does not name n38 (_shared.py:3672-3685). I printed the dataset registry's task types this session. 26 of the 41 are regression, so n38 runs on these: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. The other 15 get a skip record. The hetero_seen condition is also skipped on any dataset that loads no SMILES (n38:370-374).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: Downstream models are config['models'] with rf and svm appended if missing. Under noise run_all that is DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, the five models rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm, on every dataset. gp is never in the list. Other fits are part of the method itself: lightgbm sizes the noise and builds the semi-synthetic labels. lightgbm out-of-fold predictions drive detection, winsorising and ITLM. NGBoost gives the inverse-variance weights. robust_loss fits loss-swapped lightgbm, xgboost, dnn and rf. ridge and knn are never fitted.

Decisions: Only the dataset's two approved models from Step 1. On all 26 regression datasets n38 fits three models outside the approved pair. On five of them an approved model is missing: gp is approved on abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn) and ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn), and n38 never fits gp. So on those five datasets the model list differs in two ways at once: three extra models, and one approved model absent.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: n38 runs no search of its own. It reads the recipes once per run, before the fold loop. The reads are get_best_search_for_downstream, plus get_rule_hybrids through pool_recipe_per_downstream_model. get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index, so it ranks each configuration on its mean over all folds of a whole-dataset search. Those searches were built on every row: noise run_all builds them with precompute_hybrid_searches on data['labels'], unsliced. The two base representations come from the same whole-dataset search. Each fold then refits the hybrid's features on that fold's corrupted training labels. The choice of recipe and of base representations stays whole-dataset.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search on that fold's training rows only. Here the recipe and the two base representations were picked with every fold's held-out molecules in view. The result metadata says the same: selection_scope 'whole_dataset', recipe chosen on all rows, only the features refit.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: n38 reads the stored searches with no per-dataset cut, and nothing in the read filters configurations. General searches carry 8 budgets, 10 to 2000 features. Importance, allocation, evaluators and representation counts are the engine defaults, or the fast lists on the 14 datasets in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS. Distance searches carry 6 budgets, 10 to 500 features. Their evaluators are knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm and svm, and their models are the five plus knn. budget=None ranks over every stored budget. Augmentation members are 'none', 'uncapped' and 'capped' whenever the dataset has augmentation representations. On kiba and bindingdb_kd there is no 'uncapped'. On the distance searches 'capped' is read only under 10,000 rows.

Decisions: Steps 2-7 decide budgets, importance, allocation, evaluators and representation counts per dataset, for the general and the distance searches. Step 8 cuts augmentation everywhere except uncapped on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, distance search. All 26 regression datasets break the budget rule: each has a general budget outside its decided range. Importance, general search, by the shared map's comparison, which I re-checked against Step 3. A cut method is still read on abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer and herg_ki. Kept methods are missing on flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd: code runs them fast, lightgbm_gain only. Allocation: a cut method is read on caco2, ddg_combined, ginkgo_acsins and herg_ki, and suzuki is held. Evaluators, general: abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_titer. Representation counts, general: cut counts are read on 16 regression datasets, including herg_ki, caco2 and the adme sets. Augmentation: per the shared map, 22 regression datasets carry augmentation representations. 20 of them get uncapped and capped members the record cuts, and the other two get capped, which is also cut.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each of the five models it takes the top 2 base representations from noise_base_reps_by_model. Hybrids come from the rule set with pool_subset 'predictive_and_similarity'. Per family that is 2 general hybrids and 1 distance hybrid, and there are two families, features chosen for prediction and features chosen under objective='similarity'. That is up to 6 hybrid spaces per model: hybrid, hybrid__general2, hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1. The selection is one set for the whole run, not one per fold. n38 ignores the rule's own base ranking (get_rule_hybrids 'base_reps'). It ranks base representations inside the one stored search that held the best predictive hybrid instead.

Decisions: Per approved model, per fold: 2 best base representations and 2 best hybrids. Base: the count matches (2), but the ranking is whole-dataset and not per fold. Hybrids: up to 6 per model, not 2, chosen once rather than per fold. Models: five, not the approved two. Nothing in n38's design needs the extra hybrids. The two families and the distance slot come from get_rule_hybrids' fixed rule (2026-10-02 comment).

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n38 never builds a per-fold search. A missing whole-dataset search goes to get_precomputed_search, which runs find_best_hybrid on all rows. noise run_all does not build the distance searches, so every distance read either comes from disk or is cold-built over all rows. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, the default in submit_everything.sh per the shared map, a missing search with more than 500 configurations raises. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that member. get_rule_hybrids then prints the missing slots, and n38 records the space as unavailable. With no recipe at all, n38 runs the single representations only. If no model has a base representation, resid_sd_rep is None and every fold records an error with no noise injected.

Decisions: A needed per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n38 builds none per fold. Its fallback builds whole-dataset searches, or skips with a warning under the refusal setting.

### Other problems

- Hybrids are rebuilt per fold with no augmentation blocks. n32.cached_hybrid passes none to cached_hybrid_for_fold (n32:332-344), and n38's call passes none (n38:651-654). Yet the pool reads uncapped and capped searches (_shared.py:6040-6046). hybrid_for_fold's own docstring says a recipe that names an augmentation strategy then rebuilds a narrower feature space than the one the search chose (noise_helpers.py:982-985). So a winning augmented recipe and the features n38 builds for it differ.
- Two different rankings pick base representations. get_rule_hybrids ranks the top 2 over the whole general pool (_shared.py:7183-7194), and n38 discards that list. noise_base_reps_by_model ranks inside the single stored search that held the best predictive hybrid (n38:491-494, _shared.py:4909-4925). They can name different representations.
- resid_sd_rep, the one representation used to size the noise and build the semi-synthetic labels, is the rank-1 representation of the first model in the list (n38:502-504). That model is rf (_shared.py:565). rf is not an approved model on 21 of the 26 regression datasets (DECISIONS.md:11-47). The docstring says the owner has not signed this choice off (n38:127-131).
- With a whole-dataset recipe, build_fold_hybrid may pick WHICH representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores, which are whole-dataset scores (_shared.py:5256-5286). hybrid_for_fold first cuts the pool to the recipe's representations (noise_helpers.py:1005-1009). Could not determine whether that cut already removes the leak, because I did not open a stored blueprint to see whether bp.reps holds only rep_count representations.
- KIRBY_POOL_SUBSET overrides n38's 'predictive_and_similarity' whenever it is set (_shared.py:5955). A run with it set reads a different set of families than the file names.
- The similarity family is read on every regression dataset. Whether a similarity-objective distance search is stored for any of them could not be determined; I did not look on disk or on the server.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- The first agent left one question open: does the per-fold rebuild choose which representations to keep from whole-dataset scores? It does. A stored recipe's reps field is the whole pool, because find_best_hybrid builds the recipe from base_reps.keys() and applies the representation-count cut only inside each fold (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:4902, 4963-4983, 5388-5398). Its rep_scores are each representation's best score over every row (find_best_hybrid.py:9563-9593). n38 passes no per-fold allocation scores (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:332-344). So build_fold_hybrid keeps the top rep_count representations by those whole-dataset scores (_shared.py:5257-5286). That is a whole-dataset choice inside each fold, under R2.
- The rebuild and the search rank representations for the count cut by two different scores. The search uses that fold's allocation score per representation (find_best_hybrid.py:4969-4981). The rebuild uses each representation's best whole-dataset score across all models (find_best_hybrid.py:9573-9580). So for a recipe with a representation count, the rebuilt features can come from a different set of representations than the configuration that won.
- n38's own docstring says one hybrid per family (n38_noise_relative_to_model_error.py:121-124). The code builds every slot of the rule set, up to 3 per family and 6 per model (_shared.py:6504-6535). The docstring and the code disagree on the number of hybrid spaces.
- When noise run_all builds the general searches, it passes an adaptive pruning schedule (noise_helpers.py:1837-1838). The fallback reader instead calls find_best_hybrid with adaptive_pruning=False (_shared.py:5883). Whether these two calls file the same stored search could not be determined; I did not trace how the schedule enters the stored search's identity.


## noise n39 (tests/experiments/noise/n39_correlated_sources.py)

What it measures: It simulates several sources measuring each molecule, with correlated errors and a fixed offset per source. It then measures whether removing the offsets or weighting molecules by their label variance recovers accuracy, compared with the plain mean of the sources.

Datasets: n39 is a noise experiment. submit_everything.sh queues the noise category on 41 datasets: every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213). n39 is not in HONOURS_NOISE_CONDITION (noise_helpers.py:1584-1586). So it runs only in the noise job with no noise condition (noise_helpers.py:1755-1781, 2032-2043). n39 returns a skip on any dataset that is not regression (n39_correlated_sources.py:503-506). By the metric column of DECISIONS Step 1, 26 of the 41 are regression: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. I inferred this from the metric column; I did not load each dataset's task_type. herg_ic50 is named in the docstring (lines 22-27, 116, 145) and is not one of the 41. It runs only when launched by hand with --dataset.

### R1 models: NO

Code: n39 fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every regression dataset. run_all passes config['models'] = DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of those five. downstream_model_list adds rf and svm, which are already there. gp is never added, because n39 never calls _apply_small_dataset_models. ridge and knn are never fitted.

Decisions: Two models per dataset (Step 1). All 26 regression datasets get three models outside their pair. On five datasets an approved model is missing, because the pair includes gp: abagym_Ang2 (gp+svm), abagym_VEGF (gp+svm), ginkgo_acsins (lightgbm+gp), ginkgo_hic (gp+dnn), ginkgo_pr_cho (gp+dnn). On those five, n39 fits only one of the two approved models. No ridge and no knn agrees with the rules.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: The hybrid recipes come from get_rule_hybrids, called with no fold index. It ranks every stored configuration by its mean over all folds of a search that ran over every row of the dataset. The two base representations come from top_base_reps with rule='whole_dataset' on that same kind of search. Both are picked once for the whole dataset, before the fold loop. Each fold then refits the chosen recipe's features on its own training rows, using clean labels. Only the features are refit; which recipe and which representations are used was decided with every fold's molecules in view.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. A whole-dataset search does not comply.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: n39 runs no search of its own. It reads stored searches with budget=None, so every stored configuration at every budget competes for the top 2. Nothing in the read removes a budget, importance method, allocation method, internal evaluator or representation count. If a search is missing, get_precomputed_search builds it with all 8 budgets and the engine's default lists, or the fast lists on 14 datasets. The distance read uses the same 6 budgets, 5 evaluators and 6 models on every dataset. Augmentation: whenever the dataset carries augmentation representations, it reads the none, uncapped and capped searches, on both general and distance.

Decisions: Each dataset's Step 2-7 cuts and Step 8 augmentation rule. Every one of the 26 regression datasets has a budget cut in Step 2, so all 26 break the budget rule. Step 8 cuts augmentation everywhere except ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, which keep uncapped only, on the distance search. 22 of the 26 regression datasets carry augmentation representations. abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF and abcov_kd carry none, according to the shared helper map; I did not re-count. So 20 datasets read augmented searches that Step 8 cuts. ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic also read capped, plus uncapped on the general search. On the fast tier: qm9 matches. logd, flab_expression_koenig, bindingdb_kd and kiba are fast in the code and not in the record, which matters only if a missing search is built here.

### R4 standard selection: NO

Code: For each of 5 models, n39 uses 2 base representations and up to 6 hybrids. The 6 hybrids are the top 2 from the general searches and the top 1 from the distance searches, for each of two search families. One family chose features for prediction. The other chose them so that each molecule's activity is predicted by its five nearest neighbours. All of these are chosen once for the whole dataset, not per fold. The base representations come from one search's baselines, not from the rule's own base list.

Decisions: For each of the dataset's two models, per fold: the 2 best base representations and the 2 best hybrids. n39 differs in three ways at once: five models instead of two, up to six hybrids instead of two, and one choice for the whole dataset instead of one per fold.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n39 never builds a per-fold search. A missing stored search goes through get_precomputed_search, which builds it on every row of the dataset inside the job. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, a search with more than 500 configurations left is refused with RuntimeError. _iter_pool_searches catches that, prints a warning and skips that search. A model with no recipe gets no hybrid space, and n39 prints 'no hybrid recipe; single representations only'. Noise run_all builds no distance search at start-up. So every distance hybrid slot depends on a search stored by a separate precompute, or on a whole-dataset build or refusal here.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself, on that fold's training rows. n39 instead builds a whole-dataset search or skips the hybrid with a warning.

### Other problems

- A recipe chosen under uncapped or capped augmentation is rebuilt without its donor features. n39 calls cached_hybrid, which passes no augmentations_train to hybrid_for_fold (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:332-344; n39_correlated_sources.py:716-718). create_hybrid then skips augmentation entirely (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5984). So the fold's features differ from the configuration that won the ranking. The scores are still filed under that configuration's name.
- On datasets that keep repeat measurements (herg_ic50, bindingdb_kd), the stored search is read with the per-measurement rows (n39_correlated_sources.py:625). The folds are split per molecule (lines 541-545, 620-621). So the search's own folds and n39's folds are different partitions of different rows.
- n39 takes its base representations from noise_base_reps_by_model on one search. It ignores the base list that get_rule_hybrids returns beside the hybrids (_shared.py:7183-7194; n39_correlated_sources.py:658-660). The two rankings read different scores: one search's mean against the best over every pool member. They can name different representations.
- When a recipe has a representation count below the number of representations passed, build_fold_hybrid picks which representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5286). Those scores come from the whole-dataset search. hybrid_for_fold first cuts the pool to blueprint.reps (noise_helpers.py:1005-1012). Could not determine whether blueprint.reps already holds only the kept representations, so whether this cut runs here is undetermined.
- The docstring says 'All five downstream models' (n39_correlated_sources.py:62). That matches the code and contradicts Step 1's two models per dataset.
- By design, every hybrid is built from the clean training labels and shared by all arms (hybrid_labels='clean', lines 132-141, 748-753). The injected noise never reaches feature choice. The file states this.
- noise_helpers.py:1414-1417 reads the rule set only when the lookup is a functools.partial over the real get_best_search_for_downstream. n39 passes exactly that (lines 624-628), so the six-hybrid set applies here.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- herg_ic50 has no row anywhere in DECISIONS.md (grep count 0), but n39 is written to run on it (n39_correlated_sources.py:22-24, 116, 200). So its two approved models, its budget range and its other cuts are undefined. n39 runs it on the same five models and full stored grid as every other dataset.
- n39 also fits LightGBM on every dataset, apart from the downstream models, to make the out-of-fold predictions its weight estimates use (noise_cache.py:406-409, via oof_fn at n39_correlated_sources.py:730-734). On datasets whose approved pair has no lightgbm, this is a model outside the pair. It is part of the method by design, not a downstream model; whether R1 covers it is hers to say.
- Run standalone through main(), n39 loads through load_data (n39_correlated_sources.py:1103), which sets augmentations=None for every molecular dataset (_shared.py:4725). Run through noise run_all, it gets augmentation representations from load_noise_data (noise_helpers.py:1680-1698). The same dataset therefore reads only augmentation 'none' searches in one path and none, uncapped and capped searches in the other.
- Under the cold-search check, a search with half or more of its configurations stored proceeds and scores the rest on every row of the dataset inside the job (find_best_hybrid.py:690-695). That is a third whole-dataset build path besides the at-most-500 branch and the refusal.


## noise n40 (tests/experiments/noise/n40_model_side_regularisation.py)

What it measures: Under injected label noise, it measures whether changing the model helps: retuned settings, seed averaging, stacking, Gaussian-process noise terms and kNN neighbour counts, each paired against the same model at default settings.

Datasets: Regression datasets only. n40.run returns a skip for any other task type (n40:543-547, again at 567-568). The noise suite is queued on all 41 roster datasets (submit_everything.sh:95, 207-213), and n40 is in the noise default list (noise_helpers.py:138). A registry print this session gives 26 regression datasets: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, abcov_kd, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, qm9, suzuki. The other 15 write a skip. Folds: config n_splits = 5 from the noise runner (noise_helpers.py:1746), split by cv_split (n40:666-667). Conditions default to gaussian and dense_oofmse (n40:166), three injection draws (n40:170).

### R1 models: NO

Code: It fits five downstream models on every regression dataset: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. The list comes from config['models'] or DOWNSTREAM_MODELS, with rf and svm appended if missing. Each model gets its own base representations and hybrids. On top of that, extra arms run only in lightgbm's feature matrices: a non-negative stack of all models, several Gaussian-process arms (when a fold has 1,000 or fewer training molecules), lightgbm plus a Gaussian process on its residuals, and three kNN arms. Ridge is not used.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two approved models (Step 1). knn only where Step 9 allows it; ridge never.

### R6 missing search: NO

Code: n40 never builds a per-fold search. A missing stored search is built on all rows by get_precomputed_search. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, a search with more than 500 configurations left is refused. The pool loop prints a warning and skips that member. A failed rule read is printed and the slots are reported missing. A model with no recipe gets no hybrid spaces and runs on its base representations only. submit_everything.sh turns the refusal on by default.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself; no refusal or skip.

### Other problems

- R1 per dataset. Every one of the 26 regression datasets gets three models beyond its approved pair, since n40 always fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm. Example: herg_ki is approved for svm+dnn, and n40 also fits rf, xgboost and lightgbm.
- R1, gp. gp is approved on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho. n40 never runs gp as a downstream model with its own base representations and hybrids. gp only appears as extra arms inside lightgbm's matrices (n40:1111-1121). So on those five datasets one approved model has no comparison at all.
- R1, gp elsewhere. The Gaussian-process arms run on any fold with 1,000 or fewer training molecules (n40:1113). That includes datasets where gp is not approved, such as abagym_EGFR, ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_titer.
- Host model. The GP, kNN and kriging arms run only in lightgbm's feature matrices (n40:236, 590, 883-885, 982-985). lightgbm is in the approved pair on only five of the 26 regression datasets: abcov_kd, buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_acsins, qm9 and suzuki. On the other 21, those arms sit in the features chosen for a model the record excludes.
- knn. n40 fits kNN arms directly on every regression dataset (n40:1035-1108). Step 9 marks all 26 regression datasets 'run' for knn, but it decides knn as a downstream model in the distance search. Step 9 does not address knn fitted as an experiment arm.
- R3, budgets. Step 2 cuts at least one general budget on all 26 regression datasets, and n40's read ranks all eight. On the distance read it ranks all six budgets from 10 to 500. Step 7 narrows that on every regression dataset; for example suzuki is 50-250 and abagym_Ang2 is 25-100.
- R3, importance, general search. These have a decided cut that the defaults still run. deeplift: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, herg_ki. treeshap: bh_doyle_plates. lightgbm_gain: buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer.
- R3, importance, flab_expression_adams. deeplift was never stored there, and the full default adds it.
- R3, importance, missing methods. The code runs bindingdb_kd, flab_expression_koenig and kiba on the fast list, which has lightgbm_gain only. The record keeps all three importance methods on those datasets (dataset_policy speed printed this session; DECISIONS.md:313, 321, 332).
- R3, allocation. The default still runs methods Step 4 cut: wglobal_power2 on caco2, ginkgo_acsins and herg_ki, and power_2 plus wglobal_power2 on ddg_combined. On suzuki the decision is held, and the default runs all five. The fast list lacks softmax_T1 on flab_expression_koenig and kiba, and lacks softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2 on bindingdb_kd.
- R3, evaluators. The general default of match/rf/lightgbm/dnn includes evaluators Step 5 cut: rf on abagym_EGFR, rf/lightgbm/dnn on abagym_VEGF, dnn on buchwald_hartwig and ginkgo_colloidal, lightgbm on ginkgo_titer.
- R3, representation counts. The defaults include counts Step 6 cut on abagym_Ang2, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, buchwald_hartwig, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho and herg_ki. On bindingdb_kd, flab_expression_koenig and kiba, the fast list contains the cut count 3. bindingdb_kd also lacks its kept count 2.
- R3, distance read. bindingdb_kd and kiba have no distance rows in the record (DECISIONS.md:609), yet n40 still asks for a distance hybrid there.
- Step 8, augmentation. 22 of the 26 regression datasets carry augmentation representations (all but the three abagym_* and abcov_kd; printed this session). On all 22, n40 reads uncapped and capped searches, and its neighbour sweep builds base_1_aug_uncapped and base_2_aug_uncapped spaces. Step 8 cuts augmentation on 20 of those 22. It keeps uncapped only on ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic, on the distance search. DECISIONS.md:654 names exactly this kind of space as an open check.
- Clean labels choose the recipe. n40 does not pass label_noise to the pool read (n40:670-674). So every recipe was chosen on the clean labels of all rows, including the held-out ones. get_best_search_for_downstream's docstring says a noise-injecting experiment should pass it (_shared.py:6155-6159).
- Two rankings of base representations. n40 ranks the two base representations from the one search get_best_search_for_downstream returned (n40:703-705). The rule read ranks its own base representations across every augmentation member (_shared.py:7183-7185), and n40 ignores that list. The two lists can name different representations.
- Unsigned choice. The representation the relative-noise unit is measured in is the rank-1 base representation of the first model that has one (n40:713-722). The file says this was never signed off (n40:97-99).
- Uncapped mismatch on bindingdb_kd and kiba. The start-up general search builds uncapped there (_shared.py:5543-5548 has no exception). The pool read never asks for it (_shared.py:5989, 6041-6043). So the start-up pays for a search n40 does not read.
- Could not determine: whether the folds n40 splits into (cv_split, n40:666-667) are the same molecules as the stored search's folds. It does not matter for n40 as written, because it ranks over all folds anyway.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- Augmented recipes are rebuilt without their augmentation features. The pool may pick a recipe from the uncapped or capped search (_shared.py:6014-6046). n40 rebuilds it per fold through cached_hybrid (n40:849-853), which passes no augmentations (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:332-344). noise_cache.cached_hybrid_for_fold defaults augmentations_train=None (noise_cache.py:658-661). create_hybrid then skips augmentation entirely (src/kirby/hybrid.py:5984, 6403). So the recipe searched with augmentation features and the matrix n40 fits differ: one has them, the other is base features only. Nothing raises, and the space keeps the recipe's name.
- The neighbour sweep and the model arms use different hybrid sets. The model arms use up to six hybrid spaces per model (_shared.py:6508-6535). The sweep's hybrid spaces are only hybrid, hybrid__general2 and hybrid_similarity (similarity_space.py:126). So hybrid__distance1, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1 get model arms but no sweep rows.
- The Step 7 cuts other than budgets are also not applied on the distance read. The distance read sets only evaluators, budgets and models (_shared.py:6780-6783). Importance, allocation and representation counts fall back to engine defaults (find_best_hybrid.py:8650-8669). Step 7 cuts importance, allocation, evaluator or count on most regression datasets, for example herg_ki deeplift, wglobal_power2 and counts 2/3/5 (DECISIONS.md:637). The audit named only the distance budgets.
- The noise start-up config names allocation, importance and evaluator lists (noise_helpers.py:1745-1751), but precompute_hybrid_searches does not read config for them (_shared.py:5574-5596). Changing those config entries would not change the start-up search. This matters if someone tries to apply the decided cuts through config.
- Minor wording: 'Step 7 narrows the distance budgets on every regression dataset' holds for the 24 regression datasets with distance rows. bindingdb_kd and kiba have no Step 7 row (DECISIONS.md:609).


## noise n41 (tests/experiments/noise/n41_conformal_fdr_detection.py)

What it measures: Under injected label noise, it flags suspect training molecules with conformal p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg, grades five detectors against the injection mask, then winsorises or removes the flagged molecules and scores each downstream model on untouched held-out labels.

Datasets: The noise run_all runs n41 on every dataset in the submit roster. That roster is DATASET_REPS minus chembl_qsar and davis, 41 datasets (submit_everything.sh:207-213). n41 is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (noise_helpers.py:139). It is not in either skip list (_shared.py:3672-3675, 3684-3685). n41 itself returns a 'not_regression' skip on classification datasets (n41:524-525, 550-553). A tiny registry import this session gave 26 regression datasets, which are the ones it runs on: herg_ki, caco2, logd, qm9, adme_hlm, adme_rlm, adme_mdr1, flab_thermo_tresanco, abcov_kd, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_expression_koenig, flab_expression_adams, abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, suzuki, buchwald_hartwig, bh_doyle_plates, kiba, bindingdb_kd. The other 15 write a skip. The docstring's herg_ic50 example (n41:118) is not in the 41-dataset roster.

### R1 models: NO

Code: It fits rf, xgboost, svm, dnn and lightgbm on every dataset. downstream_model_list takes config['models'], which noise run_all sets to DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE, a copy of those five. It then appends rf and svm if they are missing. gp is never added, because nothing on this path calls _apply_small_dataset_models. svm drops out above 10,000 rows. Separately, every detector score is built from LightGBM out-of-fold predictions on every dataset.

Decisions: Two models per dataset (Step 1). knn is not a downstream model here, and ridge is excluded.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: It picks one set of hybrids for the whole dataset and reuses it on every fold. pool_recipe_per_downstream_model calls get_rule_hybrids with no fold index. That ranks every configuration by its mean over all folds of whole-dataset searches. The two base representations come from top_base_reps with rule='whole_dataset' on the same stored search. Only the features are refit, per fold, on that fold's noisy training labels. When a recipe has a representation count below 10, build_fold_hybrid chooses which representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores. Those scores come from the whole-dataset search.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only.

### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: No per-dataset cut is applied anywhere. The general read ranks every stored configuration at every budget, because budget=None. The start-up search runs FULL_BUDGETS, which is 8 budgets from 10 to 2000 features. It uses the engine's default axes, or the fast lists on the code's fast datasets. Among the 26 datasets n41 runs on, those are logd, qm9, flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd (printed this session). The distance read asks for DISTANCE_BUDGETS (10 to 500 features), DISTANCE_EVALUATORS (knn, rf, dnn, lightgbm, svm) and DISTANCE_MODELS on every dataset. Augmentation: it asks for none, uncapped and capped wherever augmentation representations exist (22 of the 26 datasets). kiba and bindingdb_kd get none and capped only. Where n41's settings differ from Steps 2-8: (1) Budgets: all 26 datasets have general budgets Step 2 cut. 24 have distance budgets Step 7 cut; kiba and bindingdb_kd have no distance decision. (2) Importance, the method is searched but Step 3 cut it: abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, ddg_combined, flab_binding_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco and herg_ki (deeplift); buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_pr_cho and ginkgo_titer (lightgbm_gain); bh_doyle_plates (treeshap). flab_expression_adams also gets deeplift, which was never stored for it. (3) Importance, the method is kept by Step 3 but missing from n41's fast grid: flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd lack deeplift and treeshap. (4) Allocation, searched but cut: caco2, ginkgo_acsins and herg_ki (wglobal_power2); ddg_combined (power_2 and wglobal_power2). suzuki is HELD but all five methods run. (5) Allocation, kept but missing: flab_expression_koenig and kiba lack softmax_T1; bindingdb_kd lacks softmax_T1 and wglobal_power2. (6) Internal evaluators, searched but cut: abagym_EGFR (rf), abagym_VEGF (rf, lightgbm and dnn), buchwald_hartwig and ginkgo_colloidal (dnn), ginkgo_titer (lightgbm). (7) Representation counts, searched but cut: abagym_Ang2, ddg_combined and ginkgo_colloidal (2); ginkgo_acsins and ginkgo_pr_cho (3); adme_hlm and ginkgo_hic (2 and 3); adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, caco2 and herg_ki (2, 3 and 5); flab_binding_koenig (3 and 5); buchwald_hartwig (3, 5 and all). flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd get count 3, which Step 6 cut. bindingdb_kd also lacks count 2. (8) Augmentation: Step 8 cuts it on 20 of the 22 datasets that carry it. ginkgo_colloidal and ginkgo_hic keep uncapped on the distance search only, yet capped is read for both as well. (9) Distance evaluators include the ones Step 7 cut, on abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, ddg_combined, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_titer and qm9. Which configurations the stored rows actually hold could not be determined without the server result databases.

Decisions: Every search the experiment reads uses the dataset's Step 2-7 budgets, importance methods, allocation methods, evaluators and representation counts, plus augmentation per Step 8.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: n41 never builds a per-fold search. Noise run_all builds the general search and the general search under objective='similarity', both on all rows. It builds no distance search. So the distance read goes to get_precomputed_search, which either cold-builds a whole-dataset search inside the job or is refused under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH. That variable is on by default in submit_everything.sh. A refusal happens when more than 500 configurations are missing. The refused member is skipped with a printed warning. The rule then lists the slot as missing. A model with no recipe gets no hybrid space, and the run continues on base representations only.

Decisions: Where a needed per-fold search does not exist, the experiment builds it itself.

### Other problems

- The hybrid build passes no augmentation blocks. cached_hybrid forwards none (n32:338-344), so build_fold_hybrid gets augmentations_train=None (noise_cache.py:719-724; _shared.py:5295). A recipe that won under 'uncapped' or 'capped' is rebuilt with the blueprint's augmentation strategy but no donor matrices. create_hybrid splits augmentations only when they are not None (hybrid.py:5983). I did not trace whether the rebuilt matrix then lacks the donor features.
- The detection-only feature spaces in n41's LOF sweep include base_k_aug_uncapped (n32:631-639, 686-717). That is a fixed uncapped augmentation build, not a search. It runs on every dataset that carries augmentation representations. Step 8 lists this exact space as an open check (DECISIONS.md:654).
- The representation that sets the noise size for the relative noise conditions is resid_sd_rep. It is the first model's rank-1 base representation, which comes from the whole-dataset ranking. The docstring says the owner has not signed this choice off (n41:106-111, 703-712).
- Run directly through main() (n41:1195-1221), the data carries no data['precomputed_searches']. So even the predictive general search is read from disk or cold-built on all rows (_shared.py:5845-5896).
- Base representations come from the one stored search that won the pool for that model (n41:693-695). The hybrids come from a separate rule read across all pool conditions (noise_helpers.py:1414-1422). So base and hybrid slots for one model can be ranked on different stored searches. I verified that these are two separate reads. I did not check whether they ever pick different searches.
- The five-model list is built in two places. The submit path builds it as noise run_all's config['models'] (noise_helpers.py:1751). A direct run builds it as get_config's models (n41:1195). Neither path reads Step 1.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R6: the general search can be refused too, not just the distance search. Tier 'general' is in _PRECOMPUTE_TIER_ROOTS (src/kirby/find_best_hybrid.py:598). noise run_all's start-up precompute catches a refusal and stores None (tests/experiments/_shared.py:5618-5626). The read then retries cold, is refused again and skips with a warning (tests/experiments/_shared.py:6107-6114).
- R1: the five Step 1 pairs that include gp (abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho; DECISIONS.md:11,13,30,32,33) are all regression, so n41 runs on them. It never fits gp on any of them (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:263-276 adds only rf and svm).
- R4/R5: the similarity spaces n41 builds for its LOF sweep, through FoldSimilarity, use only hybrid, hybrid__general2 and hybrid_similarity (n32_iterative_and_dual_selection.py:640-645). The model-input spaces carry six hybrid slots. So the LOF sweep and the model-input detectors see different hybrid sets.
- The n41 docstring says 'Then one hybrid per family of stored search' (n41_conformal_fdr_detection.py:102-104). The code builds up to three per family, so the docstring describes a set of spaces that does not run.
- Direct run through main() calls load_data, not load_noise_data (n41_conformal_fdr_detection.py:1198). Whether that data dict carries 'augmentations' could not be determined without reading load_data. If it does not, the pool read on a direct run uses augmentation 'none' only (_shared.py:6040-6046), unlike the submit path.


## noise n42 (tests/experiments/noise/n42_similarity_noise_sweep.py)

What it measures: For every noise condition, level, draw and fold, it fits models on the noisy training labels (D) and on D after one mitigation method (D'), across every similarity setting and neighbour count, and scores both on the clean held-out fold.

Datasets: All 41 datasets in the noise job. submit_everything.sh queues complexity, similarity and noise (line 95) on every DATASET_REPS key except chembl_qsar and davis (lines 207-213). n42 is in SINGLE_DATASET_EXPERIMENTS (noise_helpers.py:145) and in HONOURS_NOISE_CONDITION (noise_helpers.py:1586-1588). It is in neither skip list (_shared.py:3672-3675 nucleotide, 3684-3685 large-n), so it also runs on the six nucleotide datasets and on kiba and bindingdb_kd. On classification datasets the n30, n31, n32, n33, n35 and n41 method families are skipped (n42:1025-1031). Conditions swept come from conditions_for_task (n42:940-943, noise_helpers.py:1075-1099).

### R1 models: NO (partly)

Code: The model loop runs the five models in DOWNSTREAM_MODELS_NOISE: rf, xgboost, svm, dnn, lightgbm. svm drops out above 10,000 rows. Each model gets its own model inputs. Every model input is then fitted with rf and svm, plus the loop's own model only when it is rf, svm, lightgbm or xgboost. dnn is never fitted; its model inputs are fitted by rf and svm only. gp is never in the list. The searches it reads score five models, plus gp on small datasets and knn on the distance search.

Decisions: Only each dataset's two Step 1 models, no ridge, knn only where Step 9 allows. Every dataset breaks this, because rf and svm are fitted on every model input and five model loops run. gp is approved but never fitted on abagym_Ang2, abagym_VEGF, ginkgo_acsins, ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_pr_cho. dnn is approved but never fitted on 25 datasets: abagym_EGFR, adme_hlm, adme_mdr1, adme_rlm, bh_doyle_plates, bindingdb_kd, caco2, ddg_combined, flab_expression_adams, flab_expression_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, gb_human_enhancers_cohn, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_hic, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki, kiba, logd, the four nt_H3K datasets, qm9, tcga_brca_pam50. The distance search read includes knn on the six nucleotide datasets, where Step 9 says it is not needed. ridge is never used.

### R2 per fold: NO

Code: It picks every recipe and both base representations once, before the fold loop, from searches run over all rows. get_rule_hybrids is called with no fold index, so the hybrids are ranked on the mean over every fold, the later held-out fold included. Base representations are ranked by the whole-dataset search's own mean. Inside each fold, only the features are rebuilt on that fold's training rows, using the noisy labels. With a representation count below the pool size, the rebuild picks which representations to keep from blueprint.rep_scores. blueprint.reps is the whole pool, so that cut happens, and rep_scores are whole-dataset baseline scores.

Decisions: Every hybrid used for a fold must come from a search built on that fold's training rows only. Here the recipe choice, the base representation choice and the representation subset are all made with every row, including the held-out fold.
