### R3 same cuts: NO

Code: Every search it reads uses one global grid. General: budgets 10 to 2000 features (8), engine-default importance, allocation and representation counts, evaluators match/rf/lightgbm/dnn. Distance: budgets 10 to 500 (6), evaluators knn/rf/dnn/lightgbm/svm. The 14 datasets in FAST_SPEED_DATASETS get the fast lists instead. The hybrids are ranked with budget=None, so any stored budget can win. Augmentation members none, uncapped and capped are read wherever augmentation representations exist. Nothing reads DECISIONS.md.

Decisions: Steps 2-7 cuts per dataset and Step 8 augmentation. Only humanness_therapeutic matches on every axis: nothing is cut there and it has no augmentation representations. tcga_luad_vs_lusc keeps every grid value but has augmentation representations, which Step 8 cuts. Budgets break on the other 39 datasets, general and distance. Importance breaks on abagym_Ang2, abagym_EGFR, bh_doyle_plates, buchwald_hartwig, cdr_flexibility, ddg_combined, flab_binding_adams, flab_binding_koenig, flab_thermo_tresanco, ginkgo_pr_cho, ginkgo_titer, herg_ki. flab_expression_koenig, kiba and bindingdb_kd run lightgbm_gain only but keep all three methods. Allocation breaks on caco2, ddg_combined, ginkgo_acsins, herg_ki and held suzuki. It also lacks softmax_T1 on flab_expression_koenig and kiba, plus wglobal_power2 on bindingdb_kd. Evaluators break on abagym_EGFR, abagym_VEGF, buchwald_hartwig, ginkgo_colloidal, ginkgo_titer. Representation counts break on 19 datasets that cut a count, and bindingdb_kd lacks its kept count 2. Augmentation breaks on all 32 datasets with augmentation representations. ginkgo_hic and ginkgo_colloidal keep uncapped but still get capped.

### R6 missing search: NO (partly)

Code: It never runs a per-fold search. A missing stored search goes through get_precomputed_search, which runs find_best_hybrid on all rows. Under KIRBY_NO_COLD_SEARCH, a search with more than 500 configurations missing raises instead. _iter_pool_searches prints a warning and skips that member. The rule marks the slot missing, and n42 writes the model input as unavailable. The noise start-up never builds the distance search, so hybrid__distance1 depends on disk.

Decisions: A missing per-fold search must be built by the experiment itself. n42 builds a whole-dataset search or, with the refusal on, skips the slot with a warning.

### Other problems

- dnn's model inputs are fitted only with rf and svm. CACHEABLE_MODELS leaves dnn out because its fit is not seeded (n42:1263-1266, n23_uncertainty_cleaning.py:287). So dnn picks the features, and two other models are scored on them.
- The rebuilt hybrid keeps a representation subset chosen from whole-dataset scores. blueprint.reps is the whole pool (find_best_hybrid.py:5389-5398). build_fold_hybrid then cuts it with blueprint.rep_scores (_shared.py:5256-5286). Those scores come from the whole-dataset baselines (find_best_hybrid.py:9593).
- The base_k_aug_uncapped neighbour spaces are built on every dataset with augmentation representations (n07_remediation.py:1712-1748). Step 8 cuts augmentation on 39 of 41 datasets. DECISIONS.md:654 names this case as an open check.
- The result file's 'model_inputs' key lists only base_1, base_2 and hybrid (n42:1272). The models were also fitted on hybrid__general2 and hybrid__distance1. Only 'model_inputs_by_model' lists those two (n42:1277).
- main() defaults --pruning-mode to calibrated (n42:1313). run_all defaults to default_pruning (noise_helpers.py:1706). So a direct call and a call from run_all can read different start-up searches. Unverified whether the pruning schedule changes which stored search is read.
- Besides the downstream models, the methods fit their own learners: an out-of-fold LightGBM prediction (n42:348-350), the n32 exchange learners (n42:1033-1036) and NGBoost (n42:809-811). These are part of the methods by design and are not a selection choice.

### Missed by the first agent, found by the second

- R2: the neighbour spaces are chosen on all rows too, not only the model inputs. These are hybrid_similarity, hybrid_similarity__general2 and hybrid_similarity__distance1, plus the base_k_aug spaces built on each model's top 2 base representations. They come from the same whole-dataset ranking (n42:1039-1052, n07_remediation.py:1700-1784). So the neighbour lists of every similarity setting also depend on the held-out fold.
- R3, kiba and bindingdb_kd: n42 now asks for these two searches at fast speed. That means lightgbm_gain only, three allocation methods, and representation counts 3 and all (_shared.py:1049-1053; dataset_policy.py:709-710). The stored searches hold three importance methods and five allocation methods (DECISIONS.md:313, 315, 379, 398). So the grid n42 asks for differs from both the stored search and the decision. I could not determine whether the reader is then served the stored search or builds a new one.
- R1, side note: n42 passes dnn into the cached hybrid rebuild (n07_remediation.py:1766-1771). noise_cache.cached_hybrid_for_fold states that a model whose fit is not reproducible must not be cached (noise_cache.py:684-686). n42's own comment says dnn's fit is not seeded (n42:1263-1266). So dnn's hybrids are stored from one draw of an unseeded fit. That draw then feeds the rf and svm fits on those hybrids.
